body:
@saoudrizwan 
Added support for service account key.
When using the service account key, installation of the gcloud CLI is not required.

https://github.com/saoudrizwan/claude-dev/issues/83#issuecomment-2290208269

1. Create a new service account in IAM & admin -> Service Accounts
    e.g. `claude-dev` (claude-dev@****.iam.gserviceaccount.com)
2. Create new key (JSON) for the created service account and download credential json
3. Attach `Vertex AI User` role to the created service account in IAM & admin -> IAM
4. base64 encode the credential json as follows
    `base64 -w0 ****.json`
    > Please be careful not to use online Base64 encoding tools
5. Put encoded string to the settings window

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c1912bb9-5d7c-4be0-ad0e-9b96c7d01049)
author: u-minor

body:
I tested authentication via Service Account Key (macOS `base64` does not understand `-w0` btw, just leaving that out worked converting the `.json` file to an unbroken Base64 string)  and I can confirm that this works, Sonnet-3.5 is happily answering requests this way via Vertex AI / GCP.

BTW: I did not have to create a new Service Account to get this working, it worked using the "Compute Engine Default Service Account", which gets automatically created for every new project in GCP (it seems). Or is using this account a bad idea somehow? (I am using GCP only for a week or so, I do not really have a clue what I am doing in this complex thing, but it works for me so far)

Command line for fellow macOS users to convert the Service Account credentials JSON file to Base64 and copy the resulting string to the clipboard to paste it into the correct Claude Dev authentication field:
```shell
base64 -i [ServiceAccountCredentials.json file] | pbcopy
```

body:
Workaround until this PR gets merged:

Build from source and generate VSIX, then install from VSIX in VSCode, with these simple instructions:

```shell
$ git clone https://github.com/saoudrizwan/claude-dev
$ cd claude-dev
$ git fetch origin pull/45/head:vertexai
$ git switch -c localbuild
$ git merge vertexai # should not produce merge errors
$ npm add google-auth-library @anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk
$ git add . && git commit -m "[WIP] add necessary dependencies"
$ npm run install:all
$ npm install -g vsce
$ vsce package
```

And install the generated package e.g. `claude-dev-1.3.4.vsix` inside VSCode.
Repeat if new version gets released (and fix possible merge conflicts).

Hey folks! GCP Vertex support is now available in v1.4.17. The last 2 weeks have been hectic so I apologize taking so long to get around to this. Thank you @u-minor for your work and keeping this branch updated for others that use GCP.

Adding `"(diff -u)"` was a good idea, I got claude to consistently output valid diffs this way (only had ~70% success rate without it) but still running into some problems I've ran into before with structured outputs. It cant do basic tasks–cursor talks about this in a blog post but basically its trained on way less patch diffs than entire code files so it just *sucks* at writing code through diffs. I couldnt even get it to make a snake game on the first try... I then tried giving it the option of using full contents OR diff format, and it almost always chose full contents no matter how small the changes were.

I suspect adding in a diff format is gonna lead to pretty bad results for a lot of people that rely on claude dev so I'm hesitant to add it until I at least get the chance to try anthropic's fast edit mode.

With the new Sonnet 3.5 version out, I wanted to revisit the topic.

Anthropic introduced a lot, but quick code edit is not one of them. Also, based on the same logic of having function calling work the same for all the models out there, this might be a better approach that works for all providers.

Aider Chat [uses diff mode](https://aider.chat/docs/leaderboards/) for all of the top models on the leaderboard. They also provide some [details about how their diff works](https://aider.chat/docs/more/edit-formats.html#diff).

body:
If both "Always allow read-only operations" and "Always allow write operations" are enabled, the agent could enter an endless loop without user intervention. This removes the user's ability to provide feedback or interrupt the process, which is normally done through the approval dialogs.

@saoudrizwan, what do you think would be the best strategy to address this? One potential solution could be adding an "Interrupt" button that stops the loop after the next API call, allowing the user to provide feedback in the message input box. This would maintain the full autonomy with auto-approvals while still giving users control when needed.

body:
Hey thanks for the PR! The openrouter prompt caching should be working, but there could be a couple reasons why the cache would break and reset - the 5 minute ttl expires, an image is added to chat (ie using the browser tool), or the conversation history is truncated due to the context window limit being approached. 

Cline uses the same prompt caching logic described in Anthropic's multi-turn conversation example, where a breakpoint is added to the last two user messages: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#continuing-a-multi-turn-conversation
When you (user) send a message, a breakpoint is added to that message so everything up to and including that message is cached. The next time you make a request with the new assistant message + new user message (with the second cache breakpoint), it will read from the cache created by the former request. Here's a visual example of what I mean, where the bolded text is cached:
API Request 1: **user - assistant - user (breakpoint 1)** - assistant - user (breakpoint 2)
API Request 2: **user - assistant - user - assistant - user (breakpoint 1)** - assistant - user (breakpoint 2)

You can confirm that prompt caching is working by going to https://openrouter.ai/activity and looking at generation details for the requests you make in cline:
![Google Chrome 2024-11-11 19 48 09](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/731f7b52-8242-4c14-85c9-473706e3c65e)
This is a request that was made after a few messages into a task (I even disabled the system prompt cache breakpoint just to prove the user message breakpoints are working properly)

Also I noticed you added the prompt cache beta headers - that isn't necessary according to openrouter's docs (https://openrouter.ai/docs/prompt-caching).

If you can run two identical tasks, one with your version of prompt caching and one with mine, and then compare the cache discounts that openrouter's activity log presents to see if there's any additional savings - that could help me determine if the breakpoint counter idea you've implemented is providing any benefit. Pls feel free to re-open if you find anything inconsistent with what I've mentioned above.
author: saoudrizwan

body:
It seems like you have a different behavior for prompt caching compared to what I'm experiencing. Prompt caching for OpenRouter is not happening at all for me with v2.1.4 or the latest main branch.

I am aware of the Caching discount in the OpenRouter's activity log. That is how I confirmed prompt caching is not working for me.

Here are my tests, where I ask Cline to 'Make it possible to reorder tasks' in a simple React task app created for this test.

### **Test 1: My PR**

**Cline Version:** [https://github.com/ntrpnr/cline/tree/79c37d6a2c1c873f75db67970ca82c5886320cbe](https://github.com/ntrpnr/cline/tree/79c37d6a2c1c873f75db67970ca82c5886320cbe)  
**Provider / Model:** OpenRouter: `anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet`

body:
I do not have time at the moment but, a good first pass that minimally changes this pr would be to replace all boolean evaluations with a function evaluation.

eg: `if (this.alwaysAllowWrite)` becomes `if (this.allowWriteToFile(filename))`

Initially the function can simply `return this.alwaysAllowWrite` and we can expand it in the future.

The next step would be to replace constructor invocations:

```ts
this.cline = new Cline(this, apiConfiguration, customInstructions, alwaysAllowReadOnly, 
        alwaysAllowWrite, alwaysAllowExecute, task, images)
```

with 

```ts
this.cline = new Cline(this, apiConfiguration, customInstructions, alwaysAllowReadOnly, 
        allowWriteToFileRegex[], allowExecuteRegex[], task, images)
```

and the regular expression arrays are built from carriage-return-separated input boxes. (I am very new to TS and my array syntax above maybe wrong, but it gets the point across.)

From there all you need to do is update the "allow" testing functions to match, and this existing PR will look very much the same with two additional input text areas and some kind of split on '\n'.

body:
@KJ7LNW suggested:
> ```ts
> this.cline = new Cline(this, apiConfiguration, customInstructions, alwaysAllowReadOnly, 
>         allowWriteToFileRegex[], allowExecuteRegex[], task, images)
> ```

---

When you have the opportunity to investigate further, I recommend thoroughly testing your patterns—using regex for text and glob for filenames:
* Testing regex and glob patterns can be challenging and time-consuming due to the different escape sequences used in various operating systems and shell environments.

I have found that utilizing a boolean value, such as `true` or `false`, simplifies testing and makes it easier to maintain a codebase:
* Less code generally results in better clarity

On the other hand, I understand your desire for flexibility and security in limiting Cline's write and execution capabilities.

Meanwhile, I wouldn't be surprised if Cline maintainers _intentionally_ decide to decline this pull request to add the options `alwaysAllowWrite` and `alwaysAllowExecute`, as a _deliberate_ design choice:
* Declining this pull request would ensure a human-in-the-loop process instead of towards fully autonomous AI

For liability reasons, Cline maintainers may want to include a disclaimer.

Thank you for your time!

body:
In my testing, I have found that OpenRouter's middle-out transformation can result in unpredictable outcomes because OpenRouter removes the middle portion of the context. The removal is context-dependent on top of LLM's non-determinism.

However, some end users of Cline might find it beneficial to have the Use transforms: ["middle-out"] checkbox available. This option could be useful for those who reach the context length limit—whether it's 8192 or 200000 tokens—and prefer to continue their conversation with Cline rather than starting a new task.
author: lloydchang

body:
Add a new commit https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/862/commits/6059f103d5b92121903f7e66747fed7cd0c40eee

    fix: Don't include transforms field if checkbox is unchecked

    This way, the transforms field will only be included
    in the parameters when openRouterUseMiddleOutTransform is true.

    It allows OpenRouter's default behavior to function as-is.

    Note: All OpenRouter endpoints with 8k or less context length
    will default to using middle-out.

      transforms: ["middle-out"],
      // Compress prompts > context size.
      // This is the default for endpoints
      // with context length <= 8k

    To disable this, set transforms: [] in the request body.

**If you want to `git cherry-pick` this pull request https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/862 into your fork of Cline:**

As for steps-by-steps, I Googled via its [Search Labs' AI Overview](https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/14901683):

> **how to git cherry-pick commits from a pull request in another fork**

which replied:

> To cherry-pick commits from a pull request in another fork, follow these steps:
> 
> Fetch the fork.
> 
> `git fetch <remote-name> <branch-name>`
> 
> Replace `<remote-name>` with the name of the remote for the fork (e.g., `upstream`) and `<branch-name>` with the branch containing the pull request.
> 
> Find the commit hashes.
> 
> `git log <remote-name>/<branch-name>`
> 
> This command will display the commit history of the fetched branch.
> 
> Identify the commit hashes you want to cherry-pick.
> 
> Cherry-pick the commits.
> 
> `git cherry-pick <commit-hash-1> <commit-hash-2> ...`
> 
> Replace `<commit-hash-1>`, `<commit-hash-2>`, etc., with the actual commit hashes you want to cherry-pick.
> 
> Resolve conflicts (if any).
> 
> If there are any conflicts between your branch and the commits you are cherry-picking, Git will stop and ask you to resolve them.
> 
> * Open the conflicted files and manually resolve the conflicts.
> 
> * Add the resolved files using `git add <file>`.
> 
> * Continue the cherry-pick process using `git cherry-pick --continue`.
> 
> Push your changes.
> 
> `git push origin <your-branch>`
> 
> Replace `<your-branch>` with the name of the branch you're working on.
> 
> Example:
> 
> `git fetch upstream main`
> 
> `git log upstream/main`
> 
> `git cherry-pick 8a2b3c4 5d6e7f8`
> 
> `# Resolve conflicts if any`
> 
> `git push origin my-branch`
> 
> Generative AI is experimental.

As expected, the `middle-out` feature is proving to be unpredictable for me. 

I have a Roo Cline task with the following token counts:
- Output: 11.5 million
- Input: 42.4 thousand

I've run out of context window length using Sonnet 3.5 (200k), Gemini 2 (1M), and Gemini 1.5 (2M), and I'm currently trying to use the OpenRouter with the `middle-out` option in Gemini 2.

Root cause isn't a checkbox issue.

When I check the middle-out checkbox, the API request results in the error message: `API Request Failed: Provider returned error.`

I even tried starting a new task with the `middle-out` checkbox checked, but I received the same error message.

I believe there's an architectural limitation in Cline and Roo Cline that I can't circumvent. The context length/window limit eventually reaches a point where even Gemini 1.5, with a 2 million context length, cannot process the request. Similarly, Gemini 2 with a 1 million context length combined with OpenRouter `middle-out` fails to process it as well.

If I don’t use the `middle-out` checkbox, the API request seems to try for a long time until it times out(?) and ultimately resulting in the error: `API Request Failed: Provider returned error.`

My guess is that the message `API Request Failed: Provider returned error` is simply a generic `HTTP 400` or `HTTP 500` response. It seems like the actual error, which likely has more details, is originating from the extended provider on OpenRouter side. In this current situation, Google is the extended provider, via OpenRouter, is returning an error, but OpenRouter isn't conveying the full error message back. Alternatively, Roo Cline may not be able to interpret it.

My next step is to add an API proxy in the middle to debug further. This would allow me to analyze the HTTP request headers, request body, response headers, response body, and response status code. However, I recognize that this approach won't resolve the underlying architectural issues in Cline and Roo Cline.

body:
Great, I see that advanced settings tab is opening the extension configs.

To recap it sounds like we want to restore the hardcoded "dirsToIgnore" variable and the original .gitignore handling (read at extension launch only, no updating) to their original state.  I can also restore the hardcoded 1000 context file limit.

I will restore this comment, which perhaps still has some future value:

```
		/*
		 An event that is emitted when a workspace folder is added or removed.
		 **Note:** this event will not fire if the first workspace folder is added, removed or changed,
		 because in that case the currently executing extensions (including the one that listens to this
		 event) will be terminated and restarted so that the (deprecated) `rootPath` property is updated
		 to point to the first workspace folder.
		 */
		// In other words, we don't have to worry about the root workspace folder ([0]) changing since the extension will be restarted and our cwd will be updated to reflect the new workspace folder. (We don't care about non root workspace folders, since cline will only be working within the root folder cwd)
		// this.disposables.push(vscode.workspace.onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders(this.onWorkspaceFoldersChanged.bind(this)))
```

I wouldn’t recommend decoupling flood protection—it’s a small piece of code that neatly ties this PR together. Even relatively minor operations, like moving a medium-sized folder (~100 files), can introduce inconsistencies because not all inotify events reach the handlers, leading to a desynchronized state with the filesystem. Larger operations can further exacerbate the issue by increasing CPU load and degrading application performance.  The workaround for this is to restart the extension, but that was the work-around for the original problem too.

## Update 1
In order to emit token usage events to cline, the provider has to call a function of the VSCode LM API to count the tokens in a message. However, this seems to be sort of slow and i make use of it twice in every createMessage call. This seems to be slowing things down quite a lot the more messages the history contains.

I'm currently working on a fix for this.
author: julesmons

body:
## Update 2
I've committed some fixes for the problems i have described in "Update 1".

These should further optimize and speed up the provider by a significant amount.
The cline build (including this feature) in my editor is running much better now.

The following changes have been made:
1. Fewer calls to the countTokens of the model (Which in turn speeds up the task handling)
2. Added a sliding token count cache (this is still a proposal and i need to test and make sure it works as intended)
  - Ideally, I'd like to store the count in the message history, instead of keeping a cache.
  - Currently this cache holds a sliding window of the token count of 1000 messages (in RAM). This is an arbitrary value that I'd like to make configurable once i have verified this is a significant performance improvement.
3. The cancellation logic was not working as indended, which i have fixed.
author: julesmons

body:
## Update 3
After some testing i decided to opt for the storage of the token count in the message history.

To implement this, i had to make some changes in the `src/core/Cline.ts` file.
This might be a little out of scope, but i think the performance benefits are substantial enough to warrant it.

The now redundant sliding-window token-count cache has been removed.

---

Edit: The system prompt is currently tokenized every time the `*createMessage` function is called. It's not part of the message history and explicitly passed to `*createMessage` each time (so i can't store a value with it). However; i imagine this system prompt might be the same (or one of a couple of variants) each time. Depending on the performance i experience whilst using Cline, i might add some sort of token-count cache for the system prompt specifically in order to further optimize and speed up the provider and general user-experience.

I've been using the provider this week and kept an eye on debug logs i've placed etc. I've realised that the `getModel` function the ApiHandler providers HAS to be async to better support the VSCode Language Model API. In addition to this, the message history data-structure has to be extended with token info (to avoid needless performance hungry token counting, because the vscode lm api does not expose usage)

author: Bigsy

body:
It's very nice to hear all this positive feedback, much appreciated!

First of all; I've been using a custom build of this provider with copilot for about three weeks now.
I wouldn't exactly call it 'stable', as it freezes occasionally and has some other minor issues.
This is why i've concluded the breaking-changes i've proposed are critical. They're essentially hard-requirements in order to be able to create a smooth experience. Without them, the provider is just not ready to handle a production workload.

The test build of the provider I'm currently using has already allowed me to greatly increase my productivity, generating in the millions of tokens per day (eventually hitting the copilot token-based rate limit). I'm already excited to see what it can do when it's properly finished.

I've also seen RooCline and think their concept/idea is awesome.
Whilst working on this provider (and in the Cline code-base in general), I've found a lot of things that I would implement differently or would like to improve upon (mainly just for the fun of it).
I want to clarify that I'm not saying the Cline code is bad. Quite the opposite actually.
This fantastic project has inspired me to experiment with several Cline-subsystems (which, of course, resulted in a slew of breaking changes).

Opening lots of pull-requests would become very time consuming and cumbersome very quickly.
This inspired me to create a fork of my own called... [Recline](https://github.com/julesmons/recline/tree/recline)! (pun intended)
I've renamed my forked repo for this PR and have started by implementing all mentioned 'breaking changes' on it's main branch. As I'm writing this I'm in the midst of heavy comprehensive refactoring, re-structuring, and the implementation of some new features i thought would be nice.

I've decided to publish Recline so others can try out this provider before it's properly merged into Cline. Keep in mind; I've only tested this provider myself and you might run into some issues. If you do, please create either an issue over at Recline or comment on this PR directly. Any input on this is invaluable.

In addition to this, i want to clarify that Recline's first commit has already diverged the fork too far from the original cline main branch.
This will cause auto-merging of upstream changes to be nearly impossible, forcing any changes to Cline to be manually implemented into Recline.
In light of this, I want to re-iterate that I'm doing this for fun and that I'm not sure I'll have the time to properly maintain a fork. That being said, the fork will of course be open-source and any input or contributions are always welcome. Either trough Recline or this PR directly.

---

### **!!! This does not mean I'm abandoning this PR though !!!**

When I've perfected the VSCode LM provider in Recline, I'll make sure to update this PR with a nicely focussed and cline-compatible version of it!
I would just like to explore what _could_ be changed (what works and what does not) before deciding what _has_ to be changed/implemented, making sure no unnecessary breaking changes get merged into Cline. Recline has been created in order to allow others to try out the changes before they're released trough official channels (Cline).

In the meantime, I'm really keen to hear what @saoudrizwan thinks about:

1. The aforementioned storing the token count in the message history.
The VSCode Language Model API does not supply usage information, but has a countTokens method.
Sadly, i've found that method to be very performance heavy; exponentially slowing the provider down as the message history elongates. Storing the count would enable the provider to only count incomming messages. This way all messages are counted just once.

2. Making the getModel method async. The VSCode Language Model API has an async method to get the required data. I've attempted a workaround, but this does not work.

---

Cheers!

body:
Wow thank you for all the testing! I dug into webp a bit to see what kind of effect your change would have. The webp quality setting in Puppeteer (and in general) works on a scale of 0-100, where:

- 0 is the worst quality but smallest file size
- 100 is the best quality but largest file size
- The default, 75, is generally considered a good balance

Increasing the quality from 75 to 100 could increase the file size significantly - typically by 2-4x. Since we're encoding these screenshots as base64 strings for the API, I'd recommend we keep the default quality of 75. The visual difference is often barely noticeable, while the token impact can be unnecessarily substantial.

Please let me know if I have something wrong here, or if you disagree.

This upstream vscode bug makes it hard to parse terminal output reliably because the `OSC 633];D` end-of-command sequence is usually lost in a race (never received by Cline):
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/237208

I will work around that vscode bug in this PR with future commits.

When [237208](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/237208) is fixed, Cline will be even more reliable in terms of `execute_command`.

# Update: Background Command Execution Test - Line Processing Analysis

This test demonstrates how the system processes lines that only contain carriage returns. The command uses `echo -e -n` with `\n` to generate newlines after each number and 'a' character without a trailing carriage return.

## Command
```bash
for i in {1..10}; do echo -e -n "$i\na"; sleep 3; done
```

This creates a pattern where:

1. Each iteration prints a number followed by `\na` and then delays so we can click "proceed while running" and then verify the output to make sure it is only capturing line breaks 
2. Due to `-n` flag, no automatic newlines are added after each echo
3. The explicit `\n` in the echo creates the line breaks we see
4. The final 'a' has no newline after it due to `-n`, but is still captured in output

This pattern helps test line processing behavior when dealing with:
- Output capture of content without trailing newlines
- Consecutive newlines
- Lines containing only single characters
- Lines ending in different ways (with/without newline)

## Instruction 

I told Cline the following to test with this instruction:

> run for i in {1..10}; do echo -e -n "$i\na"; sleep 3; done . do not provide any analysis but do show any updates you get with respect to the terminal output when I reply

## Output Timeline

Output appears in Cline AI prompts via environment_details, as follows:

1. Initial output (0-3 seconds) when I clicked "proceed while running":
```
Here's the output so far:
1
a2
a3
```

1. Next update (around 9 seconds) when I told it '.' just to send an updated response:
```
### New Output
a4
```

1. Next update (around 15 seconds) when I told it '.' again just to send an updated response:
```
### New Output
a5
a6
```

1. Next update (around 21 seconds), again:
```
### New Output
a7
a8
```

1. Final output (around 27-30 seconds), and again, but after the program exited:
```
# Inactive Terminals
### New Output
a9
a10
a
```

The output appeared in chunks as the terminal updated while the command ran in the background, showing that:
- All background output is accounted for
- intermediate results are carriage-return delimited 
- the last line which contains no carriage return was received correctly when the program exited 

# Edge cases, signals, exit codes, and VSCE bug race tests

I told Cline (as above): 

> use execute_command for simple commands like echo a repeatedly until you have exhausted all test permutations. display the execute command syntax immediately upon my response of content. report the exit code. i will provide you with the exit code in my response do not display the exit code or the signal type in any part I am snippet that you are write. do not chain commands each command should be single. test exit codes using one line Perl commands to print and kill the program itself. exit code above 127 are invalid. run multiple tests and notify me of any unexpected conditions where are the output you receive is not the output that you expect. try edge cases but exclude shell special characters like !. include tests that may generate core dumps. provide a summary in markdown format and save it to doc.md. test differences between /bin/echo and echo shell built-in. also test echo -n. makes sure all program tests exit (no infinite loops). test multiple signals in the kill testing. elaborate on what was unexpected. format the response in markdown using markdown bullets where headings are bullets. if there are problems elaborates with details. nothing command output is trimmed at the beginning and end of white space. use bullets as headings.

## Cline's response:
* Echo behavior is consistent between shell builtin and /bin/echo
* Empty string handling is consistent across all echo variants
* All exit codes were within valid range (0-127)
* Core dumps were successfully generated with SIGABRT and SIGSEGV
* Signal handling produced expected termination messages
* No unexpected conditions or output discrepancies were observed

# Summary

As far as I can tell, all edge cases and behavior for background and foreground processes are behaving as expected. 

Please let me know if you find an edge case that does not work properly and I will take a look.

body:
By adding the VSCode installation folder [`${execInstallFolder}/**`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/services/configurationResolver/common/configurationResolver.ts) to `.vscode/launch.json > configurations[] > skipFiles` one may get source tracing while using methods like `console.log`. This variable has not been added to [the `launch.json` variables reference](https://github.com/Microsoft/vscode-docs/blob/main/docs/editor/variables-reference.md) yet, so a latest VSCode (Insider) build is required. It could be made as default by modifying the default `extensionHost` launch parameters at [microsoft/vscode-js-debug/src/configuration.ts > extensionHostConfigDefaults](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-js-debug/blob/main/src/configuration.ts#L883-L883).

Notice that this change in `.vscode/launch.json` would only solve source tracing issues related to console methods, not error stack traces. In order to show correct source tracing one needs to either use `source-map-support` or change the source code of [Electron](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/45221) and [VSCode](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/145473).

body:
I have found the fix. By adding one of the two lines below in the file `webview-ui/scripts/build-react-no-split.js` one can execute `npm run build` in the folder `webview-ui`. I choose the second one.

```javascript
config.resolve.fallback = { path: false }
config.resolve.fallback = { path: require.resolve("path-browserify") } // need to add "path-browserify": "^1.0.1" in `webview-ui/package.json > dependencies`
```

body:
Thank you for the PR @asbis! Please see diff.ts for how we are parsing partial search/replace blocks. We wait until the search/replace section is complete before applying. 

On a related note, I'm pretty sure 99% of the diff edit fails that occur happen because the model outputs search/replace blocks out of order they appear in the file. The extension expects and prompts the model for search blocks in the order they appear in the file, but sometimes with multiple blocks the model tries to modify a section earlier in the file.
author: saoudrizwan

body:
Thank you for the feedback! I'll look into making this process run more smoothly. I recall having a branch some time ago where everything worked well, so I’ll revisit that code to see if there’s a better approach. I’m confident we can work around the issue.

Even thought he ai does not regenerate the code exactly the same, I think that  part of the problem might be that we’re calling the function too early. One possible solution is to replace any content that can be replaced, and then explicitly tell the AI what was replaced and what wasn’t. That way, the AI stays precise in its edits.

So there should be a workaround this to optimize SEARCH and REPLACE protocol solution.

Cline will already run the terminal commands inside of a devcontainer if vscode is running one.

The goal of this PR was to:
1. Confirm that behavior
2. Add a devocontainer config for development of Cline. This will allow new contributors of Cline to get up and running quickly while also allowing them to isolate their machines from any AI generated code should they choose to use Cline, or any other AI assistant, to build Cline.

body:
After reviewing this more closely, I have a concern about the file size check. Right now `addCheckpointFiles` is getting called whenever we `.commit()`, which happens many times throughout a task, ie after each tool use. We need to keep this operation as efficient as possible, and these changes would be iterating every file and checking its size over and over again, which could be very memory intensive especially for big projects.

We'll need to revisit optimizing for non-git tracked projects, but I think our branching strategy discussed before is ultimately the ideal solution to improving checkpoints performance. Let's keep the new patterns you added for sensible file types to exclude from checkpoint tracking, but remove everything else.

body: Hi! I'm curious why we need to add this compared to the existing Mistral API?
author: saoudrizwan

body:
> Hi! I'm curious why we need to add this compared to the existing Mistral API?

The existing Mistral API used to work with the `codestral-latest` model (free). However, it now appears that model has been replaced with `codestral-2501`, which requires a paid Mistral API key.  I also see other Mistral models listed, suggesting a broader change in their offerings.

So, it seems the free `codestral-latest` access via the Mistral API is no longer available in cline.  This new provider brings back that functionality for users who rely on the free Codestral access.

Essentially, while paid Mistral models (including `codestral-2501`) are accessible through the standard Mistral API endpoint, this new provider specifically targets the free Codestral access (equivalent to the old `codestral-latest` or perhaps the free version of `codestral-2501` as offered via a dedicated endpoint)

I also noticed this documentation which seems relevant: [https://docs.mistral.ai/capabilities/code_generation/#codestral](Codestral) It mentions the `codestral` endpoint.
author: aravindjaimon

body: I wasnt aware of any differences between the two endpoints, are you sure codestral-latest wasnt just an alias for codestral-2501? I dont have any money on it, just an API key and i can use every model from Cline without any issues.
author: ViezeVingertjes

body:
Hey everyone,

Any updates on this? I was looking forward to using the `codestral-latest` model again. It was performing quite well earlier and was free, but after the recent update, I can no longer access it. Currently, I have to downgrade the Cline extension whenever I need to use Codestral.

I noticed that @aravindjaimon has already patched this—would have been great if it had been merged.
author: rahulretnan

body:
> Hey everyone,
> 
> Any updates on this? I was looking forward to using the `codestral-latest` model again. It was performing quite well earlier and was free, but after the recent update, I can no longer access it. Currently, I have to downgrade the Cline extension whenever I need to use Codestral.
> 
> I noticed that @aravindjaimon has already patched this—would have been great if it had been merged.

This should **not** be needed, i spoke to one of the developers and the `codestral` endpoint is **redundant** as Mistral now has a **full free tier** on their main endpoint. You **DO** need to create a new API key for the main endpoint, but can use it for free after that, hopefully that clears things up! :)

You can create the API key here: https://console.mistral.ai/api-keys/

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ecf43ca-c19a-4ab9-9765-f2e0e836914c)

`latest` is just an alias for `codestral-2501` at this time, but in Cline, versions are prefered so it cant break overnight if they decide to point it to a different model.

So still i believe having this feature will be good to have, as the other API key can be used as paid, and Mistral can continue giving free service through this endpoint.

author: ViezeVingertjes

body:
Hello everyone, we will not be accepting this PR.

codestral-2501 (codestral-latest) is already supported via the main Mistral API endpoint at `https://api.mistral.ai/`.   The endpoint hosed at `https://codestral.mistral.ai/` is a "Preview" of upcoming codestral models.  This is considered to be experimental or beta testing and does not align with our mission to support stable API providers.  

The preview endpoint for codestral is still OpenAI compatible and can be used with our compatibility provider.

> From this description, it seems like having one file/directory fail in the list_files implementation makes the entire operation fail. Is this correct?

Yep, and to be precise, it just returns an empty folder, which is reflected in the API Request
```
# Current Working Directory (/home/linh/test) Files
No files found.
```

The root cause is that the call to `globby(pattern, options)` (check line 74 of list-files) does not return partial browsing result if there's an exception. I have looked thoroughly and it seems like there's no option to config globby to work that way. So I believe it's either we have to ask `globby`  author for changes, or make our own implementation
author: linhtran174

body: Closing due to unexpected consequences of not using globby.
author: saoudrizwan

body:
@saoudrizwan : Can you share more about the consequences? This is probably due to current implementation only take care of the root folder `.gitignore` , but globby does handle `.gitignore` in all subfolders. I was aware of this earlier 
https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/1756#issuecomment-2660768369 but not sure if it is needed. Can make another PR to fix it.
author: linhtran174

body:
@linhtran174 Can you double check that there's no way of doing this with the existing globby implementation?

I had time to look into it briefly and I think globby allows a suppress errors option.
author: celestial-vault

body:
@celestial-vault : You're right, `suppressErrors: true` solved the problem, just tested. It makes globby returns partial browsing result instead of empty array. 
It is weird to me that fast-glob have this returning partial result by default without the need to pass the `suppressErrors` param, so I thought the param only prevent throwing exception.

body:
For future reference:

> This configuration modification affects how webpack bundles your JavaScript code, specifically focusing on code splitting behavior. Let's break it down:
> splitChunks: This is webpack's feature for splitting code into smaller chunks
> cacheGroups: { default: false } disables the default cache groups that webpack uses to automatically split common modules into separate chunks
> name: "main" forces all chunks to be combined into a single bundle named "main". This is particularly important for:
> Dynamic imports (like import() statements)
> Third-party libraries that might normally be split into separate chunks
> In your example, Mermaid.js which typically uses dynamic imports
> 2. runtimeChunk: false disables the creation of a separate runtime chunk. The runtime chunk normally contains webpack's module loading logic.
> The practical effects of this configuration are:
> Single Bundle: Instead of multiple JavaScript files, your build will produce just one main JavaScript file
> No Code Splitting: Even when using dynamic imports, everything gets bundled into one file
> Predictable Output: The build process will always generate a single, consistently named file
> This is particularly useful for VS Code webviews because:
> VS Code webviews expect a single, consistently named JavaScript file
> It simplifies resource management since you only need to handle one file
> It prevents potential loading issues that could occur with multiple chunks
> The main trade-off is that you lose the benefits of code splitting (like faster initial page load and better caching), but for VS Code webviews, this is usually the preferred approach.

body: Hi @loupzeur, is there a substansive reason to using ollama compared to the openai package? I can't tell if it would make a difference using the new library, but to me it seems to add more complication in managing another message format to trasform to and maintain. Closing in favor of continuing to use openai as much as we can to reduce tech debt, but feel free to re-open if im missing something
author: saoudrizwan

body:
Hi, @saoudrizwan the idea of this PR was that OpenAI doesn't allow to set a **context size**, and since Ollama set the context by default at 2000 characters, **Cline can't be used with Ollama since it truncate any context above 2000 characters**, thats why the Ollama LLM are never able to complete a task.

By using the Ollama package, we can set a higher context and then some models can be used (the ollama API is a bit different than the OpenAI one, since it allow more parameters).

So this PR isn't just about replacing the OpenAI's API for Ollama, it enable the user to set it context size that isn't supported by OpenAI

author: celestial-vault

body:
Good question. I am not sure. I do understand that it feels like a workaround, but it is surprisingly effective for large projects.

Here are my thoughts on the matter:
- Fundamentally it has always been a struggle to cold start a LLM session for some coding work on an existing project
- Especially for my use cases which are to add features, perform refactors, or make edits on (larger) existing projects.

After quite a lot of trial and error, what would give me by far the best results would be due to two important things:

1. always have the model know the basics about the whole project. Where to find what. Important design choices, Core libraries. Background and goal of the project etc
2. Know the relevant and related files of the thing it should work on from the beginning

Some Notes:
- Aside form the clinerules file, what i would do is to either tell it to read certain files, or open the relevant files and just tell it to read my open files
- I found that just waiting or hoping for the model to either decide to read relevant files itself or guess correctly without reading them has a high chance of failure
- Yet with basic project understanding as well as the important details in the context window, sonnet is extremely good at doing even complex real world programming in existing non trivial projects. In my experience sonnet is quite far beyond anything else in that matter, and i consistently produce high quality code and have a really nice workflow now (although expensive, but in comercial terms its nothing really)
- Anyway, I find myself getting quite annoyed by the copilot- or cline approach of picking individual files from a file picker. it just is for me specifically a terrible UX choice and i dont want to do it. i even rather tell it the approximate names of the files and wait for it to read it one by one, than use the file picker 5 times

Long story short for me the usual go to is to open the files i want it to have in working memory before i even tell it what to do. I cant think of a more convenient way for now.

That said I am fine closing this PR and since i apply my local commits to cline for my work. The point of making this PR was that i really enjoy this feature and thought others might as well
author: Evizero

body:
Hi @Evizero! Thank you for sharing your thoughts and this PR. 
Currently Cline already gets the names of the open tabs as context, and can choose to read those files if wanted.
I'd like to keep the context mentions menu as focused as possible. It might be worth adding this as [a feature request](https://github.com/cline/cline/discussions/categories/feature-requests?discussions_q=is%3Aopen+category%3A%22Feature+Requests%22+sort%3Atop) first and gauging other peoples' interest in this before we decide to add it.

author: saoudrizwan

body:
> It seems like we're not passing in any tools to the requests–these are already defined in the system prompt, and allows Cline to work with models/APIs that dont support tool calling.

@saoudrizwan It does (great job btw!), but the prompt is very optimised for Claude (XML heavy) and confuses smaller local models, especially when they've been fine-tuned to call tools with JSON-based syntaxes (and with tool descriptions in a format chosen by their Jinja template, typically just verbatim JSON schema but sometimes the template converts the tool signatures to TypeScript, e.g for functionary templates). Besides, it's not just XML vs. JSON, most models now use special tokens to signal tool calls boundaries, so it's best to show them examples in the format they know.

In a nutshell, this PR:
- Passes the tools in the query **only for llama.cpp**:
  - this allows triggering grammar-constrained tool calling (increasingly robust even for very small models @ any temperatures),
  - it ensures models are presented w/ tools in a familiar format.
- Expresses the tool call examples (in the system prompt) using the native tool call style of the model.
  - This ensures the model is confirmed in its tool call intuitions
  - This makes it more+++ likely the model's output triggers the grammar-constrained generation (specific to each model's tool call style format) that ~guarantee tool call schema compliance
- Ensures the rest of Cline is unmodified
  - tool call formatter for the examples defaults to the XML syntax,
  - the tool calls returned by llama.cpp are retrofitted into the expected XML syntax so Cline's parser feels at home

> Not sure how much of a demand there is for llama.cpp as a provider, but perhaps we could limit the change to that? Feel free to re-open

I only got disappointing results with the existing OpenAI-Compatible provider talking to llama.cpp.

But if you talk to Qwen 2.5 Coder 32B or even Phi 4 with the right prompt, they make wonders :-D

cc/ @ngxson @ggerganov
author: ochafik

body:
> Not sure how much of a demand there is for llama.cpp as a provider

Note that [llama-server now also powers HuggingFace Inference Endpoints](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions/9669) so it’s not just for local ai enthusiasts.

body:
After doing some research I feel that the actual root cause from the following facts which cause a lot of overhead:
- Introduce batching when reading output. Right now every line generates an event. Instead we can do every 50 lines or 100ms.
- Somehow realted, but it also triggers sending command to WebView each line, and it is expensive operation. Batching should fix it. 
- For storing output it use string object, and append to it each time. It cause a lot of unneeded memory allocation. Instead we can store it as array, and join only when needed.

#1089 does exactly this, it queues output content and only emits it every 100ms.

It can process 1,000,000 lines in 188ms:

```sh

     AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA

```

author: dcbartlett

body:
After looking into OpenRouter's docs a bit more.  They do not offer a secondary Domain or URL where a base change is required.  Their service is OpenAI compatible and If you are needing to use a proxy to access the service, it should work through the OpenAI Compatible Provider we already offer.

Thank you for your contribution, but we will not be accepting this change request.
author: dcbartlett

body:
Hi @dcbartlett, thank you for reviewing the PR! Let me clarify the use case:

Some users are encountering 403 provider errors with OpenRouter (tracked in #1336). While the OpenAI Compatible Provider is a potential solution, it has a significant drawback - it doesn't support claude prompt caching, which makes it considerably more expensive for users.

The custom base URL feature would allow users to route their OpenRouter requests through Cloudflare AI Gateway (https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/providers/openrouter/), which resolves the 403 errors while maintaining the cost benefits of OpenRouter's prompt caching. I've documented this solution in detail at https://luohy15.com/posts/ai/cline-openrouter-fix.

Would you be open to reconsidering this feature given this context? The goal is to provide users with a more cost-effective solution while maintaining full OpenRouter functionality. Happy to discuss any concerns or alternative approaches you might have in mind.
author: luohy15

body: Hey @dcbartlett — the OpenAI compatible provider doesn't add the Anthropic style prompt caching directives, so it would be really handy to have this feature available in the OpenRouter provider when proxying
author: alex-mcgovern

body:
I think the Solution here would be to implement prompt caching functionality for the OpenAI Compatible Provider.  There are a multitude of possible Providers that could support this outside of just OpenRouter.  As for getting 403 errors.  This is a forbidden access response that should be obeyed by the client per specifications.  What you're explaining is a potential surface to circumvent this.

I'll check with OpenRouter to verify that this is an official way to support their service, and if so, we can add an option to use "Cloud flare for traffic" and then a few fields to enter the `account_id` and `gateway_id`.

body:
When working with  LiteLLM, which provides OpenAI compatible API, it seems like you need to do this to enable thinking as outlined in Athropic's docs:

https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api/openai-sdk#extended-thinking-support

It seems to me like Cline is not doing this since it doesn't always know it's talking to Claude 3.7 Sonnet. It also seems apparent since Cline is not performing that well when using this model via my organization's LiteLLM proxy. While the proxy itself can be configured to have thinking enabled with a default budget, it is not practical to expect pre-defined endpoints for different thinking budgets to be set in the proxy itself, especially since it can be configured in the client.

The solution should be an additional configuration option when setting Cline's model to LiteLLM to explicitly pass additional arguments via the extra_body, or at least an option to set thinking and the budget explicitly to be passed.

Thanks in advance for considering my input!

body: @clicube As far as I can tell, AWS does not have a way to launch a custom model and they have a limited set of models in their list.  We should be adding their models to the drop-down instead.  Could you give some insight into why a custom model field is needed?
author: dcbartlett

body:
@dcbartlett 
Thank you for reviewing this PR.

I submitted this PR to utilize the Application Inference Profile feature, enabling multiple users within a single AWS account to track their inference costs more clearly and distinguish expenses between Cline and other applications.

When an Application Inference Profile is created, a unique ID (ARN) is assigned to each profile. Instead of using the model ID, the profile ID is used when making API calls.

According to the [AWS article](https://community.aws/content/2oa6QAE7tgxmAsgAExXY2B2MqCV/getting-started-with-bedrock-application-inference-profile), Application Inference Profiles provide several benefits:

> - Track usage metrics – When you enable model invocation logging and record to CloudWatch logs, you can track requests submitted with an application inference profile to view usage metrics.
> - Use tags to monitor costs – You can attach tags to an application inference profile and track costs for on-demand model invocation requests.
> - Cross-region inference – Increase your throughput by using a cross regional inference profile when creating the application inference profile to distribute invocations across regions.

---
By the way, I hadn't noticed that the settings were retained independently when switching Act-Plan modes. (These are the state items with the `previousMode` prefix.)

I will add this process and push it.

body:
Thanks a lot for the updates @rikaaa0928  --  I just wanted to say that I'm still working on this, and hoping to have it merged as soon as we can.  I've taken a deeper dive into the MCP spec, and have come to understand better what makes this patch awesome. Some of my key learnings:

- Really, Image MCP responses are the same as Text responses that contain base64 encodings
- I think my regex and approach will already support base64 data, so it's kind of about merging image+text modes together
- Rich MCP Display will actually download remote images for preview. An excellent addition will be to allow users to load those URL-image-previews into context as well
- Our support of Resource types is also kinda non-existent, but I'm okay with that for now

@saoudrizwan @rikaaa0928 Everything is looking pretty good. What I did was use the "echo mcp server" I made to test my compendium of URLs and features. You can find that file in our repo, it's called RICH_MCP_TESTING.md -- svgs, webp, embeds continue to work as expected There's one thing that we may want to fix. The overall spirit of "rich mcp display" is that we always display the exact text that the MCP returned, and simply augment the display with extra elements. This way, the user is always clear about what's going into context. This patch seems to *replace* the base64 encoding with the image. Up to you @saoudrizwan if that's acceptable, but I think we may want to still show both, even for base64 Input: ``` data:text/html,

body:
> @Garoth @saoudrizwan One more piece of feedback from me: if a URL is inside a code block, I'm definitely not interested to see an image thumbnail in-between the code. :) I've seen it show up a couple times and it was weird. You could do an emoticon 🖼️ on the right just so I could hover and see what's in there, but straight out showing it there is definitely unexpected and unwanted. And the 🖼️ icon should be `user-select: none` so it won't get copy-pasted.

Thanks, that's a solid point. For now, there's no clear way to decide what's in a code block or not, so I recommend just toggling to "plain mode" if you run into this issue. In the future, I'd like to do much more computationally intensive analysis of MCP responses, to be able to find "chunks" of different kinds of data in them. Then we can do this feature and a lot of other cool stuff

body:
Thank you @yt3trees for this thoughtful contribution! Multiple OpenAI-compatible profiles is a frequently requested feature, and I appreciate the persistence you've shown keeping this PR updated over the past 9 months.

## What This PR Does

This PR adds the ability to manage multiple configuration profiles for the OpenAI Compatible provider. Each profile can have its own:
- Base URL
- API Key  
- Model ID
- Azure API Version
- Custom Headers
- Model configuration settings (context window, max tokens, prices, temperature)

Users can create, switch between, and delete profiles via a dropdown UI in the settings panel. The implementation also handles plan/act mode switching, storing separate profile indices for each mode.

### Files Changed

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `proto/models.proto`, `proto/state.proto` | Added proto fields for configs JSON and selected index |
| `src/api/providers/openai.ts` | Modified constructor to apply config from selected profile |
| `src/core/controller/index.ts` | Updated mode switching to read model info from profiles |
| `src/core/storage/state.ts`, `state-keys.ts` | Added state keys and persistence logic |
| `src/shared/api.ts` | Added `openAiConfigs` array type and default config |
| `src/shared/proto-conversions/` | Proto conversion functions for the new types |
| `webview-ui/src/components/settings/providers/OpenAICompatible.tsx` | Significant UI rewrite with profile dropdown, add/delete buttons |
| `webview-ui/src/utils/validate.ts` | Added validation for profile configs |

## Critical Blocking Issues

### 1. Merge Conflicts (CONFLICTING)

The PR has merge conflicts that need to be resolved. GitHub shows `mergeable: CONFLICTING`. The codebase has evolved significantly since March 2025.

### 2. Storage Architecture Mismatch

This is the fundamental issue @0xToshii identified. The codebase has migrated from the old `src/core/storage/state.ts` pattern to a new `StateManager` class (`src/core/storage/StateManager.ts`). This PR modifies the **deleted** `state.ts` file.

The PR stores everything in `openAiConfigs` as a JSON array in global state, including API keys. This is a **security concern** because:

1. **API keys should use VS Code's secret storage** - The codebase stores all secrets via `context.secrets.store()` (see `Secrets` interface in `src/shared/storage/state-keys.ts:231`). Storing API keys in global state means they're not encrypted.

2. **The storage pattern doesn't match current architecture** - Other providers store their API key in `Secrets`, their base URL in `Settings`, and their mode-specific model IDs in `Settings` with `planMode*` / `actMode*` prefixes.

### 3. Package.json Test Script Change

The PR modifies the test script to add `cross-env` and `--loader ts-node/esm`, but this change appears unrelated to the feature and may break CI for other contributors:

```diff
-"test:unit": "TS_NODE_PROJECT='./tsconfig.unit-test.json' mocha",
+"test:unit": "cross-env TS_NODE_PROJECT='./tsconfig.unit-test.json' mocha --loader ts-node/esm 'src/**/*.test.ts'",
```

## Suggested Path Forward

To align with the current architecture, the implementation would need to:

1. **Store profile API keys separately in secrets** - Each profile's API key needs its own secret key (e.g., `openAiProfileApiKey_0`, `openAiProfileApiKey_1`, etc.)

2. **Integrate with StateManager** - Use `StateManager.setGlobalStateBatch()`, `StateManager.setSecretsBatch()` patterns instead of the old `updateGlobalState()` / `storeSecret()` functions

3. **Follow the plan/act mode pattern** - Other providers use `planModeOpenAiModelId`, `actModeOpenAiModelId` etc. Consider whether profiles should work similarly or independently

4. **Consider scope** - Given how much the codebase has changed, it may be more practical to start fresh with a new PR that follows current patterns, using this PR as reference for the UI design

## For Maintainers

### Recommendation: Needs Major Rework or Fresh Start

This PR has been open for 9+ months and the codebase has undergone significant architectural changes (StateManager migration, new storage patterns). While the feature is valuable and the UI work is solid, the implementation would need substantial rework to align with current patterns and address the security concern around API key storage.

**Options:**
1. **Close and re-implement** - A maintainer or the author could create a fresh PR following current patterns, using this as design reference
2. **Deep rework** - The author would need to significantly rewrite the storage layer integration

### Related Context

- The discussion in comments shows community interest in this feature
- @0xToshii already identified the key storage issue and attempted a re-implementation
- The author @yt3trees has been responsive and diligent about keeping the PR updated

### SME Table

| SME | Reason |
|-----|--------|
| @celestial-vault | Primary contributor to affected files (14 commits in 6 months), asked about cross-provider consistency |
| @0xToshii | Reviewed this PR, identified the storage architecture issue, attempted re-implementation |

body:
> Heya @chi-cat thanks so much for looking into this. Improving diff editing is a big priority for us internally, and I saw your discussion in [#2197 issues.](https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/2197)嘿，非常感谢你关注这个问题。改进差异编辑是我们内部的重要优先事项，我看到你在#2197 问题中的讨论了。
> 
> Currently, diff edits may fail for one of two reasons:当前，差异编辑可能因以下两种原因之一而失败：
> 
> 1. Prompt level / llm level — the model writes the wrong search block that doesn't match the actual file提示级别/llm级别——模型生成的搜索块与实际文件不匹配
> 2. Algorithm Level — the algorithm we use to apply the search/replace doesn't correctly find a way to do that, even though the underlying search text is correct算法级别——我们用于应用搜索/替换的算法未能正确找到实现方式，尽管底层搜索文本本身是正确的
> 
> You're attacking this at the algorithm level, but I fear the real problem is at the LLM input level. Also, you're creating a parallel way of doing this, instead of replacing what we're currently doing. Is there a reason to introduce v2 instead of just replacing v1 functionality?您正在算法层面解决这个问题，但我担心真正的问题在于LLM输入层面。此外，您正在创建一种并行实现方式，而不是替换现有方案。是否有必要引入 v2 版本而非直接替换 v1 功能？
> 
> Also, for your tests, if we're going to be robust about this, can we use examples from here at the very least:另外，关于你的测试，如果我们要做到足够健壮，至少应该使用这里的示例： https://github.com/Aider-AI/polyglot-benchmark

Thank you very much for your reply; the original design is excellent; regarding the two failure reasons you mentioned; the issue discussed in this PR might be closer to the latter (the model attempts to follow the instruction prompts as much as possible, but it's not perfect)

Let me briefly outline the original process

```mermaid
graph TD 
    START[Start Processing] --> PARSE[Parse diff line] 
    PARSE --> CHECK_MARKER{Is it a marker line?}
    CHECK_MARKER -->|SEARCH start| ENTER_SEARCH[Enter search state] 
    CHECK_MARKER -->|== divider line| HANDLE_MATCHING[Execute content matching] 
    CHECK_MARKER -->|REPLACE end| FINISH_BLOCK[Complete replacement block] 
    CHECK_MARKER -->|Normal line| CHECK_STATE{Current state} 
    CHECK_STATE -->|inSearch| ACCUMULATE_SEARCH[Accumulate search content] 
    CHECK_STATE -->|inReplace| ACCUMULATE_REPLACE[Accumulate replacement content] 
    CHECK_STATE -->|No state| FILTER_LINE[Discard] 
    HANDLE_MATCHING --> MATCH_STRATEGY[[Matching strategy selection]] 
    MATCH_STRATEGY --> EXACT{Exact match} 
    EXACT -->|Success| UPDATE_BUFFER[Update result buffer] 
    EXACT -->|Failure| LINE_TRIMMED{Line trimmed match} 
    LINE_TRIMMED -->|Success| UPDATE_BUFFER 
    LINE_TRIMMED -->|Failure| BLOCK_ANCHOR{Block anchor match} 
    BLOCK_ANCHOR -->|Success| UPDATE_BUFFER 
    BLOCK_ANCHOR -->|Failure| THROW_ERROR[Throw error] 
    FINISH_BLOCK --> ADVANCE_POINTER[Update processing position] 
    ADVANCE_POINTER --> CHECK_FINAL{Is it the final block?} 
    CHECK_FINAL -->|Yes| APPEND_REMAINING[Append remaining original content] 
    CHECK_FINAL -->|No| PARSE 

    classDef process fill:#4CAF50,stroke:#388E3C; 
    classDef decision fill:#FFC107,stroke:#FFA000; 
    classDef error fill:#F44336,stroke:#D32F2F; 
    classDef storage fill:#2196F3,stroke:#1976D2; 
    class START,PARSE,ENTER_SEARCH,ACCUMULATE_SEARCH,ACCUMULATE_REPLACE,UPDATE_BUFFER,ADVANCE_POINTER,APPEND_REMAINING process; class CHECK_MARKER,CHECK_STATE,EXACT,LINE_TRIMMED,BLOCK_ANCHOR,CHECK_FINAL decision; class THROW_ERROR error; class FILTER_LINE storage; linkStyle 7,9,11 stroke:#FF5722,stroke-width:2px;
```

But here I encountered two minor issues that troubled me.
First, when inSearch is false and inReplace is false; the currently traversed line will be ignored (blue block in the flowchart)

```
<<< SEARCH
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';
=======
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';
import type { ErrnoException } from 'node';
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

The error at this point triggers the expected third part of the logic

```
3. Empty SEARCH Section:
 *    - If SEARCH is empty and the original file is empty, this indicates creating a new file
 *      (pure insertion).
 *    - If SEARCH is empty and the original file is not empty, this indicates a complete
 *      file replacement (the entire original content is considered matched and replaced).
```

Secondly, when the SEARCH-REPLACE block is not properly closed, and the model generation ends (possibly due to context truncation from excessive length, or other reasons); this incorrectly appends the remaining content of the source file.

```
<<<<<<< SEARCH
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';
=======
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';
import type { ErrnoException } from 'node';
```

I believe with the development of large language models, after some time it will fully comply with instructions to generate SEARCH-REPLACE blocks; but it seems now is not yet the time; so I hope these issues can be resolved at the algorithmic level.

Firstly, incorrect content should be added to a staging area; when correct markers are found later, attempts can be made to fix it from the staging area; if content remains in the staging area when file processing completes, it likely indicates an error.
Secondly, when isFinal is triggered; after all diffContent has been processed, some status checks should be added to ensure the remaining content of the source file is appended at the appropriate position.

My code has made these adjustments based on the original process.

Regarding the test cases([https://github.com/Aider-AI/polyglot-benchmark](https://github.com/Aider-AI/polyglot-benchmark) )you mentioned; I think I can spend some time to complete them to ensure the robustness of the code. If any issues are discovered during the process, I will also make timely adjustments.
If you have any other suggestions; please also raise them.

Cline is truly a great project; it has brought me some help. Additionally, I have raised some suggestions regarding the blockAnchorFallbackMatch method in another PR #2533 , and I also hope to keep the discussion going with you.

body:
> Heya @chi-cat thanks so much for looking into this. Improving diff editing is a big priority for us internally, and I saw your discussion in [#2197 issues.](https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/2197)嘿，非常感谢你关注这个问题。改进差异编辑是我们内部的重要优先事项，我看到你在#2197 问题中的讨论了。
> 
> Currently, diff edits may fail for one of two reasons:当前，差异编辑可能因以下两种原因之一而失败：
> 
> 1. Prompt level / llm level — the model writes the wrong search block that doesn't match the actual file提示级别/llm级别——模型生成的搜索块与实际文件不匹配
> 2. Algorithm Level — the algorithm we use to apply the search/replace doesn't correctly find a way to do that, even though the underlying search text is correct算法级别——我们用于应用搜索/替换的算法未能正确找到实现方式，尽管底层搜索文本本身是正确的
> 
> You're attacking this at the algorithm level, but I fear the real problem is at the LLM input level. Also, you're creating a parallel way of doing this, instead of replacing what we're currently doing. Is there a reason to introduce v2 instead of just replacing v1 functionality?您正在算法层面解决这个问题，但我担心真正的问题在于LLM输入层面。此外，您正在创建一种并行实现方式，而不是替换现有方案。是否有必要引入 v2 版本而非直接替换 v1 功能？
> 
> Also, for your tests, if we're going to be robust about this, can we use examples from here at the very least:另外，关于你的测试，如果我们要做到足够健壮，至少应该使用这里的示例： https://github.com/Aider-AI/polyglot-benchmark

@pashpashpash Additionally, I noticed [(https://github.com/Aider-AI/polyglot-benchmark](https://github.com/Aider-AI/polyglot-benchmark) this project has automated test scripts prepared for aider; does the cline project have any relevant scripts that can be reused (hopefully yes)
author: chi-cat

body:
hi @chi-cat! thank you for taking the time to dive into diff.ts and fix the issue you were running into 🙌

i'd love for more people to dive into this class and contribute to how we translate llm structured output -> file edits in a flexible enough way to account for e.g. cases like what you saw where the model may not use the correct search/replace markers, requring this buffer approach you implemented.

just so i understand it, your changes accomplish the following: v2 uses a buffer for handling partial or malformed markers, whereas v1 processes lines in a straightforward, linear way. In v2, any lines that do not immediately fit the recognized search or replace markers go into a “pending” buffer, and specialized fix-up methods (like tryFixSearchBlock, tryFixReplaceBlock, tryFixSearchReplaceBlock) try to interpret collected text once the correct marker eventually appears.

i hope to have your continued help and guidance in improving diff editing in cline. @pashpashpash is actively working to reduce the diff edit issues users see in cline, so having @chi-cat's perspective in changes we make here would be very valuable!

body:
Note: I approved this PR because it highlighted a problem with Non UTF-8 characters that I replicated locally with the current version of cline and that problem was solved with these libraries(The problem is defined in the PR description). 


As for the packagees , the addition of jschardet and iconv-lite appears necessary to properly fix the bug described.
- Node.js's Buffer.toString(encoding) method supports a limited set of encodings (utf8, utf16le, latin1, base64, hex, ascii, binary, ucs2). It crucially lacks support for many common legacy encodings (Shift_JIS, EUC-KR, GBK, Big5, ISO-8859 series, Windows-125x, etc.).
- Node.js's built-in fs.readFile function requires you to specify the encoding beforehand if you want a string, or it returns a raw Buffer. It does not have a reliable mechanism to automatically detect the encoding of arbitrary file content.
- Without [jschardet](https://www.npmjs.com/package/jschardet) (or a similar detection library), the extension cannot reliably determine the correct encoding of files that aren't UTF-8.
-  Without [iconv-lite ](https://www.npmjs.com/package/iconv-lite)(or a similar conversion library), the extension cannot correctly decode the content of files once an encoding unsupported by Node.js's native Buffer.toString() is detected.

Attempting to handle the myriad of possible encodings without these specialized libraries would be extremely complex and error-prone, likely reinventing the wheels that these libraries already provide effectively. They directly address the core requirements of detecting and decoding non-UTF-8 text.

body:
@mrexodia , it seems this feature only works when you pass the `LiteLLM Model Name` (`litellm_params.model`), but not the `Public Model Name` (`model_name`)

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d5c04473-34f8-48fc-8626-168cfe0f816e)

If I have a defined model as:

```yaml
  - model_name: claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219-v1:0 # Public Model Name
    litellm_params:
      model: bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219-v1:0 # LiteLLM Model Name
      aws_access_key_id: xxxxxxx
      aws_secret_access_key: xxxxxxxx
      aws_session_name: xxxxxxxx
      aws_role_name: xxxxxxx
      aws_region_name: xxxxxxx
```

And I use the model ID in Cline `claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219-v1:0`, the `/spend/calculate` returns `400 Bad Request`. This is because `/spend/calculate` endpoint expects the `LiteLLM Model Name` and not `Public Model Name`.

```bash
# 400 Bad Request

curl --location 'http://localhost:4000/spend/calculate'
--header 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234'
--header 'Content-Type: application/json'
--data '{
    "completion_response": {
        "model": "claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219-v1:0",
        "usage": {
            "prompt_tokens": 9,
            "completion_tokens": 12
        }
    }
}'
```

```bash
# 200 OK

curl --location 'http://localhost:4000/spend/calculate'
--header 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234'
--header 'Content-Type: application/json'
--data '{
    "completion_response": {
        "model": "bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219-v1:0",
        "usage": {
            "prompt_tokens": 9,
            "completion_tokens": 12
        }
    }
}'
```

Did you validate this pull request for both options? LiteLLM Model Name and Public Model Name?

I'm looking forward your responses

Thanks

The file will be tracked, but if you try to commit it, it will remove it from the commit and stop tracking it for that index.  If a user resets their index, it will be tracked again.  This is needed so that we can forcefully update the package-lock with automation when needed.

@anthonyjj89 

Hey, yeah of course.

Basically, you can do `git checkout -b "your-new-branch"` while on a branch to make a branch OFF of that branch. Then, when you open a PR, you can choose the base to be the branch that you made the PR off of, rather than main. Ask ChatGPT about it and you'll quickly find out.

As far as splitting up a PR, yes, this is a tricky thing to do. Basically, try to do things in isolated units. For a feature this large, I would make sure you get buy-in in the discussions tab or the Discord before spending a lot of time on it.

In this particular PR, it seems you are adding many complementary features. I would think hard about how they could stand on their own.

body:
Hey @Huodoo, thank you for contributing this fix for proxy issues in WSL/remote development environments! I can see this addresses a real pain point that users were experiencing with network errors when `http_proxy`/`https_proxy` environment variables are set.

## What This PR Does

This PR creates a custom axios instance at `src/utils/http.ts` with `proxy: false` to prevent axios from automatically using proxy settings inherited from the environment. The PR then updates four files to import axios from this custom module instead of directly from the `axios` package:

- `src/api/providers/cline.ts` - API handler for Cline backend
- `src/api/providers/openrouter.ts` - API handler for OpenRouter
- `src/integrations/misc/link-preview.ts` - Link preview functionality
- `src/services/account/ClineAccountService.ts` - Account service API calls

The intent is to fix issue #1982 where users in WSL environments with proxy environment variables would experience network errors because axios was attempting to route requests through a proxy that couldn't reach the target APIs.

## Review Findings

### This PR Has Been Superseded

Unfortunately, this PR is now **outdated and conflicts with work that has already been merged**. Since this PR was opened in March 2025, significant proxy-related infrastructure improvements have been made:

1. **PR #7328** (merged Nov 2025) - Added comprehensive proxy support with `getAxiosSettings()` function in `src/shared/net.ts`
2. **PR #7659** (merged Nov 2025) - Extended proxy rules and added proxy support to more components
3. **PR #7263** (merged Nov 2025) - Added environment proxy support for standalone mode

The current codebase already has a well-designed solution in `src/shared/net.ts` that:
- Provides `getAxiosSettings()` which configures axios to use a fetch adapter with proper proxy support
- Provides `fetch` from `@/shared/net` that handles proxy configuration per platform (VSCode vs JetBrains/CLI)
- Documents best practices for network requests

The files this PR modifies have already been updated:
- `src/core/api/providers/cline.ts` (note: path changed from `src/api/providers/`) now imports from `@/shared/net` and uses `getAxiosSettings()`
- `src/core/api/providers/openrouter.ts` similarly updated
- `src/integrations/misc/link-preview.ts` now uses `fetch` and `getAxiosSettings()` from `@/shared/net`
- `src/services/account/ClineAccountService.ts` now uses `getAxiosSettings()`

### Why the PR's Approach Was Problematic

Even if this PR had been merged earlier, the approach of globally disabling proxy via `axios.create({ proxy: false })` would have been too blunt—it would have broken proxy support entirely for users who legitimately need it (e.g., corporate environments). The current solution in `main` is more nuanced: it respects proxy configuration while handling the specific issues with WSL/devcontainer environments properly.

---

## For Maintainers

**Recommendation: Close this PR** - The issue has already been addressed through a more comprehensive solution in merged PRs #7328, #7659, and #7263. The current `src/shared/net.ts` infrastructure properly handles proxy configuration.

The original issue #1982 has also been closed with a bot response explaining the workaround and documenting that proxy configuration issues are the root cause.

**Related Context:**
- Issue #1982 - The linked issue (closed)
- PR #7328 - Added `getAxiosSettings()` and comprehensive proxy support
- PR #7659 - Extended proxy support to more components
- PR #7263 - Environment proxy support for standalone mode
- `.clinerules/network.md` - Documentation for proper network handling

| SME | Reason |
|-----|--------|
| @dominiccooney | Primary author of the proxy support infrastructure (PRs #7328, #7659) and contributor to `src/shared/net.ts` |
