 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | package.json | Updates three direct dependency version constraints: minimatch (^3.0.3 → ^9.0.9, major jump), axios (^1.12.0 → ^1.13.6), and simple-git (^3.27.0 → ^3.33.0) to address CVEs. | | package-lock.json | Locks updated resolutions for hono (4.11.7→4.12.7), @hono/node-server (1.19.9→1.19.11), fast-xml-parser (5.3.4→5.4.1), simple-git (3.30.0→3.33.0), axios (1.13.4→1.13.6), express-rate-limit (8.2.1→8.3.1), qs (6.14.1→6.15.0), ajv (8.17.1→8.18.0), underscore (1.13.7→1.13.8), minimatch (3.1.2→9.0.9), and others. body:
Greptile Summary

This PR adds `provider` as a required parameter to `captureTokenUsage()` in `TelemetryService`, bringing it into parity with the sibling `captureConversationTurnEvent` method. The `provider` value is now included in both the `task.tokens` event properties and all OpenTelemetry metric attributes (counters and histograms), enabling downstream analytics pipelines to filter and aggregate token usage by inference provider. **Key changes:** - `captureTokenUsage` signature updated with a new `provider: string` parameter inserted between `tokensOut` and `model`, matching the parameter ordering convention of `captureConversationTurnEvent`. - A shared `attributes = { ulid, provider, model }` object is extracted, reducing repetition across ~10 `recordCounter`/`recordHistogram` call sites. - `costAttributes` updated to spread from `attributes` rather than rebuilding it inline. - Call site in `src/core/task/index.ts` updated to pass `providerId`, which was already in scope from `getCurrentProviderInfo()`. - All four unit tests updated with the new argument and extended with provider assertions.

Confidence Score: 5/5

- This PR is safe to merge — it only adds a new field to telemetry payloads with zero behavioral impact on the extension. - The change is a narrow, well-scoped plumbing fix with a single call site. TypeScript's required-parameter enforcement prevents regressions at any future call sites. Tests cover the happy path for both event properties and metric attributes with the new field. The DRY refactor of `attributes` reduces the chance of future inconsistencies. - No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a tool-call ID collision bug in the `GeminiHandler` where multiple `functionCall` parts sharing the same `responseId` would overwrite each other in downstream tool-call aggregation keyed by ID. The fix introduces a `Map` counter scoped to each `createMessage` invocation that generates stable, sequenced synthetic IDs (`-tool-0`, `-tool-1`, …) when Gemini does not supply a `functionCall.id`, and preserves Gemini-provided IDs when they are present. Key changes: - `src/core/api/providers/gemini.ts`: Introduces `responseToolCallSequence` map; `tool_call.call_id` and `tool_call.function.id` are now set to the unique per-call ID instead of the raw `chunk.responseId`. - `src/core/api/providers/__tests__/gemini.test.ts`: Adds two unit tests — one verifying ID uniqueness across multiple chunks sharing a `responseId`, and one verifying that Gemini-supplied `functionCall.id` values are passed through unchanged. - The top-level `id: chunk.responseId` field on the emitted `tool_calls` object is intentionally left unchanged (it identifies the response, not the individual call). - One gap: if Gemini were to return duplicate explicit `functionCall.id` values, those would still collide since the counter-based deduplication only runs for the absent-ID path.

Confidence Score: 4/5

- This PR is safe to merge — it is a narrow, provider-specific bug fix with no shared-infrastructure changes and passing unit tests. - The counter logic is correct for the common cases (multiple chunks sharing a responseId, and Gemini-provided IDs). A minor untested edge case exists if Gemini itself returns duplicate explicit `functionCall.id` values, but this is unlikely in practice and not a regression introduced here. - No files require special attention beyond the logic comment on `src/core/api/providers/gemini.ts` lines 258–266 regarding the duplicate-explicit-ID edge case.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/core/api/providers/gemini.ts | Adds a per-responseId counter (Map) to generate unique synthetic tool-call IDs when Gemini emits multiple function calls sharing a responseId. Logic is correct for the common case; a minor edge case exists if Gemini provides duplicate explicit functionCall.id values. | | src/core/api/providers/__tests__/gemini.test.ts | Adds two focused unit tests for the ID-uniqueness fix. Tests cover separate-chunk collision and preserved Gemini-provided IDs, but miss the primary bug trigger: multiple functionCall parts within a single streaming chunk. |

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR adds a nock-based VCR (record/playback) system for HTTP interactions to the Cline CLI, enabling deterministic e2e testing without live API calls. The approach is architecturally sound — nock is kept as an external devDependency, lazy-imported only when `CLINE_VCR` is set, and `shared/net.ts` correctly defers to `globalThis.fetch` at call-time (not capture-time) so nock's patches are visible. Key issues found: - **SIGTERM will silently discard the cassette** (`cli/src/utils/vcr.ts:127–129`): Node.js does not emit the `exit` event for unhandled SIGTERM; the `saveRecordings` handler will never run if the process is terminated this way (e.g. CI timeout). An explicit `process.on("SIGTERM", ...)` handler is needed. - **Malformed cassette file produces a confusing crash** (`cli/src/utils/vcr.ts:140`): `JSON.parse` has no error handling — a partially written or corrupted cassette throws a bare `SyntaxError` with no file path context. - **Unconsumed interceptors go undetected in playback** (`cli/src/utils/vcr.ts:152–158`): If a test makes fewer API calls than the cassette recorded, nock silently drops the leftover interceptors. An `exit` handler checking `nock.pendingMocks()` would flag this for test reliability.

Confidence Score: 3/5

- Safe for non-VCR paths; the recording mode has a data-loss bug (SIGTERM) that warrants a fix before this is used in CI. - The core design is correct and the non-VCR code path is unaffected. However, the SIGTERM issue means a recording session killed by CI will silently produce no cassette — a real data-loss scenario for the primary use-case of this feature. The JSON.parse and unused-interceptor issues are lower severity but should be fixed before the feature sees broad adoption. - cli/src/utils/vcr.ts — SIGTERM handler, JSON.parse error handling, and unconsumed interceptor check all need attention.

The proxy bypass is an acknowledged limitation. Minor refactor to remove an unnecessary else branch. | | cli/src/index.ts | VCR initialization is correctly placed before program.parse() and gated on VITEST not being set. body:
Greptile Summary

This PR introduces `cline mcp add`, a first-class CLI shortcut for registering MCP servers without hand-editing `cline_mcp_settings.json`. It supports stdio (default), HTTP (`--type http`, mapped to `streamableHttp`), and SSE transports, reuses the existing `ServerConfigSchema` for validation, and bootstraps the settings file when it doesn't yet exist. Key changes: - **`cli/src/utils/mcp.ts`** — new utility that resolves the settings path via the existing CLI config resolution chain, validates configs against `ServerConfigSchema`, guards against common URL-as-stdio mistakes, and writes the new entry atomically. - **`cli/src/index.ts`** — registers the `mcp` command group and `mcp add` subcommand; thin wrapper delegates to the utility. - **Tests** — `mcp.test.ts` covers the three core write paths; `index.test.ts` adds command-registration smoke tests. - **Docs** — `configuration.mdx` updated with concrete CLI examples for both transport types. Two issues were found in `cli/src/utils/mcp.ts`: the URL-as-stdio guard only fires when exactly one argument is passed (a URL plus any additional argument bypasses the check and writes a silently broken stdio config), and the return value of `ServerConfigSchema.parse()` is discarded, so schema-level defaults (`timeout`, `autoApprove`) and transform cleanup never reach the file on disk.

Confidence Score: 3/5

- Safe to merge with minor fixes — the logic bug in the URL guard can silently write a broken stdio config entry in an edge case. - The core feature is well-structured and isolated behind a new command. The two issues in `cli/src/utils/mcp.ts` — the incomplete URL guard and the discarded Zod parse result — are real but low-severity: the URL bypass requires a user to pass multiple arguments where the first happens to be an HTTP URL (an unusual mistake), and the missing defaults are re-applied at runtime anyway. Existing command behavior is untouched. - cli/src/utils/mcp.ts — the URL guard on lines 75–88 and the discarded parse results on lines 101 and 116.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | cli/src/utils/mcp.ts | New utility for writing MCP server entries to `cline_mcp_settings.json`. Has two issues: (1) the URL-as-stdio guard only checks when exactly one argument is passed, allowing a URL to be silently written as a `command` when extra args are present; (2) the return value of `ServerConfigSchema.parse()` is discarded, so schema-level defaults and transforms never reach the file on disk. | | cli/src/utils/mcp.test.ts | New tests covering stdio write, HTTP mapping to `streamableHttp`, and the URL-without-type error path. Good happy-path coverage; no test for the duplicate-name guard or for the multi-argument URL bypass edge case. | | cli/src/index.ts | Adds `mcp add` subcommand registration and a thin `addMcpServer` wrapper that delegates to the utility and handles error/exit. Clean integration; `exit` is already imported, action signature matches Commander's call convention. | | cli/src/index.test.ts | Adds command-registration smoke tests for `mcp add`, verifying `--type` default and option parsing. Straightforward additions that mirror existing test patterns. | | docs/cline-cli/configuration.mdx | Updates CLI docs to show the new `cline mcp add` shortcut commands for stdio and HTTP servers, and refreshes the note about interactive MCP management. Changes are accurate and helpful. |

The critical fixes address a remote code execution vulnerability in `simple-git` (CVE-2026-28292), an authorization bypass via encoded slashes in `hono` (CVE-2026-29045), and XSS via XML entity shadowing in `fast-xml-parser` (CVE-2026-25896). Key changes: - **Direct dependency bumps** in `package.json`: `simple-git` (`^3.27.0` → `^3.33.0`), `axios` (`^1.12.0` → `^1.13.6`), and `minimatch` (`^3.0.3` → `^9.0.9` — a large major-version jump in devDependencies) - **Lock file-only updates** for transitive dependencies: `hono` (4.11.7 → 4.12.7), `@hono/node-server` (1.19.9 → 1.19.11), `fast-xml-parser` (5.3.4 → 5.4.1), `@aws-sdk/xml-builder` (3.972.4 → 3.972.10), `underscore` (1.13.7 → 1.13.8), `express-rate-limit` (8.2.1 → 8.3.1), `qs` (6.14.1 → 6.15.0), and `ajv` (8.17.1 → 8.18.0) - The `minimatch` upgrade from v3 to v9 is the highest-risk change, though minimatch is not directly imported in project source code; the lock file correctly provides nested v3.x copies for tools that still require them - Transitive-only fixes rely on the lock file being committed and `npm ci` being used in CI/CD — regenerating the lock file could reintroduce some vulnerabilities

Confidence Score: 4/5

- Safe to merge after verifying build and tests pass; security fixes significantly outweigh the low upgrade risk. - The PR addresses critical security vulnerabilities with straightforward version bumps. The main risk is the `minimatch` devDependency major version jump (v3 → v9), but it is not imported directly in source code and the lock file properly manages compatibility. Transitive-only fixes are a minor long-term durability concern but acceptable given standard `npm ci` usage in CI/CD. - No files require special attention beyond verifying the build and test suite passes with the new `minimatch` v9 devDependency.

Comments Outside Diff (1)

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a complete failure of the Claude Code provider when using Claude 4.6 models with CLI v2.1+, caused by four compounding issues now all addressed. The changes span the stream-parsing layer (`claude-code.ts`), the type definitions (`types.ts`), the CLI invocation (`run.ts`), and the task loop (`index.ts`). **Key changes:** - `run.ts`: Extends the `--disallowedTools` list with 12 new CLI tools (e.g., `TaskOutput`, `AskUserQuestion`, `ExitPlanMode`, `CronCreate`) and drops obsolete names (`LS`, `MultiEdit`, `NotebookRead`, `TodoRead`, `exit_plan_mode`) — this is the primary fix that prevents 4.6 models from choosing native tool_use over Cline's XML tools. - `types.ts`: Adds `LegacyRateLimitEvent`, `RateLimitEvent`, and `UserMessage` types to the union; extends `ResultMessage.subtype` to include `"error"` and `"error_max_turns"`; adds optional `error` field on `AssistantMessage`. - `claude-code.ts`: Adds explicit branches for `rate_limit_event` (new top-level format), `user` messages, `message.error`, unknown content block types, and `is_error` on result chunks. The known `ErrorMessage` type (`type: "error"`) still falls through to the "unrecognized" catch-all logger, which is slightly misleading. - `index.ts`: Extends `assistantHasContent` check with `toolUseHandler.getAllFinalizedToolUses().length > 0` as a safety net. `getAllFinalizedToolUses()` is idempotent (reads from `pendingToolUses` without clearing), so the additional early call does not affect the subsequent call that actually populates `assistantContent`. - Three new unit tests cover the empty-content-array, `is_error` result, and legacy rate-limit-event scenarios.

Confidence Score: 4/5

- This PR is safe to merge — it fixes a complete provider failure with no regressions to other providers. - The primary fix (extending --disallowedTools) is well-targeted and directly addresses the root cause confirmed by the author via direct CLI inspection. The supporting changes in claude-code.ts and types.ts are defensive improvements that handle new CLI formats gracefully. The assistantHasContent safety net in index.ts is sound given that getAllFinalizedToolUses() is idempotent. Minor gaps remain: the known ErrorMessage type still hits the "unrecognized" logger catch-all, and one test mock has a type mismatch (result: {} vs result: string). Neither affects runtime correctness. The --disallowedTools list still requires manual maintenance and could drift again with future CLI updates. - src/integrations/claude-code/run.ts — the claudeCodeTools list has no automated enforcement against CLI drift; worth tracking in an issue.

Union is now comprehensive and clearly commented. | | src/integrations/claude-code/run.ts | Updates --disallowedTools list with 12 new CLI tools (TaskOutput, AskUserQuestion, ExitPlanMode, etc.) and removes obsolete ones (LS, MultiEdit, NotebookRead, TodoRead, exit_plan_mode). body:
Greptile Summary

This PR is a security-only dependency upgrade authored by `aikido-autofix[bot]` that addresses 20 CVEs (3 critical, 6 high, 5 medium, 6 low) spanning 10 packages. It bumps three entries in `package.json` (`minimatch` devDep, `axios`, and `simple-git`) with the remainder being transitive-dependency resolutions in the lockfile. Key changes: - **`simple-git` 3.30.0 → 3.33.0** — fixes a critical RCE (CVE-2026-28292) and an argument-injection bypass (AIKIDO-2026-10315). - **`axios` 1.13.4 → 1.13.6** — fixes a DoS via `__proto__` config poisoning (CVE-2026-25639). - **`minimatch` 3.1.2 → 9.0.9** (devDep) — fixes three ReDoS CVEs. Because v9 is semver-incompatible with v3, npm now gives isolated `minimatch@3.1.5` copies to `exceljs` (production dep) and several dev tools (`nyc`, `npm-run-all`, etc.). Whether `3.1.5` itself patches those ReDoS CVEs in the v3 line is worth confirming. - **`fast-xml-parser` 5.3.4 → 5.4.1** — fixes three CVEs including a critical XSS via DOCTYPE entity shadowing (CVE-2026-25896). This upgrade silently adds two new transitive packages to the supply chain: `fast-xml-builder@1.1.2` and `path-expression-matcher@1.1.3` (both from the same NaturalIntelligence maintainer). - **`hono` 4.11.7 → 4.12.7** and **`@hono/node-server` 1.19.9 → 1.19.11** — fix an authorization-bypass, SSE injection, cookie injection, prototype pollution, timing-attack, and ReDoS (6 CVEs total). - **`express-rate-limit`, `qs`, `underscore`, `ajv`** — patched for DoS and ReDoS CVEs via lockfile resolution bumps.

Confidence Score: 4/5

- Safe to merge — all direct and transitive CVE fixes are in place with no breaking API changes for production code. - All version bumps are within semver-compatible ranges for direct production dependencies (axios ^1.x, simple-git ^3.x). The only major version jump is minimatch (v3→v9) which is a devDependency not imported anywhere in source files. Two new transitive packages are added (fast-xml-builder, path-expression-matcher) but are from a known, reputable maintainer. The one open question — whether minimatch@3.1.5 retained by exceljs fully patches the ReDoS CVEs — carries very low practical risk given how exceljs uses the library. - package-lock.json — review the new transitive deps (fast-xml-builder, path-expression-matcher) and confirm the exceljs minimatch@3.1.5 situation does not leave a live CVE exposure.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | package.json | Three direct dependencies bumped to address CVEs: `minimatch` devDep ^3.0.3→^9.0.9 (major version jump), `axios` ^1.12.0→^1.13.6, and `simple-git` ^3.27.0→^3.33.0. Changes are clean and safe. | | package-lock.json | Lock file reflects all CVE-patched versions: hono 4.11.7→4.12.7, @hono/node-server 1.19.9→1.19.11, fast-xml-parser 5.3.4→5.4.1 (adds new transitive deps fast-xml-builder+path-expression-matcher), express-rate-limit 8.2.1→8.3.1, qs 6.14.1→6.15.0, underscore 1.13.7→1.13.8, ajv 8.17.1→8.18.0. Upgrading top-level minimatch to v9 causes exceljs and several dev tools to receive isolated copies at minimatch@3.1.5. |

Comments Outside Diff (2)

 1. `package-lock.json`, line 14161-14178 ([link](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/1d5e99a0b522eb730191c16d32092df23564ac99/package-lock.json#L14161-L14178)) **New transitive dependencies introduced by fast-xml-parser upgrade** Upgrading `fast-xml-parser` from `5.3.4` to `5.4.1` pulls in two brand-new packages that did not exist in the previous lockfile: - `fast-xml-builder@1.1.2` - `path-expression-matcher@1.1.3` Both are from the `NaturalIntelligence` organisation (same maintainer as `fast-xml-parser`) and carry MIT licences. They look legitimate, but worth being aware that this dependency upgrade silently expands the supply-chain surface by two packages. 2. `package-lock.json`, line 16953-16968 ([link](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/1d5e99a0b522eb730191c16d32092df23564ac99/package-lock.json#L16953-L16968)) **minimatch@3.1.5 still present as isolated copies in several packages** Bumping the root `minimatch` to `v9` causes `npm` to hoist isolated `minimatch@3.1.5` copies for packages whose declared range is incompatible with v9 (e.g., `exceljs`, `nyc`, `npm-run-all`, `fstream`, `spawn-wrap`, `istanbul-lib-processinfo`). The three minimatch ReDoS CVEs (CVE-2026-26996, CVE-2026-27904, CVE-2026-27903) are cited as fixed in this PR, but `exceljs` is a **production** runtime dependency, and its minimatch copy remains at `3.1.5`. The practical risk is very low — `exceljs` uses minimatch internally for file-path operations, not for processing user-controlled glob strings — but if a patched `3.x` release exists for these CVEs (e.g., `3.1.x-patched`), it would be worth auditing whether `exceljs` should also be upgraded to remove the nested v3 copy entirely.

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR introduces a nock-based VCR (record/playback) system for the Cline CLI, allowing developers to record real HTTP interactions into cassette files and replay them deterministically in e2e tests. The implementation is well-structured — nock is correctly externalized from the esbuild bundle, dynamically imported only when `CLINE_VCR` is set, and `shared/net.ts` is updated to defer to `globalThis.fetch` lazily so nock can intercept after module initialization. Key issues found: - **Silent no-op + doc mismatch for `CLINE_VCR_CASSETTE`** (`cli/src/utils/vcr.ts` lines 9, 143–145): The module JSDoc documents a default path of `./vcr-cassette.json`, but the code silently returns `null` (disabling VCR entirely) when `CLINE_VCR_CASSETTE` is not set. A user who sets `CLINE_VCR=record` without `CLINE_VCR_CASSETTE` will get no error, no output, and no cassette. - **Filter default mismatch** (`cli/src/utils/vcr.ts` lines 10–12, 152): The module JSDoc states `CLINE_VCR_FILTER` defaults to `"chat/completions"` (inference requests only), but the implementation defaults to `""` (no filter — all HTTP requests are recorded). This means auth flows, S3 calls, telemetry, etc. may be unintentionally captured and committed with cassettes. - **Redundant SIGTERM handler causes double cassette write** (`cli/src/utils/vcr.ts` lines 209–212): The existing CLI `shutdown()` handler already calls `process.exit(0)` on SIGTERM, which fires the `exit` event that saves recordings. The extra `process.on("SIGTERM", saveRecordings)` is redundant and causes `saveRecordings` to be called twice. - **Proxy silently bypassed in VCR mode** (`src/shared/net.ts` line 119): The `EnvHttpProxyAgent` setup is skipped whenever `CLINE_VCR` is set, meaning developers behind a corporate proxy will get connection errors during recording without a clear explanation.

Confidence Score: 3/5

- Safe to merge for production users (VCR is dev-only), but the documentation/default mismatches in vcr.ts should be fixed before this is widely used for test authoring. - The VCR feature is opt-in and guarded behind env vars, so production behavior is unchanged. However, the discrepancy between documented defaults and actual defaults (especially CLINE_VCR_FILTER defaulting to "" instead of "chat/completions") could cause developers to accidentally commit cassettes containing broader-than-expected HTTP traffic, and the silent no-op when CLINE_VCR_CASSETTE is unset will waste time debugging why recording is not working. - cli/src/utils/vcr.ts — documentation/code mismatches and redundant signal handler need attention before this module is used for real test authoring.

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a UI stuttering issue (#6328) by introducing a 100ms throttle on `sendPartialMessageEvent` for gRPC stream subscribers, reducing the rate of messages sent to the webview during fast model responses or in high-latency environments like VS Code Remote SSH. Callback subscribers (used by the CLI) remain unthrottled. The approach fits consistently with the existing per-`ts` coalescing pattern and the 100ms throttle already used in `DiffViewProvider`. **Key changes:** - Added module-level throttle state (`queuedPartialMessagesByTs`, `queuedPartialMessageTimeout`, `isFlushingQueuedPartialMessages`, `activePartialMessageFlush`) with a `clearQueuedPartialMessages()` reset helper. - `sendPartialMessageEvent` now splits into three paths: callback dispatch (always immediate), partial-message throttle (queued + coalesced by `ts`), and final-message bypass (sends immediately, awaits any in-flight flush first to preserve ordering). - Three unit tests added using `sinon.useFakeTimers()` covering coalescing, final-message bypass, and callback immediacy. **Issues found:** - `clearQueuedPartialMessages()` resets `isFlushingQueuedPartialMessages` and `activePartialMessageFlush` while a flush may still be running asynchronously. In the narrow window between successive `await dispatchToStreamSubscribers()` calls, a reconnecting subscriber could receive stale partial messages from the old flush. See inline comment for a generation-counter mitigation. - When a final message is processed on the fast-path (no `activePartialMessageFlush`), any pending `queuedPartialMessageTimeout` is not cancelled — it fires ~100ms later and does nothing, but the dangling timer is unnecessary.

Confidence Score: 3/5

- Safe to merge with low risk — the throttle logic is mostly correct and the identified race is a narrow, low-probability edge case (subscriber drops and reconnects during a flush iteration) that won't affect the typical single-subscriber scenario. - The core throttle design is sound and well-tested for the happy path. However, `clearQueuedPartialMessages()` unsafely resets in-flight flush state without an epoch/generation check, which creates a theoretical correctness gap when a subscriber reconnects mid-flush. Additionally, the pending timeout is not cancelled on the final-message fast-path. Neither issue is likely to manifest under normal usage conditions, but they represent correctness gaps that are worth addressing before merge. - Pay close attention to `src/core/controller/ui/subscribeToPartialMessage.ts`, specifically the `clearQueuedPartialMessages` function and the final-message handling path in `sendPartialMessageEvent`.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/core/controller/ui/subscribeToPartialMessage.ts | Adds a 100ms throttle for gRPC stream subscribers. Core logic is sound, but `clearQueuedPartialMessages()` forcibly resets `isFlushingQueuedPartialMessages` and `activePartialMessageFlush` while a flush may still be executing, creating a narrow race where a reconnecting subscriber could receive stale partials from the old flush. A pending `queuedPartialMessageTimeout` is also left uncancelled on the final-message fast-path. | | src/core/controller/ui/__tests__/subscribeToPartialMessage.test.ts | New test file with three deterministic unit tests using sinon fake timers. Covers partial coalescing, final-message bypass, and callback-subscriber immediacy. Cleanup via afterEach correctly resets module-level state. Missing a test for multiple simultaneous ts values and the race condition introduced by subscriber reconnect during flush. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Task as Task (sendPartialMessageEvent) participant SPM as subscribeToPartialMessage participant Queue as queuedPartialMessagesByTs participant Timer as setTimeout (100ms) participant Stream as gRPC Stream Subscriber participant CB as Callback Subscriber Note over Task,CB: Partial message arrives (partial=true) Task->>SPM: sendPartialMessageEvent(partial=true) SPM->>CB: dispatchToCallbackSubscribers() [immediate] SPM->>Queue: set(ts, message) [coalesce by ts] SPM->>Timer: scheduleQueuedPartialMessageFlush() Timer-->>SPM: fires after 100ms SPM->>Queue: snapshot & clear SPM->>Stream: dispatchToStreamSubscribers(latest) Note over Task,CB: Final message arrives (partial=false) Task->>SPM: sendPartialMessageEvent(partial=false) SPM->>CB: dispatchToCallbackSubscribers() [immediate] SPM->>Queue: delete(ts) [drop stale partial] alt activePartialMessageFlush is set SPM->>SPM: await activePartialMessageFlush end SPM->>Stream: dispatchToStreamSubscribers(final) [bypasses throttle] Note over Task,CB: Last subscriber disconnects SPM->>SPM: clearQueuedPartialMessages() [resets all state] ``` Last reviewed commit: 211e539

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a bug where substantive text content (code reviews, analyses, summaries) written by the model before `attempt_completion` was silently discarded in the UI when parallel tool calling was disabled and a tool had already been used in the same response. The fix modifies the text-skip logic in `presentAssistantMessage` to peek at the next content block: if the next block is `attempt_completion`, the text is rendered instead of skipped. This preserves the existing optimization of hiding model "chatter" between regular tool calls. - The change is minimal and well-scoped to the `presentAssistantMessage` method in `src/core/task/index.ts` - The logic correctly separates the `didRejectTool` check from the `didAlreadyUseTool` check, making the code clearer - There is a timing subtlety: the peek at `nextBlock` reads from the live `assistantMessageContent` array, which works well when tool execution takes non-trivial time (enough chunks arrive for `attempt_completion` to be parsed), but could miss fast-completing tools where the next block hasn't been parsed yet - No tests were added for this change

Confidence Score: 3/5

- This PR is likely safe to merge — it improves the common case but has a timing edge case that could still silently drop text. - The fix correctly addresses the reported bug for the most common scenario (tool execution takes enough time for the attempt_completion block to be parsed). However, there's a timing race where the peek at nextBlock may not find attempt_completion during streaming if the block hasn't been parsed yet, causing the text to still be silently dropped. No tests were added to verify the behavior. - `src/core/task/index.ts` — the nextBlock peek at line 2111 may not reliably detect attempt_completion during streaming

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/core/task/index.ts | Adds a peek-ahead check in `presentAssistantMessage` to avoid skipping text blocks that immediately precede `attempt_completion`. The fix works for common cases but has a streaming timing edge case. |

[tool_use(read_file), text, tool_use(attempt_completion)] Present->>Present: advance to text block alt nextBlock is attempt_completion (fix works) Present->>UI: say("text", content) Present->>Present: advance to attempt_completion Present->>Present: executeTool(attempt_completion) else nextBlock not yet parsed (timing race) Present->>Present: skip text (break) Note over Present: text silently dropped end ``` Last reviewed commit: ba0c0c3

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a bug where `LiteLlmHandler.getModel()` ignored user-configured model info (e.g., custom context windows) by adding `this.options.liteLlmModelInfo` to the fallback chain between the StateManager cache and the hardcoded defaults. - **Bug fix (1 line):** The fallback in `getModel()` now correctly resolves as: StateManager cache → user-configured `liteLlmModelInfo` → `liteLlmModelInfoSaneDefaults`. Previously, it skipped the user config entirely, causing users who set a 1M context window to hit auto-condense at ~112K (88% of the 128K default) instead of ~880K. - **Tests (3 new):** Validates all three fallback levels — defaults when no config, user config when no cache, and cache taking priority over user config. - **Minor style cleanups:** Removed unnecessary `else` after early `return` statements and a redundant type annotation — no behavioral changes.

Confidence Score: 5/5

- This PR is safe to merge — it's a minimal, well-tested one-line fix that restores intended behavior. - The core change is a single line adding `this.options.liteLlmModelInfo` to an existing fallback chain. The fix aligns with the existing comment describing the intended behavior, matches the pattern already used in the OCA handler, and is covered by 3 focused unit tests. The additional changes are cosmetic style cleanups (removing `else` after `return`, removing a redundant type annotation) with zero behavioral impact. - No files require special attention

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR adds a per-task file-read deduplication cache to `ReadFileToolHandler`. The cache stores file metadata (read count, mtime, and an optional image block for multimodal models) keyed by the lowercased absolute path. On repeated reads, the handler checks mtime to detect external modifications and, if the file is unchanged, returns the content with an escalating warning prefix (`[File already read]` on the 2nd read, `[DUPLICATE READ]` on the 3rd+). Cache entries are invalidated by `write_to_file`/`replace_in_file` (`WriteToFileToolHandler`), `apply_patch` (`ApplyPatchHandler`), and the entire cache is cleared after any non-rejected `execute_command` (`ExecuteCommandToolHandler`). **Key observations:** - The cache does **not** avoid disk I/O on hits — `extractFileContent` is called on every read regardless. The real benefit is the warning messages that nudge the model away from redundant reads. - A previous review thread identified and addressed image-block loss on cached reads, `execute_command` stale-content gaps, and redundant deleted-file invalidation — all resolved in the latest revision. - **`consecutiveMistakeCount` is not reset on a successful cached read**, diverging from the fresh-read path (line 244). This can cause the mistake limit to fire sooner than intended after a run of cache-hit reads. - The comment block explaining cache invalidation in `ExecuteCommandToolHandler` is duplicated verbatim — a copy-paste artefact. - `node:fs/promises` is imported dynamically twice in `ReadFileToolHandler` despite being a static built-in; a static top-level import would be cleaner.

Confidence Score: 3/5

- Generally safe to merge, but a behavioral regression in mistake-count tracking on cached reads should be addressed first. - The overall design is sound and the previous-review feedback has been incorporated. However, the cache-hit path silently skips the `consecutiveMistakeCount = 0` reset that the fresh-read path performs, which can cause the yolo-mode mistake limit to fire prematurely. A duplicated comment block and repeated dynamic imports are minor polish issues. No security or data-loss risks were identified. - src/core/task/tools/handlers/ReadFileToolHandler.ts — missing mistake-count reset on successful cached reads.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/core/task/TaskState.ts | Adds `fileReadCache` field to `TaskState` — a per-task `Map` storing read count, mtime, and optional image block per file path. Change is minimal and well-placed. | | src/core/task/tools/handlers/ReadFileToolHandler.ts | Core of the deduplication feature: adds mtime-based cache lookup before every read, re-reads from disk on cache hits (no disk I/O is saved), and returns escalating warning prefixes on repeated reads. Missing `consecutiveMistakeCount` reset on successful cached reads (a divergence from the fresh-read path). Uses repeated dynamic imports of `node:fs/promises` instead of a static import. | | src/core/task/tools/handlers/WriteToFileToolHandler.ts | Correctly invalidates the cache entry for the written file using `absolutePath.toLowerCase()`, consistent with the cache key used in `ReadFileToolHandler`. | | src/core/task/tools/handlers/ApplyPatchHandler.ts | Invalidates cache for all patched files and original paths of move operations. Correctly notes that deleted-file invalidation is handled in the `changedFiles` loop. Minor potential path inconsistency in multi-root workspaces (uses `resolvePath(config.cwd, ...)` rather than `resolveWorkspacePath`), though mtime eviction acts as a fallback. | | src/core/task/tools/handlers/ExecuteCommandToolHandler.ts | Clears the entire cache after any non-rejected command execution to cover unpredictable bash-side file mutations. Contains a copy-pasted duplicate comment block (cosmetic only). |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[ReadFileToolHandler.execute] --> B{Cache entry exists?} B -- No --> F[Fresh disk read via extractFileContent] B -- Yes --> C{mtime matches cached?} C -- No / stat error --> D[Evict cache entry] D --> F C -- Yes --> E[Cache hit: readCount++] E --> G[Re-read from disk via extractFileContent] G --> H{readCount >= 3?} H -- Yes --> I[Return content with DUPLICATE READ warning] H -- No --> J[Return content with 'File already read' prefix] F --> K[Reset consecutiveMistakeCount = 0] K --> L[Cache metadata: readCount=1, mtime, imageBlock] L --> M[Return file content] subgraph Invalidation N[write_to_file / replace_in_file] --> O[delete single cache key] P[apply_patch] --> Q[delete changed/moved/deleted file keys] R[execute_command - not rejected] --> S[clear entire cache] end ``` Last reviewed commit: ["PR changes"](https://github.com/cline/cline/commit/3449e003708bd4574c069bdba2f6528e8d48c7e3)

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR adds a one-shot "latch" to the double-check completion feature so the AI isn't repeatedly blocked on consecutive `attempt_completion` calls within the same edit cycle. The first completion after edits is still rejected with re-verification guidance; the immediate follow-up is accepted and latches the gate open until the next file edit resets it. **Key changes:** - `TaskState`: adds `doubleCheckCompletionLatched = false` to track whether the gate has already been passed this cycle. - `AttemptCompletionHandler`: replaces the always-reset-pending logic with a two-phase check — reject once, latch on acceptance. - `WriteToFileToolHandler` / `ApplyPatchHandler`: reset both `pending` and `latched` after a successful write/patch, so a new edit cycle always re-triggers the double-check. - `ApplyPatchHandler` also silently fixes a pre-existing bug where `didEditFile` was only set for file *deletions*, not *updates*. - Tests updated to reflect the new latch semantics, though two test conditions still use a simplified `shouldReject` expression that omits the `!latched` check, leaving a gap in coverage.

Confidence Score: 3/5

- Mostly safe but the latch does not reset on user feedback, which can silently bypass re-verification after the user explicitly signals the completion is wrong. - The core state machine (latch + pending two-phase gate, reset on file edit) is internally consistent and the tests pass. However, two tests use an incomplete `shouldReject` condition that doesn't include `!doubleCheckCompletionLatched`, leaving a gap where a latched-at-startup regression would go undetected. More importantly, the latch is never reset when the user provides corrective feedback after completion, meaning the double-check guarantee weakens after the first accepted cycle even when the user explicitly asks the AI to redo its work without making file edits. - `AttemptCompletionHandler.ts` (latch not reset on user feedback) and `AttemptCompletionHandler.doubleCheck.test.ts` (incomplete shouldReject conditions on lines 29 and 39).

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/core/task/tools/handlers/AttemptCompletionHandler.ts | Introduces the latch gate replacing the always-reset-pending approach; latch correctly persists across multiple completion calls until an edit, but does not reset when the user explicitly provides corrective feedback, which weakens the double-check guarantee. | | src/core/task/tools/handlers/__tests__/AttemptCompletionHandler.doubleCheck.test.ts | Tests updated to reflect latch semantics, but two tests use a simplified `shouldReject` condition that omits the `!doubleCheckCompletionLatched` check, leaving a gap where a latched=true startup regression would not be caught. | | src/core/task/tools/handlers/ApplyPatchHandler.ts | Adds latch/pending reset on successful patch application; also silently fixes a pre-existing bug where `didEditFile` was only set for deletions, not updates. | | src/core/task/tools/handlers/WriteToFileToolHandler.ts | Correctly resets both `doubleCheckCompletionPending` and `doubleCheckCompletionLatched` after a successful file write, placed at the right point after `saveChanges()` succeeds. | | src/core/task/TaskState.ts | Adds `doubleCheckCompletionLatched = false` with a correct initial value, consistent with the reset semantics expected by the handlers. |

The old regex `/^[^\u4e00-\u9fa5a-zA-Z0-9]+/` only covered CJK Unified Ideographs and Latin letters, silently dropping the first character of filenames in any other Unicode script. The fix replaces it with `/^[^\p{L}0-9]+/u`, using the Unicode Letter property with the `u` flag to cover all scripts universally. **Key changes:** - `CodeAccordian.tsx`: One-line regex change from a hardcoded CJK + Latin character class to `\p{L}` with the `u` flag — minimal, correct, and future-proof for any new Unicode scripts. - `CodeAccordian.test.ts`: New test file with 8 targeted cases covering the previously broken scripts (Korean, Japanese, Chinese, Arabic, Thai), mixed-script paths with leading symbols, and regression coverage for Latin/digit-starting paths. **No issues found.** The fix is idiomatic, well-explained in the updated comment block, and the test coverage is thorough. The `u` flag and `\p{L}` property escape are supported in all modern Chromium-based VS Code webviews and in Node.js 10+ (used by Vitest).

- This PR is safe to merge — the change is a single well-understood regex substitution with no behavioral regressions for Latin paths and clear gains for non-Latin scripts. - The diff is minimal (one line changed in one function), the logic is straightforward, the old behavior is fully preserved for previously working cases, and 8 new tests directly exercise the fixed code paths across all targeted Unicode scripts. - No files require special attention.

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a long-standing bug in the CLI's plain-text (pipe/`--yolo`) output mode where only the last message in `processedMessages` was emitted — meaning multi-segment assistant responses would silently drop all but the final segment. The fix widens the map value to carry `say` and `type` metadata, then filters and joins all `say: "text"` and `say: "completion_result"` entries with double newlines before writing to stdout. Key observations: - The core logic change is minimal and targeted; the filter + join approach correctly restores multi-segment output. - The output block at line 178 runs regardless of `hasError`, meaning partial text segments accumulated before an error are still emitted to stdout — this can mislead pipeline consumers into processing incomplete output. - Two docstrings (module-level line 7 and function-level line 41) still describe the old "only final completion_result" behaviour and should be updated to match the new semantics. - The new filtering logic has no dedicated unit tests; `plain-text-task.test.ts` only covers `emitTaskStartedMessage` from a different module.

Confidence Score: 3/5

- Safe to merge for the core bug fix, but the error-path leak and lack of tests warrant a follow-up before broader rollout. - The change is small and correctly addresses the stated bug. However, the output-on-error behaviour is a logic concern for pipeline consumers, two docstrings are now inaccurate, and the entirely new filtering/joining path has zero unit test coverage — reducing confidence in edge-case correctness. - cli/src/utils/plain-text-task.ts — specifically the unconditional output block on line 178 and the stale docstrings on lines 7 and 41.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | cli/src/utils/plain-text-task.ts | Core fix: `processedMessages` now stores message metadata alongside text, and the non-JSON output block filters to `say: "text"` and `say: "completion_result"` messages joined by double newlines instead of taking only the last entry. Issues: output block runs even when `hasError=true` (partial output may leak into pipelines), two docstrings are stale, and the new filtering logic has no unit tests. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Caller as CLI Caller (pipe / --yolo) participant RPT as runPlainTextTask participant PM as processedMessages Map participant Stdout as stdout Caller->>RPT: invoke with prompt RPT->>RPT: subscribeToState(controller) loop For each ClineMessage (non-partial) RPT->>PM: set(ts, { text, say, type }) end alt say === "completion_result" RPT->>RPT: completionResolve() else say === "error" RPT->>RPT: completionReject() end RPT->>RPT: await completionPromise Note over RPT,Stdout: Non-JSON, non-verbose output phase RPT->>PM: entries() → sort by ts RPT->>PM: filter(type==="say" && (say==="text" || say==="completion_result") && text) RPT->>PM: map(msg.text).join("\n\n") RPT->>Stdout: write(output + "\n") ```

Comments Outside Diff (2)

Two places need updating: 1. **Line 7** (module docstring): `"stdout: Only the final completion result text (no prefix) - perfect for piping"` → now all text + completion segments 2. **Lines 40–41** (function docstring): `"Non-JSON mode: Only writes final completion_result text to stdout"` → same mismatch 2. `cli/src/utils/plain-text-task.ts`, line 41 ([link](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/a3f1b174d505c62736ddf794dc08a3ea99ce0f79/cli/src/utils/plain-text-task.ts#L41)) **Stale function docstring** This line in the `runPlainTextTask` JSDoc still says "Only writes final completion_result text to stdout", which contradicts the new behaviour where all `say: "text"` and `say: "completion_result"` messages are joined and written.

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR introduces a `TaskPresentationScheduler` that coalesces per-chunk `presentAssistantMessage` calls into batched, timer-driven flushes, significantly reducing IPC round-trips in remote workspace environments (SSH, dev-containers, Codespaces). The remote-workspace signal is sourced from `vscode.env.remoteName` via a new `remote_name` proto field, and the scheduler uses a 90 ms cadence for remote vs. 40 ms for local by default. Semantic boundaries (first visible token, tool-call transitions, finalization) always flush immediately regardless of cadence. Key changes: - **`TaskPresentationScheduler`**: New coalescing scheduler with `requestFlush` (fire-and-schedule) and `flushNow` (await-at-boundary). Handles in-flight flush serialization, priority upgrades, and a regression-tested race condition where a post-flush continuation could steal `pendingPriority` from a concurrent `flushNow` caller. - **`latency.ts`**: Remote-workspace detection via `remoteName` only (avoids false positives from platform/version strings), with env-var overrides for both cadences. - **`index.ts`**: Each streaming chunk now calls `scheduleAssistantPresentation` (non-blocking in the hot path) instead of awaiting `presentAssistantMessage` directly; finalization calls `flushAssistantPresentationOrThrow()` to drain any coalesced content. - Two minor issues found: an unreachable dead-code guard in `requestFlush`, and an unnecessary `async` declaration on the hot-path `scheduleAssistantPresentation` method that allocates a Promise on every streaming chunk.

Confidence Score: 4/5

- Safe to merge — the scheduler logic is correct and well-tested; only minor style/optimization issues remain. - The core scheduler implementation is carefully designed, with documented invariants and a thorough test suite that covers the specific race conditions raised in prior review threads. Remote-workspace detection is conservative (false-negative rather than false-positive) and the cadence defaults are configurable via env vars. The two flagged issues — an unreachable guard and an unnecessary `async` on the hot path — are non-blocking style improvements. - `src/core/task/TaskPresentationScheduler.ts` (dead-code guard at line 70) and `src/core/task/index.ts` (hot-path `async` allocation) deserve a quick pass before merge, but neither is a correctness issue.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/core/task/TaskPresentationScheduler.ts | New coalescing scheduler for assistant message presentation. Logic for pending-priority management, flushNow wait-and-guarantee semantics, and the immediate-flush loop are all correct. One dead-code guard at line 70–72 (`if (!this.pendingPriority) return`) is unreachable and mildly misleading. | | src/core/task/index.ts | Integrates the scheduler into the streaming loop and finalization path. Remote-detection promise is correctly awaited before streaming begins. `scheduleAssistantPresentation` is declared `async` unnecessarily in the hot path, causing one Promise allocation per chunk in the common code path. | | src/core/task/latency.ts | Clean new module for cadence computation and remote-workspace detection. Env overrides read once at module load (correct). `isRemoteWorkspaceEnvironment` correctly uses only `remoteName` to avoid false positives from version/platform strings. | | src/hosts/vscode/hostbridge/env/getHostVersion.ts | Adds `remoteName` from `vscode.env.remoteName`. Correctly coerces empty-string to `undefined` (intentional false-negative direction, safe). Well-commented. | | src/core/task/__tests__/TaskPresentationScheduler.test.ts | Comprehensive test suite covering coalescing, immediate-priority bypass, concurrent flushNow semantics (including the race condition regression test), reset, error propagation, and timer upgrade. Good coverage of all previously raised edge cases. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant SL as Streaming Loop participant TPS as TaskPresentationScheduler participant PAM as presentAssistantMessage Note over SL,PAM: Normal chunk (not first token, not tool call) SL->>TPS: requestFlush("normal") TPS-->>TPS: set pendingPriority="normal"
schedule timer (40ms local / 90ms remote) Note over SL: loop continues immediately (no await) Note over SL,PAM: First token / tool-call chunk SL->>TPS: requestFlush("immediate") TPS-->>TPS: cancel any pending timer TPS->>PAM: flush() [via runFlushCycle] PAM-->>TPS: done Note over SL: loop continues immediately Note over TPS: Timer fires for coalesced normal chunks TPS->>PAM: flush() [timer callback] PAM-->>TPS: done Note over SL,PAM: Stream finalization SL->>TPS: flushNow() [via flushAssistantPresentationOrThrow] TPS-->>TPS: wait for any in-flight flush to drain TPS->>PAM: flush() [immediate priority] PAM-->>TPS: done TPS-->>SL: resolved (throws on error) ``` Last reviewed commit: ["Further fixes as per..."](https://github.com/cline/cline/commit/7d72184190c036ebb4d32918a5791b04adedd044)

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a Gemini 400 error that occurs when an assistant message contains both unsigned parts (plain text) and signed parts (functionCall/thinking with `thoughtSignature`). The Gemini API rejects `Content` objects that mix signed and unsigned parts. The fix splits such mixed messages into two consecutive `model`-role `Content` objects and updates the two call sites (`gemini.ts`, `aihubmix.ts`) from `.map()` to `.flatMap()` to handle the new `Content | Content[]` return type. **Key changes:** - `convertAnthropicMessageToGemini()` in `gemini-format.ts` now detects mixed signed/unsigned parts and returns `Content[]` when a split is needed, otherwise `Content`. - `gemini.ts` and `aihubmix.ts` updated to use `flatMap` with explicit `Array.isArray` unwrapping. **Issues found:** - The split always places unsigned parts first and signed parts second. When a model message includes a `thinking` block (signed, `thought: true`) alongside plain text (unsigned), this reorders thinking _after_ text, which reverses the natural `thinking → text` production order sent back in conversation history. - `src/core/api/providers/sapaicore.ts` defines its own local `convertAnthropicMessageToGemini` that is not updated by this PR. SAP AI Core Gemini deployments don't support thinking yet, so the bug is latent rather than active there, but worth tracking. - No new unit tests are added for the split path in `gemini-format.ts`.

Confidence Score: 3/5

- The fix correctly addresses the primary 400 error for text+functionCall mixed messages, but has a potential logic issue with thinking block ordering and leaves `sapaicore.ts` unprotected. - The core split logic is correct for the primary text+functionCall scenario. However, the fixed ordering (unsigned first, signed second) can invert the thinking→text production order when a `thinking` block is involved, which could affect multi-turn context quality. The `sapaicore.ts` provider has its own implementation not covered by this fix, creating a latent gap. No tests were added for the new branching logic. - `src/core/api/transform/gemini-format.ts` (split ordering logic) and `src/core/api/providers/sapaicore.ts` (independent implementation not updated)

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/core/api/transform/gemini-format.ts | Core of the fix: adds split logic for mixed signed/unsigned parts. Logic is correct for the text+functionCall case, but may reverse thinking→text ordering when a `thinking` block and plain text coexist. Uses `(p as any)` type casts due to `thoughtSignature` not being in `@google/genai`'s `Part` type. No new unit tests cover the split path. | | src/core/api/providers/gemini.ts | Correctly updates `.map()` to `.flatMap()` with explicit `Array.isArray` unwrapping to handle the new `Content | Content[]` return type. | | src/core/api/providers/aihubmix.ts | Same `.map()` → `.flatMap()` change as `gemini.ts`; consistent and correct. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Cline participant convertAnthropicMessageToGemini participant GeminiAPI Note over Cline: Assistant message with mixed parts:
text (no signature) + functionCall (with signature) Cline->>convertAnthropicMessageToGemini: message {role: "assistant", content: [text, functionCall]} convertAnthropicMessageToGemini->>convertAnthropicMessageToGemini: convertAnthropicContentToGemini()
→ [{ text }, { functionCall, thoughtSignature }] convertAnthropicMessageToGemini->>convertAnthropicMessageToGemini: Detect mixed signed/unsigned parts convertAnthropicMessageToGemini-->>Cline: Content[] =
[{role:"model", parts:[text]},
{role:"model", parts:[functionCall+sig]}] Cline->>Cline: flatMap flattens Content[]
into contents array Cline->>GeminiAPI: contents: [{user}, {model:text}, {model:functionCall+sig}, ...] GeminiAPI-->>Cline: 200 OK (no more 400 error) ```

Comments Outside Diff (1)

 1. `src/core/api/providers/sapaicore.ts`, line 294-326 ([link](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/8c23d86e0105823de91c884821e4c1d0d6bc98d7/src/core/api/providers/sapaicore.ts#L294-L326)) **Incomplete fix: `sapaicore.ts` has its own `convertAnthropicMessageToGemini` that is not updated** `sapaicore.ts` defines a private local `convertAnthropicMessageToGemini` (line 294) that is independent of the one in `gemini-format.ts`. This local version: - Does **not** handle `tool_use`, `thinking`, or `thoughtSignature` at all. - Uses `.map()` (line 326) rather than `.flatMap()`, so the split logic introduced in this PR would never apply here. The comment at line 343 notes that SAP AI Core doesn't support `thinkingConfig` yet, which means the bug is latent rather than currently triggered. However, once thinking support is added for SAP AI Core Gemini deployments, it will hit the same 400 error this PR is fixing. It would be safer to either: 1. Replace the local function with an import of `convertAnthropicMessageToGemini` from `gemini-format.ts` and apply the same `flatMap` pattern, or 2. Add a `TODO` comment here noting that the split logic needs to be applied when thinking support is added.

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a cross-platform bug in the Cline CLI where pressing Enter was ignored in certain Windows and CI/test environments because Ink's `key.return` flag is not reliably set — raw `"\r"` or `"\n"` input is delivered instead. The fix introduces a shared `isEnterKey(input, key)` helper in `cli/src/utils/input.ts` and systematically replaces every direct `key.return` check across 10 CLI components with a call to this helper. **Key changes:** - New `isEnterKey` utility checks `key.return === true || input === "\r" || input === "\n"`, making Enter detection robust across platforms and test runners. - All 10 affected components (`ApiKeyInput`, `AskPrompt`, `AuthView`, `BedrockCustomModelFlow`, `CheckpointMenu`, `HistoryPanelContent`, `HistoryView`, `ImportView`, `SelectList`, `SkillsPanelContent`) updated consistently. - Minor incidental cleanups: `parseInt` → `Number.parseInt` in `AskPrompt` and `CheckpointMenu`, removal of redundant explicit type annotations in `HistoryView`, and a dead `else` branch removed in `AskPrompt.getCliMessagePrefixIcon` (all code paths in the preceding `switch` already `return`). - The one naming inconsistency worth addressing: `SelectList.tsx` passes its `_input` parameter (underscore prefix conventionally signals "unused") to `isEnterKey`, which is now a contradiction — it should be renamed to `input`.

Confidence Score: 5/5

- This PR is safe to merge; it is a narrowly scoped, well-motivated bug fix with no behaviour changes outside of the Enter-key handling path. - The core change is a small, easily audited helper function applied uniformly across all affected components. There are no new dependencies, no logic restructuring, and the incidental refactors (parseInt, dead else-branch) are provably equivalent. The only issue found is the `_input` naming nit in `SelectList.tsx`, which is cosmetic and does not affect runtime behaviour. - cli/src/components/SelectList.tsx — the `_input` parameter name should be corrected to `input` now that it is actively used.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | cli/src/utils/input.ts | Adds the `isEnterKey` helper that resolves the Windows/test CI flakiness by treating raw `"\r"`/`"\n"` input as Enter alongside `key.return`. Clean, well-documented implementation. | | cli/src/components/SelectList.tsx | Swaps `key.return` for `isEnterKey`, but the `useInput` callback parameter is still named `_input` (implying unused) despite now being passed to `isEnterKey`. | | cli/src/components/AskPrompt.tsx | Four `key.return` checks replaced with `isEnterKey`; `parseInt` → `Number.parseInt`; dead `else` branch removed from `getCliMessagePrefixIcon` (all ask-switch paths return, so the else was logically equivalent). All changes are correct. | | cli/src/components/AuthView.tsx | Five `key.return` usages replaced with `isEnterKey`; also fixes the local `Select` sub-component to thread `input` into the handler (previously discarded with `_`). | | cli/src/components/SkillsPanelContent.tsx | Straightforward replacement of `key.return` with `isEnterKey(input, key)`; this is the primary component cited in the PR as having the failing test. |

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes flaky hook fixture tests by introducing `withFixtureRunner` in `test-utils.ts`, a utility that guarantees per-scenario isolation: it deletes and recreates the hooks directory, resets `HookDiscoveryCache`, reloads the fixture, and instantiates a fresh `HookFactory` runner — all before each scenario executes. All four hook test suites (`TaskStart`, `TaskResume`, `TaskComplete`, `UserPromptSubmit`) are updated to use this helper, and the `hook-executor.test.ts` cancellation test adopts platform-aware delays to prevent Windows CI timing failures. - **New `withFixtureRunner` helper** (`test-utils.ts`): overloaded to support both a self-managed env (auto-creates + auto-cleans) and a caller-managed env (reuses caller's `HookTestEnv`, defers cleanup to the caller's `afterEach`). - **Fixture test consolidation**: Success scenarios across all four suites are now run in a `for` loop within a single `it` block, while error/exception scenarios each keep their own `it`. This eliminates cross-scenario state leakage but means a failure in one loop scenario stops the rest from executing. - **Windows abort-timing fix** (`hook-executor.test.ts`): hook delay bumped to 1 500 ms and abort delay to 300 ms on Windows (was 250 ms / 25 ms in a prior iteration), with a matching 10 000 ms `this.timeout`. - **`getErrorMessage` helper**: added in each test file as a local arrow function — could be centralised in `test-utils.ts` to avoid duplication.

Confidence Score: 5/5

- Safe to merge — changes are test-only, the isolation mechanism is correct, and no production code is touched. - All changes are confined to test utilities and test files. The `withFixtureRunner` isolation logic is sound: stubs set up by `createHookTestEnv` remain active across calls, the hooks directory is fully torn down and rebuilt before each scenario, and the discovery cache is flushed. Platform-specific timing values in `hook-executor.test.ts` are well-reasoned. The only trade-off is reduced per-scenario CI granularity due to consolidating success scenarios into a single `it` loop, which is a minor diagnostic concern, not a correctness issue. - No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/core/hooks/__tests__/test-utils.ts | Adds `withFixtureRunner` helper that provides per-scenario isolation by removing the hooks directory, resetting the discovery cache, reloading the fixture, and creating a fresh runner before each invocation. Two overloads cover standalone (auto-managed env) and shared-env modes. Logic is sound; `stubHookDirs` remains active via the caller's sandbox so discovery works correctly after each `resetHookCache` call. | | src/core/hooks/__tests__/taskresume.test.ts | Replaces seven independent fixture `it` blocks with two loop-based tests. Also correctly adds `function ()` syntax to the "very old timestamps" test so `this.timeout(WINDOWS_HOOK_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS)` takes effect. Timeout also adjusted to 10 000 ms on Windows. Addresses the previously raised CI reliability concern for slow Windows/PowerShell runners. |

Greptile Summary

This PR refactors `ReadFileToolHandler.ts` by hoisting the `extractFileContent` call — which previously appeared identically in two separate code paths — into a single shared call that executes before the `validCached` re-check. The change is a clean deduplication with no functional regressions. **Key points:** - The refactoring is semantically equivalent for all primary code paths (fresh read, cached hit with valid mtime, and cache-evicted re-read), since the original code always re-read from disk regardless of cache state. - A minor edge-case improvement: in the original code, `validCached.readCount` was incremented and `validCached.imageBlock` was pushed to `userMessageContent` *before* attempting the disk read — meaning both mutations happened even when the subsequent read failed. The new code avoids these unnecessary mutations on error. - The original explanatory comment (`// Re-read from disk (cache doesn't store content to save memory)`) that clarified *why* the read always happens was removed. Adding it back (or updating it to reflect the new location) would help future contributors understand the intentional always-read-from-disk design.

Confidence Score: 4/5

- Safe to merge — the refactoring is functionally equivalent for all primary paths and fixes a minor edge-case ordering issue. - The change removes genuine code duplication and does not alter observable behaviour for users. The only meaningful difference (mutations before a failed read on a cached entry) is actually an improvement. A single style suggestion about restoring an explanatory comment is the only notable gap. - No files require special attention beyond confirming the existing unit/integration tests cover the cache-hit + failed-read edge case.

body:
The `extractFileContent` block is intentionally duplicated across the two paths for readability. The cache-hit path has the comment `// Re-read from disk (cache doesn't store content to save memory)` which explains *why* a cache "hit" still reads from disk and that context is lost when the read is hoisted above the cache check. As the greptile bot noted, the unconditional read becomes confusing without that explanation.

The duplication is only ~14 lines and both paths may diverge in the future (e.g., we might skip disk I/O on cache hits if we add content caching back). Prefer to keep it as-is for now, but appreciate the suggestion!

However if we do want to make a change here are my thoughts.
The DRY improvement is valid. Both paths were reading from disk identically. One small request: could you add a comment above the `extractFileContent` call explaining that we always read from disk because the cache only stores metadata (readCount, mtime), not content? Something like:

```javascript
// Always read from disk — the cache stores only metadata (readCount, mtime),
// not file content, to keep memory usage minimal.
```

The greptile bot flagged the same thing and without that context, a reader might wonder why we read unconditionally before checking the cache.

I don't have ability to merge PRs though. So it will have to be a Cline developer, but I think the code has better future prop and readability the way it is, so my vote is to not change, or at very least we need to make the intent clear with something like my comment example above. Sometimes we write things for our future even if there are more slimmer ways of doing something.

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR adds a `PreToolUse` hook to `.claude/settings.json` that runs `npx block-no-verify@1.1.2` before every Bash tool execution, with the goal of preventing Claude Code from issuing `git` commands with the `--no-verify` flag. **Key concerns:** - **Conflict of interest / supply chain risk**: The PR author self-discloses being the author and maintainer of the `block-no-verify` package. Merging this would add an externally-hosted npm package — authored by the PR submitter — to be fetched and executed in the context of every Bash command the agent runs. The cline project would be implicitly trusting this package at a very privileged position (pre-execution of every shell call). - **Overly broad scope**: The `matcher` is `"Bash"`, so the package intercepts all shell commands, not only `git` invocations. Every `ls`, `npm install`, `tsc`, etc. passes through this hook, giving `block-no-verify` visibility into all shell activity. - **Performance overhead**: `npx` is invoked on every single Bash tool call. Even with a cached package, this adds latency to every shell execution in a session. - **Prefer a local, auditable hook**: The existing `SessionStart` hook pattern in this repo uses a project-local shell script (`.claude/hooks/claude-code-for-web-setup.sh`). A similar, self-contained inline script or a locally checked-in hook script would achieve the same `--no-verify` blocking with no external dependency and full code auditability within this repository.

Confidence Score: 1/5

- Not safe to merge as-is — introduces execution of a third-party package authored by the PR submitter before every Bash command, with supply-chain and performance implications. - The change is small (one file, a few lines), but the risk profile is high: a self-promoted external package is given privileged hook position to intercept all shell commands, and there is an unmitigated conflict of interest with no independent audit of the package code. - .claude/settings.json

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR migrates the xAI provider from the Chat Completions API to the Responses API, adds `grok-4.20` as the new default model, and removes 14 deprecated Grok models. The architectural change is well-structured — it reuses the shared `convertToOpenAIResponsesInput` transform and `handleResponsesApiStreamResponse` utility already used by `openai-native.ts`, keeping the two providers consistent. Key changes and issues: - **Missing `maxTokens` for `grok-4.20`** (P1): The new model entry omits `maxTokens`, so `max_output_tokens: undefined` is sent to the Responses API. For every other xAI model this field is explicitly `8192`. Without a limit, grok-4.20 (a 2M-context reasoning model) can produce arbitrarily long and costly completions. - **`reasoningEffort` silently dropped** (P2): `XAIHandlerOptions.reasoningEffort` is retained in the interface but never forwarded to the Responses API `reasoning` parameter. Users who configure this setting will see no effect. - **Comment/code mismatch in `shouldSkipReasoningForModel`** (P2): The JSDoc was broadened to say "Grok models" but the implementation still only matches `grok-4`; `grok-3-mini` (reasoning-capable, still in `xaiModels`) would not be caught when routed through third-party gateways. - Note: the pre-existing `cacheReadTokens`/`cacheWriteTokens` swap in the shared `responses_api_support.ts` (`reasoning_tokens` → `cacheReadTokens`, `cached_tokens` → `cacheWriteTokens`) is inherited by xAI via this change, but was not introduced here.

Confidence Score: 3/5

- Safe to merge after addressing the missing maxTokens for grok-4.20; other issues are minor. - The API migration itself is clean and follows established patterns, but the missing `maxTokens` for the new default model is a concrete issue that could lead to unbounded (and expensive) API responses for all users of the xAI provider. The silent dropping of `reasoningEffort` and the comment/code inconsistency are lower-severity follow-ups. - src/shared/api.ts (grok-4.20 model definition) and src/core/api/providers/xai.ts (reasoningEffort usage)

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/core/api/providers/xai.ts | Migrated from Chat Completions to Responses API; clean refactor but `reasoningEffort` option is now silently unused and tool mapping logic is newly added. | | src/shared/api.ts | Adds grok-4.20 as default and removes 14 deprecated models; grok-4.20 is missing `maxTokens`, which will send `max_output_tokens: undefined` to the Responses API. | | src/utils/model-utils.ts | Updated JSDoc comment; minor inconsistency between the broadened "Grok models" comment and the `grok-4`-only implementation of `shouldSkipReasoningForModel`. | | src/utils/__tests__/model-utils.test.ts | Test cases updated to cover grok-4.20 and new grok-4 variant IDs; changes look correct. | | src/core/api/providers/cline.ts | Comment-only change clarifying that all Grok models lack a thinking payload via Chat Completions. | | src/core/api/providers/vercel-ai-gateway.ts | Comment-only change aligning the reasoning-skip note with the broader Grok family. | | src/core/api/transform/openrouter-stream.ts | Comment-only update to reflect that grok (not just grok-4) skips reasoning via the OpenRouter path. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant C as Cline Core participant X as XAIHandler participant T as convertToOpenAIResponsesInput participant R as handleResponsesApiStreamResponse participant API as xAI Responses API C->>X: createMessage(systemPrompt, messages, tools) X->>T: convertToOpenAIResponsesInput(messages) T-->>X: { input: ResponseInput } X->>X: mapResponseTools(tools) X->>API: responses.create({ model, instructions, input, tools, include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"], store: false }) API-->>R: AsyncIterable loop Stream events R-->>C: yield text / reasoning / tool_calls / usage end ```

Comments Outside Diff (2)

 1. `src/core/api/providers/xai.ts`, line 13-17 ([link](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/8b42d4ea1d0c9031689527a0d52c7a61b750fc5e/src/core/api/providers/xai.ts#L13-L17)) **`reasoningEffort` option is accepted but silently ignored** `XAIHandlerOptions` still declares `reasoningEffort?: string`, but the new Responses API call never uses it. The OpenAI Responses API supports a `reasoning` parameter (e.g. `{ effort: "low" | "medium" | "high" }`) that controls reasoning effort for models with `supportsReasoning: true` (like `grok-4.20`, `grok-4-fast-reasoning`, `grok-4-1-fast-reasoning`). Users who configure a reasoning effort in the UI will silently get the API's default instead. Consider either wiring the option through: ```typescript reasoning: this.options.reasoningEffort ? { effort: this.options.reasoningEffort as "low" | "medium" | "high" } : undefined, ``` or removing the field from the interface with a comment explaining it is not yet supported by the Responses API path. 2. `src/utils/model-utils.ts`, line 38-50 ([link](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/8b42d4ea1d0c9031689527a0d52c7a61b750fc5e/src/utils/model-utils.ts#L38-L50)) **Comment says "Grok models" but logic only checks `grok-4`** The updated JSDoc now reads *"Grok models since they don't provide a thinking payload via Chat Completions"*, implying the guard applies to all Grok variants. However, the implementation still matches only `grok-4`: ```ts return modelId.includes("grok-4") || modelId.includes("devstral") || modelId.includes("glm") ``` `grok-3-mini` (which remains in `xaiModels` and has reasoning capability) and any future grok-3 reasoning models routed via OpenRouter / Vercel / Cline gateways would not be caught by this check. If the broader claim in the comment is accurate, the guard should be widened to cover all Grok models, or the comment should be narrowed back to `grok-4`:

Greptile Summary

This automated security PR from Aikido upgrades multiple dependencies to resolve 20 CVEs, including 3 critical severity issues — a remote code execution in `simple-git`, an authorization bypass in `hono`'s static file serving, and an XSS vulnerability in `fast-xml-parser`. **Key changes:** - `simple-git`: `^3.27.0` → `^3.33.0` — fixes 2 critical/high RCE vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-28292, AIKIDO-2026-10315) - `axios`: `^1.12.0` → `^1.13.6` — fixes prototype pollution DoS (CVE-2026-25639) - `minimatch`: `^3.0.3` → `^9.0.9` (devDependencies) — fixes 3 ReDoS issues (CVE-2026-26996, CVE-2026-27903, CVE-2026-27904); this is a 6 major-version jump — see comment - Transitive-only lock-file upgrades (no `package.json` constraints): `hono` (6 CVEs), `@hono/node-server` (1 CVE), `fast-xml-parser` via `@aws-sdk/xml-builder` (4 CVEs), `ajv` (1 CVE), `express-rate-limit` (1 CVE), `underscore` (1 CVE) **Note on lock-file-only fixes:** Several critical CVE resolutions (`hono`, `underscore`, `ajv`, `express-rate-limit`) are anchored only in `package-lock.json`, not via `package.json` version constraints. This is a common and pragmatic approach for transitive dependencies, but it means if `package-lock.json` is deleted and regenerated from scratch, those fixes could be lost depending on the version ranges resolved by the parent packages at that time. The current lock file correctly pins the patched versions.

Confidence Score: 4/5

- This PR is safe to merge — it is a pure dependency security upgrade with no application logic changes, and all patched versions are correctly resolved in the lock file. - All application code is unchanged. The three direct `package.json` updates (simple-git, axios, minimatch) are security-patch releases within expected semver ranges, except for minimatch which jumps 6 major versions in devDependencies. The direct usage of minimatch in `scripts/package-standalone.mjs` is compatible with v9's API. The lock-file-only transitive fixes are correctly pinned. One point deducted for the major minimatch version jump, which warrants manual verification that dev tooling and CI pipelines are unaffected. - No production files require attention. The `scripts/package-standalone.mjs` script uses `minimatch` directly and should be validated against the v9 API after merging.

No source code, tests, or documentation reference these specific `.example` filenames, so the deletion is purely a housekeeping fix. - This PR is safe to merge — it is a pure deletion of unused developer example files with no impact on application logic. - All six changed files are being deleted, not modified. No TypeScript/JavaScript code, tests, or documentation reference these `.example` filenames. The hook discovery path (`findUnixHook`) only matches exact-name files without extensions, so these files were never executed as hooks. body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a deadlock that occurs when the user clicks **New Task** or **Exit** after a task reaches completion. The root cause is a three-way lock: `abortTask()` sets `abort=true` then `await`s `presentationScheduler.dispose()`, which in turn awaits the in-flight flush; that flush was blocked inside `ask("completion_result")` on a `pWaitFor` loop that had no way to detect the abort signal. The fix adds `|| this.taskState.abort` to the `pWaitFor` predicate so that any blocked `ask()` call wakes up as soon as `abort` becomes true, followed by an immediate throw of `"Cline instance aborted"` for all non-resume ask types — propagating the error through the flush, allowing `scheduler.dispose()` to complete, and unblocking `abortTask()`. **Key changes:** - `ask()` (`src/core/task/index.ts`): `pWaitFor` predicate extended with `|| this.taskState.abort`; a post-wait abort check (with the same `resume_task`/`resume_completed_task` carve-out already used at function entry) is added to throw immediately for non-resume asks. **Potential concern:** - `resume_task` / `resume_completed_task` ask types are intentionally excluded from throwing, but because `abort` is already `true` when `abortTask()` calls `this.ask(askType)` at line 1627, these asks will now return early with `askResponse = undefined` instead of blocking until the user clicks Resume. The immediate caller discards the return value (`.catch()` only), so no crash occurs, but any subsequent user click on the Resume button will not be caught by that particular `ask()` invocation. This is worth verifying against the controller-level resume path to confirm that resumption is driven entirely through the controller and not through the return value of that fire-and-forget `ask()` call.

Confidence Score: 4/5

- The fix is minimal, targeted, and safe to merge for the reported deadlock; a secondary edge case around resume-ask early-return deserves a follow-up verification. - The change correctly unblocks the `pWaitFor` loop when `abort=true`, matching the symmetry of the existing guard at `ask()` entry. The only nuance is that `resume_task`/`resume_completed_task` asks called from inside `abortTask()` now return early with `undefined` response instead of blocking, but the caller ignores the return value so no runtime error is introduced. Score of 4 (rather than 5) reflects this secondary resume-path concern that should be confirmed rather than assumed harmless. - src/core/task/index.ts — specifically the interaction between the `resume_task`/`resume_completed_task` carve-out in the new abort check and the fire-and-forget `ask(askType)` call inside `abortTask()` (line 1627).

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/core/task/index.ts | Adds `|| this.taskState.abort` to the `pWaitFor` condition in `ask()` and follows it with an abort-check that throws, correctly unblocking in-flight flushes when `abortTask()` sets `abort=true`, fixing the scheduler deadlock. Logic is consistent with the existing guard at function entry; exception carve-outs for `resume_task`/`resume_completed_task` are applied symmetrically. |

Sequence Diagram
