body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes an OOM crash in the VS Code extension host caused by globby's `gitignore: true` eagerly reading every `.gitignore` file in the entire directory tree — including those inside gitignored subdirectories (e.g., hundreds of nested vendor repos), producing a regex so large that V8 runs out of memory compiling it. The fix switches to `gitignore: false` and instead reads `.gitignore` files incrementally during the existing BFS traversal, so files inside already-gitignored directories are never touched. Key changes: - `readGitignorePatterns(dirPath)` — new helper that parses one `.gitignore` into glob ignore patterns (synchronous I/O; see inline comment) - `buildIgnorePatterns()` now seeds the initial ignore list with the root `.gitignore` in addition to `DEFAULT_IGNORE_DIRECTORIES` - `globbyLevelByLevel()` accumulates `.gitignore` patterns from each non-ignored directory entered, preventing traversal into gitignored subtrees - `gitignore: false` replaces `gitignore: recursive` in the globby options - Four new integration tests cover root directory patterns, file/glob patterns, subdirectory BFS reading, and the OOM prevention scenario - The `rootPath` parameter added to `globbyLevelByLevel` is never used in the function body and can be removed - Known tradeoffs (pattern scoping is global, negations skipped, anchored patterns lose their anchor) are clearly documented in the PR description

Confidence Score: 4/5

- Safe to merge with one small dead-parameter cleanup and a sync-I/O follow-up recommended - The core fix is sound — incremental `.gitignore` reading during BFS correctly avoids the OOM by never entering gitignored directories, which is the root cause. Tests are well-isolated and cover all branches including the OOM prevention scenario. The three flagged issues are all P2 style/cleanup concerns: an unused `rootPath` parameter, synchronous I/O that could block the event loop on large trees, and a directory pattern that relies on fast-glob's internal traversal optimisation for correctness rather than being explicitly self-documenting. None of these block the primary fix from working correctly. - src/services/glob/list-files.ts — unused parameter on `globbyLevelByLevel` and synchronous I/O in `readGitignorePatterns`

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/services/glob/list-files.ts | Core fix: replaces globby's eager `gitignore: true` with incremental per-directory `.gitignore` reading during BFS. Three minor style concerns: unused `rootPath` parameter, synchronous I/O inside async loop, and directory pattern semantics. | | src/services/glob/__tests__/list-files.test.ts | Four well-isolated tests added for gitignore handling: root directory patterns, file/glob patterns, subdirectory BFS reading, and the OOM-prevention case. Each test uses its own subdirectory to prevent cross-test pollution. |

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR introduces a streaming buffer to `MessageStateHandler` that defers disk writes during LLM response streaming, batching them into a single flush when the stream completes (or before tool execution). The approach is architecturally sound — the buffer lifecycle is properly guarded by the existing `stateMutex`, and the `finally` block in `index.ts` guarantees `endStreamingBuffer()` is always called even on stream failure. Key observations: - **Logic bug in `flushToDisk()`**: The condition `this.pendingDiskWrite || !this.skipDiskWrite` causes an unconditional disk write when the method is called outside streaming mode (`skipDiskWrite = false`). In the current codebase this path is never hit (the only caller is `ToolExecutor`, which runs during streaming), but the condition contradicts the documented "safe to call even if not in buffer mode" contract and will surprise future callers. The guard should be `if (this.pendingDiskWrite)` only. - **Per-chunk debug logging**: `Logger.debug(...)` fires on every buffered `updateClineMessage()` call. For long streams this generates thousands of log entries, partially undermining the I/O reduction goal. - **`addToClineMessages()` is intentionally unbuffered**, but this asymmetry is undocumented. A short comment would prevent future maintainers from inadvertently "fixing" it.

Confidence Score: 4/5

- Safe to merge after fixing the flushToDisk() condition; no data-loss risk exists in current usage, but the wrong guard is a latent correctness issue. - The overall design is correct and the buffer lifecycle is properly handled via mutex and finally-block cleanup. The one concrete bug — the `!this.skipDiskWrite` branch in `flushToDisk()` — does not affect current callers but makes the method's behavior wrong for any non-streaming caller, which is easy to introduce. Fixing that single condition brings this to merge-ready. - src/core/task/message-state.ts — specifically the `flushToDisk()` guard condition and the per-chunk debug log.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/core/task/message-state.ts | Introduces streaming buffer via `skipDiskWrite`/`pendingDiskWrite` flags. Core logic is sound, but `flushToDisk()` contains a condition (`!this.skipDiskWrite`) that causes an unconditional disk write when called outside streaming mode, and per-chunk debug logging may partially negate the I/O savings. | | src/core/task/ToolExecutor.ts | Adds a single `flushToDisk()` call before tool execution to ensure message state is persisted. Change is minimal and correctly placed after the abort check. | | src/core/task/index.ts | Wraps the streaming loop with `startStreamingBuffer()` before the `try` block and `endStreamingBuffer()` in the `finally` block, ensuring cleanup on both success and error paths. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Task as Task (index.ts) participant MSH as MessageStateHandler participant TE as ToolExecutor participant Disk as Disk (saveClineMessages) Task->>MSH: startStreamingBuffer() Note over MSH: skipDiskWrite=true, pendingDiskWrite=false loop LLM streaming chunks Task->>MSH: updateClineMessage(idx, updates) Note over MSH: skipDiskWrite=true → pendingDiskWrite=true (no disk write) end alt Tool use detected Task->>TE: handleCompleteBlock(block) TE->>MSH: flushToDisk() Note over MSH: pendingDiskWrite=true → write to disk, pendingDiskWrite=false MSH->>Disk: saveClineMessages() TE->>TE: execute tool end alt Stream error Task->>Task: catch block (error handling / retry) end Note over Task: finally block always runs Task->>MSH: endStreamingBuffer() Note over MSH: skipDiskWrite=false alt pendingDiskWrite=true MSH->>Disk: saveClineMessages() end Task->>MSH: saveClineMessagesAndUpdateHistory() MSH->>Disk: saveClineMessages() (final write) ```

During a streaming session, every call to `say()` (e.g., `say("reasoning", ...)` during streaming, or `say("error_retry", ...)` in the error handler) will still hit disk immediately. This is likely intentional for safety — new messages should be durably persisted as soon as they appear — but it creates an undocumented asymmetry: `updateClineMessage` is buffered, but `addToClineMessages` is not. A short comment noting this deliberate exclusion would make the design intent clear and prevent future maintainers from "fixing" the asymmetry incorrectly.

When the LLM calls the same tool with identical arguments 3 times in a row it receives a soft warning; at 5 repetitions `consecutiveMistakeCount` is pinned to `maxConsecutiveMistakes`, triggering the existing escalation path (fail-task in YOLO mode, ask-user otherwise). State is tracked via two new fields on `TaskState`. **Key issues found:** - **Critical bug — tool name comparison is always true:** `this.taskState.lastToolName` is overwritten on line 579 *before* it is read in the comparison on line 590. Because `block.name === this.taskState.lastToolName` now compares a value to itself, the tool-name guard is dead code. The detector degenerates to params-only matching, meaning two *different* tools that happen to share identical stringified params will incorrectly accumulate the counter instead of resetting it, potentially triggering false-positive escalations. - **Tests don't cover the production bug:** The `simulateToolCall` helper in the test file updates `state.lastToolName` *after* the comparison (the correct order), so its logic diverges from the production code. All nine tests pass, but none exercises the code path where a different tool with identical params should reset the counter. Adding a test case like `read_file {path:"src/"} → list_files {path:"src/"}` would expose the bug and prevent regression once fixed.

Confidence Score: 2/5

- Not safe to merge — the core detection logic has a P0 bug that makes tool-name matching always true, so the feature may trigger false positives and its tests don't cover the actual production behaviour. - The intent and overall structure are solid, but the single-line ordering mistake (`lastToolName` updated before the comparison that reads it) fundamentally breaks the feature's correctness guarantee. The unit tests pass only because the helper function diverges from the production code. These two issues together mean the feature ships broken and the bug is invisible to CI. A one-line fix brings this to merge-ready. - src/core/task/ToolExecutor.ts (lines 579–594) and src/core/task/__tests__/doom-loop-detection.test.ts (simulateToolCall helper)

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a bug in `SummarizeTaskHandler` where files matched by `.clineignore` were incorrectly consuming slots in the `MAX_FILES_PROCESSED` (10) budget before being skipped, which could cause the loop to `break` early and prevent legitimate files from being loaded. - **Root cause**: the `.clineignore` check ran *after* `filesProcessed++` and the `> MAX_FILES_PROCESSED` guard, so each ignored file silently ate one slot out of the 10-file limit. - **Fix**: moves the `.clineignore` check to the very top of the loop body, before any counter or dedup tracking, so ignored files are completely bypassed without affecting the budget. - The change is minimal, easy to reason about, and aligns with the ordering already used for the duplicate-file guard (`loadedFiles`) — both early-exit checks now appear before the counter increment.

The fix is correct: ignored files should not consume the processing budget. No new state is introduced, no API surface changes, and the rest of the loop logic is unaffected. - No files require special attention.

Greptile Summary

This PR introduces an opt-in "Zero-Copy Vision Gateway" integration that intercepts Puppeteer screenshots in `BrowserSession.doAction()` and replaces the base64 payload with a lightweight URL pointer fetched from a remote Glazyr MCP gateway, aiming to drastically reduce token usage during browser tasks. The approach adds two settings fields (`glazyrVisionUrl`, `glazyrVisionToken`), a new `isVisionPointer` helper in the OpenAI formatter, and a `_peekVisionBuffer` fetch method. Several issues from prior review rounds have been addressed (listener name consistency, `_glazyrClient` dead field removed, URL scheme validation on the gateway response). However, a number of critical gaps remain that block the primary user path: - **Anthropic API direct path is broken**: `formatImagesIntoBlocks` stores the URL inside the `data` field of a `type: "base64"` image block. The `isVisionPointer` guard only exists in `convertToOpenAiMessages` (OpenAI path). Any user running Cline against the Anthropic API directly will receive an API validation error for every browser action when the gateway is active. - **Webview rendering is broken**: returning a bare HTTPS URL in `BrowserActionResult.screenshot` will not render in the VS Code webview due to Content Security Policy restrictions, and breaks any downstream code that pattern-matches on `data:image/`. - **Stale frame on action failure**: the Glazyr intercept fires *after* the `try/catch` around `action()`, so a failed navigation still queries the gateway and returns a pointer to whatever frame it last captured — potentially from the previous action. - **`glazyrVisionToken` stored as plaintext**: the Bearer token is serialised to VSCode global storage rather than using the existing `SecretStorage` mechanism. - **Eval benchmark contaminated**: `evals/benchmarks/tool-precision/replace-in-file/helpers.ts` receives the same URL-bypass injection despite having no relation to the vision gateway; any benchmark image string starting with `http://` would silently be misclassified. - **Unit tests validate a non-existent runtime path**: the tests construct message objects that bypass `formatImagesIntoBlocks`, so they do not exercise the actual end-to-end flow.

Confidence Score: 1/5

- Not safe to merge — multiple critical issues break the primary user path for both Anthropic and OpenAI users, and the test suite does not cover the actual runtime flow. - Prior rounds resolved the listener mismatch, the _glazyrClient dead field, and the gateway pointer scheme validation. However, the Anthropic API direct path is still fundamentally broken (URL stored in a base64 data field), webview rendering of the screenshot is still broken, the Glazyr intercept can return a stale frame after action errors, the auth token is still stored in plaintext settings, and the unit tests still validate a bypassed code path. These are P0/P1 failures that will affect the majority of real users on every browser action when the gateway is enabled. - src/core/prompts/responses.ts and src/services/browser/BrowserSession.ts require the most attention — the former for the broken Anthropic image block construction and the latter for the stale-frame and webview issues.

body:
Flagging this PR for security review before any merge consideration. I have no affiliation with cline; I ran into this account while investigating a GitGuardian alert on an unrelated PR of mine in browser-use.

Observable facts, all verifiable from public GitHub data:

1. **Same-day campaign across agent frameworks.** The author account (`glazyr`, created 2026-03-13) opened this PR and a same-themed PR against browser-use (browser-use/browser-use#4497, "Zero-Copy MCP Vision Gateway") within ~2 hours of each other on 2026-03-24. The browser-use PR was never merged and was auto-closed as stale on 2026-06-20.

2. **Author-controlled endpoint in the data path.** The browser-use variant defaulted its gateway URL to `https://mcp.glazyr.com/mcp/sse` (`GLAZYR_VISION_URL` env fallback), i.e. agent browser screenshots would transit infrastructure controlled by the PR author. In this cline PR the gateway is opt-in via `glazyrVisionUrl` / `glazyrVisionToken` settings, and `mcp.glazyr.com` appears in the added tests.

3. **Remote-fetch surface added to the vision pipeline.** This PR introduces a "vision pointer" mechanism that treats strings beginning with `http(s)://` as URLs to fetch image data from, in place of inline screenshot data. That adds an outbound-request surface inside the screenshot path that reviewers should assess for exfiltration/SSRF potential.

4. **Hardcoded secret in the sibling PR.** GitGuardian flagged a hardcoded high-entropy secret in the browser-use variant's commit (`3f9520cdf16baffb177d83c4691150299f2f6302`, `examples/glazyr_benchmark.py`).

None of this proves malicious intent, but the combination — new throwaway account, simultaneous PRs to multiple agent frameworks, author-controlled default endpoint in the screenshot path, and a flagged hardcoded secret — warrants treating this PR as security-sensitive rather than a routine perf contribution.

This PR fixes an infinite-retry loop (issues #9684 / #9919) where the model injects an internal `task_progress` parameter into every tool call per the system prompt, and MCP servers with strict JSON schema validation reject the unknown field, causing the model to retry indefinitely with the same bad arguments. The fix is minimal and well-targeted: inside `UseMcpToolHandler.execute()`, `task_progress` is deleted from `parsedArguments` after JSON parsing but before the arguments are forwarded to `McpHub.callTool()`. The raw `block.params` (and therefore focus-chain tracking) are left untouched. A secondary cleanup removes a now-redundant `else` branch in the approval telemetry path. **Key observations:** - The strip is correctly scoped to the MCP-bound `parsedArguments` object; `block.params.task_progress` is preserved for focus-chain use. - The `parsedArguments &&` guard is safe — it handles the edge-case where `JSON.parse` returns `null` (e.g., the string `"null"`). - The `completeMessage` used in both the auto-approve `say` call and the manual-approval dialog is still built from the raw `mcp_arguments` string, so `task_progress` remains visible to users in the tool-call preview (minor UX issue, see inline comment). - The redundant `else` removal is a clean, behaviour-preserving refactor.

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR adds an early directory-path guard to `WriteToFileToolHandler.validateAndPrepareFileOperation()` to prevent cryptic `EISDIR` errors when the model passes a directory path instead of a file path to `write_to_file` or `replace_in_file`. The fix calls `fs.stat()` before the existing file-existence check and, if the path resolves to a directory, returns a clear, actionable error message and increments `consecutiveMistakeCount` so the model can self-correct. **Key changes:** - Adds `import fs from "node:fs/promises"` to the handler. - Inserts a `try/catch` block after the clineignore access check that calls `fs.stat()` and short-circuits with a user-friendly error if `isDirectory()` is true. - On directory detection, follows the same error-reporting pattern as surrounding code (`consecutiveMistakeCount++`, `say("error", ...)`, `ToolResultUtils.pushToolResult`, `didAlreadyUseTool`). **Issues found:** - The `catch {}` block silently swallows **all** `fs.stat()` errors (not just `ENOENT`). Errors like `EACCES` or `ELOOP` should be re-thrown so the model receives a meaningful error instead of a potentially more confusing downstream failure. - The example filename appended to the error message (`/index.ts`) is TypeScript-specific and may mislead the model in non-TypeScript projects.

Confidence Score: 4/5

- Safe to merge after addressing the overly broad catch block; the directory check itself is correct and non-breaking. - The core fix is sound and follows existing patterns in the codebase. The only concrete bug is the catch-all that silences non-ENOENT stat errors — fixable with a one-liner. The index.ts suggestion is a minor UX nit. No existing tests are broken and normal file operations are unaffected. - src/core/task/tools/handlers/WriteToFileToolHandler.ts — catch block at line 505 needs to be narrowed to ENOENT only.

Important Files Changed

Greptile Summary

This PR adds `kanbanEnabled` as an optional boolean field to `RemoteConfigSchema` so that administrators can control the Kanban feature via remote config. The schema change and the accompanying test updates are correct and consistent with the existing pattern for optional feature-flag fields (e.g. `mcpMarketplaceEnabled`, `yoloModeAllowed`). However, the implementation is incomplete — the new field is accepted by the schema but is never applied anywhere: - **No state key**: `kanbanEnabled` is not registered in `src/shared/storage/state-keys.ts`, unlike every other feature flag that flows through remote config. - **No transformer mapping**: `transformRemoteConfigToStateShape()` in `src/core/storage/remote-config/utils.ts` maps every other top-level remote-config field to a state-cache entry. There is no equivalent block for `kanbanEnabled`, so the value is silently discarded after parsing. - **No feature gate in the UI**: No code reads a `kanbanEnabled` state key to show or hide the Kanban surface. As shipped, setting `kanbanEnabled: false` in the remote config payload would have zero observable effect on the running extension.

Confidence Score: 2/5

- Not safe to merge — the feature is incomplete and the schema field has no effect at runtime. - The schema and test changes are internally consistent, but the core implementation is missing: there is no state key, no transformer mapping, and no UI gate that would make `kanbanEnabled` actually control the Kanban feature. Merging this as-is would silently accept the field from remote config and do nothing with it, giving admins a false sense that they have blocked Kanban when they have not. - `src/core/storage/remote-config/utils.ts` (missing transformer), `src/shared/storage/state-keys.ts` (missing state key), and whatever component renders the Kanban UI (missing feature gate).

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR adds a Kanban feature gate that checks the `kanbanEnabled` field in the user's remote config before launching Kanban. It introduces a new user-scoped API endpoint (`/api/v1/users/me/remote-config`), a corresponding `fetchUserRemoteConfig` helper, and wires the guard into both the `kanban` subcommand and the `--kanban` flag path of the default action. The supporting changes in `disk.ts`, `ClineAccount.ts`, and `api.ts` are clean and correct. The core logic has two unresolved bugs: - **`--kanban` flag falls through to TUI when disabled** — after `printWarning`, there is no `exit(1)` or `return`, so the main action handler continues and launches the interactive TUI despite the user invoking `--kanban` and remote config disabling it. - **`configData.enabled` is ignored in `fetchUserRemoteConfig`** — the existing `fetchRemoteConfigForOrganization` returns `undefined` when the API signals `enabled: false` (treating a disabled remote config as "no restrictions"), but the new function skips this check entirely. If the API returns `enabled: false` and the embedded `value` does not carry `kanbanEnabled: true`, Kanban will be incorrectly blocked and the misleading "disabled for your organization" error will be shown.

Confidence Score: 2/5

- Not safe to merge — the `--kanban` flag path falls through to the TUI when Kanban is disabled, and the `enabled` field from the API is silently ignored. - Two P1 logic bugs remain (fall-through to TUI, `enabled` field ignored), plus the previously flagged `kanban` subcommand issues (wrong parameter order, missing `return`/`await`). The infrastructure changes (disk.ts, ClineAccount.ts, api.ts) are solid, but the core gating logic in both CLI entry points has correctness problems that affect the primary user path this PR is meant to address. - `cli/src/index.ts` (both entry points for Kanban) and `src/core/storage/remote-config/fetch.ts` (`fetchUserRemoteConfig`) require the most attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | cli/src/index.ts | Adds `startKanban` async helper and wires it into the `kanban` subcommand and `--kanban` flag paths. The `--kanban` flag path falls through to the TUI when Kanban is disabled (missing `exit(1)` after the warning); the `kanban` subcommand also has the related `return`/parameter-order issues flagged in prior threads. `HostProvider` double-init is correctly guarded. | | src/core/storage/remote-config/fetch.ts | Adds `fetchUserRemoteConfig` (user-level endpoint). The `UserRemoteConfigResponse.enabled` flag is not checked, diverging from how `fetchRemoteConfigForOrganization` handles a disabled config (could incorrectly block Kanban). Cache write is unawaited. Fallback cache read now correctly matches the write path (`undefined` orgId → `remote_config.json`). | | src/core/storage/disk.ts | Makes `organizationId` optional across `readRemoteConfigFromCache`, `writeRemoteConfigToCache`, and `deleteRemoteConfigFromCache`, and updates `GlobalFileNames.remoteConfig` to produce `remote_config.json` when no org ID is provided. Clean, correct change. | | src/services/account/ClineAccountService.ts | Adds `fetchRemoteConfig()` method wrapping `USER_REMOTE_CONFIG` endpoint, with proper error handling. Minor cleanup of the `else` branch after `No Content` check. No issues. | | src/shared/ClineAccount.ts | Adds `UserRemoteConfigResponse` interface with `organizationId`, `value`, and `enabled` fields. Straightforward type addition. | | src/shared/cline/api.ts | Adds `USER_REMOTE_CONFIG = "/api/v1/users/me/remote-config"` to the endpoint enum. No issues. |

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR introduces a `code_intelligence` tool that exposes JetBrains PSI (Program Structure Interface) capabilities — symbol search, definitions, references, callers/callees, and type hierarchy — to Cline agents running inside JetBrains IDEs. The feature is fully gated: it is invisible to VSCode/CLI users (no toggle, no tool in prompt) and only activates when both a PSI host bridge is present **and** the user enables it via a new Experimental toggle. **Key changes:** - New `code_intelligence` tool spec with `contextRequirements` gating on `codeIntelligenceAvailable` - `CodeIntelligenceToolHandler` handles query parsing, PSI dispatch, and richly-formatted results - `codeIntelligenceEnabled` setting plumbed through proto, state-keys, `updateSettings`, and webview context - `codeIntelligenceAvailable` derived from `HostProvider.psi !== undefined` for both the system-prompt context and the settings toggle visibility - 9 unit tests + 12 system-prompt snapshot tests verifying gating behaviour **Issues found:** - `consecutiveMistakeCount` is reset to `0` before the empty-queries validation check (`queries.length === 0`), meaning a model that passes a non-empty but comment/whitespace-only `queries` value will have its mistake counter silently cleared instead of incremented (P1) - `config.callbacks.say("tool", ...)` fires before the empty-queries guard, leaving a dangling tool-start message in the UI for invalid inputs (P2) - `()` is unconditionally appended to every symbol name in formatted results regardless of kind, which could mislead the model about whether a class, variable, or constant is callable (P2) - `ExternalHostBridgeClientManager` always instantiates `psiClient`, making `HostProvider.psi` permanently non-`undefined` for any external-bridge environment — safe today (JetBrains-only) but a forward-compatibility concern (P2)

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge with a one-line fix to the `consecutiveMistakeCount` reset ordering in `CodeIntelligenceToolHandler`. The feature is well-structured, properly gated, and invisible to non-JetBrains users. The P1 bug (mistake count reset before empty-query validation) is isolated to this new handler, does not affect existing tools, and has a trivial fix. All other findings are P2 style/UX notes. `src/core/task/tools/handlers/CodeIntelligenceToolHandler.ts` — specifically the ordering of `consecutiveMistakeCount = 0` vs. the `queries.length === 0` guard.

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR enhances the "Generate Commit Message" feature by reading project-specific commit conventions from `.clinerules` (file or directory) and `commitlint.config.*` / `.commitlintrc.*` files at the repo root, then injecting them into the AI generation prompt. **Key changes:** - New `loadCommitRules(repoPath)` function reads `.clinerules` (single file or directory) and the first matching `commitlint` config file, concatenating their contents into a `# Project Rules` section prepended to the prompt. - `performCommitMsgGeneration` gains an optional `repoPath` parameter so the rules can be loaded without touching existing call sites. - `COMMITLINT_CONFIG_PATTERNS` lists nine file name variants for commitlint discovery. **Issues found:** - `readDirectory` traverses subdirectories recursively (uses `{ recursive: true }`), so a `.clinerules/` tree with nested files will dump all of them into the prompt — likely unintentional. - The injected rules content has no size cap, unlike the git diff (truncated at 5 000 chars); a large config could exceed the model's context window. - `.commitlintrc` (no extension, valid JSON) is missing from the pattern list.

Confidence Score: 3/5

Safe to merge for the basic (file) case, but the recursive directory read is a real runtime issue that can bloat the prompt significantly in repos that use a `.clinerules/` directory tree. The recursive `readDirectory` call is a concrete behavioral defect: any `.clinerules` directory with sub-folders will pull in far more content than intended, inflating prompts and potentially causing generation failures. The missing size cap compounds this. The fix is small but the P1 should be addressed before merging. src/hosts/vscode/commit-message-generator.ts — specifically the `loadCommitRules` function.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/hosts/vscode/commit-message-generator.ts | Adds `loadCommitRules` to inject `.clinerules` and `commitlint` config into the commit-message prompt; recursive directory traversal and missing size cap are the main concerns. |

Greptile Summary

This PR upgrades five transitive dependencies in the `docs/` directory (the Mintlify-powered documentation site) to remediate security vulnerabilities. Five packages are patched: `ajv` (8.17.1→8.18.0), `minimatch` (3.1.2→3.1.4), `qs` (6.14.1→6.14.2), `socket.io-parser` (4.2.5→4.2.6), and `yaml` (2.8.2→2.8.3). The `package.json` overrides are also kept in sync to pin the new minimum versions for `qs` and `minimatch`. Key observations: - The scope is limited to `docs/` dev tooling; the main extension and its `package.json`/`package-lock.json` are not touched. - The PR description claims **9 CVEs resolved**, but only **7 are actually addressed** in the diff. `lodash` (CVE-2025-13465) stays at `4.17.21` — likely because no upstream patch exists yet for the `4.x` series — and `zod` (CVE-2023-4316) stays at `3.21.4`, which is within the vulnerable range `3.21.0–3.22.3`. A `zod` override (e.g. `"zod@<3.22.4": "3.22.4"`) could address the latter. - The `overrides` pattern `"minimatch@<=3.1.4": "3.1.4"` correctly forces any transitive resolution of minimatch below 3.1.4 up to the patched version.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge; changes are limited to docs-site dev dependencies and the five patched packages are correctly resolved. The five package upgrades are valid security fixes with correct lock-file and override entries. The only concern is that 2 of the 9 advertised CVEs (lodash, zod) are not actually remediated in this diff, which is a false-assurance issue worth tracking but not a blocker for the changes that are present. docs/package.json — the lodash and zod CVEs are unaddressed and a zod override could be added here

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a persistent \"Thinking…\" loader bug in the chat view by extracting loader-visibility logic into a pure, testable `shouldShowThinkingLoader()` helper and replacing two broken conditions in `MessagesArea.tsx`. **Root causes fixed:** - The old `isToolGroup(lastVisibleRow)` guard showed the thinking loader any time the last visible row was a tool group, including after tool execution had fully completed. - The old `lastVisibleMessage.partial !== true` guard was inverted — it treated *complete* (non-partial) messages as \"still waiting,\" keeping the loader alive after real response content was already rendered. **Changes:** - `messageUtils.ts`: New `shouldShowThinkingLoader()` uses an explicit allow-list (no grouped rows yet, `user_feedback`/`user_feedback_diff`, `checkpoint_created`, pending `api_req_started` with no cost) and returns `false` for everything else, including completed tool groups, finished text messages, and ask states. - `MessagesArea.tsx`: `isWaitingForResponse` is now a single-line memo that delegates to `shouldShowThinkingLoader`. The `lastVisibleMessage` and `lastVisibleRow` inputs are no longer needed for this computation (they remain used by the separate `handoffToReasoningPending` guard). - `messageUtils.test.ts`: 10 new unit tests covering all acceptance criteria for `shouldShowThinkingLoader`.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — both documented bugs are correctly fixed, the logic is well-tested, and no regressions were found. All remaining comments are P2 (a missing edge-case test and a clarifying code comment). The core logic of `shouldShowThinkingLoader` is a straightforward allow-list that correctly covers every transitional state, the two broken conditions are removed, and the 10 unit tests validate the key paths. The `handoffToReasoningPending` guard in `MessagesArea.tsx` is unchanged and continues to handle the reasoning stream handoff correctly. No files require special attention.

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes 7 CVEs across three transitive dependencies — `node-forge` (1.3.3 → 1.4.0), `path-to-regexp` (8.3.0 → 8.4.0), and `brace-expansion` (1.1.12 / 2.0.2 → 2.0.3) — addressing critical cryptographic and DoS vulnerabilities. **Key changes and observations:** - **`brace-expansion` override strategy** (`package.json`): The selector `"brace-expansion@<=2.0.3": "2.0.3"` is well-targeted — it upgrades both the `1.x` instance used by `minimatch@3.1.5` and the scattered `2.0.2` instances used by `glob`, `mocha`, etc., while correctly leaving the `5.0.x` instances required by `@vscode/vsce` and `rimraf` untouched. - **`node-forge` and `path-to-regexp` updated via lockfile only** (no `overrides` entries): Both packages' parent dependents (`jks-js` requires `^1.3.2`; `router` requires `^8.0.0`) have version ranges that are satisfied by the fixed versions, so npm will continue to resolve to them naturally. Consider adding `overrides` entries (e.g. `"node-forge@<1.4.0": "1.4.0"`) for an additional guardrail, though the lockfile pins alone are sufficient today. - **Collateral `peer` metadata changes** in `package-lock.json`: ~30 packages (mostly `@rollup/*` platform binaries, `@babel/jest`, `@grpc/grpc-js`, `@opentelemetry/api`) had their `"peer"` flag toggled. Brace-expansion v2's exported API is backward-compatible with v1 for the patterns minimatch relies on, so this is safe in practice.

Confidence Score: 5/5

PR is safe to merge — all three vulnerable libraries are correctly patched, and no functional code is changed. All 7 CVEs are addressed with correct version bumps. The override strategy for brace-expansion is well-scoped. node-forge and path-to-regexp fixes are lockfile-only but stable. Collateral peer-flag changes are cosmetic. No P0 or P1 issues found. No files require special attention; all changes are in package manifest and lockfile.

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a path inconsistency in the global hooks directory resolution on WSL/Linux: `refreshHooks()` and `resolveHooksDirectory()` were hardcoding `os.homedir() + "/Documents"` while `ensureHooksDirectoryExists()` (and the equivalent Rules/Workflows helpers) already used `getDocumentsPath()`, which respects the XDG documents directory via `xdg-user-dir`. The mismatch silently caused global hooks created through the UI to be written to one path while the runtime looked for them in another, resulting in hooks never firing on WSL setups where `xdg-user-dir DOCUMENTS` returns a non-default location. Key changes: - `refreshHooks.ts` and `utils.ts` now call `getDocumentsPath()` instead of constructing `os.homedir()/Documents` directly, aligning them with `disk.ts` and making all hooks code consistent with how Rules and Workflows already resolved their directories. - `src/shared/api.ts` updates the context window for all 7 MiniMax model variants from 192,000 to 204,800 tokens (200 × 1,024). This change is unrelated to the WSL fix and is not mentioned in the PR description — worth a quick confirmation that it's intentional. - Both modified files now have an unused `import os from \"os\"` that should be cleaned up (the only previous consumer, `os.homedir()`, was removed by this PR).

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the core fix is correct and all remaining findings are minor style issues (unused imports, unconditional subprocess call when override is set). The fix correctly aligns all global hooks path resolution with the existing `getDocumentsPath()` pattern already used by `ensureHooksDirectoryExists()`, `ensureRulesDirectoryExists()`, and `ensureWorkflowsDirectoryExists()`. No logic errors were introduced. The only open findings are P2 style concerns (unused `os` imports in both files, unnecessary `getDocumentsPath()` call when an override is supplied) that don't affect correctness or production behavior. The unrelated MiniMax context-window update in `api.ts` appears to be a straightforward numeric correction. No files require special attention beyond the minor cleanup of unused `os` imports in `refreshHooks.ts` and `utils.ts`.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/core/controller/file/refreshHooks.ts | Correctly replaces hardcoded `os.homedir()/Documents` with `getDocumentsPath()` for consistent XDG/WSL support; leaves an unused `os` import and calls `getDocumentsPath()` unconditionally even when the override is present. | | src/core/hooks/utils.ts | Same fix as `refreshHooks.ts` — `resolveHooksDirectory()` now uses `getDocumentsPath()`; same unused `os` import and unconditional subprocess spawn when override is supplied. | | src/shared/api.ts | Updates MiniMax model context windows from 192,000 to 204,800 (200 × 1,024) tokens for all 7 MiniMax model variants; unrelated to the WSL hooks fix but appears to be a straightforward model-spec correction. |

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR adds post-release Slack notifications to both the extension (`publish.yml`) and CLI (`npm-main.yaml`) publish workflows. After a successful release, a `chat.postMessage` call is made to the `#releases` channel (`C0APVKGGZFC`) via `slackapi/slack-github-action@v3.0.1`, posting the version, changelog content (extension only), and a relevant link. **Key issues found:** - **Missing `continue-on-error: true` on both Slack steps (P1)** — The release artifacts (npm package, VS Marketplace extension, GitHub Release, git tags) are all created _before_ the Slack step runs. If the notification fails for any reason (token not configured, API unavailable, payload too large), GitHub Actions will mark the entire workflow run as failed — even though the release itself succeeded. - **Changelog text has no length guard against Slack's 3000-char limit (P1)** — Slack's Block Kit enforces a hard 3000-character maximum on section block text. The `Get Changelog Entry` step in `publish.yml` reads changelog content with no truncation, meaning a large release entry could exceed the limit and cause `chat.postMessage` to return `invalid_blocks`. - **Action pinned to mutable version tag, not commit SHA (P2)** — `slackapi/slack-github-action@v3.0.1` in both files uses a movable tag rather than a commit SHA, which is the recommended practice for supply-chain security hardening.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge after adding continue-on-error: true to both Slack steps and a changelog truncation guard; without these, a Slack failure after a successful release will incorrectly mark the CI run as failed. Two P1 issues: missing continue-on-error: true on both Slack notification steps and no guard against Slack's 3000-char block text limit for changelog content. These are straightforward fixes but represent real operational risk on the next release. Both .github/workflows/publish.yml and .github/workflows/npm-main.yaml need continue-on-error: true on the Slack steps; publish.yml also needs changelog truncation before the Slack payload.

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant GHA as GitHub Actions participant NPM as NPM / VS Marketplace participant GH as GitHub Releases participant Slack as Slack API Note over GHA: publish.yml (extension) GHA->>NPM: vsce publish / ovsx publish GHA->>GH: Create GitHub Release (with changelog) GHA->>Slack: chat.postMessage (tag + changelog + diff link) Slack-->>GHA: OK / error Note over GHA: npm-main.yaml (CLI) GHA->>NPM: npm publish --tag latest GHA->>GHA: git tag v{version}-cli && push GHA->>Slack: chat.postMessage (version + npm link) Slack-->>GHA: OK / error ```

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR adds the ability for users to delete image/file attachments while editing a previously sent message. When entering edit mode on a message that has attachments, thumbnails are now rendered with a hover-activated "×" delete button. Cancelling edit (Escape or blur) resets attachments to their originals; committing via "Restore Chat" or "Restore All" sends only the remaining attachments. > ⚠️ **Note — PR title mismatch**: the PR title reads *"feat: add new MiniMax-M2.7 and MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed models with updated configurations"* but has nothing to do with the actual changes. The description correctly describes the attachment-editing feature. Please update the title before merging. **Key changes:** - `webview-ui/src/components/chat/UserMessage.tsx` — adds `editedImages` / `editedFiles` local state, threads them through the existing `Thumbnails` component (which already supports optional `setImages`/`setFiles` delete callbacks), resets them on cancel/blur, and passes them to `sendMessageFromChatRow` instead of the raw props. - The no-op early-return guard was extended to also check whether the attachment arrays changed — however it contains a bug: when `images` or `files` props are `undefined`, the optional-chain expression `images?.length` evaluates to `undefined` rather than `0`, so `undefined === editedImages.length (0)` is `false`, causing a checkpoint restore to fire even when nothing changed (see inline P1 comment).

Confidence Score: 4/5

PR introduces a P1 regression where editing a message without attachments and clicking 'Restore Chat' (with no changes) triggers a spurious checkpoint restore; the one-line fix is straightforward. The feature logic and the Thumbnails component integration are correct. The P1 bug in the no-op guard (images?.length vs 0) needs to be fixed before merging because it causes an unnecessary checkpoint restore and message re-send on every save of an attachment-free message when the text is unchanged. webview-ui/src/components/chat/UserMessage.tsx — specifically the no-op guard on lines 47-49.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | webview-ui/src/components/chat/UserMessage.tsx | Adds editable attachment state (`editedImages`, `editedFiles`) and wires the `Thumbnails` component's deletable-thumbnail API in edit mode; contains a P1 bug in the no-op guard where optional `images?.length` evaluates to `undefined` rather than `0`, causing spurious checkpoint restores on attachment-free messages. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant UM as UserMessage participant T as Thumbnails participant CS as CheckpointsService participant CR as ChatRow User->>UM: Click message (enters edit mode) activate UM UM->>T: Render with setImages / setFiles callbacks User->>T: Hover thumbnail → click × T->>UM: setEditedImages / setEditedFiles (delete item) alt User presses Escape or blurs UM->>UM: setEditedImages(images ∥ []) UM->>UM: setEditedFiles(files ∥ []) note over UM: Attachments reset to originals else User clicks Restore Chat UM->>UM: Check no-op guard note over UM: ⚠ Bug: images?.length === undefined ≠ editedImages.length === 0 UM->>CS: checkpointRestore(messageTs) CS-->>UM: OK UM->>CR: sendMessageFromChatRow(editedText, editedImages, editedFiles) end deactivate UM ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown This is a comment left during a code review. Path: webview-ui/src/components/chat/UserMessage.tsx Line: 47-49 Comment: **No-op guard breaks when `images`/`files` props are `undefined`** `images?.length` evaluates to `undefined` when `images` is not provided (the prop is typed as optional). Meanwhile `editedImages` is always initialized to `images || []`, so its `.length` is `0`. Since `undefined !== 0`, the early-return condition is `false` even when nothing actually changed — triggering a full checkpoint restore for a no-op edit on any message that has no attachments. Before this PR the guard was simply `text === editedText`, which correctly short-circuited for attachment-free messages. The new check regresses that case. Fix with the nullish-coalescing operator so that `undefined` is treated as an empty array: ```suggestion if (text === editedText && (images?.length ?? 0) === editedImages.length && (files?.length ?? 0) === editedFiles.length) { ``` How can I resolve this? If you propose a fix, please make it concise. --- This is a comment left during a code review. Path: webview-ui/src/components/chat/UserMessage.tsx Line: 47-49 Comment: **Length-only comparison misses same-length content changes** The no-op guard compares only the *length* of `editedImages`/`editedFiles` against the original props. If all items were deleted and the same number of different items were added (or if order changed), the guard would incorrectly short-circuit and suppress the restore. In the current UI users can only delete — not add or reorder — so this cannot occur today, but it is a latent fragility worth noting. A shallow equality check (e.g. `JSON.stringify`) would be more correct and make the intent explicit: ```suggestion if (text === editedText && JSON.stringify(images ?? []) === JSON.stringify(editedImages) && JSON.stringify(files ?? []) === JSON.stringify(editedFiles)) { ``` How can I resolve this? If you propose a fix, please make it concise. `````

Greptile Summary

This PR adds a new file `src/shared/api/types.ts` with the intent of introducing an optional `stream?: boolean` flag to control per-provider streaming, in order to fix HTTP 400 errors from vLLM and similar inference servers. However, the implementation does not achieve its stated goal. Key issues: - **Dead code — not wired into the real interface.** The canonical `ApiHandlerOptions` lives in `src/shared/api.ts` and extends `Partial`. The new file creates a completely separate, parallel `ApiHandlerOptions` interface that is never imported by any file in the codebase. The `stream` field and `DEFAULT_STREAMING_ENABLED` constant therefore have no effect. - **Wrong field names.** The new interface uses generic names (`apiKey`, `apiModelId`, `apiBaseUrl`, etc.) that don't correspond to the provider-specific field names (`openAiApiKey`, `anthropicBaseUrl`, etc.) used throughout the 45+ existing provider handlers. - **No provider updates.** The PR description mentions using `options.stream ?? true` in callers, but none of the provider files (`openai.ts`, `ollama.ts`, etc.) have been updated to read this flag, so the vLLM streaming fix is not actually implemented. To address the stated goal, `stream?: boolean` should be added directly to `ApiHandlerOptions` in `src/shared/api.ts` (or to `API_HANDLER_SETTINGS_FIELDS` in `src/shared/storage/state-keys.ts`), and the relevant providers should be updated to use `options.stream ?? true` where they currently hard-code streaming.

Confidence Score: 2/5

- Safe to merge in the sense that it adds no breaking changes, but the intended fix is entirely ineffective and the new file is dead code. - Three P1 findings: the new `ApiHandlerOptions` interface duplicates and shadows the real one without connecting to it, the field names don't match the actual codebase conventions, and neither the `stream` flag nor `DEFAULT_STREAMING_ENABLED` are imported or used anywhere. Greptile Summary

This PR adds word-delete (Option+Backspace, Ctrl+Backspace) and fixes Option+Arrow word navigation across terminal emulators by introducing two complementary keyboard protocols (xterm `modifyOtherKeys` level 2 and Kitty) and a `PassThrough` stdin proxy that intercepts and translates the resulting modifier-key escape sequences before Ink processes them. body:
Greptile Summary

This PR is an automated security upgrade from Aikido that patches 8 CVEs across four transitive dependencies: `node-forge` (1.3.3→1.4.0), `path-to-regexp` (8.3.0→8.4.2), `@xmldom/xmldom` (0.8.11→0.8.12), and `brace-expansion` (1.1.12→2.0.3). The only change to `package.json` is a new `overrides` entry to force `brace-expansion` to `2.0.3`; the remaining three package upgrades are reflected solely in `package-lock.json`. - **node-forge 1.4.0** (fixes 4 HIGH CVEs): Stricter RSASSA PKCS#1 v1.5 padding checks, Ed25519 non-canonical signature rejection, `basicConstraints` enforcement in certificate chain validation, and an early-exit guard in `BigInteger.modInverse()` to prevent infinite-loop DoS. Breaking changes only tighten cryptographic correctness and should not affect legitimate usage in this codebase. - **path-to-regexp 8.4.2** (fixes 2 CVEs — 1 HIGH, 1 LOW): Limits generated regex combinations to < 256 to prevent ReDoS from crafted route patterns. Note: the PR description references `8.4.0` but the resolved version is `8.4.2`. - **@xmldom/xmldom 0.8.12** (fixes 1 HIGH CVE): `createCDATASection` now throws `InvalidCharacterError` when the data contains `]]>`, preventing XML injection. The package is used transitively by `mammoth` and `playwright-core`; neither the source code nor tests call `createCDATASection` directly with attacker-controlled data. - **brace-expansion 2.0.3** (fixes 1 LOW CVE): The `overrides` entry `"brace-expansion@<=2.0.3": "2.0.3"` deduplicates all sub-2.0.3 copies (including the former `1.1.12` used by `minimatch`) into a single `2.0.3` install. Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a quota-exhaustion UX issue where a `429` response with a very large `retry-after` header (e.g., 1 hour) would silently consume all retry attempts by waiting the full duration between each attempt. The fix adds a `STOP_THRESHOLD_MS` constant (5 minutes) that causes the retry loop to immediately re-throw the original error whenever the computed delay exceeds the threshold, so users see the quota error right away. - **`src/core/api/retry.ts`**: Adds `STOP_THRESHOLD_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000` and a guard after the `retry-after` header delay computation; throws immediately when `delay > STOP_THRESHOLD_MS` - **`src/core/api/retry.test.ts`**: Adds a regression test using `retry-after: "3600"` (1 hour), verifying the method is only called once and `setTimeout` is never invoked - Logic ordering is correct: the `isLastAttempt` guard fires before the threshold check, so the new path is only reached on non-final attempts - The threshold is a module-level constant with no per-call-site configurability; exposing it via `RetryOptions` would allow per-provider tuning

The fix is contained to two files, the logic is correct (threshold check is properly gated behind the isLastAttempt guard), and the regression test directly validates the new behavior. The fix passes `block.partial` through to `this.say()` so that intermediate chunks treat the error as a streaming (partial) message rather than a final one, and only the last non-partial chunk produces the definitive error row and pushes the tool result. - The change is surgical — one line in the plan-mode restriction branch of `ToolExecutor.ts`, with no changes to tool-gating logic, mode settings, or result semantics - The fix is functionally correct and resolves the reported spam behavior - A minor inefficiency remains: `removeLastPartialMessageIfExistsWithType` is still called unconditionally before every `say` — including on every partial chunk. Guarding the removal with `if (!block.partial)` would be cleaner. - No test coverage exists for the plan-mode streaming scenario in `ToolExecutor.test.ts`"

body:
Thanks for the PR! The direction is right but it needs a couple of fixes before we can merge:

1. **`os.userInfo()` needs a try-catch** - this call throws in Docker containers and CI runners where the UID isn't in `/etc/passwd`. Since this runs in the singleton constructor at module load, an unhandled throw crashes the whole extension. Wrap it in try-catch and fall back to the old `cline` directory name. See `src/utils/shell.ts` line 156 for the existing pattern.

2.  **Migration for existing users** - Changing the directory name orphans files in the old `/tmp/cline` for every existing user (not just multi-user setups). The fix should either: (a) only use the per-user name when the shared directory has permission issues, or (b) include a one-time migration that moves/deletes the old directory. Option (a) is simpler and avoids breaking single-user setups.\n\nCould you update the PR to address these? Happy to re-review once those are in.

body:
Confirming this fixes the specific failure mode on Manjaro Linux.

**Repro I was hitting:**
- Command with a literal newline in the string: `python3 -c "import time\ntime.sleep(1)"` or `curl ... | python3 -c "..."`
- Command completes in ~1s in the PTY
- `execution.read()` stream never ends — `]633;D` marker not delivered for multi-line commands on Linux/bash
- 30s notification fires → command marked Skipped → user restarts VS Code → task resumed → model retries same command → infinite loop

The `onDidEndTerminalShellExecution` path fires correctly for these cases and breaks out of the loop without waiting for the missing marker. The 30s idle timeout is a solid safety net for anything that slips past both signals.

**On the e2e (ubuntu) failure:** The failing check (`e2e / editor.test.ts / Multi-Roots`) is in the teardown phase and is outside the changed files. It reproduces on a clean checkout without this PR — pre-existing flake, not a regression from this change.

All greptile P1 issues (interval leak, iterator cleanup, changelog file) are addressed in the latest commit. This looks ready for a maintainer review.

body: For reference: the upstream root cause (VS Code's bash shell integration not delivering the `]633;D` completion marker for multi-line commands on Linux) is tracked at microsoft/vscode#316556.
author: RobinAngele

body:
One correction to my earlier comment: I said "the `onDidEndTerminalShellExecution` path fires correctly for these cases." That turns out to be inaccurate.

microsoft/vscode#250764 documents that `onDidEndTerminalShellExecution` **also does not fire** for commands containing newlines on Linux/bash — same root cause as the `read()` stream hang, because both signals depend on the `]633;D` marker that the bash shell integration script fails to deliver after multi-line input.

This means for the specific Linux multi-line case, the completion signal chain is:
- `onDidEndTerminalShellExecution` → ❌ doesn't fire
- `]633;D` OSC marker → ❌ not delivered
- Natural stream closure → ❌ never happens
- **30s idle timeout → ✅ actual safety net**

The idle timeout in this PR is therefore the real fix for the Linux multi-line hang, not just a last-resort fallback. The `onDidEndTerminalShellExecution` path still provides value for other failure modes where the marker is delayed but eventually delivered.

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes the missing `use_subagents` tool description in the hardcoded `TOOL_USE_SECTION` override templates for GLM, Hermes, and XS variants. Because these variants use text-based (non-native) tool calling, models only know about tools explicitly described in the system prompt; the tool was registered in `.tools()` but never added to the override strings. The fix converts `HERMES_TOOL_USE_TEMPLATE` from a plain string to a context-aware function and adds the `use_subagents` description block to all three templates, gating it on `context.subagentsEnabled === true && !context.isSubagentRun` to match the canonical tool spec's conditions. Snapshots for 12 test scenarios (GLM × 4, Hermes × 4, XS/lmstudio × 4) are updated accordingly and 1353 tests pass.

Confidence Score: 5/5

All prior P1 concerns from the review thread (unconditional inclusion in GLM, static string in Hermes, unconditional XS branch) are fully resolved in this revision. Remaining observations are purely test-coverage gaps (no snapshot tests for the disabled/subagent-run paths), which are P2 and don't affect correctness. No files require special attention.

Greptile Summary

This PR replaces the ephemeral `nanoid(5)` server key with a deterministic djb2 hash, fixing routing failures when a model's cached tool names reference keys that changed after an extension restart (issue #8087). The core logic is correct and well-tested. Two minor issues worth addressing before merge: - `McpHub.static hashServerName` is unused dead code — no caller in the codebase references it, and the \"backward compatibility\" rationale doesn't apply to a brand-new API. It should be removed. - Hash collisions are handled silently: if two server names produce the same 5-char hash, `mcpServerKeys` is overwritten without any warning, permanently misrouting one server's tools. A collision log warning would surface this in the rare case it occurs.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge; both remaining findings are P2 quality improvements that don't block correctness. The fix is correct and well-scoped. The two findings are both P2: one is unused dead code (the static property), and the other is a pre-existing gap in collision handling that now only becomes a permanent miss rather than a session-scoped miss. Neither affects normal operation for the overwhelming majority of users. src/services/mcp/McpHub.ts (unused static property) and src/services/mcp/server-key.ts (silent collision handling)

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/services/mcp/server-key.ts | New utility introducing deterministic djb2 hash for MCP server keys; collision handling is silent and warrants a warning log. | | src/services/mcp/McpHub.ts | Replaces nanoid with deterministic buildServerKey; adds an unused static hashServerName property with a misleading "backward compatibility" comment. | | src/services/mcp/__tests__/McpHub.serverKeys.test.ts | 10 unit tests covering determinism, format, edge cases; no collision-detection test, but coverage is otherwise solid. |

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Model as LLM Model participant Task as Task Runner participant McpHub participant SK as server-key.ts Note over McpHub,SK: Extension restart or MCP reconnect McpHub->>SK: buildServerKey(serverName) SK->>SK: djb2 hash, base-36, 5 chars SK-->>McpHub: deterministic 6-char key McpHub->>McpHub: mcpServerKeys.set(key, serverName) Note over Model,Task: Model uses cached tool name from prior session Model->>Task: tool call with cached key Task->>McpHub: getMcpServerByKey(key) McpHub-->>Task: same serverName as before Task->>McpHub: invoke tool on correct server ```

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a deadlock where `ask("command_output", …)` inside `flushBuffer` could stay pending indefinitely after the terminal process completed, errored, or timed out, because no code path was releasing that blocked ask. The fix introduces a lightweight sequence-ID guard around the pending ask and a `releaseAnyPendingCommandOutputAsk` helper that is called on all three terminal lifecycle exits, with a new `resolvePendingAsk` callback in `Task` to satisfy the underlying `pWaitFor` poll in `Task.ask()`. The approach is correct and well-scoped; the only P2 findings are a confusing double-`if` pattern in the release helper and a missing test for the timeout release path.

Confidence Score: 5/5

- Safe to merge; all remaining findings are P2 style/test-coverage suggestions that do not affect correctness. - The deadlock fix is logically sound: the sequence-ID guard prevents double-resolution, the `finally` block in `flushBuffer` ensures `bufferStuckTimer` is always cleared even on early return, and the `lastMessageTs` mechanism in `Task.ask()` correctly invalidates the old ask if a new one is created immediately after release. No P0 or P1 issues were found. - No files require special attention beyond the P2 style note on `releaseAnyPendingCommandOutputAsk` in `CommandOrchestrator.ts`.

This PR adds a new `kanban/remote-access.mdx` documentation page covering six methods for accessing Kanban remotely (local network, Tailscale, Docker, SSH tunnel, Ngrok, Cloudflare Tunnels) and registers it in `docs.json`. The content is well-structured and the security warnings throughout are appropriate — however, the included AWS CDK example has two issues worth fixing before users start copying it into production deployments.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Documentation-only PR — no runtime risk to the extension — but the CDK example ships with a public SSH security hole and a pinned development branch that will silently break future deployments. Two P1 findings in the CDK example: an open SSH ingress rule (security risk for users copying the code) and a `remote-kanban` branch reference that is likely a development artifact and may disappear. Both are easy fixes that should be resolved before the docs go live. docs/kanban/remote-access.mdx — the AWS CDK code block (lines 186 and 207)

Security Review

 - **SSH open to 0.0.0.0/0** (`docs/kanban/remote-access.mdx`, line 186): The CDK example adds an inbound rule allowing TCP 22 from any IPv4 address. The stack already includes SSM access and Cloudflare Tunnel, making public SSH unnecessary and exposing the instance to brute-force and exploit attempts.

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a 404 error when using Claude models on Vertex AI with the `"global"` region by overriding the `baseURL` passed to the `AnthropicVertex` SDK constructor. The `AnthropicVertex` SDK builds its base URL as `${region}-aiplatform.googleapis.com`, producing the non-existent `global-aiplatform.googleapis.com` when region is `"global"`; the fix injects the correct `aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1` host only for that case.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — targeted, well-documented fix for a confirmed 404 regression with no side effects on other regions or providers. The change is minimal and surgical: a single conditional spread that only activates when `vertexRegion === "global"`, consistent with the same string comparison already used in `VertexProvider.tsx`. The `baseURL` override is confirmed correct per the Google Cloud docs, and the SDK still uses `region: "global"` to include `/locations/global/` in request paths. No other regions or providers are affected. No files require special attention.

body:
Greptile Summary

Fixes an indefinite hang in `VscodeTerminalProcess.run()` when a shell rejects a command at parse time (e.g., `tail … 2>1& | echo -`), causing VS Code's shell-integration stream to yield nothing and never close. The fix races each `iterator.next()` call against `onDidEndTerminalShellExecution` via `Promise.race`, breaking out of the loop when the end-of-execution event fires. Both concerns from prior review threads (missing `iterator.return()` cleanup and missing exit-code capture from the end event) are now addressed in the `finally` block and the event handler respectively.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — fix is correct, both prior P1 concerns are addressed, and the one remaining note is a low-probability edge case with graceful fallback. Both issues flagged in prior review threads (missing `iterator.return()` cleanup and missing exit-code capture from the end event) are resolved in this revision. The `finally` block properly disposes the listener and calls `await iterator.return?.()`. The single remaining comment is a P2 theoretical edge case (stale end-event from a prior command on the same terminal) that degrades gracefully via the existing `returnCurrentTerminalContents()` fallback, not a blocker. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/hosts/vscode/terminal/VscodeTerminalProcess.ts | Core fix: replaces `for await` with a manual `while` loop that races stream iteration against `onDidEndTerminalShellExecution`; iterator cleanup and exit-code capture from the event are both handled correctly. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant C as run() participant S as stream iterator participant V as VS Code
onDidEndTerminalShellExecution C->>V: register listener (shellIntegration match) C->>S: executeCommand() / stream.read() alt Parse-rejected command (stream never yields) S--xC: (no chunks, iterator hangs) V-->>C: event fires → resolveEndOfExecution() C->>C: Promise.race resolves END_SENTINEL → break C->>S: iterator.return() [finally] V-->>C: dispose listener [finally] C->>C: returnCurrentTerminalContents() fallback C->>C: emit("completed", ...) else Healthy command (stream closes normally) S-->>C: chunk(s) yielded → processed S-->>C: {done:true} → break (endOfExecutionTriggered:false) C->>S: iterator.return() [finally] V-->>C: dispose listener [finally] C->>C: emit("completed", ...) end ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown This is a comment left during a code review. Path: src/hosts/vscode/terminal/VscodeTerminalProcess.ts Line: 79-88 Comment: **End-event listener matches on shell integration scope, not on the specific execution** Because `e.execution === execution` is not reliable (as the PR correctly documents), the match is on `e.shellIntegration === terminal.shellIntegration`. This means the listener will also trigger for any other `executeCommand`-initiated execution that finishes on the same terminal — including, in theory, a stale `onDidEndTerminalShellExecution` from the immediately-prior command if VS Code delivers that event slightly late (after the new `run()` has already registered its listener). In that edge case the `while` loop exits before the stream delivers any chunks, `fullOutput` stays empty, and the `returnCurrentTerminalContents()` fallback at line 251 fires, providing degraded-but-functional output. Given that sequential commands are the only realistic scenario and VS Code's event dispatch is prompt in practice, the risk is very low — but worth noting if intermittent "no output captured" reports appear for the first command in a session. How can I resolve this? If you propose a fix, please make it concise. `````

body:
Follow-up: verified the `backgroundExec` path (`StandaloneTerminalManager` → `StandaloneTerminalProcess`) is not vulnerable to the same hang.

**Repro:** set Terminal Execution Mode to "Background Exec" and ran the same parse-error command `tail -10 /var/www/html/index.html 2>1& | echo -`.

**Result:** completes at t+40ms with exit code 1 and the zsh parse error captured on stderr. Instrumented timings:

```
[t+0ms]   orchestrate enter, terminalType: standalone, timeoutSeconds: 30
[t+0ms]   run() enter, shell: /bin/zsh, args: [-l, -c, <command>]
[t+39ms]  stderr data: "zsh:1: parse error near `|'" (28 bytes)
[t+40ms]  child close, code: 1, signal: null
[t+39ms]  orchestrator 'completed' fired
```

**Why it's safe on this path:**

1. Direct `child_process.spawn` rather than a VS Code shell-integration async iterable. Shell exits on parse failure → `close` event fires → `completed` emits. No iterator to get wedged on.
2. The orchestrator is given a real `timeoutSeconds: 30` here (vs. `undefined` on the shell-integration path). Even if `close` somehow didn't fire, there's a hard 30s ceiling.

So this fix is scoped correctly to the VS Code integrated terminal with shell integration. #10196 moves everything to the standalone runtime, which sidesteps this whole class of bug.

Confidence Score: 1/5

Not safe to merge — multiple P0/P1 defects cause a compile failure and runtime API errors for all Vertex AI users. Six independent P1+ issues: missing import (compile error), tool_choice API error on every tool-less request, broken input-token accounting, wrong model registry placement, missing isVertex flag (auth failure for Gemini on Vertex), and proto fields absent (headline feature non-functional). Any one of these blocks production use of Vertex AI. src/core/api/providers/vertex.ts, src/shared/api.ts, webview-ui/src/components/settings/providers/VertexProvider.tsx, src/shared/storage/state-keys.ts (proto regeneration required)

Path: webview-ui/src/components/settings/providers/VertexProvider.tsx Line: 173-178 Comment: **`VSCodeTextField` not imported** `VSCodeTextField` is used here but not imported from `@vscode/webview-ui-toolkit/react`. The current import on line 5 only includes `VSCodeDropdown`, `VSCodeLink`, and `VSCodeOption`. This will cause a compile-time reference error. Add `VSCodeTextField` to the import on line 5: ```typescript import { VSCodeDropdown, VSCodeLink, VSCodeOption, VSCodeTextField } from "@vscode/webview-ui-toolkit/react" ``` How can I resolve this? If you propose a fix, please make it concise. --- This is a comment left during a code review. The new code passes `this.options` directly, so `GeminiHandler` will attempt Gemini-API-key authentication for Vertex-hosted Gemini models, causing authentication failures. ```suggestion private ensureGeminiHandler(): GeminiHandler { if (!this.geminiHandler) { this.geminiHandler = new GeminiHandler({ ...this.options, isVertex: true, }) } return this.geminiHandler } ``` How can I resolve this? Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a UI state desync where switching models via the \"Recommended\" or \"Free\" model cards would display stale pricing (often \"Free\") from the previously selected model. The fix has three parts: (1) using `searchTerm !== configModelId` as a pending-state signal in the `useMemo` so price data resolves optimistically from `clineModels` instead of waiting for the gRPC round-trip, (2) guarding `handleModelChange` against writing `undefined` as `clineModelInfo` when the new model isn't yet in `clineModels`, and (3) adding an `isLoading` prop to `ModelInfoView` so the UI shows \"Loading...\" rather than stale prices during the async window.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the fix is well-scoped, backward compatible, and the loading state is correctly unreachable for models absent from clineModels due to the existing hasInfo gate. All findings are P2 style suggestions. The core logic — optimistic model ID resolution, undefined-guard in handleModelChange, and the isLoading prop — is correct. The isLoading case for context window is unreachable in practice, so no correctness risk exists. No files require special attention.

Logic is sound and dependency array is correctly updated. | | webview-ui/src/components/settings/common/ModelInfoView.tsx | Adds optional `isLoading` prop that replaces stale Input/Output price values with "Loading..."; backward compatible (defaults to false). Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a path traversal vulnerability in `validateAccess()` by adding workspace boundary enforcement before the `.clineignore` check, and flipping the error-handler to deny-by-default. The fix is correct and well-tested, but `readIncludedFile()` in the same class has a parallel gap: `!include` directives are not boundary-checked, so a malicious `.clineignore` containing `!include ../../../../etc/shadow` would still cause the controller to read files outside the workspace. - **P1 — `readIncludedFile` lacks workspace boundary check**: `path.join(this.cwd, includePath)` is called without a `startsWith("..")` guard, meaning a crafted `!include` line can reach arbitrary paths outside the workspace via the same attack surface this PR targets.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Addresses the primary path traversal but leaves a parallel read-outside-workspace vector in readIncludedFile open. The validateAccess fix is correct and the tests are solid. However, readIncludedFile() has the same class of vulnerability (out-of-workspace file read via !include traversal) that is not addressed by this PR and is a present, exploitable defect on the same attack surface. src/core/ignore/ClineIgnoreController.ts — specifically the readIncludedFile method (lines 138–147)

The file watcher makes this auto-trigger on write. The PR fixes `validateAccess` but this parallel read path remains unguarded.

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes two independent bugs in hook templates: (1) incorrect field names (`tool` → `toolName`, `durationMs` → `executionTimeMs`, `task` → `taskMetadata.*`) that caused hooks to receive `null` values, and (2) broken shell escaping where `echo \"{\\\"cancel\\\":false,...}\"` inside a TypeScript template literal produced invalid bash output, replaced correctly with single-quoted `echo '{\"cancel\":false,...}'`. Dynamic string interpolation in `TaskStart` is now safely encoded via `jq --arg` with a `sed` fallback, and tests gain an unconditional timeout increase to prevent flakiness on non-Windows hosts.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — all changes are targeted bug fixes with no functional regressions. All changes are correct: field names match actual runtime payloads, single-quoted echo strings are unambiguously safe, jq-based encoding handles all characters properly, and the sed fallback is only reached on systems without jq where the default ISO timestamp is always safe. The timeout fix improves test reliability. No P0/P1 issues found. No files require special attention.

Greptile Summary

This PR adds a `maxRetryAfter` cap (default 60 s / 60 000 ms) to the `withRetry` decorator so that a large `retry-after` header value — such as the 3-hour window Gemini returns on quota exhaustion — causes an immediate rethrow rather than a silent multi-hour hang. - **`retry.ts`**: Adds `maxRetryAfter` to `RetryOptions` and `DEFAULT_OPTIONS`, and inserts a guard that throws immediately when the computed header-driven delay exceeds the cap. Includes a minor cleanup (`parseInt` → `Number.parseInt`, class-field type annotation). - **`retry.test.ts`**: Properly stubs `Date.now` in the Unix-timestamp test (fixing the previously reported coverage gap), and adds two new tests — one that confirms the cap triggers on a 3-hour header and one that confirms normal retry behaviour for a sub-cap header.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the guard is additive, isolated to the retry-after header branch, and does not touch exponential backoff or any other retry path. The change is small and surgically placed: one new option with a sensible default, one early-throw guard, and well-targeted tests. The only previously flagged issue (Unix-timestamp test no longer exercising the Unix path) has been fixed in this revision by properly stubbing Date.now. No files require special attention.

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes two silent failures against Claude Code CLI v2.1+: the `\"result\" in chunk` guard that always returned false (causing every task to fail with an unrecognized-chunk warning), and the `error_max_turns` case that was incorrectly treated as a hard error. It also migrates the test runner from `ts-node` to `tsx/cjs` for Node 22 compatibility and rewrites tests to use dependency injection instead of sinon module stubs.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge after addressing the `seenMaxTurns` / execa rejection interaction in `run.ts`. The two primary bug fixes in `claude-code.ts` and `types.ts` are correct and well-tested. The `seenMaxTurns` guard in `run.ts` may be silently bypassed because execa's default `reject: true` can cause `await cProcess` to throw before line 99 is reached, leaving the catch block to re-throw and trigger `withRetry` retries on what should be a normal max-turns completion. The risk is real but has been tested to work against the live CLI, so may not manifest in practice — warranting a 4 rather than 3. src/integrations/claude-code/run.ts — catch block should check `seenMaxTurns` before re-throwing to guard against execa's default reject behaviour.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/core/api/providers/claude-code.ts | Core fix: removes the `"result" in chunk` guard that silently failed on CLI v2.1+; adds `error_max_turns` exception to `is_error` check; adds `_runClaudeCode` DI hook for testability. Logic is sound. | | src/integrations/claude-code/run.ts | Adds `seenMaxTurns` tracking and exit-code suppression; lazy-imports `execa`. The `seenMaxTurns` guard at line 99 may be unreachable if execa rejects at `await cProcess` before that line — the catch block does not check `seenMaxTurns` before re-throwing. | | src/integrations/claude-code/types.ts | Makes `ResultMessage.result` optional — correctly reflects CLI v2.1+ behaviour where the field is omitted on success. | | src/core/api/providers/__tests__/claude-code.test.ts | Rewrites tests to use DI factory instead of sinon module stubs; adds two regression tests for the v2.1+ success format and `error_max_turns`. Clean and thorough. | | src/test/requires.ts | Adds a CJS stub for `unicorn-magic` (pure-ESM dependency of execa) so the test runner doesn't fail on `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`. Stub surface matches what execa actually calls. | | src/core/workspace/WorkspaceRootManager.ts | Moves `execa` import to lazy `await import("execa")` inside `detectVcs` to fix CJS loading in tests; minor TypeScript style clean-up of redundant type annotations. | | .mocharc.json | Switches Mocha loader from `ts-node/register` to `tsx/cjs` + `tsconfig-paths/register` for Node 22 compatibility. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant CC as ClaudeCodeHandler participant RF as runClaudeCode (run.ts) participant CLI as Claude Code CLI CC->>RF: call runFn(options) RF->>CLI: spawn process (execa) CLI-->>RF: stream-json chunks (stdout) RF-->>CC: yield AssistantMessage CLI-->>RF: result chunk (type=result, subtype=success, no 'result' field) RF-->>CC: yield result chunk Note over CC: OLD: "result" in chunk → false → skip → Logger.warn
NEW: chunk.type === "result" → handle it CC-->>CC: yield usage (totalCost from total_cost_usd) alt error_max_turns (CLI exits with code 1) CLI-->>RF: result chunk (subtype=error_max_turns, is_error=true) RF->>RF: processState.seenMaxTurns = true RF-->>CC: yield result chunk Note over CC: OLD: is_error=true → throw
NEW: subtype=error_max_turns → skip throw, yield usage RF->>RF: await cProcess (exit code 1) Note over RF: seenMaxTurns=true → suppress exit-code throw CC-->>CC: complete normally (no retry) end ```

Comments Outside Diff (1)

 1. `src/integrations/claude-code/run.ts`, line 98-104 ([link](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/0525bf3289caaa3d629315fb7e7fb0b5720d85f6/src/integrations/claude-code/run.ts#L98-L104)) **`seenMaxTurns` guard may be bypassed by execa's default rejection** `execa` defaults to `reject: true`, so `await cProcess` (line 98) rejects with an `ExecaError` when the CLI exits with code 1. That rejection jumps straight to the `catch` block — the `!processState.seenMaxTurns` guard on line 99 is never evaluated for the `error_max_turns` case. The catch block doesn't check `seenMaxTurns`, so it re-throws (via the `startOfCommand` path), and `withRetry` in `ClaudeCodeHandler` then retries the entire call up to 4 more times — each hitting the same max-turns limit.
