body:
Greptile Summary

This automated security bot PR pins `@anthropic-ai/sdk` from `0.81.0` to `0.91.1` via a root-level `overrides` entry to address CVE-2026-41686 (overly permissive file modes in `BetaLocalFilesystemMemoryTool`). However, the four mermaid CVEs and the `diff`/`@opentui/core` CVE described in the PR body are not addressed — no version changes or overrides were added for those packages. - `@anthropic-ai/sdk` upgraded 0.81.0 → 0.91.1 via `overrides` in `sdk/package.json`; `bun.lock` reflects the resolved version change. - `mermaid` (still `11.14.0`) and `@opentui/core` (still `0.1.102`) are unchanged, leaving CVE-2026-41148, CVE-2026-41149, CVE-2026-41150, CVE-2026-41159, and CVE-2026-24001 unresolved. - The workspace root also gains a direct `@anthropic-ai/sdk` dependency entry in the lock file, which is redundant when an `overrides` entry already exists for the same package.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The @anthropic-ai/sdk upgrade is safe to land, but the PR leaves five of six advertised vulnerabilities unpatched — mermaid CSS/DOM injection and diff ReDoS remain in the resolved dependency tree. The @anthropic-ai/sdk bump is a narrow, well-scoped change with low regression risk. The concern is what the PR does not do: mermaid 11.14.0 retains four injection/DoS vulnerabilities and the diff package retains its ReDoS exposure. Both packages are actively used in the CLI rendering path, so those gaps matter. Merging as-is gives a false sense of security coverage. sdk/package.json and sdk/bun.lock — both need additional overrides entries for mermaid and the diff package (used via @opentui/core) before the stated security goals of this PR are met.

Security Review

 - **CSS/DOM injection (mermaid, 4 CVEs unresolved):** CVE-2026-41148, CVE-2026-41149, CVE-2026-41159 allow unsanitized `classDef` values and config options (`fontFamily`, `themeCSS`, `altFontFamily`) to inject arbitrary CSS/HTML escaping the SVG sandbox. CVE-2026-41150 allows a denial-of-service via a crafted Gantt `excludes` attribute. `mermaid` remains at `11.14.0` with no override applied. - **ReDoS/DoS in `diff` package (CVE-2026-24001, unresolved):** The `parsePatch`/`applyPatch` methods in the `diff` package (resolved at `8.0.2`, used by `@opentui/core@0.1.102`) are vulnerable to infinite loops and ReDoS via crafted line-break characters in patch headers. No override was added. - **`@anthropic-ai/sdk` file-permission issue (CVE-2026-41686, resolved):** The upgrade to `0.91.1` addresses overly permissive default file modes in `BetaLocalFilesystemMemoryTool`, which could allow local attackers to read or tamper with persisted agent state on shared systems.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/package.json | Adds @anthropic-ai/sdk override (0.81.0 → 0.91.1) to fix CVE-2026-41686; missing overrides for mermaid and @opentui/core/diff to address the other 5 claimed CVEs | | sdk/bun.lock | Lock file pins @anthropic-ai/sdk to 0.91.1; mermaid still at 11.14.0 and @opentui/core at 0.1.102 with no version overrides, leaving 5 of 6 advertised CVEs unresolved |

Individual workspace `clean` scripts are removed and all clean logic is now consolidated at the root level. - **`sdk/scripts/clean.ts`**: Reads workspace globs from root `package.json`, expands them with `Bun.Glob.scan`, then serially removes `dist` and `node_modules` from each workspace directory plus the repo root (root is deleted last to avoid removing hoisted binaries before workspaces are cleaned). - **Per-package `package.json` files** (7 packages): `clean` scripts removed; `apps/cli`, `apps/examples/vscode`, and `packages/core` also drop the `rm -rf dist` prefix from their `build` scripts. - **`sdk/package.json`**: Root `clean` delegates to `bun run scripts/clean.ts`; the full `build` pipeline (`bun run clean && bun install && ...`) continues to clean before every build.

body:
Pushed a follow-up fix in 18f8e98af.

Root cause of the focused core test failure:

The resolver was added to root `@cline/shared`, but the helper imports Node filesystem APIs through `node:fs`. Root `@cline/shared` has both node and browser entrypoints, and Vitest/Vite can resolve that package through the browser condition. In that runtime shape, `resolveExistingFilePath` was not present, so `createFileReadExecutor` imported `undefined` and every file-read test failed with `TypeError: resolveExistingFilePath is not a function`.

I considered a few fixes:

- Changing export condition precedence would make the test pass, but it changes root `@cline/shared` resolution semantics and can create browser bundling risk.
- Keeping this on root `@cline/shared` would mean root shared now exposes a node-only filesystem API, which is not a good contract for browser consumers.
- Creating a new `@cline/shared/path-resolution` subpath felt too specific and would add another public import surface.

The fix I pushed moves the resolver under the existing `@cline/shared/storage` entrypoint instead. That subpath is already the shared place for node filesystem/path behavior, so core and CLI can share the helper without making root `@cline/shared` node-only.

The telemetry plumbing in this PR looks correct end-to-end (both the auto path through `createContextCompactionPrepareTurn(configWithProvider)` in `local-runtime-host.ts` and the manual path through `compactInteractiveMessages`), but I the CLI entry point is missing the actual wiring of the telemetry service into the run config. So in practice `config.telemetry` will be `undefined` at runtime for the CLI and neither `task.compaction_executed` nor `task.compaction_skipped` will fire.

One extra change needed in `sdk/apps/cli/src/main.ts`:

```diff
-import { captureCliExtensionActivated } from "./utils/telemetry";
+import { captureCliExtensionActivated, getCliTelemetryService } from "./utils/telemetry";
```

and in the run-options object (currently around line ~857, alongside `logger`/`loggerConfig`):

```diff
 			mode: args.mode,
 			logger: loggerAdapter.core,
 			loggerConfig: loggerAdapter.runtimeConfig,
+			telemetry: getCliTelemetryService(loggerAdapter.core),
 			defaultToolAutoApprove,
 			toolPolicies,
 			enableSpawnAgent: !isYoloMode,
```

Rationale: `Config extends Omit<CoreSessionConfig, "apiKey" | "mode">` so `telemetry` is part of the type, but `main.ts` doesn't populate it today. `splitCoreSessionConfig` then has nothing to forward into `LocalRuntimeBootstrapConfig.telemetry`, so `configWithProvider.telemetry` lands as `undefined` in both `createContextCompactionPrepareTurn` and `compactInteractiveMessages`. The `captureCompactionExecuted(undefined, ...)` calls then no-op silently.

With this one extra line, the rest of the plumbing in this PR fires as intended.

The host layer then double-counted each prior turn's tokens on top of the baseline, producing quadratically inflated totals. - **One-line fix** in `agent-runtime.ts`: adds `this.state.usage = cloneUsage(DEFAULT_USAGE)` alongside the existing resets for `iteration`, `pendingToolCalls`, and `lastError`, matching the same pattern already used in `restore()`. - **New regression test** in `agent-runtime.test.ts` drives the runtime through two back-to-back calls with distinct usage values and asserts each result carries only its own turn's tokens, not a cumulative sum.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The fix is a one-liner that mirrors an identical reset already present in restore(). The accumulation logic, cloneUsage, and DEFAULT_USAGE are all unchanged and well-understood. The new test exercises the exact failure mode described in the PR, and the full agent test suite passes. No edge cases are introduced. No files require special attention.

Greptile Summary

This PR adds two JSON files written to the task directory — `agent_prompt_info.json` (system prompt + thinking mode) and `agent_io_log.json` (all request/response pairs) — intended to capture a complete trace of a task session. - `writeAgentOutputFiles()` is called exclusively from `abortTask()`, so files are never written at the moment of a successful `attempt_completion`; they are silently skipped if VS Code is closed after task completion. - Each IO log entry stores a full copy of the system prompt, duplicating data already written to `agent_prompt_info.json` and inflating the log file size significantly for multi-turn tasks.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The feature works only for the abort/cancel path; successful task completions followed by a VS Code close will silently produce no output files. The core write path is never triggered at the natural task-completion point — only when abortTask() runs. A user who finishes a task and closes VS Code before starting a new one gets no files at all. The full system prompt is also redundantly embedded in every IO log entry, creating disproportionately large output files for multi-turn tasks. src/core/task/index.ts — the placement of writeAgentOutputFiles() and the per-entry system prompt duplication both need attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/core/storage/disk.ts | Adds two new entries (`agentPromptInfo`, `agentIoLog`) to the `GlobalFileNames` registry — straightforward constant additions with no logic changes. | | src/core/task/index.ts | Adds in-memory collection of system prompt, thinking mode, and per-request IO entries, writing them to disk inside `abortTask()` only; successful task completions where the extension is closed without a subsequent abort will never produce these files. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User participant Task participant FS as Filesystem Note over Task: makeApiRequest called Task->>Task: "set collectedSystemPrompt" Task->>Task: "create currentRequestIoEntry" Task->>Task: "stream API response" Task->>Task: "push entry to collectedIoLog" alt User aborts task User->>Task: "abortTask()" Task->>FS: "writeAgentOutputFiles()" FS-->>Task: "files written" else Successful completion then VS Code closed Task-->>User: "completion_result ask shown" Note over Task,FS: "abortTask() never called - files never written" end ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 3 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 3 src/core/task/index.ts:1644 **Output files never written for successful task completions** `writeAgentOutputFiles()` is only called inside `abortTask()`. When a task succeeds via `attempt_completion`, the agentic loop breaks out without ever calling `abortTask()`. If the user closes VS Code before starting a new task, `abortTask()` is never invoked and neither `agent_prompt_info.json` nor `agent_io_log.json` is written to disk. Additionally, post-completion API calls will be silently included in the log when `abortTask()` does eventually fire, mixing them with the original task requests. ### Issue 2 of 3 src/core/task/index.ts:2092-2102 **`system_prompt` duplicated in every IO log entry** `system_prompt` is stored in full on every entry in `collectedIoLog` and also written separately to `agent_prompt_info.json`. For a typical Cline system prompt (~10–30 KB) across a 10-request task, this inflates `agent_io_log.json` by 100–300 KB of redundant data. Consider omitting `system_prompt` from individual log entries and relying on the separate prompt-info file. ```suggestion this.currentRequestIoEntry = { request_number: this.taskState.apiRequestCount, timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), provider: providerInfo.providerId, model: providerInfo.model.id, mode: providerInfo.mode, messages: contextManagementMetadata.truncatedConversationHistory, tools: tools || [], response: null, } ``` ### Issue 3 of 3 src/core/task/index.ts:1836-1847 **Non-atomic file writes inconsistent with the rest of `disk.ts`** `disk.ts` exposes `atomicWriteFile` (temp-file + rename) to prevent readers from seeing partial data. The new `writeAgentOutputFiles` calls `fs.writeFile` directly, so a crash mid-write could leave a truncated JSON file. ```suggestion await Promise.all([ atomicWriteFile( path.join(taskDir, GlobalFileNames.agentPromptInfo), JSON.stringify(promptInfo, null, 2), ), atomicWriteFile( path.join(taskDir, GlobalFileNames.agentIoLog), JSON.stringify(ioLog, null, 2), ), ]) ``` `````

body:
Related context on #10713:

#10713 fixes a separate usage-accounting issue in `AgentRuntime`: consecutive `run()` or `continue()` calls on the same runtime instance can carry prior run usage forward unless per-run usage state is reset. That helps keep `result.usage` and backend/session accounting from accumulating previous runs.

This PR fixes the CLI TUI display path. The status bar token number represents current context size, but during streaming it was adding `inputTokens + outputTokens` onto the previous displayed value. Even with #10713, the TUI would still briefly overstate the context count if it continued treating each usage event as additive display state.

So the two fixes are complementary:

- #10713: resets per-run runtime usage so backend/result usage is scoped correctly
- This PR: keeps the live TUI token display aligned with current context size by using the latest `inputTokens`

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a bug where the CLI TUI status bar showed an inflated token count during streaming by treating `inputTokens + outputTokens` from usage events as an additive delta on top of the previous display value. The fix changes `addUsageDelta` to set `lastTotalTokens` directly to the latest positive `inputTokens` value (which already represents the full prompt/context size for that call) while leaving the cost accumulation path unchanged. - **Token display**: `setLastTotalTokens(inputTokens)` replaces `setLastTotalTokens(prev => prev + inputTokens + outputTokens)`, eliminating the inflation from summing context size with output tokens. - **Cost display**: Remains additive across streaming events and is overwritten with the authoritative `result.usage.totalCost` when the turn completes, correcting any streaming drift. - The guarded `if (inputTokens > 0)` check ensures the display is not reset to zero when a streaming event carries only `outputTokens`.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The change is small and correctly scoped to the TUI display layer; the fix aligns the live token display with the same `inputTokens`-as-context-size semantics already used at turn completion. The logic change is straightforward and the new behaviour is correct: `inputTokens` represents full prompt context size and should be set directly, not accumulated alongside output tokens. The only gap is that no unit test directly covers `addUsageDelta`, leaving the fixed invariant unguarded against future regressions. sdk/apps/cli/src/tui/contexts/session-context.tsx — the changed function `addUsageDelta` has no dedicated test coverage

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/apps/cli/src/tui/contexts/session-context.tsx | Core fix: `addUsageDelta` now sets `lastTotalTokens` to `inputTokens` (absolute context size) instead of accumulating `inputTokens + outputTokens`; logic is correct but there are no unit tests directly covering this function's new behaviour |

Greptile Summary

This PR adds a `--worktree` flag to the Cline CLI that auto-creates a detached git worktree under `~/.cline/worktrees///` and re-points the task's `cwd` at the new worktree, mirroring Kanban's behavior. The core helper (`createTaskWorktree`) lives in `sdk/apps/cli/src/utils/worktree.ts` and the CLI wiring is in `main.ts`. - **New utility** (`worktree.ts`): discovers git root, generates a 5-char hex task ID (with 16-attempt collision avoidance), creates the worktree directory and runs `git worktree add --detach \u2026 HEAD`, and cleans up the parent directory on failure if it was freshly created. - **CLI wiring** (`main.ts`): session-exists guard runs before worktree creation for `--id` paths; piped-stdin is explicitly allowed alongside `--worktree`; `args.cwd` is rewritten to the new worktree path so all downstream sandbox/workspace resolution uses the correct root. - **Tests**: new unit tests in `worktree.test.ts` cover path layout, detached-HEAD state, cleanup on failure, and path-traversal/null-byte rejection; new integration tests in `main.test.ts` cover prompt, interactive, piped-stdin, non-TTY rejection, and session-validation flows.

Safe to merge; the feature is opt-in and the new code is well-covered by unit and integration tests. The worktree helper correctly separates the git-not-installed case from not-a-git-repo, guards against path-traversal and null-byte taskIds, and cleans up freshly created directories on failure. body:
Took a closer look at this against the Kanban worktree behavior and also tested the narrow CLI implementation.

I tested the PR head with a manual smoke test against a throwaway git repo, which confirmed it creates `~/.cline/worktrees/<id>/<repo>`, the worktree is detached at `HEAD`, the worktree HEAD matches the source repo HEAD, and status starts clean.

A couple things I want to call out so we are intentional about the product behavior:

- This is not full Kanban parity. Kanban does extra setup after `git worktree add`, especially mirroring ignored paths like dependency/build/env dirs into the task worktree with symlinks. I recognize this is the CLI and it probably should not inherit all of Kanban’s task lifecycle behavior, but users coming from Kanban may expect those worktrees to be more ready-to-run than a plain git worktree.
- Successful CLI worktrees are not cleaned up when the session ends. The PR only cleans up the parent dir on creation failure. So `~/.cline/worktrees/<id>/<repo>` will accumulate until the user manually runs `git worktree remove ...` or we add an explicit cleanup command/flag/lifecycle later.
- Because of the above, I think the help text/docs should probably make the persistence clear, something like: “Creates a detached worktree under `~/.cline/worktrees`; remove it manually with `git worktree remove` when done.”

None of this looks like it should affect normal users who do not pass `--worktree`. The new behavior is gated behind the flag. I mainly want us to be clear that this is a simple isolated-worktree launcher, not the full Kanban task workspace lifecycle.

> Optional. API key for authenticating requests using Bearer token authentication. When provided, this will be used instead of AWS SigV4 authentication. It uses the AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK environment variable by default.

Greptile Summary

This PR introduces a full MacM4LocalAgent provider integration into the `cline/cline` fork: a new `MacM4Handler`, warm-up pre-flight logic, static tier catalogue, UI settings panel, savings/badge widgets, CI workflow changes, and an idempotent macOS install script. The PR description explicitly notes it is **not intended for upstream** — it disables all existing CI/CD workflows, changes the `package.json` publisher to `martinfr-certifyos`, and embeds GCS paths and GCP project IDs specific to an internal team stack. - **Context-window logic**: `isMacM4LocalLongModelId` matches `"hybrid-auto"`, causing `getContextWindowInfo()` to override the handler-reported 1M context window to 131K and apply 70% truncation (~91K max). The switch-case approach (branching on raw integer values 16_384 and 131_072) will also misclassify future models from other providers that happen to share those context sizes. - **xs system-prompt enforcement**: `isMacM4LocalModel()` returns `true` for any use of the `macm4` provider regardless of tier, so cloud tiers (`claude-opus-4-7`, `hybrid-auto` routing to cloud) receive the compact xs prompt that strips BROWSER, MCP, WEB_FETCH, USE_SUBAGENTS, and several other tool capabilities. - **Build workflow secret suppression**: `npx vsce package --allow-package-secrets sendgrid` bypasses the packager's SendGrid key-pattern check; if a real credential is present in the bundle it will be distributed to all VSIX installers.

Confidence Score: 2/5

Not safe to merge to upstream main: disables all existing CI/CD, changes the extension publisher identity, and contains logic errors that silently cap context and strip tool capabilities for cloud tiers. Three independent defects fire for every macm4 cloud-tier user: hybrid-auto context is throttled to ~91K regardless of which cloud model the router actually uses; all macm4 cloud tiers receive the compact xs system prompt that strips browser, MCP, and several other tool families; and the build workflow suppresses vsce's credential scan for SendGrid. Together with the upstream-inappropriate publisher change and wholesale workflow disablement, the PR needs significant revision before it can land. context-window-utils.ts (hybrid-auto context throttling and switch-case collision), xs/config.ts (cloud tiers get xs prompt), model-utils.ts (isLocalModel covers all macm4 tiers), build-vsix.yml (SendGrid secret suppression), package.json (publisher identity change)

Security Review

This flag is only required when a SendGrid API-key-shaped string is actually present in the bundled source; if a real key exists it will be distributed to every VSIX installer from the GCS bucket. - No other credential leakage, injection, or auth-boundary issues were identified in the changed code.

Also introduces a fragile switch-case that will silently mis-classify any future model whose contextWindow happens to equal 131_072 or 16_384. | | src/core/prompts/system-prompt/variants/xs/config.ts | Adds MacM4-specific xs prompt enforcement via `isMacM4LocalModel`, but that function returns true for any `macm4` provider regardless of tier, so cloud tiers (claude-opus-4-7, claude-haiku-4-5, hybrid-auto routing to cloud) all receive the stripped xs prompt that removes BROWSER, MCP, WEB_FETCH, LIST_CODE_DEF, NEW_TASK, APPLY_PATCH, and USE_SUBAGENTS. | | src/utils/model-utils.ts | Adds `isMacM4LocalModel` (new helper) and registers `"macm4"` as a local provider in `isLocalModel`. This PR resolves 49 CVEs across 15 packages by upgrading transitive and direct dependencies. Most fixes are lockfile-only semver-range advances (basic-ftp, hono, path-to-regexp, etc.); the four manifest changes are uuid (patch), protobufjs override (patch), a new brace-expansion targeted override, and zod (major v3 → v4). - **Lockfile-only transitive fixes** (basic-ftp, @xmldom/xmldom, fast-xml-parser, hono, @hono/node-server, path-to-regexp, fast-uri, follow-redirects, ip-address, brace-expansion 2.x/5.x): straightforward within already-declared parent ranges, no application risk. - **Manifest patch bumps** (uuid `^11.1.1`, protobufjs `7.5.6`, brace-expansion `<1.1.13` override): minimal risk. - **zod `^3.24.2` → `^4.4.0`**: a major version bump with 11 documented breaking changes per the PR description; none of the ~7 source files consuming zod were updated, raising the possibility of silent runtime regressions in schema validation (MCP config parsing, OAuth credential handling, remote config deserialization).

The lockfile-only transitive fixes and patch-level manifest bumps are safe; the zod major-version change needs verification before merging. All transitive and patch-level dependency bumps look correct and low-risk. The zod major-version jump is the only manifest change that alters runtime behavior across multiple critical validation paths with no accompanying code adjustments. package.json — the zod version constraint change from v3 to v4; all files in src/ that import from zod should be compiled and tested against the new version before merging.

Greptile Summary

This PR adds NVIDIA NIM as a first-class provider across the classic extension, webview settings, CLI, proto/storage, and SDK, and automatically injects `X-BILLING-INVOKE-ORIGIN: Cline` on all requests to `integrate.api.nvidia.com` — both through the new dedicated provider and through OpenAI-compatible configs that point at the public NIM endpoint. - New `NvidiaHandler` wraps the OpenAI-compatible API with the billing header baked in; `openai.ts` is updated to inject the same header automatically when the base URL matches the public NIM host, preserving any user-supplied value. - Provider wiring is complete end-to-end: proto fields, state-keys secrets, provider-keys mapping, webview settings UI, CLI model/provider picker, proto conversion, and SDK built-in/gateway registration. - The billing-header helpers (`isPublicNvidiaNimBaseUrl`, `addNvidiaBillingOriginHeader`, etc.) are duplicated verbatim in `src/shared/net.ts` and `sdk/packages/shared/src/llms/requests.ts` by design (the two stacks are independent), but this creates a silent maintenance coupling.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The billing-header injection is narrowly scoped to the public NIM host and correctly preserves user-supplied values; all proto field numbers are unique and non-conflicting, and the provider wiring is complete across all layers. The core header-injection logic and end-to-end wiring are solid. The only notable gap is in the webview settings utility: custom NVIDIA model IDs entered by users will display the default model's capability flags (reasoning, tools) in the UI, while the handler itself correctly uses neutral defaults for those same models — a visible but non-blocking display inconsistency. webview-ui/src/components/settings/utils/providerUtils.ts — the NVIDIA normalizeApiConfiguration case hardcodes nvidiaDefaultModelInfo rather than using a neutral fallback for custom model IDs.

follows the established OpenAI-compatible provider pattern, always injects the billing-origin header, and correctly falls back to openAiModelInfoSaneDefaults for non-default model IDs. | | src/core/api/providers/openai.ts | Injects addNvidiaBillingOriginHeaderForBaseUrl into both Azure and non-Azure client creation paths; Azure URLs never match the NVIDIA NIM host so existing behavior is fully preserved for those paths. | | webview-ui/src/components/settings/utils/providerUtils.ts | NVIDIA provider case added; normalizeApiConfiguration hardcodes nvidiaDefaultModelInfo regardless of model ID, causing a display mismatch vs. the handler's openAiModelInfoSaneDefaults fallback for custom models. | | sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/vendors/openai-compatible.ts | Correctly applies addNvidiaBillingOriginHeaderForBaseUrl before constructing the OpenAI-compatible provider, preserving existing user headers. | | sdk/packages/shared/src/llms/requests.ts | SDK-side duplicate of the NVIDIA billing-origin helpers; body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes the unbounded protected-tail problem (CLINE-2185) by adding `trimProtectedTail` to `runBasicCompaction`: when the in-flight turn alone exceeds the compaction budget, oldest completed `tool_use`/`tool_result` pairs are dropped from inside the tail while preserving the typed user prompt, the last assistant message, and any assistant carrying an in-flight (result-less) tool_use. A parallel refactor introduces `reconstructPrefixMessages`, which replaces the direct candidate-map and correctly re-injects compaction summary messages that `sanitizeMessageForBasic` had previously silently dropped from the output. - **Tail trimming** (`trimProtectedTail` + `removeTailCandidatesByPredicate`): aborts any atomic closure that would pull a preserved candidate into the removal set. - **`reconstructPrefixMessages`**: replaces `candidates.map(c => c.message)`; compaction summary messages in `compactable` are now faithfully forwarded. - **Removal of both early bails**: `compactable.length === 0` bail dropped so tail-trim runs on prefix-less turns; `candidates.length === 0` bail superseded by `reconstructPrefixMessages`.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge; the tail-trim path is well-guarded and the new test suite covers all preservation invariants including the compaction-summary retention case flagged in the previous review thread. The previous review thread raised a concern about silently dropping compaction summaries when the second early bail was removed. That concern is addressed by reconstructPrefixMessages, which explicitly re-inserts any isCompactionSummaryMessage entry from compactable that was not a basic candidate, and a dedicated test verifies the round-trip. body:
Greptile Summary

This PR widens `MessageBuilder`'s truncation candidate set beyond `tool_result` blocks to also include top-level `text` and `file` blocks, and ties the aggregate text budget to the model's actual `maxInputTokens` (×3 chars/token) rather than a hardcoded 6 MB cap. `modelInfo.maxInputTokens` is now threaded from the orchestrator through `prepareMessagesForModelRequest` → `prepareProviderMessagesForApi` → `buildForApi`. - `thinking` and `redacted_thinking` blocks are intentionally excluded from candidates because truncating their text would invalidate the API signature; they are also removed from `countMessageTextBytes` so they no longer inflate the overflow calculation. - `tool_use.input` truncation is explicitly deferred to Layer B (CLINE-2192), and `CHARS_PER_TOKEN` is promoted to a public export so both layers share the same chars-per-token constant.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge; both previously-flagged issues (thinking bytes inflating the uncollectable overflow, and thinking-text mutation invalidating the API signature) are cleanly resolved. The two concrete defects called out in prior review rounds are both addressed: thinking blocks are removed from countMessageTextBytes so they no longer make the budget goal unreachable, and thinking blocks are skipped in collectTruncationCandidates so signatures are never invalidated. The orchestrator threading is mechanical and touches only the call sites. Remaining notes are test-coverage quality and a PR-description inaccuracy, neither of which affects runtime behaviour. message-builder.test.ts — the file-block aggregate-budget test exercises the per-block truncation path rather than the aggregate path it describes; worth correcting before CLINE-2192 stacks on top.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/core/src/session/services/message-builder.ts | Core logic changes: countMessageTextBytes no longer counts thinking bytes (fixing the previously-flagged unkillable-bytes issue), collectTruncationCandidates now adds text and file blocks, truncateToTotalTextBudget derives budget from maxInputTokens, and the sort gains a deterministic tiebreaker. | | sdk/packages/core/src/session/services/message-builder.test.ts | Seven new CLINE-2191 test cases added. The file-block aggregate-budget test uses maxToolResultChars (50 K) smaller than the budget (200 K), so truncation is done by the per-block pass rather than the aggregate pass it intends to cover. | | sdk/packages/core/src/runtime/orchestration/session-runtime-orchestrator.ts | Threads modelInfo.maxInputTokens into createRuntimeHooks and createRuntimePrepareTurn → prepareMessagesForModelRequest → prepareProviderMessagesForApi → buildForApi. Change is mechanical and correct. | | sdk/packages/shared/src/llms/tokens.ts | CHARS_PER_TOKEN promoted from module-private to public export; no logic change. | | sdk/packages/shared/src/index.ts | Re-exports CHARS_PER_TOKEN alongside the existing estimateTokens export. | | sdk/packages/shared/src/index.browser.ts | Mirrors the index.ts CHARS_PER_TOKEN re-export for browser consumers. |
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 2 sdk/packages/core/src/session/services/message-builder.test.ts:590-591 The test name promises coverage of the **aggregate** budget path for `file` blocks, but it doesn't actually exercise that path. `MessageBuilder(50_000, undefined, 200_000)` sets `maxToolResultChars = 50_000`, so `transformBlock` → `truncateMiddle` trims the 4 MB file to ≤50 KB during the per-block pass. Because 50 KB < 200 KB budget, `truncateToTotalTextBudget` short-circuits on the early-return guard and never enters the loop. Setting `maxToolResultChars` well above the aggregate budget (e.g., `new MessageBuilder(10_000_000, undefined, 200_000)`) would make the aggregate pass the active code path and give this test its claimed coverage. ```suggestion it("truncates top-level file blocks under the aggregate budget (CLINE-2191)", () => { // maxToolResultChars must exceed the aggregate budget so the per-block // pass does not truncate first; otherwise truncateToTotalTextBudget // short-circuits and the aggregate path is never exercised. const builder = new MessageBuilder(10_000_000, undefined, 200_000); ``` ### Issue 2 of 2 sdk/packages/core/src/session/services/message-builder.ts:893-907 **PR description vs. implementation mismatch on `thinking` blocks** The "Changes" section of the PR description states the candidate set "now collects … `thinking` block text", but the code (and the new tests) correctly show that all `thinking` blocks — signed or unsigned — are **skipped**. The code comment and test `"truncates assistant text but preserves signed thinking blocks"` both confirm the intentional skip. This is purely a description inaccuracy, but it could mislead a reviewer or a developer reading the PR later into believing that `thinking` content is being middle-truncated today. Worth correcting in the PR body so the record is accurate for CLINE-2192 reviewers who will stack on top of this. `````

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR adds a `PostAssistantTurn` hook that fires once per complete assistant turn — after all tool calls have executed and the checkpoint is saved — filling the gap between per-tool `PostToolUse` and end-of-task `TaskComplete`. The hook is observation-only (`cancel` and `contextModification` are ignored), consistent with `Notification` and `TaskComplete`. - **proto/hooks.proto**: New `PostAssistantTurnData` message with `assistantText`, `toolNames`, `turnNumber`, and `taskMetadata`; wired into `HookInput.oneof` at field 19. - **hook-factory.ts / templates.ts**: Interface entry and bash template added, following existing hook conventions. - **task/index.ts**: Hook fires inside the `assistantHasContent` guard, after `pWaitFor(userMessageContentReady)` and `saveCheckpoint()`, with `turnNumber` derived from `Math.ceil(apiConversationHistory.length / 2)`.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The change is a well-scoped additive hook with no impact on existing call paths; the only rough edge is a hardcoded `hooksEnabled: true` that diverges from the rest of the codebase. The hook fires in a guarded block after saveCheckpoint so it cannot disrupt existing turn logic. The turnNumber arithmetic is correct given the state of apiConversationHistory at that point. The hooksEnabled: true hardcode is safe today but inconsistent with every other call-site and creates a latent risk if the outer guard is ever restructured. src/core/task/index.ts — the `hooksEnabled: true` field in the new executeHook call.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/core/task/index.ts | Adds PostAssistantTurn hook invocation after pWaitFor+saveCheckpoint; `hooksEnabled: true` is hardcoded instead of passing the actual setting value. | | src/core/hooks/hook-factory.ts | Adds PostAssistantTurn to the Hooks interface with a PostAssistantTurnData payload; consistent with existing hook type declarations. | | proto/cline/hooks.proto | Adds PostAssistantTurnData message and wires it as field 19 in HookInput's oneof; follows field-number sequencing and message structure of existing hooks. | | src/core/hooks/templates.ts | Adds a bash hook template for PostAssistantTurn with jq-based parsing; template is clear and follows existing conventions. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant API as LLM API participant Task as Task (index.ts) participant Tools as Tool Handlers participant CP as CheckpointManager participant Hook as PostAssistantTurn Hook API->>Task: stream assistant response Task->>Task: accumulate assistantTextOnly + tool blocks Task->>Tools: execute tool calls (presentAssistantMessage) Tools-->>Task: "userMessageContentReady = true" Task->>Task: pWaitFor(userMessageContentReady) Task->>CP: saveCheckpoint() CP-->>Task: done Task->>Hook: "executeHook(PostAssistantTurn, {assistantText, toolNames, turnNumber, taskMetadata})" Hook-->>Task: result (cancel/contextModification ignored) Task->>Task: recursivelyMakeClineRequests(userMessageContent) ```

Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 1 src/core/task/index.ts:3207-3230 Pass the real `hooksEnabled` value rather than hardcoding `true`. All other `executeHook` call-sites pass `getHooksEnabledSafe(...)` directly so the executor can guard itself independently of any outer `if` block. ```suggestion // Fire PostAssistantTurn hook — observation-only, fires after every complete turn if (getHooksEnabledSafe(this.stateManager.getGlobalSettingsKey("hooksEnabled"))) { const toolNames = this.taskState.assistantMessageContent .filter((block) => block.type === "tool_use") .map((block) => (block as { type: "tool_use"; name: string }).name) const turnNumber = Math.ceil(this.messageStateHandler.getApiConversationHistory().length / 2) await executeHook({ hookName: "PostAssistantTurn", hookInput: { postAssistantTurn: { assistantText: assistantTextOnly, toolNames, turnNumber, taskMetadata: { taskId: this.taskId, ulid: this.ulid }, }, }, isCancellable: false, say: this.say.bind(this), messageStateHandler: this.messageStateHandler, taskId: this.taskId, hooksEnabled: getHooksEnabledSafe(this.stateManager.getGlobalSettingsKey("hooksEnabled")), model: getHookModelContext(this.api, this.stateManager), }) } ``` `````

body:
Re: HostProvider not setup unhandled promise rejections

After investigating, these unhandled rejections are pre-existing across the entire hook test suite and are _not caused by this PR._

Root cause: hook-factory.ts calls telemetryService.safeCapture() whenever a taskId is present. The telemetryService export is a Proxy whose property accesses return async functions, meaning safeCapture's try/catch cannot catch the rejection that occurs when TelemetryService.create() calls HostProvider.get() in a test environment where HostProvider is not initialized. This is not guarded anywhere in the hook test setup.

Evidence this is pre-existing:

git log 1f5e2086a..origin/main -- src/services/telemetry/ src/hosts/host-provider.ts → no output (main has not fixed this since our branch point)
git diff origin/main HEAD -- src/services/telemetry/ src/hosts/host-provider.ts → no output (our PR does not touch these files)
taskstart.test.ts, taskcomplete.test.ts, user-prompt-submit.test.ts and every other hook test in src/core/hooks/__tests__/ use the identical new HookFactory() + taskId pattern and are equally affected
Our new post-assistant-turn.test.ts follows the exact same established pattern as those files. Fixing the underlying issue (initializing HostProvider in hook test setup, or guarding the telemetry proxy against uninitialized state) is worthwhile but is a separate concern from this PR.

The one remaining CI failure (JetBrains) requires a companion update in cline/intellij-plugin for the new postAssistantTurn proto variant — that's an internal repo, so a team member will need to apply it.

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes the missing `CLINE_OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` support by wiring the env var through the runtime config path and spreading it into the OpenTelemetry `Resource`, while ensuring Cline's own `service.name` and `service.version` always take precedence. The build-time equivalent (`OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`) is also threaded through the esbuild define map and `BUILD_CONSTANTS` for consistency. - `resourceAttributes` field added to `OpenTelemetryClientConfig`; parsed in both `getOtelConfig()` (build-time) and `getRuntimeOtelConfig()` (runtime) using the existing `parseKeyPairsIntoRecord` helper. - `createOpenTelemetryResource()` extracted from the `OpenTelemetryClientProvider` constructor to make the attribute-merging logic independently testable, with a unit test that confirms user-supplied `service.name` is overridden by Cline's identity. - The debug-mode separator log line is now always emitted at the end of the initialization block rather than being conditionally gated on `otlpHeaders` being present.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge — the change is additive, the attribute-override ordering is correct, and the existing OTEL infrastructure is unchanged. The functional logic is sound: user attributes are spread first, then Cline's service identity is unconditionally written over them, so the authoritative identity cannot be accidentally replaced. Two minor gaps exist: the new unit test in `otel-config.test.ts` will silently produce a null config (and a failing assertion) if the test runner sets `IS_TEST=true` before the module loads, and `remoteConfigToOtelConfig` is the only place that maps config fields without an equivalent `resourceAttributes` entry, which could confuse future maintainers. `src/shared/services/config/__tests__/otel-config.test.ts` for the test-environment guard concern, and `src/shared/services/config/otel-config.ts` for the undocumented omission in `remoteConfigToOtelConfig`.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | esbuild.mjs | Adds `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` injection to the esbuild define map, consistent with the existing OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS pattern. | | src/shared/constants.ts | Adds `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` to `BUILD_CONSTANTS`, following the existing pattern for build-time OTEL env vars. | | src/shared/services/config/otel-config.ts | Adds `resourceAttributes` to the config interface and wires parsing in both build-time and runtime paths; `remoteConfigToOtelConfig` is not updated, likely intentional since `RemoteConfigFields` does not carry a resource attributes field. | | src/services/telemetry/providers/opentelemetry/OpenTelemetryClientProvider.ts | Extracts `createOpenTelemetryResource()` for testability; correctly spreads user attributes first then overrides with Cline's authoritative `service.name`/`service.version`. Debug separator moved to always fire in debug mode. | | src/shared/services/config/__tests__/otel-config.test.ts | New test covers parsing of `CLINE_OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` into the runtime config, but relies on `IS_TEST` not being set in the unit test runner for `isOpenTelemetryConfigValid` to return a non-null result. | | src/services/telemetry/providers/opentelemetry/__tests__/OpenTelemetryClientProvider.test.ts | Tests that user-configured `service.name` is overridden by Cline's identity; spread-of-undefined behaviour is safe in ES2018+ for the undefined `resourceAttributes` case. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[Build time\nOTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES] -->|esbuild inject| B[BUILD_CONSTANTS\n.OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES] B -->|getOtelConfig| C[OpenTelemetryClientConfig\n.resourceAttributes] D[Runtime env var\nCLINE_OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES] -->|getRuntimeOtelConfig| C E[VS Code remote settings\nRemoteConfigFields] -->|remoteConfigToOtelConfig| F[OpenTelemetryClientConfig\nno resourceAttributes mapping] C -->|createOpenTelemetryResource| G["Resource {\n ...user attrs,\n service.name: 'cline',\n service.version: ExtensionRegistryInfo.version\n}"] G --> H[MeterProvider] G --> I[LoggerProvider] ```

Comments Outside Diff (1)

 1. `src/shared/services/config/otel-config.ts`, line 105-127 ([link](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/3b8bbc248d389b8f5d555c19168b34d4decabf21/src/shared/services/config/otel-config.ts#L105-L127)) **`remoteConfigToOtelConfig` does not forward `resourceAttributes`** Every other `OpenTelemetryClientConfig` field produced by `getOtelConfig` and `getRuntimeOtelConfig` has a corresponding mapping in `remoteConfigToOtelConfig`. `resourceAttributes` is the only field that is silently absent. If `RemoteConfigFields` gains a resource-attributes setting in the future, or if a caller merges remote config with env-var config and expects attributes to pass through, they will be dropped without warning. Greptile Summary

This PR implements Layer B, the final hard byte-budget guarantee for provider requests. After Layer A's heuristic truncation, a new `enforceHardByteBudget` pass in `MessageBuilder` enforces the `maxInputTokens * 3` byte ceiling via aggressive string-leaf middle-truncation and deterministic block-removal fallback. The orchestrator's retry loop measures the full serialized request (including system prompt, tools, and options overhead) and adjusts the message budget across up to 3 attempts. - **`message-builder.ts`**: Adds `enforceHardByteBudget` with two passes — string-leaf truncation (priority-ordered, EMERGENCY_FLOOR_BYTES floor) followed by block-removal fallback; introduces `pruneEmptyTextContent` to strip empty strings and empty arrays before returning, preventing provider 400s; `getDropPriority` now uses `findLatestTypedUserMessageIndex` so the typed prompt is truly last-resort (priority 4). - **`session-runtime-orchestrator.ts`**: Wraps `messageBuilder.buildForApi` in `buildApiMessagesForRequestBudget`, a bounded retry loop that measures the actual serialized `AgentModelRequest` and tightens overhead estimates between attempts; buffers emergency-truncation notices and telemetry so only the final successful attempt emits user-visible signals. - **`core-events.ts` / tests**: Adds `EMERGENCY_TRUNCATION` and `REQUEST_OVERHEAD_EXCEEDS_BUDGET` constants with typed helpers, opt-out tests, and event catalog entry in `opentelemetry-events.mdx`.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge; the three previously-flagged correctness gaps (typed-prompt priority ordering, empty-string content surviving prune, stale buffer emission) are all resolved and directly tested. All prior blocking findings on message-builder.ts and the orchestrator have been addressed: the typed prompt now correctly receives the highest drop-protection priority via findLatestTypedUserMessageIndex, pruneEmptyTextContent removes zeroed strings and empty text blocks before returning, and buffered notice/telemetry are reset at the top of each retry loop iteration so a clean second attempt does not re-emit stale truncation signals. The two remaining observations are both conservative — a slight overhead overcount in the retry loop and a double-notice edge case when non-message payload alone exceeds the budget — neither of which can cause an under-budgeted request or data loss. session-runtime-orchestrator.ts: the overhead recalculation in the retry loop mixes AgentMessage (with id/createdAt) for the full-request count and MessageWithMetadata for the message-only count, leading to slightly inflated overhead estimates in retries.

For the edge case where the system prompt or tools alone blow the budget this double-notice is confusing — the first notice implies partial success while the second correctly signals failure. Consider suppressing `flushBufferedEmergencyTruncation` when `requestBytes > maxRequestBytes`, since the overhead-exceeds-budget notice already communicates the degraded state. `````

Greptile Summary

This PR guards against CLI process crashes caused by unhandled promise rejections from detached hub event handler side paths. When the hub WebSocket disconnects while async follow-up work (e.g. `capability.respond`, `approval.respond`, `capability.progress`) is still in-flight, the rejected promise previously escaped to Node's unhandled-rejection handler and exited the process. - Attaches `.catch()` at the `void this.handleCapabilityRequest(event)` and `void this.handleApprovalRequested(event)` call sites, routing failures to a new `captureDetachedHubEventError` method. - Adds `captureDetachedHubEventError`, a try/catch-guarded helper that calls `captureSdkError` at warn severity so telemetry itself cannot become a secondary unhandled rejection. - Wraps the `capability.progress` fire-and-forget `command()` call in the same catch path, closing one more detached boundary inside `handleCapabilityRequest`.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge — the change is limited to attaching error boundaries around existing fire-and-forget hub event dispatch calls and does not alter any command semantics or session lifecycle. The fix is targeted and correct: it closes the unhandled-rejection escape paths that caused the CLI to exit after a WebSocket disconnect. The one pre-existing subtlety is that a transport error on the success capability.respond path lands in the same catch block as a handler failure, so telemetry will log it under the same operation name as a genuine handler error. The single changed file hub-runtime-host.ts is well-contained. The handleCapabilityRequest catch block (lines 1813-1828) is worth a second look for the transport-vs-handler error conflation noted above.

body:
The CLI did not likely crash because of the `ls` or `grep` command itself. The more likely sequence is:

1. The CLI was using the local hub websocket to coordinate runtime work.
2. A hub event came in that required the CLI side to do follow-up async work, for example responding to a capability or approval request.
3. Around the same time, the hub websocket disconnected or the run was aborted.
4. That follow-up async work then tried to send a response over a socket that was already closed.
5. Because that work was launched from an event callback and intentionally not awaited, the rejection could escape as an unhandled promise rejection.
6. The CLI has a fatal process handler for unhandled rejections, so it logged the websocket/run-abort error and exited back to the shell.

So from the user’s perspective it looks like “the CLI randomly closed after an `ls` and `grep`,” but the actual issue is a race in hub event cleanup: a best-effort response path can fail after the transport is gone, and that failure was being treated like a process-fatal bug.

This PR keeps the behavior narrow. It does not change hub reconnect behavior or command execution. It just makes those detached hub event side paths explicitly handled and records them as warn-level telemetry with session/event context, so a dropped websocket can be diagnosed without taking down the CLI.

This PR fixes a breaking migration path for legacy Cline users whose stored provider ID was `openai` (meaning OpenAI-Compatible in the old extension). The new SDK treated `openai` as an unknown provider, causing startup failures. The fix canonicalizes `openai-compatible` as the built-in SDK provider for OpenAI-Compatible endpoints, keeps `openai` only as a legacy alias, and routes the CLI onboarding/model-selector to a free-text model ID input rather than a catalog dropdown for this provider. - Adds `BUILT_IN_PROVIDER.OPENAI_COMPATIBLE = \"openai-compatible\"` and re-points the `openai` alias from `openai-native` to `openai-compatible`, with corresponding migration code that rewrites stored settings, preserves all legacy fields (API key, base URL, headers, Azure metadata), and writes synthetic model metadata (128k context, streaming/tools/images capabilities) for the migrated model. - Adds a `ModelIdInputContent` dialog component and `usesModelIdInput` routing helper in the CLI so that selecting the OpenAI-Compatible provider presents a plain text model-ID field instead of a finite catalog dropdown. - Removes the previous URL-sniffing heuristic that tried to redirect `api.openai.com` legacy users to a different provider; all legacy `openai` users now land on `openai-compatible` regardless of base URL.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — migration logic is well-scoped, all changed paths are covered by tests, and no regressions were found in native-OpenAI or other provider flows. The migration correctly uses the legacy "openai" key to look up secrets/baseUrl while writing settings under the canonical "openai-compatible" ID. body:
Context-window note for reviewers:

This PR intentionally gives OpenAI Compatible fallback model metadata a 128k context window for now.

The ideal follow-up is to expose model metadata configuration again for OpenAI Compatible, especially context window / max input tokens. Legacy extension users could configure that through the OpenAI Compatible model configuration section, and custom endpoints vary a lot here.

I chose 128k as the fallback because it matches the legacy extension's OpenAI Compatible sane default and avoids overestimating context for common endpoints. Without this, the SDK had no model metadata for OpenAI Compatible defaults, which led to inconsistent behavior: some paths treated context as unknown, automatic compaction fell back to 200k, and manual CLI compaction fell back to 64k.

So this is meant as a conservative migration-safe default, not as the long-term replacement for user-configurable context metadata.

```ts
return {
  id: modelId,

  maxTokens: model?.maxTokens,
  contextWindow: model?.contextWindow,
  maxInputTokens: model?.maxInputTokens,
  capabilities: capabilities.size > 0 ? [...capabilities] : undefined,
```

This PR adds a persisted `runCommandsTimeoutMs` global setting that controls the native `run_commands` shell timeout in the SDK CLI. The schema defaults and validates the value (positive integer, fallback to 30 000 ms), threads it into both the bash tool's per-command `withTimeout` guard and the underlying executor's spawn-level timeout, and exposes a cycling preset toggle in the interactive config panel. - **Global settings** (`global-settings.ts`): new `runCommandsTimeoutMs` field with `.catch(30000).default(30000)` so invalid or missing values always resolve safely. - **Runtime builder** (`runtime-builder.ts`): reads from global settings at tool-build time and passes the resolved value to both `bashTimeoutMs` (inner per-command timeout) and `executorOptions.bash.timeoutMs` (executor spawn-level timeout); the tool wrapper's `timeoutMs` is `2 × bashTimeoutMs` by pre-existing design. - **CLI UI** (`config-view.tsx`, `use-config-panel.tsx`, `run-interactive.ts`): new cycling preset toggle (30 s → 60 s → 120 s → 300 s), persists on change via `writeGlobalSettings`, and restarts the session so the new timeout takes effect immediately.

Greptile Summary

This PR adds per-command timeout support to the SDK `run_commands` native tool path, addressing schema validation failures triggered by models (e.g. GPT-5.5) that emit `{ "commands": [...], "timeout": 120000 }`. Rather than accepting a top-level timeout, the PR introduces per-command `timeout` on each structured command entry, detects the top-level pattern and rejects it with a self-correcting error, and raises the outer tool `timeoutMs` to `MAX_RUN_COMMANDS_TIMEOUT_MS` to avoid the tool runner cutting off legitimate per-command overrides. - `StructuredCommandInputSchema` gains `timeout: OptionalRunCommandsTimeoutSchema` and `.catchall(z.any())`, and `normalizeValidatedRunCommandsInputWithTimeouts` resolves per-command timeouts before dispatch. - `withTimeout` is rewritten to clear its timer on settlement (fixing a timer-leak) and wraps rejections with the new `TimeoutError` brand so callers can distinguish timeout failures. - `assertNoTopLevelRunCommandsTimeout` guards both execute functions with a descriptive error guiding models to the per-command pattern; `config-view.tsx` gains smarter cycling logic for custom (non-preset) timeout values.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge; the per-command timeout dispatch is correct end-to-end and the guard against top-level timeout provides a clear self-correcting error. All changed code paths are covered by focused tests. The withTimeout rewrite correctly clears its timer on settlement, eliminating the previous leak. Per-command timeout resolution, the fallback to configured default, and the outer tool ceiling are all verified. The two remaining findings are surface-level — a dead union variant and a silent field-drop that predates this PR — neither affects the timeout-dispatch behaviour this PR introduces. schemas.ts (dead z.array(z.string()) variant) and helpers.ts (normalizeStructuredCommandInput drops cwd silently despite catchall on the schema) are worth a second look, but neither blocks the feature.

union ordering leaves z.array(z.string()) in StructuredCommandsInputUnionSchema unreachable. | | sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/helpers.ts | Adds NormalizedRunCommand, TimeoutError, assertNoTopLevelRunCommandsTimeout, and normalizeValidatedRunCommandsInputWithTimeouts; withTimeout rewrite correctly clears its timer on settlement. normalizeStructuredCommandInput silently drops extra fields (including cwd) while the schema now advertises accepting them via catchall. | | sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/definitions.ts | createBashTool and createWindowsShellTool updated to use per-command timeout dispatch via normalizeValidatedRunCommandsInputWithTimeouts; outer timeoutMs raised to MAX_RUN_COMMANDS_TIMEOUT_MS; both callers correctly assert no top-level timeout before validation. | | sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/executors/bash.ts | BashExecutor signature extended with optional timeoutOverrideMs; spawnAndCollect Model->>ToolExecute: "{ commands: [{command, timeout}] }" ToolExecute->>Assert: check for top-level timeout Assert-->>ToolExecute: ok (no top-level timeout) ToolExecute->>ValidateWithZod: RunCommandsInputUnionSchema ValidateWithZod-->>ToolExecute: validated input ToolExecute->>Normalize: (validated, defaultTimeoutMs) Normalize-->>ToolExecute: "[{command, timeoutMs}]" loop Per command (concurrent) ToolExecute->>withTimeout: executor(...), timeoutMs withTimeout->>Executor: command, cwd, context, timeoutMs Executor-->>withTimeout: result / TimeoutError withTimeout-->>ToolExecute: result / TimeoutError end ToolExecute-->>Model: ToolOperationResult[] Note over Model,Assert: Top-level timeout path Model->>ToolExecute: "{ commands: [...], timeout: 120000 }" ToolExecute->>Assert: check Assert-->>ToolExecute: throws TOP_LEVEL_TIMEOUT_ERROR ToolExecute-->>Model: error with self-correcting message ```

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes Gemini/Vertex (and AIhubmix) tool-result serialization by building a per-request `tool_id → tool_name` lookup map across the entire message list, so `functionResponse.name` is always the original function declaration name rather than the opaque call ID. - **`gemini-format.ts`**: Adds `rememberGeminiToolUse` / `getGeminiFunctionResponseName` helpers and a new `convertAnthropicMessagesToGemini` entry-point that threads a shared `GeminiToolNameById` map through all messages; also begins setting `functionCall.id` and `functionResponse.id` for proper Gemini multi-turn correlation. - **`gemini.ts` / `aihubmix.ts`**: Switch from a per-message `.map(convertAnthropicMessageToGemini)` call to the new batch function so the shared map is populated before any `tool_result` lookup. - **`gemini-format.test.ts`**: New unit tests covering the happy path (same `tool_use_id`) and the `call_id` metadata fallback path.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The change is safe to merge — it is a targeted serialization fix with no side-effects on non-Gemini providers and is backed by a live smoke test against Vertex. The logic is straightforward: a shared map is built in a single forward pass over the message list, ensuring every tool_result lookup finds its corresponding name before the map entry is needed. Both providers that use the Gemini format have been updated consistently, and the new unit tests verify the two key resolution paths. src/core/api/transform/gemini-format.ts deserves a second look for the unreachable error guard and the unbraced switch-case declaration, both of which are already flagged in prior review threads.

Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 2 sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/routing/provider-option-rules.ts:275-295 **`budgetTokens` silently suppressed for Gemini 3 models** The `applies` guard includes `typeof input.request.reasoning?.budgetTokens === "number"` as a trigger, but `buildGeminiThinkingConfig` returns `undefined` for any Gemini 3 model that has only `budgetTokens` set (no `effort`). Since `suppresses: { genericThinking: true, genericEffort: true }` is applied at rule-match time, a caller that sets `{ budgetTokens: 8192 }` against `gemini-3-flash-preview` will have both the Gemini thinking config and the generic thinking suppressed — the model is called with no thinking config at all, even though thinking was requested. Consider either excluding `budgetTokens` from the `applies` condition for Gemini 3 paths or converting `budgetTokens` to the nearest `thinkingLevel` bucket. ### Issue 2 of 2 sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/model-facts.ts:121-131 **Broad `includes` fallback could match model metadata incidentally** The final fallback `|| descriptor.includes("gemini-flash")` in `isGeminiFlashModel` operates on the concatenated descriptor that includes `context.model.name` and `context.model.metadata?.family`. A model whose family is `"gemini-flash"` but whose actual model ID is something else would be mis-classified as a Flash model, triggering `"minimal"` as the disabled thinking level instead of `"low"`. Using the same anchored regex for the fallback — or at minimum restricting `includes` to `modelId` only — would be safer. `````

I re-tested this branch against the real providers after the routing changes.

The extra branching in `provider-option-rules.ts` is intentional because Gemini thinking is not one uniform wire format:

- Direct Gemini/Gemini provider needs `providerOptions.google.thinkingConfig`.
- Vertex Gemini needs `providerOptions.vertex.thinkingConfig`.
- Gemini 2.5 models use `thinkingBudget`.
- Gemini 3 models use `thinkingLevel`.
- Disabled thinking is model-specific:
  - Gemini 2.5 Flash: `thinkingBudget: 0`
  - Gemini 2.5 Pro: `thinkingBudget: 128`
  - Gemini 3 Flash: `thinkingLevel: "minimal"`
- `includeThoughts: true` is only used when we request effort/budget-visible thoughts.
- `includeThoughts: false` suppresses visible thoughts but still allows thought signatures to be preserved for tool-use continuation.
- `xhigh` is normalized to `high` before reaching this layer.

body:
Context on the required `test` gate, since this is easy to miss when reviewing the workflow diff.

Before this PR, the `test` check meant the VS Code test matrix actually ran and passed. Branch protection requires the `test` status, so that was meaningful.

With path filtering, the expensive VS Code matrix needs to become conditional:

```yaml
if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.vscode == 'true'
```

The subtle part is that GitHub treats a conditionally skipped job as a successful check, including for required checks. So if the real matrix job keeps the required name `test`, then a docs-only, SDK-only, or testing-platform-only PR can satisfy branch protection because `test` was skipped successfully.

That is fine for unrelated changes, but it is risky for testing-platform-only changes:

```text
detect-changes.testing_platform == true
detect-changes.vscode == false

test-platform-integration runs
test is skipped
branch protection still sees test as passing
```

If `test-platform-integration` fails but is not itself required by the ruleset, branch protection may not block the merge even though the selected root CI job failed.

The fix is to separate the expensive test runner from the required check name:

```text
vscode-test:
  runs the actual VS Code matrix when vscode paths changed

test:
  tiny aggregate gate that always exists and keeps the required status name
```

The aggregate `test` job now means:

```text
if no root test paths changed:
  pass

if vscode paths changed:
  require vscode-test to pass

if testing platform paths changed:
  require test-platform-integration to pass
```

That preserves the existing branch protection rule, keeps the CI savings, and makes the required `test` check mean what it looks like it means: the correct subset of root CI passed.

I also intentionally kept `scripts/**` in the testing-platform filter. The testing platform job depends on root scripts transitively for proto generation, standalone packaging, host bridge mocks, test server startup, and orchestration. Enumerating those scripts exactly would be brittle in a fast-moving codebase, and missing one would silently skip the integration job again.

Greptile Summary

This PR implements the pure compaction budget projection engine behind the `BudgetProjectionOptions`/`BudgetProjectionResult` contract, adding `buildBudgetProjection` and `findLatestTypedUserMessageIndex` to the `budget-projection` package. The algorithm clones provider-shaped messages, removes unsafe blocks outside the live tail, prunes resulting empty messages, then applies a text-truncation pass and an oldest-first message-drop loop while protecting tool-use/tool-result closure boundaries and the latest typed user turn. - The three-phase reduction pipeline (unsafe-block drop → text truncation → whole-message drop) is logically sound and the tool-pair closure BFS correctly keeps paired messages atomic. - The text-truncation pass in both `truncateToolResultContent` and `truncateMessageText` returns subsequent content blocks **at full size** once `remaining` reaches zero, rather than zeroing them out — making the truncation pass ineffective for multi-block content and forcing the drop loop to compensate. - `pruneEmptyMessages` records `reason: "over_budget"` for messages that became empty solely because all their unsafe blocks were removed, which misidentifies the cause for action consumers.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — this is a pure computation module with no provider side-effects; the drop loop correctly enforces the budget even when the truncation pass falls short. The three-phase pipeline is algorithmically correct end-to-end: the outer estimatedTokens recheck after every truncation or drop ensures convergence regardless of how effective the truncation pass was for any individual message. The multi-block truncation shortfall and the misleading reason for emptied messages are quality issues that do not produce incorrect projection results. sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/context/budget-projection/project.ts — the truncation helpers truncateToolResultContent and truncateMessageText.

Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 4 sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/context/budget-projection/project.ts:235-251 When `remaining` drops to zero or goes negative after the first block is processed, every subsequent block in the array is returned **at its original, un-truncated size**. For a tool_result whose content is `[{type:"text", 10 000 chars}, {type:"text", 10 000 chars}]` and `maxChars = 100`, the output is ~10 100 chars — two orders of magnitude over budget. Mirroring the fix in `truncateToolResultContent`, short-circuit to empty/zero content instead of silently keeping the original. ```suggestion let remaining = maxChars; return { ...message, content: message.content.map((block) => { if (block.type === "text") { if (remaining <= 0) return { ...block, text: "" }; const text = truncateText(block.text, remaining); remaining -= text.length; return { ...block, text }; } if (block.type === "file") { if (remaining <= 0) return { ...block, content: "" }; const content = truncateText(block.content, remaining); remaining -= content.length; return { ...block, content }; } if (block.type === "thinking") { if (remaining <= 0) return { ...block, thinking: "" }; const thinking = truncateText(block.thinking, remaining); remaining -= thinking.length; return { ...block, thinking }; } if (block.type === "tool_result") { if (remaining <= 0) return block; const content = truncateToolResultContent(block.content, remaining); remaining -= safeJsonSize(content); return { ...block, content }; } return block; }), }; ``` ### Issue 3 of 4 sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/context/budget-projection/project.ts:160-167 A message that had all its blocks removed by `dropUnsafeBlocks` (because every block was an image or `redacted_thinking`) gets a `dropped_message` action with `reason: "over_budget"`. Greptile Summary

This PR hardens the shared Playwright/Electron e2e teardown path that was causing 60-second worker timeout flakes on CI. Instead of calling `app.close()` and `page.close()` bare, the fixture now uses bounded helpers (`closeAppForTeardown`, `closePageForTeardown`) that emit diagnostics on overage and SIGKILL the Electron process when `app.close()` exceeds 10 seconds. - **`withTimeout` + force-kill loop** — a generic race-wrapper drives both the page and app close paths; when the app close times out, window titles are collected for diagnostics, SIGKILL is sent, and a 2-second exit poll runs before cleanup tasks proceed. - **Spec cleanup** — explicit `page.close()` calls removed from `chat.test.ts` and `diff.test.ts`; the shared `page` fixture now owns the full lifecycle via `closePageForTeardown`. - **Minor hygiene** — dead `wrappedOpenVSCode` scaffolding removed; dynamic `require(\"node:fs\")` replaced with a static import.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — all changes are confined to test infrastructure and do not touch any product code. The teardown helpers are well-structured: withTimeout correctly suppresses orphaned rejections via void promise.catch(), the fixture dependency order (page before app) ensures the right teardown sequence, and the SIGKILL path is gated behind a process.killed/exitCode guard before attempting. No existing tests are broken and no product paths are touched. No files require special attention. Both comments are non-blocking suggestions on helpers.ts.

Important Files Changed

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant PF as page fixture participant AF as app fixture participant H as E2ETestHelper participant EL as Electron/VS Code PF->>H: closePageForTeardown(page) H->>EL: page.close() [10s timeout] alt closes in time EL-->>H: resolved H-->>PF: done else times out or errors H->>H: log warning H-->>PF: done (continue) end AF->>H: closeAppForTeardown(app) H->>EL: app.close() [10s timeout] alt closes in time EL-->>H: resolved H-->>AF: return else times out or errors H->>EL: getWindowDiagnostics [1s/window] H->>H: log diagnostics H->>EL: process.kill(SIGKILL) EL-->>H: exit event [2s poll] H-->>AF: return end AF->>AF: "rmForRetries(userDataDir, extensionsDir, cline-e2e-*)" ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 2 src/test/e2e/utils/helpers.ts:194-197 When `page.close()` throws an error (e.g., a Playwright CDP connection error), the `.catch` handler returns `{ timedOut: false }`, so `result.timedOut` is `false` and the function exits silently. The error is logged, but the code path is semantically "did not time out → nothing more to do," which can mask a failing close. Contrast with `closeAppForTeardown` where a thrown error is mapped to `{ timedOut: true }` and triggers the force-kill path. If the page truly cannot be closed, the caller might benefit from knowing that the close failed (vs. merely being slow) so the app teardown can be more aggressive from the start. ```suggestion const result = await E2ETestHelper.withTimeout(page.close(), E2ETestHelper.TEARDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS).catch((error) => { console.warn(`[e2e teardown] page.close() failed: ${error}`) return { timedOut: true as const } }) ``` ### Issue 2 of 2 src/test/e2e/utils/helpers.ts:248-254 **SIGTERM block is only reachable on SIGKILL exception** The SIGTERM block is only reached when `process.kill("SIGKILL")` throws (i.e., the OS rejects the call, not when it returns `false`). A reader unfamiliar with the flow might expect SIGTERM to be a general fallback for "SIGKILL didn't work." A brief inline comment — e.g., `// Only reached if SIGKILL threw (process may still be alive); attempt a softer termination` — would make the intent clear without changing any behavior. `````

Updated this PR after the Harbor repro/Claude review.

Key change: the projection engine no longer treats the latest typed user prompt as the start of a protected suffix. It now protects:

```text
first typed prompt: no whole-message drop, still truncatable
latest typed prompt: pinned individually
unresolved tool_use tail: protected
completed tool_use/tool_result pairs: fair game, dropped atomically
```

This is what lets completed multi-MB tool results after the latest prompt actually leave the projected payload.

Greptile Summary

Greptile Summary

This automated security fix upgrades 19 package versions (across 15 npm packages) to remediate 49 CVEs including critical RCE in `protobufjs`, command injection in `basic-ftp`, XML injection in `@xmldom/xmldom`, and prototype pollution in `zod`. The dependency-only PR touches `package.json` and `package-lock.json` with no application logic changes. - **protobufjs** overridden from `7.5.5` → `7.5.6`; `basic-ftp`, `@xmldom/xmldom`, `path-to-regexp`, `hono`, `@hono/node-server`, `fast-uri`, `follow-redirects`, `fast-xml-parser`, `fast-xml-builder`, `ip-address`, and `brace-expansion` advanced via lockfile or parent-bump. - **`zod` major-bumped from `^3.24.2` to `^4.4.0`** — a new major with several breaking API changes; the existing codebase uses single-argument `z.record(z.string())` in `src/services/mcp/schemas.ts` (7 call sites), which is removed in Zod v4 and will throw at runtime. - **`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` bumped from `^1.25.1` to `^1.26.0`** to allow patched `hono` and `@hono/node-server` resolutions.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The lockfile-only and minor version bumps are safe; the zod major version jump introduces a runtime-breaking API removal that was not addressed in application code before merging. The z.record() single-argument removal in Zod v4 directly breaks MCP settings parsing at every call site in src/services/mcp/schemas.ts. This path runs whenever the extension reads MCP server configuration, making it a regression that would affect all users on first launch after the upgrade. src/services/mcp/schemas.ts needs all z.record(z.string()) and z.record(ServerConfigSchema) single-argument calls updated to two-argument form before this PR is safe to merge.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | package.json | Upgrades 5 direct/overrides entries (protobufjs, uuid, zod, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, brace-expansion override) to pull in security fixes across 15 transitive packages; the zod major-version bump (v3→v4) is not accompanied by a migration of the codebase's z.record() single-argument usages, which will fail at runtime. | | package-lock.json | Large lockfile churn reflecting transitive resolution of 19 package version advances; zod resolves to a single root instance at 4.4.3 (marked peer), chromium-bidi retains its own nested zod@3.23.8 as expected. |
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 2 package.json:584 **Zod v3→v4 major bump breaks `z.record()` calls at runtime** Zod v4 dropped the single-argument `z.record(valueSchema)` form; it now requires two arguments: `z.record(keySchema, valueSchema)`. `src/services/mcp/schemas.ts` calls `z.record(z.string())` six times (lines 26, 29, 48, 52, 70, 74) and `z.record(ServerConfigSchema)` once (line 96) — all in the single-argument form that no longer exists. Every call to `McpSettingsSchema.parse()` or any schema containing `ServerConfigSchema` will throw at runtime until those call sites are updated to `z.record(z.string(), z.string())` / `z.record(z.string(), ServerConfigSchema)`. ### Issue 2 of 2 package.json:584 **`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` lists `zod` in both `dependencies` and `peerDependencies`** `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.26.0` has a known issue where it declares `zod` in both `dependencies` and `peerDependencies`, which can cause npm to install a nested `node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/node_modules/zod` alongside the root-level `zod@4.4.3`. When that happens TypeScript sees two distinct `$ZodType` class declarations and treats them as nominally incompatible — schemas built with the root `zod` fail the `AnySchema` constraint expected by SDK APIs such as `registerTool`. The lockfile currently resolves to a single `node_modules/zod` instance (marked `"peer": true`), but the behaviour is environment-dependent and may differ under pnpm or bun. `````

body:
This fixes the Bedrock model picker by treating `baseUrl` as optional for providers that do not use an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

Before this change, Bedrock had a bundled model manifest, but `getProviderConfig("bedrock")` discarded it because the manifest had no `baseUrl`. That meant the picker lost Bedrock’s `knownModels` and only showed manual model ID entry. Bedrock should not require a user-entered base URL for the bundled catalog to load.

The updated flow allows built-in provider defaults to be returned without a `baseUrl`, so Bedrock keeps its bundled model catalog while still leaving `baseUrl` undefined at runtime unless the user explicitly configures an endpoint.

I also tightened the AWS setup path:
- region/profile handling is shared between onboarding and provider config
- profile changes update auto-filled regions without overwriting manually edited regions
- IAM/default credential-chain auth now passes the resolved region into `fromNodeProviderChain`

Validated with unit tests for provider defaults, Bedrock credentials, provider readiness, and CLI AWS config value behavior.
