Greptile Summary

This PR makes `HubRuntimeHost.abort()` and the server-side `handleRunAbort` handler resilient to `Error`-typed abort reasons and rejected runtime abort hooks, preventing hub daemon poisoning after interactive CLI aborts. - **`hub-runtime-host.ts`**: Extracts the existing `abortReasonMessage` fallback into a new `messageFromUnknown` helper that returns `string | undefined`, allowing `Error` instances (and objects with a `message` field) to be serialized before being sent to the daemon via `run.abort`. - **`run-handlers.ts`**: Wraps `ctx.sessionHost.abort()` in a try/catch so a rejected promise is logged as `run.abort_failed` (warn) rather than escaping the command handler; `cancelPendingCapabilityRequests` is moved into `finally` to guarantee cleanup whether or not the abort hook throws.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the fix is narrow and both changed code paths are covered by new unit tests. The change is well-scoped: `messageFromUnknown` cleanly replaces an inline type-guard in `abort()`, and the try/catch/finally in `handleRunAbort` correctly preserves the pre-existing sequential behaviour for the success path while adding resilience on the failure path. No telemetry, auth, or schema boundaries are touched. Tests cover the two new branches directly. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/core/src/hub/runtime-host/hub-runtime-host.ts | Refactors abort reason serialization: splits `abortReasonMessage` into `messageFromUnknown` (returns `string | undefined`) and a thin fallback wrapper, then uses `messageFromUnknown` in `abort()` so `Error` objects are properly serialized before transport. | | sdk/packages/core/src/hub/server/handlers/run-handlers.ts | Wraps `sessionHost.abort()` in try/catch/finally so abort-hook rejections are caught and logged as `run.abort_failed`, capability-request cleanup always runs, and the command always returns `{ applied: true }`. | | sdk/packages/core/src/hub/runtime-host/hub-runtime-host.test.ts | Adds a test asserting that an `Error`-typed abort reason is serialized to a plain string before the `run.abort` command is dispatched. | | sdk/packages/core/src/hub/server/handlers/run-handlers.test.ts | Adds a test verifying that a rejected `abort` hook still produces `{ ok: true, payload: { applied: true } }` from `handleRunAbort`. |

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a regression where Bedrock Converse image data could not be replayed from chat history because `JSON.stringify`/`JSON.parse` round-trips transform `Uint8Array` and `Buffer` into plain objects (`{\"0\":82,\"1\":73,...}` or `{\"type\":\"Buffer\",\"data\":[...]}`). The fix extracts a new `normalizeImageData` helper that recognizes all four serialized forms and returns a proper `Uint8Array`. - **`bedrock.ts`**: Adds `normalizeImageData` private method handling base64 strings, `Uint8Array`/`ArrayBuffer` instances, plain number arrays, Buffer JSON, and numeric-key JSON objects; `ContentItem.source.data` widened to `unknown`. - **`bedrock.test.ts`**: Two new regression tests verify round-tripped `Uint8Array` (numeric-key object) and `Buffer` JSON are correctly restored before sending to Bedrock."

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge; the core fix is correct and the two new code paths are well-tested for the regression scenario. The normalization logic is sound for all realistic history formats. Two minor gaps exist: the Buffer JSON branch doesn't validate that array elements are integers before casting (unlike the parallel Array branch), and the numeric-key path accepts the empty-string key because Number("") === 0. Neither is reachable through normal Bedrock history data, so they carry low practical risk. Both changed files are straightforward; bedrock.ts (the normalizeImageData method) is where the validation gaps live.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/core/api/providers/bedrock.ts | Extracts image-byte normalization into a new `normalizeImageData` private method handling base64 strings, Uint8Array, ArrayBuffer, plain number arrays, Buffer JSON, and numeric-key JSON objects; ContentItem.source.data widened to unknown. Two minor validation gaps in the Buffer JSON and numeric-key object branches. | | src/core/api/providers/__tests__/bedrock.test.ts | Adds two regression tests covering the two new JSON-serialized image-data formats (numeric-key object and Buffer JSON). The error/throw path and pre-existing base64/Uint8Array/ArrayBuffer paths are not covered by new cases, but those are unchanged codepaths. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[processImageContent] --> B[normalizeImageData] B --> C{typeof data} C -->|string| D["strip data-URI prefix\nBuffer.from(base64)"] C -->|object| E{instanceof check} E -->|Uint8Array| F[new Uint8Array copy] E -->|ArrayBuffer| G[new Uint8Array wrap] E -->|Array| H{all integers?} H -->|yes| I[Uint8Array.from array] H -->|no| Z[throw Unsupported] E -->|plain object| J{type === 'Buffer'?} J -->|yes| K[Uint8Array.from data array] J -->|no| L{numeric-key contiguous?} L -->|yes| M[Uint8Array.from sorted values] L -->|no| Z D --> N[return Uint8Array] F --> N G --> N I --> N K --> N M --> N ```

Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 2 src/core/api/providers/bedrock.ts:1123-1127 The Buffer JSON branch casts `maybeBufferJson.data` directly to `number[]` without validating element types. `Uint8Array.from(["a", "b"] as unknown as number[])` produces `[0, 0]` — silently corrupt image data. The plain-array path at line 1119 already validates with `Number.isInteger`, so applying the same guard here makes both paths consistent and prevents silent corruption from any malformed history entry. ```suggestion if (data && typeof data === "object") { const maybeBufferJson = data as { type?: unknown; data?: unknown } if ( maybeBufferJson.type === "Buffer" && Array.isArray(maybeBufferJson.data) && (maybeBufferJson.data as unknown[]).every((v) => typeof v === "number" && Number.isInteger(v)) ) { return Uint8Array.from(maybeBufferJson.data as number[]) } ``` ### Issue 2 of 2 src/core/api/providers/bedrock.ts:1129-1141 **Empty-string key maps to index 0 in the numeric-key path** `Number("")` returns `0`, so an object like `{ "": 82 }` passes every guard — `Number.isInteger(0)` is `true`, `0 === index` (index 0) is `true` — and gets returned as a 1-byte `Uint8Array([82])` instead of throwing. This is unlikely to appear in real Bedrock history, but adding an explicit `key.length > 0` check on the raw string before converting to a number would close the gap without any false negatives. `````

This PR adds an mtime+size keyed in-memory cache to `readGlobalSettings()`, reducing repeated reads from a full `readFile` + `JSON.parse` + Zod validation round-trip down to a single `statSync` + four comparisons on the hot path. It also adds `Object.freeze` on the returned settings (and their array fields) so callers cannot accidentally corrupt the module-level cache. - **Cache implementation** (`global-settings.ts`): single-entry `CachedSettings` object keyed by `(path, mtimeMs, size)`; invalidated explicitly on every `writeGlobalSettings` call and lazily re-validated on every `readGlobalSettings` call via `statSync`. - **Freeze guard**: `freezeSettings()` shallow-freezes both the settings object and each mutable array field (`disabledTools`, `disabledPlugins`) before storing in cache, closing the mutation-via-reference trap. - **`toggleDisabledTool` cleanup**: collapsed two branched write paths into a single `writeGlobalSettings` call; return semantics (`true` = tool is now disabled) are preserved. - **`paths.ts`**: cosmetic rename of unexported `LEGACY_AGENT_SKILLS_DIRECTORY_NAME` → `LEGACY_AGENT_SKILLS_CONFIG_DIR`; no functional change.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the refactor is narrow in scope, all changed behaviour is covered by new tests, and the cache invalidation logic is straightforward. The cache correctly invalidates on every internal write and re-validates on every read via a cheap statSync. The freeze guard closes the mutation-via-reference gap. The single-entry cache design is intentional and fits the single-config-path use case. No functional regressions were found. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/core/src/services/global-settings.ts | Core refactor: adds mtime+size cache with explicit write-side invalidation and Object.freeze on returned values; toggleDisabledTool simplified to a single write path; logic is correct and well-structured. | | sdk/packages/core/src/services/global-settings.test.ts | Adds 6 focused caching tests covering: write-side invalidation, external mtime detection, multi-path keying, missing-file default, frozen-object enforcement, and missing→present file transition. | | sdk/packages/shared/src/storage/paths.ts | Cosmetic rename of unexported constant and whitespace adjustment; no functional or API changes. |

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes OAuth credential loss in the SDK's `ProviderSettingsManager` when a subsequent partial save (e.g., model or reasoning update) omits the `auth` block, silently replacing the full stored entry and making the account appear signed out on the next turn. - A new `preserveOAuthAuthFields` helper is inserted between schema parsing and the write step in `saveProviderSettings`. For any provider in `OAUTH_PROVIDER_IDS`, it carries the previous `auth` block forward when the incoming settings omit it, and does a shallow merge when the incoming settings supply only a partial `auth` update. - Two focused regression tests are added: one for a Cline model-only save preserving the full auth block, and one verifying that a partial `auth` update retains existing refresh metadata (refresh token, expiry, account ID) from the prior entry.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge. The change is narrowly scoped to the storage boundary for managed OAuth providers and does not alter sign-out or delete flows. The fix is applied at the right abstraction level — inside `saveProviderSettings` before the write — so all existing partial-save call sites benefit without individual changes. The shallow auth merge is appropriate because all auth fields are primitives. The only behavioral gap is that there is no path through `saveProviderSettings` to intentionally clear OAuth auth without deleting the provider entry, but the PR explicitly documents that sign-out goes through a direct map removal, making this by design. No files require special attention. Both changed files are straightforward and self-contained.

Important Files Changed

Greptile Summary

This PR eliminates a Bun native crash caused by creating two OpenTUI renderers in the same process when using `cline history`. Instead of spawning a standalone history TUI that then spawns a second renderer for the resumed session, the `cline history` command now opens the normal interactive TUI with `initialView: "history"`, triggering the existing in-app history picker on mount via a deferred `openHistory()` effect. - **Deleted** `history-standalone.tsx` and `history-resume.ts` (the child-process workaround) — the two-renderer pattern is no longer possible. - **Narrowed** `runHistoryList` return type from `Promise` to `Promise` and converted it to a plain text/JSON listing helper; interactive history is now exclusively handled by the TUI path. - **Added** `run-interactive.ts` guard (`initialView !== "history"`) to skip eager `sessionRuntime.ensureReady()` while the history picker is open, avoiding a startup race between the picker dialog and session initialization.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change removes the two-renderer crash path entirely and replaces it with the existing single-renderer dialog pattern already used for in-app history. All changed paths follow existing, well-tested patterns: the mount-time openHistory() effect mirrors the existing openConfig() effect, the initialView !== 'history' ensureReady() guard mirrors the existing loadDeferredInitialMessages guard, and the return-type narrowing of runHistoryList removes genuinely dead code. The beforeEach in main.test.ts sets stdin.isTTY = true, so the new TTY-dependent test is sound. No logic errors or unsafe behaviors were found. No files require special attention.

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR completes the event-publishing loop for scheduled run outcomes by wiring `schedule.execution.failed` (and verifying `schedule.execution.completed`) events through the full stack: cron runner → hub server transport → session client → connector adapters. The hub transport had already mapped both event types to their underscore wire names, but the cron runner never called `eventPublisher` on failure paths, and the session client had no handler for the `schedule.execution_failed` wire event. - **`cron-runner.ts`**: Adds `publishScheduleExecutionEvent`, called after `store.completeRun` in both the success and `catch` paths, guarded by `spec.source === \"hub-schedule\"` and an `eventPublisher` presence check. - **`session-client.ts`**: Adds early-return branches before the `sessionId` guard to map `schedule.execution_completed` / `schedule.execution_failed` wire events to dot-notation `HubStreamEvent` objects, extracting `sessionId` from the payload when the envelope field is absent. - **All six connector adapters**: Widens the event-type guard to also pass `schedule.execution.failed` through to `deliverScheduledResult`, which already handled non-success statuses via its else branch.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change is a straightforward completion of an already-prepared event pipeline with no correctness issues in the new code paths. Every changed file touches only event-passing plumbing. The hub server transport already had both event name mappings in place; this PR wires the remaining callsites and adds symmetric tests covering both the success and failure paths end-to-end. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/core/src/cron/runner/cron-runner.ts | Adds publishScheduleExecutionEvent private method and wires calls after completeRun in both the success and catch paths; status mapping from stored run state is correct for both done→success and failed→failed. | | sdk/packages/core/src/hub/client/session-client.ts | Adds early-return branches for schedule.execution_completed and schedule.execution_failed hub wire events and maps them to dot-notation eventType; also refactors cloneRecord to be called once at the top of mapHubEvent. | | sdk/packages/core/src/cron/service/schedule-service.ts | Tightens eventPublisher payload type from unknown to Record and threads the publisher down to CronRunner. | | sdk/packages/core/src/cron/service/schedule-service.test.ts | Adds a new sqliteIt test for failed execution event publishing and extends the existing success test to assert the published event payload. | | sdk/packages/core/src/hub/client/session-client.test.ts | Adds two new tests covering schedule.execution_completed and schedule.execution_failed frame mapping with payload-level sessionId extraction. | | sdk/apps/cli/src/connectors/adapters/discord.ts | Widens the event-type guard to also let schedule.execution.failed through to deliverScheduledResult; the function already handles non-success status via its else branch. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant CR as CronRunner participant HT as HubServerTransport participant WS as WebSocket Hub participant SC as HubSessionClient participant AD as Connector Adapter CR->>CR: "completeRun(status:done|failed)" CR->>CR: publishScheduleExecutionEvent(eventType, spec, runId) CR->>HT: "eventPublisher(schedule.execution.completed|failed, payload)" HT->>HT: map dot to underscore notation HT->>WS: publish(buildHubEvent(mapped, payload)) WS-->>SC: "WebSocket frame schedule.execution_completed|failed" SC->>SC: mapHubEvent early return branch SC-->>AD: "HubStreamEvent eventType schedule.execution.completed|failed" AD->>AD: guard passes for both completed and failed AD->>AD: deliverScheduledResult(scheduleId, status, errorMessage) ``` Reviews (2): Last reviewed commit: ["add unit tests"](https://github.com/cline/cline/commit/b53331eab398157ef31491134e4ffdf9950a2591) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=33121333)

HTTPS-only enforcement throws early on HTTP URLs that match plugin patterns, a 30-second AbortController timeout covers stalled connections, and a 10 MB streaming cap guards memory. Greptile Summary

This PR extends the `cline plugin install` command to accept single-file plugin URLs in addition to npm packages, git repos, and local paths. GitHub `blob` URLs are normalized to `raw.githubusercontent.com` before download, the file is stored under `_installed/remote/-/`, and the existing local-file entry-discovery path is reused for the downloaded file. - Adds `normalizeRemotePluginFileUrl`, `installRemoteFile`, and related routing in `plugin.ts` to detect, fetch, and stage remote plugin files; updates `parsePluginSource`, `getInstallPath`, and `getInstallSourceKey` to handle the new `\"remote\"` source type. - Adds two parse tests and one install test (using `vi.stubGlobal` for `fetch`) in `plugin.test.ts`. - Updates file headers in every SDK example plugin so users can install them with a single `cline plugin install ` command.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The new remote-file download path works correctly for the intended GitHub use case but accepts plain HTTP URLs, leaving room for a network attacker to substitute plugin content during install. The new installRemoteFile function has no fetch timeout (CLI can hang indefinitely on a slow server), accepts http:// URLs that can be intercepted and replaced with malicious code before reaching disk, and calls response.text() with no size cap. The GitHub URL normalization and install-path routing logic itself is correct, and existing npm/git/local paths are unaffected. sdk/apps/cli/src/commands/plugin.ts — specifically the installRemoteFile function and the scheme guard in normalizeRemotePluginFileUrl

Security Review

 - **MITM on HTTP installs** (`plugin.ts` `normalizeRemotePluginFileUrl`): The URL scheme guard accepts both `http://` and `https://`, so any non-GitHub URL ending in `.ts`/`.js` served over plain HTTP can be intercepted and replaced with arbitrary code before it reaches the user's disk.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/apps/cli/src/commands/plugin.ts | Core of the PR — adds remote file source detection, URL normalization (GitHub blob→raw), download, and install path routing; missing fetch timeout and response size cap, and HTTP is accepted alongside HTTPS | | sdk/apps/cli/src/commands/plugin.test.ts | Adds parse and install tests for GitHub blob and raw URLs using vi.stubGlobal; coverage is reasonable for the happy paths but no tests for HTTP URLs, timeout, or oversized responses | | sdk/apps/cli/src/main.ts | Minor description update to the plugin install command; no --remote flag added (auto-detection only), consistent with existing --npm/--git pattern |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[cline plugin install source] --> B{sourceType flag?} B -->|--npm| C[npm branch] B -->|--git| D[git branch] B -->|none| E{local path-like?} E -->|yes| F[local branch] E -->|no| G{normalizeRemotePluginFileUrl} G -->|github.com blob/raw URL| H[normalize to raw.githubusercontent.com] G -->|raw.githubusercontent.com URL| I[use URL as-is] G -->|other https URL ending .ts/.js| J[use URL as-is] G -->|no match| K[parseGitSource] H --> L[installRemoteFile: fetch + write to staging] I --> L J --> L L --> M[collectPluginEntries on stagingRoot] M --> N[replaceInstallPath to _installed/remote/filename-hash/] K --> O[installGitPackage] C --> P[installNpmPackage] D --> O F --> Q[installLocalPackage] Q --> R[_installed/local/...] O --> S[_installed/git/...] P --> T[_installed/npm/...] ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 4 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 4 sdk/apps/cli/src/commands/plugin.ts:718-738 **No fetch timeout — CLI can hang indefinitely** `fetch(parsed.url)` is called with no `AbortController` / timeout signal. If the remote server accepts the TCP connection but never sends headers (or stalls mid-body), the CLI will hang indefinitely with no way for the user to interrupt it through normal means. A standard pattern is to wrap the call with an `AbortController` and call `abort()` after a reasonable timeout (e.g. 30 s). ### Issue 2 of 4 sdk/apps/cli/src/commands/plugin.ts:218-220 **HTTP URLs allowed — remote plugin downloads are MITM-able** `normalizeRemotePluginFileUrl` accepts both `http://` and `https://` schemes. Because the PR is explicitly designed to make sharing one-liner install commands easy, a crafted `http://` link shared in docs or chat is a practical attack surface: a network-level attacker can substitute arbitrary code that will be saved and later executed as a plugin. Restricting downloads to `https://` would close this path entirely and is consistent with the GitHub-specific normalization that hardcodes `https://raw.githubusercontent.com`. ```suggestion if (!/^https:\/\//i.test(source)) { return null; } ``` ### Issue 3 of 4 sdk/apps/cli/src/commands/plugin.ts:233-237 **Misleading boolean variable named `filePath`** `isGitHubFilePath` returns a `boolean`, but the result is stored in a variable named `filePath`. A reader naturally expects `filePath` to hold a string, which makes the subsequent `if (!filePath)` branch confusing. Renaming to `isGitHubFile` makes the intent immediately obvious. ```suggestion const parts = parsed.pathname.split("/").filter(Boolean); const isGitHubFile = isGitHubFilePath(parsed.pathname); if (!isGitHubFile) { return null; } ``` ### Issue 4 of 4 sdk/apps/cli/src/commands/plugin.ts:730-735 **No response-body size limit** `response.text()` reads the entire body into a JavaScript string before writing to disk. A server that sends a multi-GB response (whether malicious or misconfigured) will exhaust the process heap before the write ever starts. Capping the download — for example by reading via a `ReadableStream` and tracking bytes written — or at minimum rejecting responses whose `Content-Length` header exceeds a reasonable threshold (e.g. 10 MB) would bound memory use. `````

Greptile Summary

This PR removes the 5% output-token discount that the live catalog normalizer was applying when a model's context window equalled its reported output limit, and instead applies conservative per-request output caps inside the gateway at streaming time. - **`catalog-live.ts`**: drops the `discounted` calculation entirely; `maxTokens` now mirrors the provider-reported `limit.output` value directly, and capability arrays are deduplicated with `Array.from(new Set(...))`. - **`gateway.ts`**: adds `estimateRequestInputTokens` (with a circular-reference–safe fallback serializer) and `resolveGatewayRequestMaxTokens`, which computes the minimum of the requested cap, `model.maxOutputTokens`, the `DEFAULT_GATEWAY_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` (32 000) default, and the context-window remainder; on overflow it returns `undefined` instead of 1 so the provider surfaces the real error. - Tests cover all new resolution paths including the context-overflow `undefined` return, circular-tool estimation, and end-to-end AI-SDK `maxOutputTokens` pass-through via compat.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge. The changes replace a catalog-time heuristic with runtime caps that correctly account for actual prompt size, and all new resolution paths are covered by focused unit tests. The catalog normalizer change is a straight removal of an invented discount with no downstream breakage; the new gateway logic is well-guarded (circular-ref–safe serialization, integer-safe math, explicit overflow return), and the three test suites validate every branch including the context-overflow undefined path and the AI-SDK maxOutputTokens pass-through. No files require special attention.

Greptile Summary

This PR removes the required `--bot-username` / `-m` flag from Telegram connector setup by inferring the bot's username automatically via the Telegram `getMe` API endpoint when the flag is omitted. An explicit username is still accepted for backward compatibility. - **Token-only startup path** (`telegram.ts`): adds `resolveTelegramBotUsername` (which calls `fetchTelegramBotUsername` → `getMe` when no username is configured), a `readTelegramBotId` helper to detect already-running connectors by token prefix before making a network call, and `backgroundArgs` injection so the spawned child process receives the resolved `--bot-username` and skips the redundant API call. - **Schema and wizard** (`options.ts`, `platforms.ts`): `botUsername` is now `string | undefined` in `ConnectTelegramOptions`, `botId` is persisted to `TelegramConnectorState`, and the interactive wizard removes the \"Bot username\" field, requiring only the token. - **Docs and tests**: all CLI examples drop `-m my_bot`; new unit tests cover arg-parsing, `getMe` mocking, failure surfacing, and the \"already running\" early-exit path.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge; the change is a well-scoped UX improvement with backward-compatible defaults. The username-inference logic is correctly gated: the early duplicate-detection check (by botId) avoids a network round-trip when a connector is already running, the backgroundArgs injection ensures the spawned child receives a concrete --bot-username so it never makes a redundant getMe call, and JSON/HTTP error paths are cleanly separated. The type change (botUsername?: string) is backward-compatible, and the new botId field in state is optional. Greptile Summary

This PR propagates `idle` and `pending` as first-class non-terminal session statuses across the CLI, hub records, persistence layer, and runtime host, replacing the previous pattern where interactive sessions remained `"running"` regardless of their actual activity state. - **Type system**: Adds `NON_TERMINAL_SESSION_STATUSES`, `NonTerminalSessionStatus`, `TerminalSessionStatus`, and `isNonTerminalSessionStatus` / `isTerminalSessionStatus` guards in `common.ts`; propagates `idle` and `pending` to `records.ts`, `hub.ts`, `chat-schema.ts`, and SQLite/persistence update paths. - **Runtime**: `LocalRuntimeHost` now calls `markTurnIdle` after a completed turn and wraps `requestToolApproval` to transition through `pending` while awaiting user approval; `stopSession` and `dispose` use `isNonTerminalSessionStatus` to keep interactive sessions alive when idle or pending. - **History**: `filterAndProjectHistoryRows` is introduced to both filter zero-message sessions and project legacy `running` interactive sessions as `idle` when the last message is a completed assistant turn.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge with one fix: idle and pending child sessions are silently skipped by the parent-cancel and dead-session-reconciliation cleanup paths. The applyStatusToRunningChildSessions query in team-child-session-manager.ts still hardcodes status: 'running'. With this PR, child subagent sessions can legitimately be in idle or pending states. body:
Greptile Summary

This PR adds retry middleware with exponential backoff to all seven SDK vendor providers (Anthropic, Bedrock, Google, Mistral, OpenAI, OpenAI-compatible, Vertex), addressing the long-standing gap where legacy providers had `@withRetry()` decorator support but SDK providers had none. The middleware handles 429/5xx/network errors, respects `retry-after` headers, and is wired into each vendor via `wrapLanguageModel`. - **New `retry.ts` middleware**: implements `createRetryMiddleware`, `composeMiddleware`, `isRetriableError`, `calculateBackoffDelay`, and `getRetryDelayFromError` with full unit test coverage. - **Vendor integration**: all vendor factories now wrap their model with retry middleware; Mistral and OpenAI-compatible vendors compose retry with the existing `splitToolImagesMiddleware`, correctly placing retry as the outermost layer. - **Two issues to address**: (1) `retryAllErrors: true` bypasses the `AbortError` guard in `isRetriableError`, causing cancelled requests to be retried; (2) the underlying AI SDK clients (Anthropic, OpenAI) have their own default retry mechanisms that are not disabled, potentially stacking retries multiplicatively.

Confidence Score: 3/5

Not safe to merge as-is: intentional request cancellations can be silently retried when `retryAllErrors: true` is configured, and the underlying AI SDK clients may double-stack retries. The `retryAllErrors` flag short-circuits the AbortError guard, so a cancelled request can loop through the full retry budget rather than immediately propagating the cancellation. Separately, none of the vendor factory calls disable the AI SDK clients' own built-in retry mechanism, meaning a persistent error can trigger multiplicatively more API calls than the configured `maxRetries` implies. Primary concern is `retry.ts` (the `retryAllErrors` + AbortError interaction); secondary concern spans all vendor files where the underlying SDK client `maxRetries` is not set to 0.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/middleware/retry.ts | New retry middleware with exponential backoff and jitter; `retryAllErrors` flag bypasses the AbortError guard in `isRetriableError`, causing intentional cancellations to be retried. | | sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/middleware/retry.test.ts | Comprehensive unit tests for retry logic; no test covers `retryAllErrors: true` with an AbortError input to catch the bypass bug. | | sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/vendors/anthropic.ts | Integrates retry middleware; underlying `@ai-sdk/anthropic` SDK defaults to 2 built-in retries, creating double-retry stacking without `maxRetries: 0` on the provider factory. | | sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/vendors/mistral.ts | Composes retry middleware with existing `splitToolImagesMiddleware`; composition order looks correct with retry as the outermost layer. | | sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/vendors/openai-compatible.ts | Composes retry with `splitToolImagesMiddleware`; same pattern as mistral, correctly places retry as the outermost layer. | | sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/vendors/vertex.ts | Integrates retry middleware for both Claude (via `createVertexAnthropic`) and non-Claude (via `createVertex`) model paths; consistent with the other vendors. | | sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/vendors/openai.ts | Integrates retry middleware; same double-retry concern applies since `@ai-sdk/openai` uses the OpenAI SDK with its own retry mechanism by default. | | sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/vendors/bedrock.ts | Adds retry middleware with optional context; pattern is consistent with other vendors. | | sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/vendors/google.ts | Integrates retry middleware on top of Google Generative AI provider; consistent implementation with other vendors. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Caller participant RetryMiddleware participant SplitToolImages participant ProviderSDK participant API Caller->>RetryMiddleware: doStream() loop "attempt <= maxRetries" RetryMiddleware->>SplitToolImages: doStream() [if composed] SplitToolImages->>ProviderSDK: doStream() [after transformParams] ProviderSDK->>API: HTTP request alt Success API-->>ProviderSDK: 200 stream ProviderSDK-->>RetryMiddleware: stream RetryMiddleware-->>Caller: stream else 429 or 5xx or network error API-->>ProviderSDK: error ProviderSDK-->>RetryMiddleware: throw error RetryMiddleware->>RetryMiddleware: isRetriableError check alt retriable and retries left RetryMiddleware->>RetryMiddleware: sleep with backoff else not retriable or exhausted RetryMiddleware-->>Caller: throw error end end end ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 2 sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/middleware/retry.ts:351-353 **`retryAllErrors: true` silently retries intentional cancellations** When `retryAllErrors` is set, the short-circuit `config.retryAllErrors || isRetriableError(error)` evaluates to `true` for every error — including `AbortError`. The careful guard in `isRetriableError` that returns `false` for `AbortError` is never consulted. If no `signal` is forwarded (e.g. Bedrock and Mistral accept an optional context), the `sleep()` abort check also won't fire, so the retry loop will happily re-issue a request the caller explicitly cancelled. ```suggestion // Check if we should retry. // Always respect AbortError regardless of retryAllErrors — intentional // cancellation must never be silently retried. const isAbortError = error && typeof error === "object" && (error as Record).name === "AbortError"; const isRetriable = !isAbortError && (config.retryAllErrors || isRetriableError(error)); const hasRetriesLeft = attempt < config.maxRetries; ``` ### Issue 2 of 2 sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/vendors/anthropic.ts:20-32 **Double-retry risk: underlying SDK has its own retry mechanism** `createAnthropic` (and the other AI SDK factory calls) passes the configured `fetch` but leaves the underlying SDK's `maxRetries` at its default (the Anthropic SDK defaults to 2 retries; OpenAI SDK to 2 as well). With this middleware adding up to 3 outer retries, a persistent 429/5xx error can trigger up to 12 total API calls (3 outer × 4 inner attempts for the Anthropic SDK), and the outer `retry-after` delay can silently stack on top of the inner SDK delays. Consider setting `maxRetries: 0` on each SDK factory call to give the middleware sole ownership of retry semantics. `````

- `go.work.sum`: I agree with the substance. It is unrelated to the move, so it is a little noisy in a giant PR, but I would not block on it.
- root `biome.json`: this is a real area to check, but the approach makes sense. The main risk would be root-level Biome behavior for non-VS Code areas, but `sdk/biome.json` still exists, so this seems acceptable.

My conclusion: I am comfortable with this PR as a mostly mechanical move, but only after PR 10962 is merged into this branch and the combined branch has green relevant CI. 10961 by itself is expected to be broken; 10961 plus the fixed workflow/task follow-up is the version I would approve.

body:
Main blockers:

- `apps/vscode/tsconfig.json` currently breaks TypeScript from inside `apps/vscode`. The aliases and include paths were changed to `apps/vscode/src/*` and `apps/vscode/src/**/*`, but because the tsconfig itself lives in `apps/vscode`, those resolve as nested paths. Running `npx tsc --noEmit` from `apps/vscode` fails immediately with no matching inputs plus TS5090 path errors. I locally changed those paths back to `./src/*` and `src/**/*`, and plain `tsc` passed after that, so this looks like a targeted config regression.

- The workflow changed-file filters still watch the old pre-move paths. In `.github/workflows/ext-vscode-test.yml` and `.github/workflows/ext-vscode-test-e2e.yml`, filters still use entries like `src/**`, `webview-ui/**`, `proto/**`, `scripts/**`, `assets/**`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, and `tsconfig*.json`. After the move, future PRs touching `apps/vscode/src/**`, `apps/vscode/webview-ui/**`, `apps/vscode/proto/**`, etc. can skip the VS Code checks entirely.

- CI is currently red on this PR. The latest visible checks have e2e failing on ubuntu, windows, and macos. Given this PR is specifically meant to make the moved extension build/test correctly, I would not merge until the full stack is green.

- This PR force-adds about 157k lines of generated files under paths that the repo still ignores: `apps/vscode/src/generated/`, `apps/vscode/src/shared/proto/`, and `apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/services/grpc-client.ts`. If the intent is still to keep generated outputs untracked, these should not be committed. If the intent changed, `.gitignore` and the repo policy should be updated explicitly.

- `.github/dependabot.yml` still points npm updates at `/` and `/webview-ui`; those should likely become `/apps/vscode` and `/apps/vscode/webview-ui`.

- Some artifact and coverage paths still look root-relative to the old layout, for example Qlty upload paths like `coverage-unit/lcov.info` and `webview-ui/coverage/lcov.info`.

- `.vscode/settings.json` still has `--proto_path=proto`, which looks stale after moving protos to `apps/vscode/proto`.

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes Vertex AI Gemini authentication by passing GCP project settings through to the `google-auth-library` and disabling API-key \"express mode\" when a GCP project ID is present. It also corrects the Vertex model catalog by mapping to the `google-vertex` models.dev key instead of `google-vertex-anthropic`, so Gemini models are included alongside Claude models. - **`vertex.ts`**: When `options.project`/`options.projectId` is set, `apiKey` is forced to `undefined` and `googleAuthOptions.projectId` is passed to `createVertex`, routing auth through the google-auth-library instead of API-key express mode; `ensureFetch` is now applied consistently to both the Gemini and Claude paths. - **`handler-factory.ts`**: Adds a new `vertex` branch in `buildGatewayProviderOptions` that maps `providerConfig.gcp.projectId` → `options.project`/`options.projectId` and `gcp.region` → `options.location`/`options.region`. - **`provider-keys.ts`**: Fixes the catalog generation key from `google-vertex-anthropic` to `google-vertex` so that future catalog refreshes pull in both Gemini and Claude Vertex models; also removes the hardcoded Claude `defaultModelId` from the vertex built-in spec so the first Gemini model becomes the default.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge; the auth bypass logic is well-scoped, tests cover all three code paths, and the changes are isolated to the Vertex provider. The Gemini auth fix and GCP config forwarding are correct and well-tested. The Claude (Vertex Anthropic) path doesn't receive googleAuthOptions when a GCP project is set, creating a minor asymmetry that could matter in environments where the credential project needs to be overridden explicitly. Removing the hardcoded defaultModelId from the vertex spec silently shifts the provider default from a Claude model to the first Gemini catalog entry, which is a quiet behaviour change for existing users who never specified a model. sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/vendors/vertex.ts (Claude path missing googleAuthOptions) and sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/builtins.ts (implicit default model change).

This PR makes the `name` field on `ToolResultContent` first-class by adding it to the shared interface and propagating it through the codec, `MessageBuilder`, and all associated tests. It also adds GCP service-account (`googleAuthOptions`) support to the Vertex provider and bundles a generated model catalog refresh. - **Tool-name propagation**: `ToolResultContent` gains a required `name: string` field; `agent-message-codec.ts` now forwards `block.name` instead of hardcoding `""`, and `MessageBuilder.createMissingToolResultBlocks` also sets `name: toolName`. - **Vertex GCP auth**: `createVertexProviderModule` now derives `googleAuthOptions.projectId` from `config.options.project/projectId` so service-account auth works without an explicit API key; `ensureFetch` replaces the raw `config.fetch` reference for consistency. - **Provider catalog**: `provider-keys.ts` swaps the vertex `modelsDevKey` from `"google-vertex-anthropic"` to `"google-vertex"`, `defaultModelId` is removed from the vertex `BuiltinSpec`, and the generated model catalog is refreshed.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The tool-name propagation is correct for new messages, but adding `name` as a required field without a runtime fallback creates a gap for any session history that predates this change. The codec now reads `block.name` directly, but stored `ToolResultContent` objects from existing sessions never had this field. This PR fixes a bug where tasks created with only attachments (no text) were silently dropped from the task history view due to an empty `task` string being treated as falsy in the history filter. - **`message-state.ts`**: Adds `generateFallbackTaskDescription()` to produce a human-readable label (e.g. `[1 image(s)]`) when `taskMessage.text` is empty, so the stored `HistoryItem.task` is never an empty string for attachment-only messages. - **`getTaskHistory.ts`**: Relaxes `hasRequiredFields` from `item.ts && item.task` to `!!item.ts` so that legacy entries with an empty-string `task` (created before this fix) still appear in history rather than being silently hidden.

Confidence Score: 3/5

This PR adds a `withMinimumReleaseAgeBypass` helper that applies package-manager-specific flags or environment variables to disable the minimum release age gate when the user explicitly runs `cline update`, while leaving the background auto-update and kanban update paths unchanged. - **npm** gets `--min-release-age=0` appended to the install command; **bun** gets `--minimum-release-age=0`; **Yarn** gets `YARN_NPM_MINIMAL_AGE_GATE=0` injected as an env var; **pnpm** receives all three env var forms (`PNPM_CONFIG_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE`, `pnpm_config_minimum_release_age`, `npm_config_minimum_release_age`) to cover v9, v10, and v11+ behaviour. - The `ManualUpdateCommand` type is introduced to carry the optional `env` map through to `spawn()`, where it is merged on top of `process.env` only when the map is present.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change is narrowly scoped to the manual update path with no impact on background or kanban updates. The bypass logic is isolated in a pure, easily-testable helper. All four named package managers are covered in both code and tests, the UNKNOWN case passes through unchanged, and env merging in spawn() is correct. The only gap is that the test does not assert PNPM_CONFIG_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE alongside the lowercase key, which is a minor coverage omission rather than a production defect. No files require special attention beyond the minor pnpm test assertion gap in update.test.ts.

The change is purely additive documentation. The Auxen base URL and API key format are clearly explained, and the five-step quickstart is straightforward. The only gap is that users following these steps will see misleading token-based cost estimates in Cline's Model Configuration panel because Auxen's per-minute billing model is not acknowledged there. docs/provider-config/openai-compatible.mdx — review the Model Configuration guidance and the nested-heading MDX pattern.

Greptile Summary

This PR moves runtime tool-approval and ask-question interactions from modal overlay dialogs to inline panels that replace the chat composer, so the transcript stays visible while the user responds. - **Inline response panel** (`inline-tool-response.tsx`): Two components (`ToolApprovalResponse`, `AskQuestionResponse`) render inside a `Shell` frame at the bottom of the chat. Keyboard navigation (arrows, number shortcuts, Enter, Escape) and mouse clicks are both supported. State is managed through ref/state pairs to avoid stale closures in the keyboard handler. - **Queue-based bridge** (`use-runtime-dialog-bridge.tsx`): Pending interactions are queued via `useRef`; only the head is exposed as React state. Completed interactions advance the queue automatically. `dismissAll` is called on effect cleanup to resolve any in-flight promises on unmount. - **Root wiring** (`root.tsx`, `chat-view.tsx`): `isRuntimeInteractionOpen` gates both the textarea-focus effect and `useRootKeyboard`, ensuring normal shortcuts are blocked while a prompt is pending.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge. The change replaces modal dialogs with inline panels and is well-scoped to the CLI TUI layer, with no impact on core runtime logic. All six changed files make coherent, contained changes. The queue-based bridge uses stable useCallback deps so the registration effect runs exactly once per mount. Existing modal dialogs for non-runtime UI are untouched. Keyboard-blocking guards in root.tsx correctly prevent composer shortcuts from leaking through while a prompt is active, and the key prop on InlineToolResponse guarantees clean state resets between interactions. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/apps/cli/src/tui/components/inline-tool-response.tsx | New component implementing inline tool-response panels for ask-question and tool-approval interactions. Uses ref/state pairing to safely read current values in keyboard closures. The key prop on the parent ensures full re-mount on each new interaction, resetting all local state correctly. | | sdk/apps/cli/src/tui/hooks/use-runtime-dialog-bridge.tsx | Refactored from dialog-based to queue-based inline approach. Stable useCallback deps throughout; enqueue and dismissAll are stable, so the useEffect registers handlers exactly once per mount. Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a regression introduced by #10946 where the SDK gateway began synthesising a concrete `max_output_tokens` request parameter from catalog metadata even when the caller never requested one, causing ChatGPT OAuth Codex requests to fail with `Error: unsupported parameter: max_output_tokens`. - **`gateway.ts`**: Removes `DEFAULT_GATEWAY_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` and the implicit default output cap; `resolveGatewayRequestMaxTokens` now returns `undefined` immediately when no explicit `requestedMaxTokens` is provided, and the `stream()` method only calls the resolver when `request.maxTokens` is a positive finite number. - **`ai-sdk.ts`**: `maxOutputTokens` is now conditionally spread into the `streamText` call only when `request.maxTokens` is defined, preventing the parameter from reaching backends that reject it. - **Tests**: Existing tests updated to assert the no-implicit-cap behavior; a new ChatGPT OAuth regression test verifies that `openai-codex` requests omit `maxOutputTokens` when the caller does not supply a max tokens value.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the fix is narrowly scoped, well-tested with a dedicated regression case, and removes behaviour that was actively breaking a production flow. The change cleanly reverts a single behavioural regression (implicit output cap injection) while preserving the catalog correctness work from the source PR. All affected code paths are covered by updated or new unit tests, and no callers of the removed export remain in the repo. No files require special attention beyond the minor guard-consistency note in ai-sdk.ts.

Important Files Changed

Greptile Summary

This PR extends the existing VCR cassette infrastructure in `@cline/shared` with an optional request-body contract mechanism. When `CLINE_VCR_INCLUDE_REQUEST_BODY=1` is set during recording, each cassette entry gains a sanitized, canonicalized `requestBody` field; playback then asserts the live request matches that contract, enabling detection of request-shape regressions like the motivating ChatGPT OAuth case. - **`vcr.ts`**: Adds `readRequestBody` / `readRequestContentType` helpers, a `compareCodeUnits`-based canonical JSON stringifier, and `assertRequestBodyMatches` called before `consumed[matchIndex] = true` so a body mismatch does not permanently burn a cassette slot. Sensitive key redaction is normalized to lowercase in `REDACT_KEYS_EXACT`. - **`types/vcr.ts`**: Adds the optional `requestBody` field to `VcrRecording`; old cassettes without the field continue to replay unchanged. - **`vcr.test.ts`**: New test suite covering JSON body sanitization, form-encoded body handling, the Content-Type guard for URL-encoded parsing, successful playback with differing runtime secrets, and the fail-then-retry flow for body mismatches.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge; the change is purely additive, existing cassettes without the new `requestBody` field are unaffected, and the body-assertion slot fix is correct and well-tested. All changed code is confined to the VCR test-utility layer with no runtime product impact. The opt-in nature of `CLINE_VCR_INCLUDE_REQUEST_BODY` and the backward-compatible `requestBody?: string` type mean nothing breaks for existing cassettes. The one notable gap — `Blob`/`ReadableStream` bodies producing a vacuous empty contract — is a non-blocking limitation that cannot cause false failures, only missed coverage for body types that are not used in the motivating LLM-provider test paths. No files require special attention; `vcr.ts` is the most complex file but is comprehensively covered by the new test suite.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/shared/src/vcr.ts | Core VCR implementation extended with request-body recording and assertion; `consumed` slot correctly marked only after a passing body assertion; `readRequestBody` silently returns `undefined` for Blob/FormData/ReadableStream bodies. | | sdk/packages/shared/src/types/vcr.ts | Adds optional `requestBody` field to `VcrRecording`; backward-compatible change, old cassettes without the field replay as before. | | sdk/packages/shared/src/vcr.test.ts | New test suite covering all major request-body contract scenarios including the important fail-then-retry case that validates the slot-not-consumed fix. | | sdk/packages/llms/README.md | Documentation-only addition of the `CLINE_VCR_INCLUDE_REQUEST_BODY=1` flag to the provider cassette recording instructions. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Test participant VCR as VCR (globalThis.fetch) participant Real as Real fetch / Cassette rect rgb(200, 230, 200) Note over Test,Real: Record mode (CLINE_VCR=record + CLINE_VCR_INCLUDE_REQUEST_BODY=1) Test->>VCR: "fetch(url, { body: "..." })" VCR->>VCR: readRequestBody() → raw string VCR->>VCR: readRequestContentType() VCR->>Real: originalFetch(url, init) Real-->>VCR: Response stream VCR->>VCR: "sanitizeRecording(rec, includeRequestBody=true)" Note right of VCR: sanitizeSerializedRequestBody()
→ canonicalStringify(sanitizeValue(…)) VCR->>VCR: writeFileSync(cassette) [requestBody field written] end rect rgb(200, 210, 240) Note over Test,Real: Playback mode (CLINE_VCR=playback) Test->>VCR: "fetch(url, { body: "..." })" VCR->>VCR: findIndex() → matchIndex VCR->>VCR: assertRequestBodyMatches() [if rec.requestBody defined] alt body matches VCR->>VCR: "consumed[matchIndex] = true" VCR-->>Test: Replayed Response else body mismatch VCR-->>Test: throws Error (slot NOT consumed) Test->>VCR: fetch(url, corrected body) VCR->>VCR: same slot still available → matches VCR-->>Test: Replayed Response end end ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 1 code review issue. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 1 sdk/packages/shared/src/vcr.ts:419-439 `readRequestBody` returns `undefined` for `Blob`, `FormData`, and `ReadableStream` bodies. When that happens, `rec.body` is stored as `""` (via the `?? ""` fallback), and `sanitizeSerializedRequestBody("")` produces `""` — so the cassette ends up with `requestBody: ""`. During playback the same code paths produce `""` again, so the assertion always passes and no body contract is actually enforced for these types. Any regression that moves from a `Blob` body to no body at all would be silently missed. Adding a `Blob` branch and noting the `ReadableStream` / `FormData` limitation explicitly would prevent cassette authors from being surprised by a vacuously-passing contract. ```suggestion if (init?.body) { if (typeof init.body === "string") { return init.body; } if (init.body instanceof URLSearchParams) { return init.body.toString(); } if (init.body instanceof ArrayBuffer) { return new TextDecoder().decode(init.body); } if (ArrayBuffer.isView(init.body)) { return new TextDecoder().decode( new Uint8Array( init.body.buffer, init.body.byteOffset, init.body.byteLength, ), ); } if (init.body instanceof Blob) { return new TextDecoder().decode(await init.body.arrayBuffer()); } // ReadableStream and FormData cannot be read here without consuming or // serializing them in a lossy way — return undefined so the caller // records no body contract rather than a misleading empty one. return undefined; } ``` `````

Greptile Summary

This PR eliminates the ~1 s pause when a user starts a fresh CLI conversation via `/new` or the TUI clear action by deferring backend session creation until the next real prompt is sent. Previously, both flows called `restartEmpty()`, which eagerly stopped the old session and immediately created a replacement — the creation cost in hub-backed runs was the bottleneck. - **Lazy reset path (`resetForNewSession`)**: stops the active session and clears state without creating a replacement. `ensureReady()` gains an `activeSessionId` early-return so it only creates a new backend session when one is genuinely needed (i.e., at the next `sendCurrentTurn`). The TUI `clearConversation` further short-circuits when no messages have been submitted, skipping even the stop call. - **Generation guard (`sessionStartGeneration`)**: an integer counter is bumped on every reset or restart; `startFreshSession` and `startResumedSession` capture the counter before their async `manager.start()` call and drop (and stop) the result if the counter changed, preventing stale in-flight starts from becoming the active session. - **Eager paths preserved**: `restartEmpty()` / `restartWithMessages()` remain fully eager for model, account, compaction, and team changes that need an active session immediately.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change is narrowly scoped to the /new and TUI clear paths, all existing eager restart flows are untouched, and the generation guard cleanly handles in-flight session races. The lazy reset logic is straightforward and well-tested. The generation counter correctly prevents stale manager.start() results from becoming active. The hasSubmitted short-circuit in clearConversation aligns with actual session lifecycle. No existing restart flows were altered. No files require special attention.

Logic is well-structured and correctly handles the relevant race conditions. | | sdk/apps/cli/src/runtime/interactive/chat-command-runner.ts | Switches /new command from the eager restartEmpty() path to the new lazy resetForNewSession(), and adds resetForNewSession to the InteractiveChatCommandRuntime pick type. | | sdk/apps/cli/src/runtime/interactive/session-runtime.test.ts | New test file covering deferred session creation, fresh-start after a resumed session reset, and the eager restartEmpty() path remaining unchanged — good coverage of the three intended behaviors. | | sdk/apps/cli/src/runtime/interactive/chat-command-runner.test.ts | Adds a test verifying that /new calls resetForNewSession and not restartEmpty; also updates the mock to include the new method. | | sdk/apps/cli/src/runtime/run-interactive.ts | Wires the new onNewSession TUI prop to sessionRuntime.resetForNewSession(); all other callbacks (model, account, compaction changes) correctly retain the eager ensureReady() + restart pattern. | | sdk/apps/cli/src/tui/root.tsx | Skips backend reset entirely when the session has never been submitted (no messages sent), and routes through the new lazy onNewSession prop otherwise. Greptile Summary

This PR hardens handoff-path handling in the `agents-squad` example plugin by introducing explicit pre-validation (`validateHandoffRelativePath`) and replacing a string-prefix containment check with a more robust `path.relative()`-based escape check. It also removes the `.regex()` call from the `HandoffPathInput` Zod schema, replacing it with `.describe()`, to fix compatibility with the OpenAI Codex provider. - **Path validation** (`validateHandoffRelativePath`): new guards for empty, absolute (`/`-prefixed), overly long, disallowed-character, and `..`-segment paths are added before the resolve step, providing defense-in-depth alongside the containment check. - **Containment check** (`resolveHandoffPath`): replaces `resolved.startsWith(dir + \"/\")` with `path.relative()` + `isAbsolute` inspection, making the escape detection cross-platform and correct for the edge case where `resolved === dir`. - **Schema change**: `.regex()` removed from `HandoffPathInput`; validation responsibility now lives entirely in `validateHandoffRelativePath`, so any future code path that parses the schema without calling `resolveHandoffPath` would bypass the character-set and `..` enforcement.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The change is safe to merge; the core containment logic is correct and more robust than before. The `relative()`-based containment check and the layered `validateHandoffRelativePath` guards are all sound. The two concerns are: `HANDOFF_PATH_ALLOWED_RE` silently allows `..` at the regex level, leaving the explicit split-based check as the only guard (easy to accidentally drop); and removing `.regex()` from the Zod schema means the schema no longer enforces character-set or traversal rules at parse time. Neither is an active defect in the current code paths, but both reduce the margin for safe future modification. sdk/examples/plugins/agents-squad/index.ts — specifically the `HANDOFF_PATH_ALLOWED_RE` constant and the `HandoffPathInput` schema definition.

Greptile Summary

This PR adds schema portability validation for plugin tool `inputSchema` definitions, blocking non-portable JSON Schema constructs (currently regex lookarounds) at registration time — both in the shared `ContributionRegistry` and in the plugin sandbox bootstrap — rather than letting them surface as opaque runtime failures against AI providers that don't support ECMAScript 2018+ regex. - A new `schema-compat.ts` module provides `collectToolInputSchemaCompatibilityIssues` (recursive schema walker) and `assertToolInputSchemaPortable` (throws on first violation), which are wired into `createTool`, `ContributionRegistry.registerTool`, and the sandbox `PluginApi.registerTool`. - Both `index.ts` and `index.browser.ts` export the new types and functions, and tests cover the `createTool` path and the raw contribution-registry path.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge for the common case; the validation correctly blocks lookaround-carrying schemas at registration time with good test coverage. The scanner in `containsRegexLookaround` does not account for character-class context: a valid pattern such as `[(?!)]` (a character class containing literal `(`, `?`, `!`, `)`) would be incorrectly rejected with a "lookaround" error. Additionally, regex patterns used as keys in `patternProperties` are not validated at all. Both gaps leave the compatibility gate incomplete or potentially over-eager, but neither affects the common real-world patterns the PR targets. sdk/packages/shared/src/tools/schema-compat.ts — the `containsRegexLookaround` and `collectToolInputSchemaCompatibilityIssues` functions have the gaps described above.

This PR upgrades 16 dependency packages to remediate 54 CVEs, ranging from critical RCE vulnerabilities in `protobufjs` to DoS, prototype pollution, and injection flaws in `basic-ftp`, `@xmldom/xmldom`, `hono`, `axios`, and others. The single `package.json` change bumps `axios` from an exact pin of `1.15.2` to `1.16.1`; all other version changes are lockfile-only. - **axios 1.16.1** introduces two new nested lockfile entries (`agent-base@6.0.2` and `https-proxy-agent@5.0.1`) that were not previously present; these older sibling packages now live under `node_modules/axios/node_modules/` to support the CONNECT-tunnel proxy fix. - **fast-xml-parser 5.7.3** pulls in additional side-effect bumps not enumerated in the PR description: `@smithy/types` (4.13.1→4.14.2), `path-expression-matcher` (1.2.0→1.5.0), `strnum` (2.2.2→2.3.0), and a new `xml-naming@0.1.0` package. - **zod 4.4.3** (nested under `@sap-ai-sdk/prompt-registry`) carries documented behavioral breaking changes including `.merge()` throwing on refinements, stricter required-`undefined` property handling, and changed tuple-default materialization.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge after confirming the newly introduced nested packages (agent-base@6.0.2, https-proxy-agent@5.0.1) are advisory-clean and the unlisted side-effect bumps don't break AWS SDK integration. All 54 CVEs targeted by the PR are addressed and all 18 enumerated version changes are correctly reflected in the lockfile. The two concerns are observational: the axios upgrade silently introduces older nested packages that weren't in the lockfile before, and the fast-xml-parser chain pulls in four additional packages outside the scope of the PR's own breaking-changes analysis. Neither is a confirmed defect, but both warrant a quick advisory check before merging. package-lock.json — specifically the new node_modules/axios/node_modules/ subtree and the @smithy/types, path-expression-matcher, strnum, and xml-naming entries introduced as side effects of the @aws-sdk/xml-builder parent bump.

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a hub-mode CLI failure where a detached daemon replacement causes the next `runTurn` to fail with `session not found` because the daemon's in-memory session map is gone while the CLI still holds the original session id and contribution handlers. - `LocalRuntimeHost.getSessionOrThrow` now attaches `code: \"session_not_found\"` to the thrown error so the entire stack can distinguish it from other failures. - `run-handlers.ts` short-circuits on that code, returning a typed `errorReply` to the client instead of publishing a terminal `run.failed` event, keeping the session recoverable. - `HubRuntimeHost` retains the original `StartSessionInput` and capabilities per session; on a `session_not_found` from `run.start`, it rebuilds the hub session with the same id, re-registers client contributions, and retries the turn exactly once.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Targeted bug fix with focused test coverage; the happy path and recovery path are both exercised, and existing stopSession/dispose cleanup ensures no state leaks past the session lifetime. The recovery flow in recoverMissingActiveSessionOnce registers session state before the create command but does not release it if the command throws, leaving handlers and subscriptions partially overwritten until stopSession runs. Sessions created via restoreSession are also silently excluded from daemon-replacement recovery since that path never populates sessionStartContexts. hub-runtime-host.ts — the recovery error path and the restoreSession gap warrant a second look.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/core/src/hub/runtime-host/hub-runtime-host.ts | Core fix: adds RetainedStartContext storage per session, refactors session.create into a reusable helper, and adds the runTurn recovery wrapper that retries once after a session_not_found error. Two minor gaps: recovery failure path does not call cleanupPlannedSession, and restoreSession never populates the retained context map. | | sdk/packages/core/src/hub/server/handlers/run-handlers.ts | Returns a typed session_not_found error reply instead of publishing run.failed, enabling the client-side retry. The errorCode helper has a minor edge case where code: undefined returns the string undefined rather than undefined. | | sdk/packages/core/src/runtime/host/local-runtime-host.ts | Tags the session-not-found error with code: session_not_found via Object.assign, enabling the typed error propagation chain. Minimal and correct change. | | sdk/packages/core/src/hub/runtime-host/hub-runtime-host.test.ts | Adds a well-structured recovery test that mocks HubCommandError, verifies session.create is called twice with the same sessionId, and checks client contributions are re-registered correctly. | | sdk/packages/core/src/hub/server/handlers/run-handlers.test.ts | Adds a targeted test verifying that session_not_found returns an errorReply without publishing a run.failed event. | | sdk/packages/core/src/runtime/host/local-runtime-host.test.ts | Updates the missing-session test to assert the new code: session_not_found property on the thrown error. |

Sequence Diagram

Sessions from this path silently fall through the `if (!retained) return false` guard in `recoverMissingActiveSessionOnce`. Greptile Summary

This PR adds VCR-backed smoke tests for four provider adapters (`cline`, `openai-codex`, `anthropic`, `openai-compatible`) to catch request-shape regressions — like the `max_output_tokens` leak fixed in #10990 — without requiring live credentials. Each cassette records the canonical request body as a contract: if an adapter starts emitting an unexpected field, playback will fail with a body-mismatch error before any real API call is needed. - **New test harness** (`provider-vcr.test.ts`): supports record and playback modes, validates cassette `requestBody` contracts during setup, scrubs response IDs/timestamps/encrypted blobs after recording, and cleans up partial cassettes on failure. - **Four cassette fixtures** covering Cline, ChatGPT OAuth, Anthropic, and OpenRouter-compatible request shapes; the `openai-codex` fixture is missing the `contentType` field present in the other three cassettes. - **Vitest alias** added to resolve `@cline/shared` from source rather than stale `dist`; this alias applies to the entire `@cline/llms` test suite, not just the VCR tests.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — changes are additive test infrastructure only; no production code paths are modified. All changes are new test files and a Vitest config alias. The only concrete defect is a missing contentType field in one cassette fixture, which causes VCR playback to skip the SSE streaming simulation for the openai-codex adapter. The tests still pass because the adapter does not currently require the content-type header, so this is a robustness gap rather than a broken test. sdk/packages/llms/src/tests/provider-vcr/openai-codex-gpt-5-4.json — missing contentType compared to the other three cassettes.

Important Files Changed

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Dev as Developer / CI participant Test as provider-vcr.test.ts participant VCR as @cline/shared VCR participant Adapter as Provider Adapter Dev->>Test: "bun -F @cline/llms test:vcr" Test->>Test: configureVcr(cassettePath) Test->>VCR: initVcr("playback") VCR->>VCR: patch globalThis.fetch, load cassette Test->>Adapter: createHandlerAsync(config) Test->>Adapter: createMessage(systemPrompt, messages) Adapter->>VCR: fetch(providerUrl, requestBody) VCR->>VCR: assertRequestBodyMatches() VCR-->>Adapter: replay cassette response Adapter-->>Test: text/usage/done chunks Test->>Test: expect assertions Test->>Test: keepRecordedCassette() Test->>VCR: disposeAll() Test->>Test: afterEach cleanup ```

Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 1 sdk/packages/llms/src/tests/provider-vcr/openai-codex-gpt-5-4.json:8-9 Missing `contentType` field — unlike the other three cassettes, this one omits `contentType`. The VCR library's SSE fallback heuristic checks `response.trimStart().startsWith("data:")`, but this response begins with `"event: response.created"`, so the heuristic returns false. As a result, playback won't set `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, the SSE streaming simulation (chunked delivery + `Cache-Control`/`Connection` headers) won't engage, and the adapter receives the full body in a single non-streamed `Response`. This PR wraps the history-session resume block in `withLoadingDialog` to eliminate the idle-looking gap between closing the history picker and completing session hydration. The change is contained to a single hook file and reuses the existing `withShownDialog` helper, which guarantees the dialog is closed in `finally` whether the resume succeeds or throws. - The entire resume-and-hydrate block (including the empty-session error branch and the success path that calls `session.clearEntries`, `session.appendEntry`, and `setAppView`) is moved inside the loading-dialog callback unchanged. - Error handling is preserved: `onResumeSession` failures still propagate out of `withLoadingDialog` and are caught by the outer `try/catch`, and `refocusTextarea()` is still called unconditionally after the block.

The entire resume-and-hydrate sequence is moved intact into `withLoadingDialog`, which closes the dialog in `finally` in all code paths. Error propagation to the outer `catch` and the unconditional `refocusTextarea()` call are both preserved. The underlying `withShownDialog` helper has existing unit-test coverage for both success and failure cleanup, so the new call site inherits that guarantee. No files require special attention.

Greptile Summary

This PR hardens the Slack connector's reliability by adding process-local TTL caches (10 min) and in-flight deduplication for both `users.info` (participant labels) and `users.list` (outbound mention resolution), fixing bot-mention stripping on raw Slack events, introducing a typed `RuntimeSessionNotFoundError` for structured stale-session recovery, and adding `bindingScope` to keep Slack channel threads from sharing bindings across different thread IDs. - **Caching & rate-limit mitigation**: `fetchCachedSlackUserLabel` wraps `users.info` with `withSlackTeamBotToken` and caches per team+user; `fetchCachedSlackUsers` caches `users.list` per team but fetches via the default `webClient` without `withBotToken` — unlike the `users.info` path, this can use the wrong installation token in multi-workspace OAuth deployments. - **Stale-session recovery**: `handleConnectorUserTurn` now catches `RuntimeSessionNotFoundError`, calls `clearSession`, starts a replacement session, and retries the turn once; `onReplyFailed` fires only if the retry itself fails, and `createEmptyRuntimeReplyResolver` is re-evaluated with the fresh session ID. - **Thread binding scope**: `ConnectorBindingScope` ("thread" | "participant") gates key resolution and lookup so Slack channel threads are keyed by thread ID and DMs are keyed by participant, preventing cross-thread binding collisions.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge for single-workspace Slack deployments; multi-workspace OAuth installs will silently lose outbound mention resolution due to the missing token swap in the users.list path. The stale-session recovery, bindingScope partitioning, mention-stripping, and structured error propagation are all well-tested and correct. The one confirmed defect is that fetchCachedSlackUsers only accepts Pick and therefore cannot call withSlackTeamBotToken before invoking users.list. In multi-workspace OAuth mode the webClient holds a single default token, so the call either fails for the target team or returns the wrong credentials. The error is swallowed as a warning — unlike the users.info path which correctly wraps with withSlackTeamBotToken. apps/cli/src/connectors/adapters/slack.ts — specifically fetchCachedSlackUsers, resolveSlackOutboundMentions, and postSlackResolvedText, which need getInstallation/withBotToken wired through for multi-workspace correctness.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/cli/src/connectors/adapters/slack.ts | Major additions: TTL caches + in-flight deduplication for users.info and users.list, stripLeadingSlackMention / resolveSlackTurnText, formatSlackRuntimeText with context envelope, resolveSlackOutboundMentions + postSlackResolvedText, --token alias, bindingScope propagation. users.list is fetched without the team-specific withBotToken wrapper that users.info correctly uses, breaking multi-workspace mention resolution. | | apps/cli/src/connectors/connector-host.ts | Stale-session recovery refactored: postRuntimeReply extracted as inner closure, structured isConnectorRuntimeSessionMissingError check, clearSession + replacement session start + retry with re-created resolveFallbackText. notifyReplyFailed deferred to catch rather than inline onFailed callback. Logic is correct and well-tested. | | apps/cli/src/connectors/thread-bindings.ts | Adds ConnectorBindingScope (thread | participant), wires it through resolveThreadBindingKey, findBindingForThread, readBindingForThread, persistThreadBinding, loadThreadState, and mergeThreadState. Thread-scoped bindings now key by thread ID instead of participant key, fixing cross-thread pollution for Slack channels. | | sdk/packages/core/src/runtime/session-errors.ts | New file: RuntimeSessionNotFoundError typed error class with code = session_not_found and isRuntimeSessionNotFoundError predicate. Replaces fragile string-matching at call sites. | | sdk/packages/core/src/hub/server/handlers/run-handlers.ts | handleSessionInput now intercepts RuntimeSessionNotFoundError and returns a structured errorReply with RUNTIME_SESSION_NOT_FOUND_ERROR_CODE, so the code survives RPC serialisation and isRuntimeSessionNotFoundError can match it on the client side. | | apps/cli/src/connectors/adapters/slack.test.ts | New tests for --token alias, bindingScope DM vs channel scoping, mention stripping, formatSlackRuntimeText, cached participant labels, outbound mention resolution (unique, ambiguous, multi-word), users.list caching, and postSlackResolvedText end-to-end. | | apps/cli/src/connectors/connector-host.test.ts | New tests: transport-addressed slash command after mention stripping; stale-session replacement for both structured and wrapped error variants; onReplyFailed fires only after retry failure; Discord empty-runtime fallback uses fresh-session id after recovery. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Slack participant SlackConnector participant ConnectorHost participant SessionRuntime participant SlackAPI Slack->>SlackConnector: onNewMention / onSubscribedMessage SlackConnector->>SlackConnector: resolveSlackTurnText (strip bot mention from raw text) SlackConnector->>SlackConnector: "persistSlackThreadContext (bindingScope=thread|participant)" SlackConnector->>SlackAPI: users.info (fetchCachedSlackUserLabel, withBotToken) SlackAPI-->>SlackConnector: participantLabel (cached 10 min) SlackConnector->>ConnectorHost: handleConnectorUserTurn(text, addressedToBot) ConnectorHost->>ConnectorHost: "commandAddressedToBot = addressedToBot OR isCommandAddressedToThisBot" ConnectorHost->>SessionRuntime: postRuntimeReply(sessionId, request) alt Session found SessionRuntime-->>ConnectorHost: reply text ConnectorHost->>SlackConnector: postFinalReply(text) SlackConnector->>SlackAPI: users.list (fetchCachedSlackUsers, webClient only) SlackAPI-->>SlackConnector: member list (cached 10 min) SlackConnector->>SlackConnector: resolveSlackOutboundMentions SlackConnector->>Slack: thread.post(resolvedText) else Session not found (stale) SessionRuntime-->>ConnectorHost: RuntimeSessionNotFoundError ConnectorHost->>SessionRuntime: clearSession(staleId) ConnectorHost->>SessionRuntime: getOrCreateSessionId (new session) ConnectorHost->>SessionRuntime: postRuntimeReply(freshId, request) SessionRuntime-->>ConnectorHost: reply text ConnectorHost->>Slack: thread.post(reply) end ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 2 apps/cli/src/connectors/adapters/slack.ts:598-621 **`users.list` fetched without team-specific bot token** `fetchCachedSlackUsers` only accepts `Pick`, so it calls `users.list` with whatever token the default `webClient` was initialised with. In contrast, `fetchCachedSlackUserLabel` wraps its `users.info` call inside `withSlackTeamBotToken`, swapping in the correct per-team installation token. For multi-workspace OAuth deployments, the default `webClient` token may not have `users:read` for the target team, causing the `users.list` call to fail. The failure is silently swallowed and logged as a warning, so outbound mention resolution degrades to returning the unresolved text — but there is no visible indication to the sender that mentions were skipped. The fix is to pass `getInstallation` and `withBotToken` down through `resolveSlackOutboundMentions` / `fetchCachedSlackUsers` (matching the signature of `fetchCachedSlackUserLabel`) and wrap `fetchSlackUsers` with `withSlackTeamBotToken` the same way `fetchSlackUserLabel` is wrapped. ### Issue 2 of 2 apps/cli/src/connectors/adapters/slack.ts:614-624 **`undefined` participant label not written to the TTL cache** When `withSlackTeamBotToken → fetchSlackUserLabel` resolves to `undefined` (the user exists but has no `display_name`, `real_name`, or `name` in their profile), the result is intentionally skipped by `if (label) { writeSlackCache(...) }`. The pending entry is still removed in `finally`, so the next call will re-execute `users.info` for the same user — effectively bypassing the cache for profile-less users. Consider caching a sentinel value (e.g., the raw `userId` string) so that repeated messages from a user with no Slack profile info do not re-hit the API on every turn. `````

@greptileai please re-review after addressing the two Slack API rate-limit concerns.

Current head: `8660e6a2ce`

What changed:
- Added a process-local TTL cache for Slack `users.info` labels, keyed by team/user.
- `persistSlackThreadContext` now loads existing thread state before resolving participant profile labels, so it reuses a stored participant label when the same user is sending again instead of calling `users.info` on every inbound Slack message.
- Added in-flight request sharing for participant label fetches to avoid duplicate `users.info` calls under concurrent turns.
- Added a process-local TTL cache for Slack `users.list`, keyed by team, and in-flight request sharing for outbound mention resolution.
- Outbound reply mention resolution now passes the Slack team ID into the cache key, so repeated replies in the same workspace do not re-fetch the full member list.
- Added regressions for cached participant labels and cached member-list mention resolution.
