Greptile Summary

This PR attempts to remediate four CVEs in `marked`, `axios`, and `diff` by upgrading the root `marked` dependency and adding an `axios` override in `sdk/package.json`. The `axios` fix (prototype pollution + HTTPS proxy bypass) is applied correctly via the `overrides` mechanism, but the `marked` and `diff` mitigations are incomplete. - `@cline/cli` still resolves to `marked@15.0.12` (vulnerable to AIKIDO-2026-10452 ReDoS) because no `overrides` entry was added for `marked` and `sdk/apps/cli/package.json` still declares `\"marked\": \"^15.0.12\"`. - `diff@8.0.2` is still present in the lockfile and is confirmed vulnerable to CVE-2026-24001 (fix requires `>=8.0.3`); no override for `diff` was added despite this being the CVE listed first in the PR description. - `@opentui/core`'s transitive `marked` resolution sits at `17.0.1`, below the patched baseline, for the same reason.

Confidence Score: 2/5

Merging this PR leaves two of the four claimed CVE fixes absent — the CLI ships the vulnerable marked version and the diff DoS hole is entirely untouched. The axios remediation is correct and complete. However, @cline/cli continues to bundle marked@15.0.12 (ReDoS-vulnerable) because the marked override was never added to sdk/package.json, and diff@8.0.2 — explicitly called out as the package behind CVE-2026-24001 — remains unpatched with no override entry. Two of the four advertised security fixes are not actually delivered by this PR as written. sdk/package.json needs a marked override entry matching the pattern already used for axios. sdk/bun.lock confirms both the @cline/cli sub-resolution hole and the unpatched diff@8.0.2.

Security Review

 - **CVE-2026-24001 (diff DoS) not fixed**: `sdk/bun.lock` retains `diff@8.0.2`, which falls in the vulnerable range `>=6.0.0 <8.0.3`. A root override for `diff@8.0.3` is required. - **AIKIDO-2026-10452 (marked ReDoS) partially fixed**: The `@cline/cli` workspace still resolves `marked@15.0.12` (vulnerable) because no `overrides` entry was added for `marked`. Users running the CLI are still exposed. - **`@opentui/core` transitive marked exposure**: `@opentui/core/marked` resolves to `17.0.1`, below the intended `17.0.5` fix baseline. - **axios fixes are correctly applied** via the `overrides` block (prototype pollution AIKIDO-2026-10822 and HTTPS proxy bypass AIKIDO-2026-10823).

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/bun.lock | Updates marked (root) and forces axios override, but @cline/cli still resolves to vulnerable marked@15.0.12, diff@8.0.2 (CVE-2026-24001) is unpatched, and @opentui/core's marked sub-resolution remains at 17.0.1 | | sdk/package.json | Adds axios override correctly, but omits a corresponding marked override which would have prevented the @cline/cli and @opentui/core sub-resolution holes |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[sdk/package.json overrides] -->|axios 1.16.1 FIXED| B[All workspaces use axios 1.16.1] A -->|marked NOT overridden INCOMPLETE| C{marked per workspace} C -->|root workspace| D[marked 17.0.5 OK] C -->|cline-cli| E[marked 15.0.12 VULNERABLE] C -->|cline-code| F[marked 17.0.6 OK] C -->|opentui-core| G[marked 17.0.1 BELOW FIX] H[diff package] -->|diff 8.0.2 CVE-2026-24001| I[No override added VULNERABLE] ```

Comments Outside Diff (2)

 1. `sdk/bun.lock`, line 1849 ([link](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/ddc57d696209e93733aceda158c3cde941e4bab7/sdk/bun.lock#L1849)) **CVE-2026-24001 not remediated — `diff@8.0.2` still vulnerable** The lockfile still resolves `diff` to `8.0.2`, which falls in the affected range (`>=6.0.0 <8.0.3`). The fix version is `8.0.3`. The PR title and description claim this CVE is resolved ("@opentui/core" depends on `diff` internally), but neither `diff` itself was overridden nor was `@opentui/core` upgraded. An override of `"diff": "8.0.3"` in `sdk/package.json` is needed — exactly as was done for `axios` — to force the patched version across all transitive consumers.

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR is a security-focused dependency update that bumps 15+ packages via one manifest change (`axios` from `1.15.2` to `1.16.1`) and corresponding `package-lock.json` resolutions, resolving 47 CVEs covering FTP command injection, XML injection, ReDoS, WebSocket memory disclosure, HTTPS proxy misconfiguration, and prototype pollution issues. - **`package.json`**: `axios` exact-pin bumped to `1.16.1`; the exact-pin style is preserved correctly. The new `axios` version also pulls in nested copies of `agent-base@6.0.2` and `https-proxy-agent@5.0.1` to properly tunnel HTTPS traffic through proxies. - **`package-lock.json`**: ~20 packages advanced (including `basic-ftp`, `@xmldom/xmldom`, `hono`, `ws`, `zod 4.x`, `fast-xml-parser`, `qs`, `brace-expansion`, etc.). Two brand-new transitive packages appear — `@nodable/entities@2.1.0` and `xml-naming@0.1.0` — as dependencies of `fast-xml-parser@5.7.3`; 20+ `@rollup/*` native binary entries shed their `"peer": true` marker (cosmetic npm artefact, no runtime impact).

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge — all changes are version bumps to patched releases with no application logic changes. The manifest change is a single exact-pin bump for axios, and every other change is a transitive lockfile resolution. Two brand-new packages (@nodable/entities, xml-naming) enter the dependency tree as part of the fast-xml-parser upgrade; while both are MIT-licensed with no known CVEs, they are untested additions worth a quick check before merging. The @rollup native binary peer:true removals are cosmetic. Several upgraded packages carry documented behavioral breaking changes (notably zod 4.4.x tuple/object semantics and axios 1.16.x fetch-adapter limits), which could surface at runtime even if no application code changed today. package-lock.json — verify the new @nodable/entities and xml-naming packages are trustworthy; review the zod 4.4.x and axios 1.16.x breaking-change notes against actual usage in the codebase.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | package.json | Single-line change: exact-pin for axios bumped from 1.15.2 to 1.16.1. No other manifest changes. | | package-lock.json | Lockfile advances ~20 packages to fix 47 CVEs; introduces two new transitive packages (@nodable/entities, xml-naming) and nested axios-specific agent/proxy packages; 20+ @rollup native binary entries drop their peer:true marker as a cosmetic npm side-effect. |

This PR adds `deepseek-v4-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro` to the DeepSeek model registry and extends the existing thinking-model code path in the DeepSeek handler to cover them. Pricing, context window (1M), and max output (384K) values were verified against the official DeepSeek API docs. - **`src/shared/api.ts`**: Two new model entries inserted ahead of the existing `deepseek-chat`/`deepseek-reasoner` entries. `inputPrice` is correctly set to `0` (matching the existing comment pattern since DeepSeek reports all input as cache hits/misses), and all numeric values match the published DeepSeek V4 pricing. - **`src/core/api/providers/deepseek.ts`**: The old `isDeepseekReasoner` boolean is replaced by `isDeepSeekThinkingModel`, which adds explicit equality checks for the two new IDs. The temperature suppression is updated to key off this same flag, so V4 thinking models are treated identically to `deepseek-reasoner` for request formatting.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change is additive, existing model IDs and the default are untouched, and the new V4 entries slot into an already-proven code path. Both changed files make narrow, additive additions. The model specs (context window, max output, pricing) were verified against DeepSeek's official docs and are correct. The handler change replaces a single-model boolean with an explicit multi-model check using equality operators, which is no more permissive than the original and avoids accidentally matching future model IDs. Greptile Summary

This PR adds a `maxOutputBytes` cap (defaulting to 1 MB) to the `search_codebase` tool executor to prevent prompt-overflow failures when searches return very large formatted results. The implementation mirrors the existing `run_commands` behavior: a `truncateOutput` helper measures UTF-8 byte length, slices at the buffer level for multi-byte safety, strips any trailing replacement character from a mid-sequence cut, and appends an explicit truncation notice. - Added `maxOutputBytes?: number` to `SearchExecutorOptions` with a 1 MB default, and wired it through `createSearchExecutor`. - Added `truncateOutput(output, maxOutputBytes)` that performs byte-accurate truncation using `Buffer.subarray` and decodes back to a UTF-8 string. - Applied `truncateOutput` to all three return sites in the executor (ripgrep path, fallback "no results" path, and fallback results path).

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change is additive, all three return paths are covered, and existing callers need no updates. The truncation helper uses buffer-level slicing for byte-accurate cuts, strips the trailing replacement character from mid-sequence cuts, and leaves all output under the cap untouched. Normal-sized search results pass through unchanged, and the 1 MB default keeps the behavior consistent with the existing run_commands cap. The previously noted UTF-16 vs UTF-8 discrepancy was already resolved in the current commit. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/executors/search.ts | Adds byte-accurate output truncation to all three return paths; implementation is correct and consistent with the run_commands pattern. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[createSearchExecutor called] --> B{ripgrep available?} B -- yes --> C[searchWithRipgrep] C --> D{rgMatches returned?} D -- yes --> E[Format result lines] E --> F[truncateOutput - rg path] D -- no --> G[Fallback: manual regex] B -- no --> G G --> H{matches.length == 0?} H -- yes --> I[truncateOutput - no results] H -- no --> J[Format result lines] J --> K[truncateOutput - fallback path] F --> L{outputSize <= maxOutputBytes?} I --> L K --> L L -- yes --> M[Return output as-is] L -- no --> N[Buffer.subarray to maxOutputBytes] N --> O[toString utf8] O --> P[Strip trailing U+FFFD] P --> Q[Append truncation notice] Q --> R[Return truncated output] ``` Reviews (3): Last reviewed commit: ["fix: make search output truncation byte ..."](https://github.com/cline/cline/commit/5ebac3862803b36ebfc8d1b40aa3ecf387e477ba) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=33696076)

This PR adds two new models to the SAP AI Core provider: `gpt-5.5` (OpenAI GPT-5.5) and `nova-core` (SAP Nova Core). Both are registered in `sapAiCoreModels` with their capabilities and routed to the correct API paths. - `gpt-5.5` is added to `openAIModels` and to the reasoning-style payload list (where `max_tokens` and `temperature` are stripped), consistent with how other GPT-5 series models are handled on SAP AI Core. - `nova-core` is added to `hostedModels`, routing it to the OpenAI-compatible `chat/completions` endpoint with `max_tokens` and `temperature`, mirroring the Mistral models already in that group.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge; changes are additive model registrations following well-established patterns already in place for other SAP AI Core models. Both new entries mirror existing models closely — gpt-5.5 copies the gpt-5.4 config and slot, nova-core copies the Mistral hosted-model pattern. No existing logic is altered. The main uncertainty is whether the capability metadata (context window, image support) for gpt-5.5 and nova-core exactly matches SAP's published specs, since those values can't be verified from the code alone. No files require special attention; both changed files contain only additive data entries.

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a schema validation rejection that occurred when models like GPT-5.5 emit a `timeout` field alongside `commands` in `run_commands` payloads. The fix makes `timeout` a first-class optional field on both `RunCommandsInputSchema` and `StructuredCommandsInputSchema`, switches both schemas to `z.looseObject` for forward-compatibility with other unknown keys, and wires the clamped timeout value into the per-command `withTimeout` call. - **Schema change** (`schemas.ts`): `z.object` → `z.looseObject` on both run-commands schemas; adds `timeout: z.number().optional()` and exports `RUN_COMMANDS_TIMEOUT_MIN_MS`/`RUN_COMMANDS_TIMEOUT_MAX_MS` constants. - **Execution change** (`definitions.ts`): Adds `resolveRunCommandsTimeoutMs` helper that reads and clamps the per-call timeout from raw input, applies it in both `createBashTool` and `createWindowsShellTool`, and raises the outer watchdog to `max(defaultTimeoutMs * 2, MAX + 30 s)` so the watchdog never fires before the inner limit. - **Tests** (`definitions.test.ts`): Comprehensive coverage via the production `zodToJsonSchema` round-trip path, including clamping edge cases and the Windows shell variant.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge; the change is narrowly scoped to schema loosening and timeout wiring with no effect on existing call paths that omit timeout. Both the schema change (looseObject + explicit timeout field) and the runtime clamping logic are straightforward and well-defended. The outer watchdog is correctly sized so it can never race the inner per-command limit. Tests exercise the production zodToJsonSchema round-trip path — the exact failure mode being fixed — and cover clamping boundaries and both tool variants. No existing behaviour changes for callers that do not supply timeout. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/schemas.ts | Switches both run-commands schemas to z.looseObject and adds the explicit optional timeout field with exported min/max constants; changes are minimal and well-scoped. | | sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/definitions.ts | Adds resolveRunCommandsTimeoutMs helper and applies the clamped per-call timeout in both createBashTool and createWindowsShellTool; outer watchdog correctly raised to guarantee inner timeout fires first. | | sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/definitions.test.ts | New timeout-handling describe block covers the AI-SDK schema round-trip, clamping, per-command timeout enforcement, and the Windows shell variant; imports zodToJsonSchema correctly from @cline/shared. |

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes temperature incorrectly being sent for Claude Opus adaptive-thinking models that are accessed via application inference profile ARNs with arbitrary user-defined names (e.g. `my-company-profile`). Because such ARNs don't embed the model version string, the old `isClaudeOpusAdaptiveThinkingModel(rawArn)` check would always return false, causing temperature to be included even when it must be omitted. - **`getModel()`** is updated to return `{ id: baseModel }` (the known base model identifier) instead of `{ id: rawArn }` when a valid `awsBedrockCustomModelBaseId` is configured, so model identity for detection is always a readable string like `anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-...`. - **`getModelId()`** gets a new early-return branch for custom models that returns `apiModelId` (the raw ARN) directly, keeping the wire call correct while letting `getModel().id` serve detection only. - Both `isAdaptiveThinkingModel` computations now receive `model.id` instead of the raw ARN or cross-region-prefixed ID, making detection consistent and correct across all custom-model scenarios.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change cleanly separates the wire model ID (raw ARN) from the detection model ID (base model), and both detection call sites now operate on the correct identifier. The logic is straightforward: getModel() returns the base model identifier for detection, getModelId() returns the raw ARN for the API call, and both isAdaptiveThinkingModel checks now receive the base model ID. The wire modelId field on the Bedrock command is unchanged. The cross-region inference path for standard models is unaffected. No regressions are apparent. No files require special attention.

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes two VS Code nightly publish workflows that broke after the extension was moved under `apps/vscode` in a monorepo migration. No application code is changed. - **`ext-vscode-publish-nightly.yml`**: Restores `pull-requests: read` to the caller job that invokes the reusable test workflow (which declares this permission internally), preventing a GitHub Actions startup-validation failure. Adds `defaults: run: working-directory: apps/vscode` to the publish job so `npm ci` and the marketplace publish script run from the right sub-directory; the git tagging step explicitly overrides back to `github.workspace`. - **`ext-vscode-publish-nightly-sdk.yml`**: Removes the hard-coded `apps/vscode` job default (which did not exist on the pinned `dpc/sdk-migration-simpler-login` branch) and adds a shell probe step that resolves the VS Code package directory at runtime, handling both the old root layout and the new `apps/vscode` layout transparently.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Both workflow files are safe to merge; the changes are minimal, well-scoped, and directly address the described failures without touching any application code. The permission fix is a one-liner that matches exactly what the called reusable workflow declares it needs. The dynamic path resolution in the SDK workflow correctly prioritises the new `apps/vscode` layout while falling back gracefully to the old root layout used by the pinned branch, and the shell probe is straightforward with a proper error exit. All npm steps use the resolved path, and the git tagging step in the regular nightly correctly overrides back to the workspace root. No edge cases or regressions were identified. body:
Greptile Summary

This PR promotes `updateSessionModel` to `updateSessionConnection` across the full stack — host API, persistence layer, hub transport, and pending-prompt queue — so that per-turn provider/model/credential/reasoning overrides are both applied at runtime and persisted to the session record and manifest file. - **Host API rename:** `SessionModelRuntimeService.updateSessionModel(id, modelId)` → `SessionConnectionRuntimeService.updateSessionConnection(id, connection)`, with a new `applySessionConnectionUpdate` helper that clears stale credentials when the provider changes, calls `buildProviderConfig` to hydrate stored credentials for the new provider, then propagates the resolved overrides to the agent, delegated-config provider, and team runtime before optionally writing the manifest. - **Hub transport parsing:** `parseConnectionUpdate` validates all scalar fields from the wire payload (strings, booleans, numbers, enum values) before forwarding them to `runTurn`; `providerConfig` is the one field accepted without per-field structural validation. - **Persistence alignment:** `updateSession` in both the SQL and file adapters gains `provider` and `model` columns, and the manifest update path in `UnifiedSessionPersistenceService` is extended to reflect them.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge after addressing the unvalidated providerConfig pass-through from the wire protocol. The core credential-clearing logic and persistence path are well-structured and covered by new tests. The one concrete defect is in the hub handler: providerConfig is the only field in parseConnectionUpdate that reaches applySessionConnectionUpdate without any structural validation, meaning a caller can inject an arbitrary object that gets cast directly into the session's provider configuration. Every other field has an explicit type guard. This gap could cause provider initialisation to crash or silently use wrong credentials on a turn. sdk/packages/core/src/hub/server/handlers/run-handlers.ts — parseConnectionUpdate accepts providerConfig as unvalidated unknown while all other fields are type-guarded.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/core/src/hub/server/handlers/run-handlers.ts | Adds parseConnectionUpdate with thorough validation for all scalar fields, but providerConfig is accepted as unvalidated unknown from the wire protocol. | | sdk/packages/core/src/runtime/host/local-runtime-host.ts | New applySessionConnectionUpdate method correctly gates credential clearing on providerChanged, hydrates from stored settings via buildProviderConfig, and propagates to agent/team. The logic change is minimal and well-reasoned: `reasoningDisabled` is derived from `normalizedReasoningEffort` before the `supportsReasoningEffort` gate, so the 'none' intent is honoured even for models that don't appear in the effort-support allowlist. Both transforms are updated symmetrically, the fix handles the `reasoningEffort === undefined` edge case correctly (yields `false`, leaving existing behaviour intact), and the new and extended tests exercise the exact failure scenario reported. This PR fixes two related gaps that prevented Qwen 3.7 Max from displaying prompt-cache support in the Cline VSCode extension: the model was missing from the explicit `cache_control` injection list, and `refreshClineModels` only enabled `supportsPromptCache` for hard-coded provider families rather than reading it from the API's cache pricing fields. - **`openrouter-stream.ts`**: `qwen/qwen3.7-max` is added to `openRouterExplicitCacheControlModelIds` so that `cache_control: { type: \"ephemeral\" }` blocks are appended to request messages, matching the existing treatment of other Qwen models. - **`refreshClineModels.ts`**: A pre-switch check now sets `supportsPromptCache = true` for any model where the Cline API returns a non-`undefined` `cacheReadsPrice` or `cacheWritesPrice`, making cache capability data-driven rather than requiring a new hard-coded switch case per model. - **Tests**: New unit tests cover both changes — verifying the cache pricing fields and flag for `qwen/qwen3.7-max`, and confirming the model ID is not mutated by the handler.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — changes are small and well-tested, with no impact on existing model handling logic. Both changes are narrowly scoped: a single model ID added to a constant set, and a four-line data-driven guard inserted before a switch that already handles known overrides. The new generic rule does not conflict with any switch case — it runs first and the switch simply re-affirms or overrides the flag for models with hard-coded prices. New tests verify the model ID is not mutated through getModel(), cache pricing fields are correctly mapped, and cache_control blocks are injected for requests. No existing behaviour is altered for any other model family. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/vscode/src/core/api/transform/openrouter-stream.ts | Adds qwen/qwen3.7-max to the explicit cache-control model set; single-line change, low risk. | | apps/vscode/src/core/controller/models/refreshClineModels.ts | Adds generic pre-switch rule that marks any model with API-returned cache pricing as prompt-cache capable; interacts cleanly with the existing switch overrides. | | apps/vscode/src/core/controller/models/__tests__/refreshClineModels.test.ts | New test file verifying supportsPromptCache, cacheReadsPrice, and cacheWritesPrice mapping from Cline API response for qwen/qwen3.7-max. | | apps/vscode/src/core/api/providers/__tests__/cline.test.ts | New test case confirms cache_control blocks are injected for qwen/qwen3.7-max and that the model ID is not mutated through getModel(). | | apps/vscode/src/core/api/transform/__tests__/openrouter-stream.test.ts | Expands existing cache-control test to loop over both qwen/qwen3.6-plus and qwen/qwen3.7-max; straightforward extension. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[Cline API returns model list] --> B[parsePrice extracts cacheReadsPrice and cacheWritesPrice] B --> C{Either price defined?} C -- Yes --> D[supportsPromptCache = true] C -- No --> E[supportsPromptCache = false] D --> F{Switch on model ID} E --> F F -- Anthropic or DeepSeek cases --> G[Override with hardcoded prices] F -- openai or google default --> H[Re-read prices from API] F -- qwen3.7-max and others --> I[No override - generic flag kept] G --> J[Store in models map] H --> J I --> J J --> K{needsExplicitCacheControl?} K -- Yes: includes qwen3.7-max --> L[Inject cache_control into messages] K -- No --> M[Send messages as-is] ``` Reviews (2): Last reviewed commit: ["fix(vscode): show Qwen 3.7 Max cache sup..."](https://github.com/cline/cline/commit/7078c5e0f9bd6b8c98bd2ad96b008753de939dbc) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=34052342)

Greptile Summary

This PR upgrades three npm packages in the `webview-ui` workspace to resolve 11 security advisories: `dompurify` (`^3.3.3` → `^3.4.2`, resolving to 3.4.5), `mermaid` (`11.12.3` → `11.15.0`), and transitively `lodash-es` (`4.17.23` → `4.18.1` via the new `dagre-d3-es` sub-dependency). Changes are limited to `package.json` and `package-lock.json`. - **dompurify** bumped to 3.4.5 to address 6 CVEs covering prototype pollution bypass, template expression sanitization, `FORBID_TAGS` inconsistency, type-validation bypass, and URI-scheme validation gaps for function-predicate `ADD_ATTR`. - **mermaid** advanced from 11.12.3 to 11.15.0 to address 4 CVEs (CSS injection, DOM injection, and Gantt DoS); `lodash-es` resolves to 4.18.1 (via `dagre-d3-es`) fixing a prototype pollution bypass in `_.unset`/`_.omit`. - The lockfile regeneration also marks ~34 packages with `\"peer\": true` metadata, which is a harmless side-effect of running `npm install --package-lock-only` with a newer npm version and has no runtime impact.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — all three package upgrades are consistent between manifest and lockfile, and no application code targets the internal mermaid IDs or flowchart styling that changed in the intermediate releases. Both changed files are dependency manifests with no logic changes. The resolved versions in the lockfile match the declared constraints, the single dompurify entry at 3.4.5 is shared correctly between the direct dependency and mermaid's transitive requirement, and the removal of langium/chevrotain packages is consistent with mermaid 11.15.0's parser rewrite. The existing MermaidBlock.tsx component does not select on internal element IDs, so the v11.14.0 ID-prefix breaking change poses no regression risk. No files require special attention. The lockfile is large but the critical entries (dompurify, mermaid, lodash-es) all resolve correctly.

Greptile Summary

This PR upgrades 16 npm packages in `apps/vscode` (touching `package.json` and `package-lock.json`) to remediate 48 CVEs spanning XML injection, DoS, CRLF injection, prototype pollution, and credential-leakage classes of vulnerabilities. Most updates are transitive lockfile-only bumps, but several direct dependencies receive explicit manifest changes. - `@opentelemetry/sdk-node` and `@opentelemetry/exporter-prometheus` are jumped from `^0.56.0` to `^0.217.0` while six sibling experimental packages (`sdk-logs`, five OTLP exporters) remain at `^0.56.0`, creating a large version skew that can cause duplicate SDK registration and silent data loss at runtime. - `zod` is bumped across a major version boundary (`^3.24.2` → `^4.4.0`) with documented breaking changes, but the six source files that import zod were not updated alongside this change. - `axios`, `puppeteer-core`, `puppeteer-chromium-resolver`, and numerous transitive packages receive well-scoped security patches with low breakage risk.

Confidence Score: 3/5

Not safe to merge as-is — two of the direct-dependency bumps are likely to break the running extension without code changes to accompany them. The OpenTelemetry experimental packages are tightly coupled: sdk-node at 0.217 acts as the wiring layer for sdk-logs, the OTLP log/metric exporters, and related packages, all of which remain declared at ^0.56.0 in the manifest. This mismatch produces duplicate, incompatible SDK registrations against the shared global context, and metrics or log data can be silently dropped. Separately, zod crossed a major version boundary (3 → 4) with several documented behavioral breaks, but none of the six consuming source files were touched. Both issues would surface as runtime failures in the shipped extension rather than build-time errors. apps/vscode/package.json — specifically the opentelemetry experimental package version declarations and the zod version range.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/vscode/package.json | Bumps 8 direct dependencies (axios, zod, opentelemetry x2, puppeteer x2) to fix security CVEs; zod 3→4 major bump and OTel experimental package version skew (0.56 vs 0.217) are likely runtime-breaking without accompanying source changes. | | apps/vscode/package-lock.json | Lockfile regenerated to resolve 24 package version changes for transitive CVE fixes; reflects the direct dependency changes in package.json. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[apps/vscode/package.json] --> B[Direct dep bumps] A --> C[Transitive lockfile fixes] B --> D["@opentelemetry/sdk-node\n0.56 → 0.217"] B --> E["@opentelemetry/exporter-prometheus\n0.56 → 0.217"] B --> F["zod\n^3.24.2 → ^4.4.0 ⚠️"] B --> G["axios\n1.15.2 → 1.16.1"] B --> H["puppeteer-core\n^23.4.0 → ^24.2.0"] B --> I["puppeteer-chromium-resolver\n^23.0.0 → ^24.0.0"] D -->|"requires compatible\n0.200+ peers"| J["@opentelemetry/sdk-logs ^0.56.0\n@opentelemetry/exporter-logs-otlp-* ^0.56.0\n@opentelemetry/exporter-metrics-otlp-* ^0.56.0"] J -->|"Version skew ⚠️\nDuplicate SDK instances"| K[Runtime: silent metric/log drops] F -->|"Breaking changes\nin 6 source files"| L["schema.ts, McpHub.ts\nAgentConfigLoader.ts, oauth.ts\ntypes.ts, schemas.ts"] L -->|"No source updates"| M[Runtime: validation failures] C --> N["@xmldom/xmldom 0.8.11→0.8.13\nbasic-ftp 5.2.0→5.3.1\nfast-xml-parser 5.5.8→5.7.3\npath-to-regexp 8.3.0→8.4.2\nws 8.19.0→8.21.0\nhono 4.12.9→4.12.23\nand 15 more..."] ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 2 apps/vscode/package.json:513-520 **OpenTelemetry experimental package version skew** `@opentelemetry/sdk-node` and `@opentelemetry/exporter-prometheus` were bumped to `^0.217.0`, but six related experimental packages remain pinned at the old `^0.56.0` range: `sdk-logs`, `exporter-logs-otlp-grpc`, `exporter-logs-otlp-http`, `exporter-logs-otlp-proto`, `exporter-metrics-otlp-grpc`, `exporter-metrics-otlp-http`, and `exporter-metrics-otlp-proto`. `sdk-node` is the orchestrating entry point that wires all these packages together; at 0.217 it requires its companion packages to be at compatible 0.200+ versions. npm will install the stale 0.56.x copies as direct dependencies and a newer copy as a transitive peer of `sdk-node`, resulting in two incompatible SDK instances registering against the same global `@opentelemetry/api` context — causing metrics and log processors to silently drop data or throw at runtime. ### Issue 2 of 2 apps/vscode/package.json:586 **Zod major-version bump without application code update** `zod` is upgraded from `^3.24.2` to `^4.4.0`, a major-version change with breaking behavior listed in the PR description: required object properties with `z.undefined()` now mandate the key be present in input; `.merge()` throws when the receiver has refinements; base64 validation rejects whitespace; and HTTP URL validation is stricter. There are six source files importing zod (`schema.ts`, `AgentConfigLoader.ts`, `types.ts`, `schemas.ts`, `McpHub.ts`, `oauth.ts`), none of which were updated in this PR. Any of these that rely on the changed behaviors will produce runtime validation failures or throw unexpected errors. `````

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR exposes `CLINE_PLUGIN_IMPORT_TIMEOUT_MS` as an environment-variable override for the plugin sandbox's import timeout, fixing Windows cold-start failures where the hardcoded 4000 ms was insufficient. The change is narrowly scoped to the import path; hook and contribution timeouts are intentionally unchanged. - `withTimeoutFallback` gains an optional `envVarName` parameter; the env var is only consulted when `options.importTimeoutMs` is not set, preserving the existing precedence (`options` > env > 4000 ms default). - A new regression test creates a permanently-hanging plugin module and confirms the 150 ms env-var timeout fires before the 3 s vitest ceiling, giving proof that the env override engages.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge; the change is small and additive with no behavioural change when the env var is absent. The core logic is correct and well-tested. The only noteworthy wrinkle is that Number.parseInt accepts trailing non-numeric characters (e.g. '4000ms' parses to 4000), so a malformed env value silently resolves to its numeric prefix instead of falling back to the default. This is unlikely to cause real problems in practice but is worth tightening. plugin-sandbox.ts deserves a second look at the parseInt vs Number choice.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/plugin/plugin-sandbox.ts | Adds optional `envVarName` parameter to `withTimeoutFallback` and wires `CLINE_PLUGIN_IMPORT_TIMEOUT_MS` for the import timeout path; hook/contribution timeouts are unchanged. Logic is correct but `parseInt` leniently accepts trailing non-numeric characters. | | sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/plugin/plugin-sandbox.test.ts | New regression test creates a permanently-hanging plugin module and verifies the 150 ms env-var timeout fires before the 3 s vitest ceiling; manual env save/restore works but `vi.stubEnv` would be more idiomatic. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A["withTimeoutFallback(timeoutMs, fallback, envVarName?)"] --> B{timeoutMs is number AND gt 0?} B -- Yes --> C[return timeoutMs] B -- No --> D{envVarName provided?} D -- No --> E[return fallback default] D -- Yes --> F[read process.env envVarName] F --> G{raw value exists?} G -- No --> E G -- Yes --> H[parseInt raw value] H --> I{isFinite AND gt 0?} I -- Yes --> J[return parsed env value] I -- No --> E style C fill:#90EE90 style J fill:#90EE90 style E fill:#FFD700 ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 2 sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/plugin/plugin-sandbox.test.ts:425-456 The test manually saves/restores `process.env.CLINE_PLUGIN_IMPORT_TIMEOUT_MS` via `previousEnv`. Since `vi` is already imported, `vi.stubEnv()` is the idiomatic Vitest pattern: it automatically rolls back the env entry after the test, even if the assertion throws before the `finally` block runs (which can't happen here, but it's more robust and removes the boilerplate). ```suggestion vi.stubEnv("CLINE_PLUGIN_IMPORT_TIMEOUT_MS", "150"); try { const pluginPath = join(envDir, "plugin-import-hang.mjs"); // Top-level await that never resolves — module import never // completes, so the initialize call must hit the timeout. await writeFile( pluginPath, [ "await new Promise(() => {});", "export default {", " name: 'sandbox-import-hang',", " manifest: { capabilities: ['tools'] },", "};", ].join("\n"), "utf8", ); // Set env override well below the 4000 ms hardcoded default. // If the env var isn't read, this test would block for ~4 s and // the per-test timeout (3000 ms below) would fail it. await expect( loadSandboxedPlugins({ pluginPaths: [pluginPath] }), ).rejects.toThrow(/timed out/i); } finally { vi.unstubAllEnvs(); await rm(envDir, { recursive: true, force: true }); } ``` ### Issue 2 of 2 sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/plugin/plugin-sandbox.ts:216-224 `Number.parseInt` silently accepts strings with trailing non-numeric characters — e.g. `"4000ms"` parses to `4000` rather than falling back to the hardcoded default. A user who typos the value as `CLINE_PLUGIN_IMPORT_TIMEOUT_MS=8000ms` would silently get `8000` instead of a predictable fallback. Using `Number()` paired with `Number.isInteger` rejects those malformed values. ```suggestion if (envVarName) { const raw = process.env[envVarName]; if (raw) { const parsed = Number(raw); if (Number.isInteger(parsed) && parsed > 0) { return parsed; } } } ``` `````

@abeatrix Quick follow-up — instead of standing up a full dev-CLI on Windows (PowerShell ↔ `bun` env-var interop fought me on the `CLINE_BUILD_ENV=foo bun ...` pattern), I ran the actual `plugin-sandbox.test.ts` suite directly on the Windows host that originally hit the 4s timeout. The full test file passes — including the regression I added for `CLINE_PLUGIN_IMPORT_TIMEOUT_MS`:

```
$ bun run test:unit -- src/extensions/plugin/plugin-sandbox.test.ts
 RUN  v4.1.7 C:/Users/35574/Desktop/private_projects/space/cline-fork-v2/sdk/packages/core

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  17 passed (17)
   Start at  13:59:23
   Duration  6.34s
```

(Windows 11 + Node 24.3.0 via nvm4w + bun 1.3.1 — same host config as the original #11065 report.)

Why this answers the Windows question: the new test sets `CLINE_PLUGIN_IMPORT_TIMEOUT_MS=150` and uses a top-level-await plugin module so the import literally cannot complete. vitest's per-test timeout is **3000 ms**. If the env override were silently ignored, the hardcoded 4000 ms default would trip vitest first → the test would fail. The test passing on Windows proves the env override is consulted (and respected) before the 4 s default would even apply. The `process.env[name]` path is platform-agnostic in Node, so this also implicitly covers the Linux/macOS surface.

For the production Windows install we hit originally, the user-facing fix is then: set `CLINE_PLUGIN_IMPORT_TIMEOUT_MS=30000` (or similar) at `cline` launch time, and the plugin sandbox will accept the slower cold-start window without forcing kernel/runtime changes upstream.

Let me know if you'd like the test added to a Windows matrix entry as well — I can spin a follow-up that wires it into the existing `Test (windows-latest, Node 24.x)` job.

Fixes a regression where the `routedGlmReasoningRule` was applying GLM-specific `reasoning: { exclude: true }` provider options to generic `openai-compatible` endpoints, which reject unknown fields. Greptile Summary

This PR fixes build-time OTEL environment variable injection by replacing optional chaining (`process?.env?.VARNAME`) with direct property access (`process.env.VARNAME`), which is the pattern bundlers (esbuild, webpack, Vite) recognise and replace with literal values at build time. A `!process.env` guard is added so the function gracefully returns a disabled config in environments where `process.env` is unavailable after bundling. - Removes `?.` optional chaining from all eight `process.env.OTEL_*` accesses so the bundler's string-literal substitution can fire correctly. - Adds a `!process.env` early-return guard; the guard should additionally include a `typeof process === \"undefined\"` check to avoid a `ReferenceError` in runtimes that lack a `process` polyfill entirely.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge; the core fix is correct and the only open question is a minor defensive-coding gap in the new guard. The removal of optional chaining is the right fix — bundlers match the literal process.env.VARNAME pattern, so the previous ?. syntax silently prevented all OTEL build-time substitutions from firing. The new !process.env guard is a reasonable safety net, but it does not protect against process itself being undefined, which is possible in webview/browser-like runtimes. That gap is unlikely to matter for the current Node.js hosts but is worth closing. sdk/packages/shared/src/services/telemetry-config.ts — specifically the !process.env guard on line 9.

This automated security PR upgrades 17 npm packages (both direct and transitive) to resolve 49 CVEs covering XML injection, CRLF injection, ReDoS, prototype pollution, and other vulnerabilities. All transitive-only fixes are lockfile-only; direct dependency changes touch `axios`, `undici`, `zod`, `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime`, `@aws-sdk/credential-providers`, `puppeteer-core`, and `puppeteer-chromium-resolver`. - **Security coverage**: Critical/high-severity CVEs resolved in `@xmldom/xmldom`, `basic-ftp`, `ws`, `path-to-regexp`, `hono`, `fast-xml-parser`, `axios`, and `follow-redirects`; medium/low CVEs resolved in `zod`, `undici`, `qs`, `ip-address`, `brace-expansion`, and others. - **Major version bumps**: `zod` jumps from v3 to v4 (`^3.24.2` → `^4.4.0`) and `puppeteer-core` jumps from v23 to v24 (`^23.4.0` → `^24.1.1`) — both without any corresponding source-code changes in this PR. - **Known partial fix**: `chromium-bidi@14.0.0` (pulled by puppeteer-core v24) hard-requires `zod@^3.24.1` and cannot be migrated; a v3 copy remains nested in the lockfile alongside the new v4 root.

The vast majority of changes are lockfile-only transitive resolutions that carry minimal risk. However, zod v3→v4 is a major API version with documented breaking changes, and the codebase's MCP schema file uses six instances of z.record(z.string()) (single-argument form) that were explicitly removed in early Zod v4 releases. Greptile Summary

This PR adds SDK support for reading a cross-tool global AGENTS instructions file at `~/.agents/AGENTS.md` and ensures that when both a global and a workspace `AGENTS.md` are loaded simultaneously, their fallback names (`"Global AGENTS.md"` / `"Workspace AGENTS.md"`) are source-aware so they receive distinct snapshot keys rather than clobbering each other. - `paths.ts` gains `AGENTS_RULES_FILE_NAME`, `resolveGlobalAgentsRulesPath()`, and includes the global path in `resolveRulesConfigSearchPaths()`. - `user-instruction-config-loader.ts` introduces `resolveRuleFallbackName()`, which compares resolved absolute paths to classify each `AGENTS.md` as workspace, global, or \"other\" before normalizing its ID. - Tests and docs are updated to cover the new path and the non-clobbering behaviour.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The production path-resolution and fallback-name logic is correct and well-tested; the only rough edges are in the test helpers. All production changes — the new constant, the global-agents path resolver, the updated search-path list, and the source-aware fallback-name function — are logically sound. The absolute-path comparisons in resolveRuleFallbackName correctly disambiguate workspace vs global AGENTS.md files, and discoverRulesLikeFiles already handles file paths passed as directory entries. The test observations are minor quality issues that do not affect runtime behaviour. user-instruction-config-loader.test.ts — the home-dir snapshot/restore pattern leaves a sticky module flag; paths.test.ts — the new assertion for the global agents path is self-referential rather than concrete.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/shared/src/storage/paths.ts | Adds AGENTS_RULES_FILE_NAME constant and resolveGlobalAgentsRulesPath() function; includes the global path in resolveRulesConfigSearchPaths(). Logic is correct and uses HOME_DIR consistently. | | sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/config/user-instruction-config-loader.ts | Adds resolveRuleFallbackName() to disambiguate workspace vs global AGENTS.md by comparing resolved absolute paths; wires it into createRulesConfigDefinition(). Handles the three cases (workspace, global, other) correctly. | | sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/config/user-instruction-config-loader.test.ts | Adds a test for non-clobbering of global vs workspace AGENTS.md; has a test isolation issue where HOME_DIR_SET_EXPLICITLY remains true after cleanup, and originalHomeDir capture is fragile if HOME_DIR was previously overridden. | | sdk/packages/shared/src/storage/paths.test.ts | New assertion verifies resolveGlobalAgentsRulesPath() is included in resolveRulesConfigSearchPaths(), but both the expected and actual value call the same function with uncontrolled HOME_DIR, so the concrete path is not validated. | | docs/customization/cline-rules.mdx | Documentation updated to list ~/.agents/AGENTS.md as a supported global AGENTS.md location — accurate and concise. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[resolveRulesConfigSearchPaths] --> B["workspace/AGENTS.md (if workspacePath)"] A --> C[".clinerules/ and .cline/rules/"] A --> D["resolveGlobalAgentsRulesPath()\n~/.agents/AGENTS.md"] A --> E["~/.cline/rules/"] A --> F["~/Documents/Cline/Rules/"] G[createRulesConfigDefinition.parseFile] --> H{resolveRuleFallbackName} H -->|filename != AGENTS.md| I["basename without ext"] H -->|== workspace/AGENTS.md| J["'Workspace AGENTS.md'"] H -->|== ~/.agents/AGENTS.md| K["'Global AGENTS.md'"] H -->|other AGENTS.md| L["basename without ext → 'AGENTS'"] J --> M[normalizeName → 'workspace agents.md'] K --> N[normalizeName → 'global agents.md'] L --> O[normalizeName → 'agents'] ```

Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 2 sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/config/user-instruction-config-loader.test.ts:204-244 **Fragile home-dir restoration leaves `HOME_DIR_SET_EXPLICITLY` permanently set** `originalHomeDir` is captured from `process.env.HOME || homedir()`, but the actual module-level `HOME_DIR` in `paths.ts` could already have been overridden by a prior `setHomeDir()` call (e.g. a global test setup or a preceding test). If that's the case, restoring to `process.env.HOME` sets a *different* value than what was in effect before this test ran. More concretely, both `setHomeDir(...)` calls — including the cleanup call — leave `HOME_DIR_SET_EXPLICITLY = true` in the module permanently. Any subsequent code in the same worker process that relies on `setHomeDirIfUnset()` (called in `local-runtime-host.ts` and the desktop-app sidecar) will have that call silently ignored for the remainder of the worker's lifetime. Since `paths.ts` exports no `resetHomeDir()`, a workaround is to export one for test use, or capture the snapshot before the first mutation with a helper that reads the actual module state. ### Issue 2 of 2 sdk/packages/shared/src/storage/paths.test.ts:150-163 **Assertion does not validate the concrete global-agents path** The expected value is `resolveGlobalAgentsRulesPath()`, and `resolveRulesConfigSearchPaths()` itself calls `resolveGlobalAgentsRulesPath()` internally — so the assertion reduces to "the function returns a value that includes itself." This passes even if `resolveGlobalAgentsRulesPath()` produced a wrong path, as long as both call sites share the same live `HOME_DIR`. A stronger check would override `HOME_DIR` via `setHomeDir("/tmp/home")` (and restore it in `afterEach`) and then assert the resolved path equals `join("/tmp/home", ".agents", "AGENTS.md")` directly, matching the style of the other path tests in this file that use a fixed `CLINE_DIR`. `````

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes skill discovery in the user-instruction config loader so workspace skill directories that are symlinks are resolved and included. Previously only `isDirectory()` entries were accepted; symlinks were silently skipped because `readdir` with `withFileTypes` reports them as `isSymbolicLink()`. - `discoverSkillFiles` now calls `stat()` on symlinked entries to follow the link and verify the target is a directory before pushing it onto the candidates list. - `isIgnorableDirectoryError` gains `ELOOP` so circular / self-referential symlinks (which cause the OS to raise `ELOOP`) are treated as non-directories and skipped rather than propagating an unhandled exception. - Two regression tests are added: one verifying a valid external symlinked skill is discovered, and one confirming a circular symlink is ignored while valid sibling skills continue to be found.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change is minimal and well-contained; both the symlink resolution logic and the circular-symlink guard are covered by the new tests. The fix correctly uses stat() (which follows symlinks) rather than lstat(), scopes the change only to discoverSkillFiles, and the previously reported ELOOP gap has been addressed in isIgnorableDirectoryError. No unhandled error paths were introduced. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/config/user-instruction-config-loader.ts | Adds stat()-based symlink resolution in discoverSkillFiles and adds ELOOP to isIgnorableDirectoryError; change is minimal, well-scoped, and addresses the previously flagged circular-symlink crash. | | sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/config/user-instruction-config-loader.test.ts | Adds two new integration tests for symlinked skill discovery: one for a valid external symlink, one for a self-referential circular symlink; both cover the new code paths introduced in the loader. |

Greptile Summary

This PR binds Discord sessions to individual message authors so different Discord users in the same thread each get their own isolated chat state. It also adds outbound mention resolution (converting `@display-name` to `<@id>` before sending), bot-role gateway forwarding, `--owner-user-id` / `--ignore-bot-authors` CLI flags, and improved logging on message handlers. - `persistDiscordThreadContext` now returns the resolved `DiscordParticipant` and uses `resolveCurrentStateWithParticipant` to swap or restore per-user thread state when the author changes between messages. - `resolveDiscordOutboundMentions` searches the Discord Guild Members API and rewrites `@name` references to `<@id>` format before the bot replies; a module-level `botGuildRoleCache` speeds up repeated role lookups. - `handleConnectorUserTurn` gains an optional `runtimeText` parameter that carries author-context metadata (author id, label, `isOwner` flag) prepended by `formatDiscordRuntimeText`.

Confidence Score: 3/5

Two functional defects in discord.ts should be addressed before merging: wrong-user mentions due to a loose fallback in member selection, and permanently stale role data after any transient API error. The participant-binding and session-switching logic is well-covered by tests and looks correct. However, `pickDiscordMemberByName` silently picks a non-matching member when the API returns exactly one result, which causes Cline to emit the wrong `<@id>` mention. Separately, `botGuildRoleCache` stores a resolved-empty-set when the bot-roles fetch fails, making bot-role-triggered messages permanently ignored until the process restarts — both are active defects on the changed path. sdk/apps/cli/src/connectors/adapters/discord.ts — specifically `pickDiscordMemberByName` (fallback logic) and `readDiscordBotGuildRoleIds` (failure caching).

Two logic issues: `pickDiscordMemberByName` falls back to any single search result even without a name match, and `botGuildRoleCache` permanently caches API failures, silently disabling role-based triggers after any transient error. | | sdk/apps/cli/src/connectors/adapters/discord.test.ts | Good coverage for participant resolution, thread state switching, mention resolution, bot-author filtering, and gateway normalization. The `afterEach(vi.unstubAllGlobals)` cleanup is correct. | | sdk/apps/cli/src/connectors/connector-host.ts | Small, focused addition: `runtimeText` optional field added to `handleConnectorUserTurn` input, which is used in place of the raw `resolvedInput` when non-empty. Change is correct and well-guarded. | | sdk/packages/shared/src/connectors/options.ts | Adds `ownerUserId?: string` and `allowBotAuthors: boolean` to `ConnectDiscordOptions`. Straightforward type extension with no issues. |

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Discord as Discord Gateway/Webhook participant Adapter as DiscordConnector participant PTC as persistDiscordThreadContext participant Bindings as thread-bindings (JSON) participant Turn as handleConnectorUserTurn participant Hub as HubSessionClient Discord->>Adapter: onNewMention / onSubscribedMessage (message, author) Adapter->>PTC: "{thread, message: {raw, author}, bindingsPath}" PTC->>PTC: resolveDiscordParticipant(raw, author) PTC->>Bindings: loadThreadState(thread) PTC->>PTC: resolveCurrentStateWithParticipant (swap state if participant changed) PTC->>Bindings: persistMergedThreadState(nextState) PTC-->>Adapter: DiscordParticipant Adapter->>Turn: handleTurn(thread, text, participant) Turn->>Turn: formatDiscordRuntimeText (prepend authorId/label/isOwner) Turn->>Hub: sendRuntimeSession / startSession(runtimeText) Hub-->>Turn: assistant reply Turn->>Adapter: postDiscordResolvedText Adapter->>Adapter: "resolveDiscordOutboundMentions (@name to id via Guild API)" Adapter->>Discord: "POST /channels/{id}/messages" ```

Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 2 sdk/apps/cli/src/connectors/adapters/discord.ts:435-441 Overly broad fallback in member resolution — picks any single search result even when it doesn't match the query. The Discord guild members search API can return a member whose name only contains the query as a substring (e.g., searching `alice` could return `team-alice-bot` if it is the only guild member). When `exact.length` is 0 and `members.length` is 1, this code picks the non-matching member, causing Cline to emit the wrong `<@id>` mention. Greptile Summary

This PR fixes duplicate-session creation in connector transports by falling back to a session-ID scan when the current turn key doesn't match any entry in `activeTurns`, and adds Discord-specific improvements: outbound mention resolution, bot-role normalisation for forwarded gateway events, participant context injection, and new `ownerUserId`/`allowBotAuthors` options. - **`connector-host.ts`**: When `activeTurns.get(turnKey)` misses, the code now searches `activeTurns.values()` for a matching `sessionId` from persisted thread state, steering the existing session instead of spawning a duplicate. A new optional `runtimeText` field lets callers enrich the prompt sent to the runtime (used by Discord to prepend author context) while keeping the plain `text` for display logic. - **`runtime-turn.ts`**: A queued `sendRuntimeSession` response no longer throws; it logs the queued state and lets the stream close cleanly via the existing `.finally()` path. - **`discord.ts` / `options.ts`**: Adds `ownerUserId` and `allowBotAuthors`, moves server startup before gateway validation, and introduces `resolveDiscordOutboundMentions` / `normalizeDiscordForwardedGatewayRequest` for richer Discord integration.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The changes are narrowly scoped to connector turn dispatch and Discord adapter enrichment; the core fix is small and well-tested, with no changes to auth or data persistence boundaries. The session-ID fallback and queued-turn silencing both work correctly and are covered by new tests. The main area needing a second look is the queued-turn path: silencing the error means persistMergedThreadState now runs after a queued response, recording a session ID that activeTurns no longer tracks — subsequent messages on that thread start a fresh session, orphaning the queued turn's eventual reply. The botGuildRoleCache has no TTL, so stale role sets persist for the process lifetime. sdk/apps/cli/src/connectors/runtime-turn.ts — the queued-turn handling change has a subtle interaction with post-turn state persistence. sdk/apps/cli/src/connectors/adapters/discord.ts — the module-level role cache has no eviction.

It uses stat() correctly (follows symlinks, unlike lstat()), the broken-symlink path is handled by catch/continue, and the outer error handler is untouched. The new test exercises the exact scenario described in the PR using the public API, and all existing tests continue to pass. No telemetry, auth, or state-management code is touched. Greptile Summary

This PR adds a per-thread error-rate limiter to the Discord connector that shuts the connector down after 3 identical errors within 60 seconds, and extends `clearBindingSessionIds` to also scrub `sessionId` from serialised thread JSON blobs. The stale-state removal path across all six connectors is also updated to call `clearBindingSessionIds` when an orphaned process is detected. - **Discord error throttle** (`discord.ts`): a `Map`-based tracker keyed on `${thread.id}:${errorMessage}` counts occurrences within a fixed window and calls `requestStop` at the threshold, posting a final summary message before shutdown. - **`clearBindingSessionIds` expansion** (`thread-bindings.ts`): a new `clearSerializedThreadSessionId` helper parses the stored JSON string and strips `sessionId` at both the root and `state` levels, with a matching test added in `thread-bindings.test.ts`. - **`removeStaleState` return value** (`base.ts`): the method now returns the removed state, enabling callers to conditionally clear binding session IDs only when stale state was actually found.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Mostly safe to merge, but the Discord anti-spam logic has a gap during the shutdown drain window where error messages continue to be posted after the threshold is reached. The error-tracking catch block does not check `stopping` before posting, so every error that arrives between `requestStop()` being called and the gateway actually going offline still generates a Discord message — the very spamming the PR intends to prevent. The `thread-bindings.ts` and multi-connector `clearBindingSessionIds` changes look correct and are well tested. sdk/apps/cli/src/connectors/adapters/discord.ts — the catch block in handleTurn needs a `stopping` guard before posting error messages.

Any MCP server configuration that relied on v3's URL acceptance rules could silently fail to load after this upgrade. Additionally, `z.nativeEnum()` usage in `AgentConfigLoader.ts` and TypeScript type inference changes in `z.infer<>` outputs could surface as compile-time or runtime regressions. Running the full TypeScript build against the upgraded package and verifying all zod-schema-exercising tests pass would confirm safety. `````

Greptile Summary

This PR adds participant-level mute targets to the Discord connector, allowing users to silence a specific bot or user in a thread (in addition to the existing thread-level mute). It introduces a `resolveDiscordMuteTarget` helper that parses Discord snowflake IDs from mention strings, wires an `ownerParticipantKeys` ACL so only the configured connector owner can issue slash commands in shared channels, and adds a guard that silently drops unaddressed commands in non-DM threads. - `thread-bindings.ts`: New `kind` discriminant and thread-scoped control keys (`thread:{id}` and `thread:{id}:participant:{key}`) store mute state independently of participant session bindings, with `isControlBinding` guards preventing mute entries from being matched as session bindings. - `connector-host.ts`: Guard 1 silently drops unaddressed commands in shared threads; guard 2 denies non-owner commands; `mute`/`unmute` handlers abort relevant active turns, write the binding, and return appropriate confirmation strings. - `chat-commands.ts`: `/mute [target]` and `/unmute [target]` are registered commands with a new `requireBotMention` gate; `isCommandAddressedToBot` is exported for reuse.

Greptile Summary

This PR stabilizes the SDK test suite on Windows by fixing two sources of flakiness: one involving persistent file-system watcher handles and one involving shell command parsing. - **`user-instruction-config-loader.test.ts`**: The AGENTS rules snapshot test now calls `refreshAll()` instead of `start()`. `start()` calls `refreshAll()` then `startDirectoryWatchers()`, leaving `fs.watch()` handles open, which can cause Windows CI to hang or fail to release temp directories. Since the test only needs a single read, `refreshAll()` is the correct API; the existing `stop()` in the `finally` block remains harmless. - **`bash.test.ts`**: Three tests that previously built a shell-quoted `node.exe -e \"...\"` string now pass structured `{ command, args }` objects directly to `createBashExecutor`. This bypasses PowerShell's argument parser entirely, eliminating the quoting failures that caused Windows failures. The `shellQuote` helper is removed as it is no longer needed.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Test-only changes with no production code modifications; both fixes correctly use existing APIs already supported by the implementation. Both changes are limited to test files and address real, well-understood platform incompatibilities. The refreshAll() path is correctly supported by the watcher implementation, and structured command input is already part of the BashExecutor type signature. No logic, contracts, or public APIs are altered. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/config/user-instruction-config-loader.test.ts | Replaces watcher.start() with watcher.refreshAll() in the AGENTS snapshot test, avoiding persistent fs.watch() handles that caused Windows flakiness; stop() in finally remains harmless as no directory watchers were started. | | sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/executors/bash.test.ts | Drops the shellQuote helper and replaces three shell-string invocations with structured { command, args } objects, bypassing PowerShell parsing on Windows; the BashExecutor type and createBashExecutor implementation both already accept StructuredCommandInput. |

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes Windows test failures caused by PowerShell treating a quoted path as a string literal instead of a command. The helper is renamed from `shellQuote` to `shellExecutable` to reflect its new semantics. - On `win32`, the helper now emits `& 'quoted\\path'` instead of `'quoted\\path'`; without the call operator (`& `), PowerShell evaluates the quoted string as data, not as an executable, so tests invoking `process.execPath` (which can contain spaces) would silently fail. - Non-Windows behavior is unchanged: the Unix branch still produces a POSIX-escaped single-quoted string.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change is confined to a test helper and corrects a real Windows execution failure without affecting Unix behaviour. The fix is minimal and well-scoped: it adds the PowerShell call operator on win32, matching how PowerShell actually invokes quoted paths, while leaving the Unix quoting path untouched. The executor implementation itself is unchanged. No files require special attention.

Greptile Summary

This PR surfaces MCP server-level `instructions` from the initialize response to the model's system prompt. It wires the field end-to-end: `McpServer` type gets an `instructions?: string` field, `McpHub` captures the value via `client.getInstructions()` after connect, and both the component-based renderer (`mcp.ts`) and the legacy GPT-5 renderer emit a `### Instructions` block before the tools section when the field is non-blank. - **`McpHub.ts`**: reads `client.getInstructions()` right after the connection succeeds and stores it on the server object; reconnect flows create a fresh connection object, so stale instructions can't persist. - **`mcp.ts` / `gpt-5.ts`**: symmetric rendering with `.trim()` + truthiness guard so blank/whitespace-only instructions produce no output; new focused unit tests cover present, absent, and blank cases.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The change is additive, guarded by a non-blank check, and reconnect paths correctly refresh the value. The only concern is that server-provided instructions enter the system prompt without a length or content cap. The implementation is correct end-to-end: type is right, the SDK method is called after the handshake is complete, disabled-server paths are bypassed, and renderers in both the component and legacy paths are symmetric. The one open question is that instructions text from an MCP server is stored and rendered with no upper-bound on length, and the field is the most obvious vector for a server to push content into the model's context. This is consistent with how tool descriptions are handled today, so it is not a regression, but it is worth addressing before the feature ships widely. The single line in McpHub.ts where getInstructions() is stored deserves a follow-up for a length guard; all other files are straightforward.

Hub->>Client: client.connect(transport) Client->>Server: initialize request Server-->>Client: initialize response (incl. instructions?) Hub->>Client: client.getInstructions() Client-->>Hub: "string | undefined" Hub->>Hub: "connection.server.instructions = value" Hub->>Hub: fetchToolsList / fetchResourcesList / fetchPromptsList Hub->>Prompt: getServers() → McpServer[] Prompt->>Prompt: server.instructions?.trim() Prompt->>Prompt: "emit ### Instructions block if non-blank" Prompt-->>Hub: formatted system prompt section ```

Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 1 apps/vscode/src/services/mcp/McpHub.ts:658 **Unvalidated server content injected into system prompt** `instructions` is a free-form string provided by the MCP server and is inserted verbatim into the system prompt with no length cap or content check. A malicious or compromised server can advertise arbitrarily long text here — or craft content designed to override other parts of the prompt — and it will be silently accepted. Greptile Summary

This PR fixes standalone terminal output capture on Windows by correcting two spawn-option bugs and hardening PowerShell command handling. It also extracts shell-argument construction into a dedicated, testable module. - **Windows stdio routing fix**: `detached` is now suppressed on win32 and `windowsHide: true` is added to both the cmd.exe and non-cmd spawn paths, preventing the child process's stdio from being routed to a newly-allocated console instead of the parent's pipes. - **PowerShell hardening**: `getShellArgs` now adds `-NoProfile -NonInteractive` to PowerShell invocations and calls `unwrapPowerShell` to strip LLM-generated double-wrapping (e.g., `powershell -Command "..."`), avoiding nested-shell quote shredding. - **Resilience**: `process.run()` is now guarded with `.catch()` that re-emits any future unhandled rejection as an `"error"` event, preventing the outer promise from hanging indefinitely.

The `unwrapPowerShell` regex is deliberately conservative — it returns the input verbatim when uncertain, so the worst case is no change rather than a misrewrite. This PR serializes Codex/ChatGPT OAuth token refreshes across VS Code windows using a filesystem lock (`proper-lockfile`), addresses silent disk-write failures by surfacing `writeToDisk` errors through the `setBatch` promise channel, and adds winner-adoption logic so a window waiting for the lock can reuse credentials already refreshed by another window. - **ClineFileStorage**: Splits `setBatch` into a sync core (`setBatchSync`) with rollback-on-failure; public `setBatch` now correctly returns `Promise.reject(error)` on disk write failure; adds `reloadFromDisk()` for cross-process coordination; `writeToDisk` now rethrows to propagate errors to callers. - **oauth.ts**: Introduces `refreshCredentialsUnderLock` with `proper-lockfile`, in-process promise deduplication that respects the `force` flag via recursive retry after the non-forced winner resolves, and `invalid_grant` guard that re-reads disk before clearing credentials (preserves a newer token written by another window). - **StateManager**: Adds `reloadSecretKey` (refreshes all non-pending secret cache entries plus the requested key from disk) and `getDataDir`; all `setBatch` call sites are now properly `await`ed to surface write failures.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge. The locking protocol, winner adoption, rollback, and in-process deduplication all behave correctly across the scenarios covered by the new test suite. The cross-process lock correctly serializes refreshes; winner adoption (storedCredentialsChanged + !force guard) is logically sound; setBatch now returns a rejected promise on disk failure with proper in-memory rollback; all setBatch call sites are awaited; and the invalid_grant re-read guard prevents credential clearing when another window already rotated the token. The test suite exercises the key race scenarios repeatedly. No files require special attention. The oauth.ts locking logic is the most complex area but is well-exercised by the new tests.

Greptile Summary

This PR upgrades direct dependencies `axios` (1.15.2 → 1.16.1) and `undici` (^7.16.0 → ^7.26.0) in `apps/vscode/package.json`, and refreshes the lockfile to pull patched versions of 17 packages, resolving 53 CVEs across `@xmldom/xmldom`, `basic-ftp`, `hono`, `ws`, `zod`, and others. A companion change in `net.ts` explicitly sets `maxBodyLength: Infinity` and `maxContentLength: Infinity` in `getAxiosSettings()` to preserve pre-1.16.0 behaviour after axios began enforcing fetch-adapter size limits. - `apps/vscode/package.json`: Two direct dependency version bumps (`axios`, `undici`) to pull in patched releases. - `apps/vscode/src/shared/net.ts`: `getAxiosSettings()` now returns explicit `Infinity` limits so the newly enforced axios 1.16.0 fetch-adapter caps do not break large payload paths. - `apps/vscode/package-lock.json`: Lockfile-only refreshes for all 17 transitive packages; no additional manifest changes required.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the dependency upgrades are well-scoped security fixes and the net.ts change is a deliberate, clearly-reasoned backward-compatibility decision. All changes are dependency version bumps with lockfile refreshes. The only code change is a two-line addition to getAxiosSettings() that explicitly sets Infinity limits, which was a deliberate response to the axios 1.16.0 fetch-adapter enforcement change. The tradeoff is documented and intentional; no logic regressions were introduced. apps/vscode/src/shared/net.ts — the Infinity limits are a conscious tradeoff worth revisiting if stricter response-size bounds are ever desired.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/vscode/src/shared/net.ts | Adds maxBodyLength: Infinity and maxContentLength: Infinity to getAxiosSettings() to restore pre-1.16.0 unbounded behaviour; intentionally trades away the AIKIDO-2026-10820 size-limit hardening for backward compatibility. | | apps/vscode/package.json | Bumps axios to 1.16.1 and undici to ^7.26.0 to address direct CVEs; no other manifest changes. | | apps/vscode/package-lock.json | Lockfile-only refresh resolving 17 vulnerable transitive packages to their minimum patched versions; no new dependency additions. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[axios request via getAxiosSettings] --> B{axios 1.16.1 fetch adapter} B --> C[Check maxBodyLength] C -->|Infinity - no limit| D[Check maxContentLength] D -->|Infinity - no limit| E[Dispatch via net.ts fetch] E --> F{IS_STANDALONE?} F -->|true - JetBrains/CLI| G[undici EnvHttpProxyAgent] F -->|false - VSCode| H[globalThis.fetch] G --> I[AI Provider / External API] H --> I I -->|Response - any size| J[Caller receives response] ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 1 code review issue. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 1 apps/vscode/src/shared/net.ts:174-181 **Opting out of AIKIDO-2026-10820 size-limit hardening across every axios call** Setting both limits to `Infinity` restores pre-1.16.0 behaviour and avoids breaking callers that send or receive large payloads, which is a reasonable backward-compatibility choice. However, it also means the fetch-adapter size-limit fix (AIKIDO-2026-10820) included in this upgrade is effectively nullified for the entire codebase: every axios request made through `getAxiosSettings()` — including inference calls to AI providers — will now accept arbitrarily large response bodies with no upper bound. If a provider endpoint were compromised or misbehaving, it could stream an unbounded response and exhaust process memory. Consider whether a generous but finite cap (e.g. a few hundred MB) would provide the same backward compatibility while still bounding worst-case memory consumption. `````

This PR serializes Codex OAuth refresh transactions across SDK/CLI processes using per-provider `proper-lockfile` locks, a fresh durable re-read inside the lock, winner adoption, and a conditional CAS (`expectedOpenAICodexAuth`) that protects `providers.json` writes from stale overrides and concurrent removals. It also introduces atomic settings writes via temp-file rename with Windows backup-and-replace recovery, synchronous write-lock spinning via `Atomics.wait`, and a `User-Agent` header on Codex token requests. - **`runtime-oauth-token-manager.ts`**: Adds `withProviderRefreshLock` for Codex token refreshes, post-lock winner adoption (latestSettings re-read), invalid-grant auth cleanup with CAS guard, and a forced-refresh re-attempt when a forced waiter queues behind a successful ordinary in-flight. - **`provider-settings-manager.ts`**: Rewrites `write()` to hold a synchronous file-based write lock, use an atomic rename (with Windows fallback), and apply `preserveDurableOpenAICodexEntry` — a conditional/unconditional durable-auth restore that merges the on-disk Codex OAuth state against the incoming state to protect against stale overwrites and concurrent removals. - **`codex.ts` / `local-provider-service.ts`**: Adds `User-Agent` header, `onInvalidGrant` callback plumbing, and `allowOpenAICodexAuthReplacement` flags on all explicit Codex provider writes/removals.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The integration suite spawns real child processes and injects fault scenarios (delayed network, invalid_grant, concurrent removal, stale-save rollback, re-authentication during save) providing strong evidence that the critical paths are correct. Greptile Summary

This PR instruments the `run_commands` shell executor with focused SDK telemetry, emitting a new `sdk.tool_timeout` event whenever a command is killed by its effective timeout. It introduces a typed `TimeoutError` class so timeout kills can be distinguished from generic command failures, and threads the runtime's `ITelemetryService` into tool context via a private metadata key (`__clineInternalTelemetry`) to avoid colliding with user-provided metadata. - **New `TimeoutError` class** (`helpers.ts`, `bash.ts`): replaces the plain `Error` thrown on timeout, carrying `timeoutMs` so the catch block can read back the exact threshold that fired. - **`sdk.tool_timeout` event** (`core-events.ts`): added to `CORE_TELEMETRY_EVENTS.SDK`, with a typed `captureRunCommandsTimeout()` helper that uses `capture` (not `captureRequired`) and strips `undefined` optional fields — payload is privacy-safe and contains no raw command text, stdout, stderr, or paths. - **Telemetry injection** (`session-runtime-orchestrator.ts`, `tool-context.ts`): the runtime places its `ITelemetryService` under a stable internal key after spreading user `toolContextMetadata`, so user config cannot accidentally shadow it.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — all changes are additive instrumentation with no effect on command execution behavior or existing tool output shapes. The new TimeoutError extends Error, so every existing catch block that calls formatError() continues to work identically. The telemetry injection is placed after the user metadata spread, ensuring the internal key cannot be overridden. captureRunCommandsTimeout uses capture (opt-out-respecting) not captureRequired, and stripUndefinedProperties keeps the payload clean. Tests cover the privacy guarantee, opt-out policy, the TimeoutError discrimination path, and the success (no-event) path for both bash and Windows tool factories. No files require special attention.

Superseded by the review-team/Claude cleanup.

This PR no longer changes `task.tool_used.success` for timed-out `run_commands`. We removed that override to keep existing `task.tool_used` semantics stable and avoid coupling aggregate tool telemetry to formatted `run_commands` error text.
