body:
Greptile Summary

This PR adds support for bundling skills directly inside plugin packages. When a plugin is installed or loaded, Cline now walks from each plugin entry file up to its package boundary, then checks for a `skills/` directory there, and registers any discovered `SKILL.md` files using the existing skill loader. No new registration API is required of plugin authors. - **Plugin root detection** uses a two-pass walk: first recognizing the CLI installer wrapper layout (`parent/package/index.ts` → skill root is `parent/package/`), then falling back to the first ancestor `package.json` that declares the entry — stopping there to avoid monorepo root leakage. - **Runtime vs. config paths are intentionally split**: at session startup, skill directories are derived from successfully loaded+targeted plugin paths (`resolvePluginSkillDirectoriesFromPaths`); pre-runtime config commands and the settings service use a "best-effort" synchronous discovery path (`resolveAgentPluginSkillDirectories`) that does not filter by provider/model targeting. - **`userInstructionService` is no longer forwarded** from the CLI into `localRuntime`; the runtime builder creates its own service with full plugin context, so the session always has an authoritative view of available skills.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the feature is entirely additive, all existing skill paths are unchanged, and the new plugin-skill discovery is well-tested across standard, wrapper, and monorepo layouts. The package-root derivation logic is carefully guarded (monorepo boundary stop, installed-wrapper detection, targeting gate), runtime and config paths are separated cleanly, and the `userInstructionService` decoupling from `localRuntime` ensures sessions always see a consistent skill set. No existing behavior is broken. No files require special attention; the two observations are style/completeness items with no impact on the runtime skill resolution path.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/plugin/plugin-config-loader.ts | Core of the feature: adds package-root derivation, `resolvePluginSkillDirectoriesFromPaths`, and `resolveAgentPluginSkillDirectories`; also adds `pluginPaths` to the `resolveAndLoadAgentPlugins` return type. Logic is sound; minor inconsistency noted between `dedupePaths` (normalizes) and the caller-side `dedupeDirectoryPaths` (returns originals). | | sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/config/user-instruction-config-loader.ts | Adds `resolveSkillDirectories` and `dedupeDirectoryPaths`; wires `pluginSkillDirectories` / `includePluginSkills` into the skills config definition. The `dedupeDirectoryPaths` helper returns un-normalized (original) paths while `dedupePaths` in plugin-config-loader returns normalized paths — inconsistency is benign in current call sites but worth noting. | | sdk/packages/core/src/services/local-runtime-bootstrap.ts | Computes `pluginSkillDirectories` from the successfully-loaded plugin paths and threads it through `runtimeBuilderInput`. Logic is clean and correctly handles the plugin-load-failure case (empty list rather than undefined). | | sdk/packages/core/src/runtime/orchestration/runtime-builder.ts | Creates the user-instruction service with `pluginSkillDirectories` / `includePluginSkills` gated on `pluginsEnabled`; correctly falls back to fresh discovery when `pluginSkillDirectories` is undefined (direct builder calls). | | sdk/packages/core/src/settings/settings-service.ts | Adds `includePluginSkills: true` and `cwd` to the skills service; however `pluginPaths` from the agent config is not forwarded, so plugins configured via an explicit `pluginPaths` field won't have their skills shown in the settings view. | | sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/plugin/plugin-config-loader.test.ts | Good coverage: standard package, missing path, installed wrapper layout, monorepo boundary, provider/model targeting. All scenarios tested. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[Plugin entry path] --> B[collectPluginSkillRootCandidates] B --> C{Is dir named 'package'\nwith declaring parent\npackage.json?} C -- yes --> D[Root = 'package/' dir\nCLI installer wrapper layout] C -- no --> E{Has package.json\nin current dir?} E -- yes, declares entry --> F[Root = current dir\nStandard package layout] E -- yes, does not declare --> G[Stop — monorepo boundary\nno skills discovered] E -- no --> H[Walk up to parent] H --> C D --> I[Check root/skills/ exists] F --> I I -- exists --> J[Add to skill directories] I -- missing --> K[Skip] subgraph Runtime path L[resolveAndLoadAgentPlugins] --> M[loadedPlugins.pluginPaths\nonly active+targeted plugins] M --> N[resolvePluginSkillDirectoriesFromPaths] N --> J J --> O[pluginSkillDirectories passed\nto RuntimeBuilderInput] O --> P[UserInstructionConfigService\ncreated in runtime-builder] end subgraph Config / Settings path Q[createConfigUserInstructionService\nsettings-service / config.ts / main.ts] --> R[resolveAgentPluginSkillDirectories\nbest-effort, no targeting filter] R --> S[Standard discovery paths only\nno explicit pluginPaths] end ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 2 sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/config/user-instruction-config-loader.ts:120-132 `dedupeDirectoryPaths` adds the **normalized** path to `seen` but pushes the **original** (potentially un-normalized) path to the output array, while `dedupePaths` in `plugin-config-loader.ts` consistently pushes the normalized path. In current call sites every directory is already absolute, so there's no behavioral difference, but the asymmetry makes the helper misleading — a caller passing a relative path would get a relative path back while dedup still works. Returning the normalized path (matching `dedupePaths`) makes the contract explicit. ```suggestion function dedupeDirectoryPaths(directories: ReadonlyArray): string[] { const deduped: string[] = []; const seen = new Set(); for (const directory of directories) { const normalized = resolve(directory); if (seen.has(normalized)) { continue; } seen.add(normalized); deduped.push(normalized); } return deduped; } ``` ### Issue 2 of 2 sdk/packages/core/src/settings/settings-service.ts:80-88 **Plugin skills from `pluginPaths` not visible in settings / config view** `includePluginSkills: true` is set, but `pluginPaths` from the agent config is not forwarded here. The resulting call to `resolveAgentPluginSkillDirectories` only discovers plugins in the standard search paths (`.cline/plugins/` etc.), so plugins loaded via an explicit `pluginPaths` entry in the agent config will have their skills visible at runtime (via the authoritative runtime-builder path) but invisible in the settings view and `cline config skills` output. The PR description claims these three surfaces agree, but they diverge for that subset. The same gap exists in `config.ts`'s `createConfigUserInstructionService` and in `main.ts`. Passing the agent config's `pluginPaths` through to `CreateSkillsConfigDefinitionOptions.pluginPaths` where available would close it. `````

body:
1. **High** `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/plugin/plugin-config-loader.ts:125`

   `resolveAgentPluginSkillDirectories()` calls `resolveAgentPluginPaths()` without guarding configured `pluginPaths` errors. A stale or missing optional plugin path can now abort user-instruction service setup, even though normal plugin loading is best-effort and caught in bootstrap.

   Suggested fix: make plugin skill discovery best-effort, returning valid discovered skill dirs and routing diagnostics through the existing plugin diagnostics path.

2. **High** `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/config/user-instruction-config-loader.ts:140`

   Plugin skill dirs are appended after normal skill dirs, but skill IDs still use only `skill.name`; the watcher overwrites duplicate IDs. Installing a plugin with `review` can silently replace a user/workspace `review` skill.

   Suggested fix: preserve user/workspace precedence, namespace plugin skill IDs by plugin/package, or surface duplicate names as explicit ambiguity.

3. **Medium** `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/plugin/plugin-config-loader.ts:79`

   `collectPluginSkillRootCandidates()` accepts the first ancestor with any `package.json` as the plugin package root. A standalone plugin under a normal repo can accidentally expose `/repo/skills` as plugin-bundled skills.

   Suggested fix: only accept package roots whose manifest declares the current Cline plugin entry, or constrain this to known installed-wrapper/package layouts.

4. **Medium** `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/plugin/plugin-config-loader.ts:121`

   Skill discovery uses resolved plugin paths, not the actually active plugin set. Provider/model-targeted plugins can be filtered out by plugin loading while their bundled skills remain exposed.

   Suggested fix: derive skill roots from loaded/target-matching plugins, or apply the same targeting checks during skill-root discovery.

5. **Medium** `sdk/packages/core/src/settings/settings-service.ts:168`

   Plugin-bundled skills are reported as plain `workspace`/`global` and toggleable, so settings can mutate package-owned `SKILL.md` files directly.

   Suggested fix: classify them as `workspace-plugin`/`global-plugin` and decide whether disabling should be package mutation or a host-owned override.

6. **Low** `sdk/examples/plugins/README.md:3`

   SDK-side plugin author docs do not mention bundled skills or how to verify them with `cline config skills`.

   Suggested fix: add a short bundled-skills section with layout, minimal `SKILL.md`, and loading conditions.

body:
Thanks, I pushed `746f0d44e` to address the two runtime correctness issues you called out as most important.

For 1, `resolveAgentPluginSkillDirectories()` now uses a best-effort path resolver for optional configured plugin paths. A stale configured path is skipped for skill discovery, while valid configured or discovered plugins can still contribute skill dirs. The strict resolver stays intact for plugin loading itself, so normal diagnostics still come from the existing plugin load path.

For 4, plugin loading now returns the plugin paths that actually survived import, provider/model targeting, and duplicate override resolution. Local runtime converts only that active plugin path list into plugin skill directories and passes it into the runtime-built instruction service. If plugin loading ran and produced no active plugins, the explicit empty list prevents the runtime from rediscovering skipped plugin skills.

I also stopped the CLI from handing its early prompt-expansion instruction service into session runtime. That service is created before provider/model-targeted plugin loading, so reusing it was the path where inactive plugin skills could leak into the actual runtime.

I left the other notes as follow-ups for now. I agree collision precedence should become an explicit priority map, and package-owned skill disabling probably wants host-owned state rather than mutating frontmatter in installed plugin packages. Those feel like policy/API decisions on top of this runtime correctness fix.

body:
Pushed `e9ab7ce3d` for the ancestor skill discovery issue.

Problem reproduced:

A plugin entry like `root/packages/myplugin/src/index.ts` with no plugin-local `package.json` caused `collectPluginSkillRootCandidates()` to climb to the first ancestor `package.json`. In a monorepo, that can be `root/package.json`, which meant `root/skills` was treated as plugin-bundled skills. That leaks unrelated or private workspace skills into the plugin skill set.

Fix:

Skill roots are now only accepted when the package root can prove ownership of the plugin entry. The resolver accepts:

- an installed plugin wrapper `package/` directory only when the wrapper manifest declares that plugin entry
- a package root only when its `cline.plugins` manifest declares that plugin entry

It no longer accepts arbitrary ancestor `package.json` files, and it no longer adds `dirname(entryPath)` as a fallback root. I added an inline comment at the resolver explaining the monorepo leak and why the manifest guard is intentional.

Regression coverage:

- Added a test for `root/packages/myplugin/src/index.ts` plus `root/skills/private-root-skill/SKILL.md`; it now resolves no plugin skill dirs.
- Confirmed the exact repro now returns `[]`.
- Confirmed installed plugin wrappers still expose their own bundled skills through `config skills --json`.

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a Gemini-specific schema rejection where MCP servers emit `type: \"OBJECT\"` (uppercase) and omit `properties` entries for fields listed in `required`. The normalizer is extended to lowercase `type`, detect object-like schemas structurally (via `properties`/`required`/`additionalProperties` presence), and inject empty placeholder schemas (`{}`) for any required field not already in `properties`. - `normalizeAiSdkToolInputSchema` in `ai-sdk.ts` is significantly reworked to handle uppercase types and missing property definitions, and the normalized schema is now consistently used in both the AI SDK `jsonSchema()` call and the internal `validate` callback (fixing a pre-existing mismatch where the validator used the original unnormalized schema). - A new integration test in `gateway.test.ts` confirms the normalized shape passed to `streamText` for the primary reported scenario (`type: \"OBJECT\"`, `required: [\"port\"]`, no `properties`).

Confidence Score: 4/5

The change is safe to merge for the reported scenario; the normalization logic is correct and well-tested for the primary case. The fix correctly handles uppercase type values and missing properties entries for the top-level tool input schema, and incidentally fixes a pre-existing mismatch between the schema sent to Gemini and the schema used for local validation. Two gaps remain: nested property schemas with uppercase types are not recursively normalized, and a non-array required field passes through un-cleaned. Neither blocks the stated fix, but they leave the normalizer incomplete for less common schema shapes. sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/ai-sdk.ts — specifically the recursive normalization gap in property values and the non-array required passthrough

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/ai-sdk.ts | Extends normalizeAiSdkToolInputSchema to lowercase the type field, detect object-like schemas by structural keywords, and inject empty placeholder schemas for required fields absent from properties. Also fixes a pre-existing inconsistency where the validate callback used the original unnormalized inputSchema while the jsonSchema call used the normalized one. | | sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/gateway.test.ts | Adds one integration test for the primary bug scenario (type: OBJECT, required fields missing from properties) verifying the normalized schema passed to streamText. Does not cover nested property schemas or schemas already using lowercase type. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[Tool inputSchema from MCP server] --> B[normalizeAiSdkToolInputSchema] B --> C{Has string type?} C -- Yes --> D[Lowercase type field] C -- No --> E[Keep type as-is] D --> F{isObjectLike?} E --> F F -- No --> G[Return schema unchanged] F -- Yes --> H[Copy existing properties or start empty] H --> I{schema.required is array?} I -- Yes --> J[Filter to string keys] I -- No --> K[required is undefined] J --> L[Add empty placeholder for each missing required key] L --> M[Return: type forced to object, merged properties, filtered required] K --> M ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 2 sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/ai-sdk.ts:236-244 **Nested property schemas not recursively normalized** The lowercase-type fix is applied only to the top-level schema. If an MCP server emits a nested property like `{ type: "object", properties: { config: { type: "OBJECT", ... } } }`, the inner `type: "OBJECT"` will reach Gemini unchanged and trigger the same schema-validation error the PR is trying to fix. A recursive pass over `properties` values would close this gap. ### Issue 2 of 2 sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/ai-sdk.ts:247-254 **Original `required` survives the spread when it is not an array** When `schema.required` exists but is not an array (e.g. `required: true`), the local `required` variable is `undefined`, so the final `...(required ? { required } : {})` contributes nothing. The invalid value from `...schema` therefore passes through un-overridden and reaches Gemini. This is an unlikely MCP edge case, but the function's contract implies it normalises the schema; silently forwarding an invalid `required` field contradicts that intent. `````

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR makes two independent resilience fixes in the VS Code file-search path: it wraps `getBinaryLocation("rg")` in a `try/catch` that falls back to well-known system `rg` paths (and finally to a bare `rg`/`rg.exe` PATH lookup), and it makes `getActiveFiles()` catch failures from the `getOpenTabs` host RPC instead of propagating them to the caller. - **`resolveRipgrepPath` + `findSystemRipgrep`**: new helpers in `file-search.ts` intercept a missing-bundled-binary error, probe `/usr/bin/rg`, `/opt/homebrew/bin/rg`, and `/usr/local/bin/rg` (with `X_OK`), and return the first accessible path — or a bare `"rg"`/`"rg.exe"` as a final PATH-based fallback. - **`getActiveFiles` hardening**: the `getOpenTabs` gRPC call is now wrapped in `try/catch`; a failure logs a warning and returns an empty `Set` so the rest of the file-search pipeline continues unimpeded. - **Regression tests**: two new mocha cases are added — one for each fallback path — using sinon stubs to simulate the missing-binary and missing-host-RPC failure modes.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The change is safe to merge — both fallback paths degrade gracefully and errors are surfaced only through logging, not by breaking the search pipeline. The new code paths are narrow and well-contained. findSystemRipgrep always returns a string, getActiveFiles returns an empty Set on failure, and the existing ripgrep error handler still fires if the final fallback binary is also absent. Two dedicated regression tests exercise both failure modes end-to-end. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/vscode/src/services/search/file-search.ts | Adds `resolveRipgrepPath` + `findSystemRipgrep` helpers to fall back from a missing bundled binary to the system `rg`, and wraps `getActiveFiles` to swallow `getOpenTabs` RPC failures gracefully. | | apps/vscode/src/test/services/search/file-search.test.ts | Adds two regression tests for the new fallback paths; also adds two new `accessStub.withArgs` entries in `beforeEach` to make the default mock binary path accessible. Tests correctly simulate both failure modes. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A["executeRipgrepForFiles()"] --> B["resolveRipgrepPath()"] B --> C{"getBinaryLocation('rg') succeeds?"} C -- Yes --> D["Use bundled rg path"] C -- No/throws --> E["findSystemRipgrep()"] E --> F{"Check /usr/bin/rg (X_OK)"} F -- accessible --> G["Return /usr/bin/rg"] F -- not found --> H{"Check /opt/homebrew/bin/rg (X_OK)"} H -- accessible --> I["Return /opt/homebrew/bin/rg"] H -- not found --> J{"Check /usr/local/bin/rg (X_OK)"} J -- accessible --> K["Return /usr/local/bin/rg"] J -- not found --> L["Return bare 'rg'/'rg.exe' (PATH fallback)"] D & G & I & K & L --> M["spawn(rgPath, args)"] ``` Reviews (2): Last reviewed commit: ["Merge branch 'main' into fix/file-search..."](https://github.com/cline/cline/commit/de4829596d23af248806814519a7674cbcb142d0) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=34832002)

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes the Claude Code provider failing when newer models (e.g. claude-opus-4-5, claude-sonnet-4-6) emit native `tool_use` responses instead of XML text under `--max-turns 1`, causing Claude Code to exit with code 1 after the response was already fully streamed. - Adds `hasReceivedResult` tracking so that an exit-code-1 error is suppressed when the result chunk was already yielded, preventing a spurious error from an otherwise complete response. - Expands the `claudeCodeTools` disallowed-tools list from ~14 entries to ~30 PascalCase entries (including new categories: interactive, plan/worktree, scheduling, task management) to prevent models from calling built-in tools natively and consuming the single allowed turn. - Adds explicit handling for previously-ignored `error` and `rate_limit_event` stream chunk types, and improves error messages by collecting stderr from both execa's attached field and the stream listener.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The core fix addresses a real and reproducible bug, but the error-suppression guard is not tightly scoped to the max-turns scenario and could hide unrelated Claude Code failures. The hasReceivedResult suppression checks only exitCode === 1 without verifying that stderr contains 'Reached maximum number of turns', so any Claude Code process that exits with code 1 after emitting a result chunk is silently swallowed. The removal of the legacy snake_case exit_plan_mode entry also carries unverified risk on the exact code path this PR is meant to fix. src/integrations/claude-code/run.ts — the hasReceivedResult suppression logic and the updated claudeCodeTools list both warrant close attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | src/integrations/claude-code/run.ts | Adds hasReceivedResult tracking to suppress exit-code-1 errors after a result is already yielded; expands the disallowed-tools list with PascalCase names and new categories; improves multi-source error capture. The suppression check is broader than the described scenario (no stderr validation), and the removal of the snake_case exit_plan_mode entry carries risk if the CLI still uses that name. | | src/core/api/providers/claude-code.ts | Adds handling for previously-ignored error and rate_limit_event stream chunks. Error chunks throw immediately; rate_limit_event chunks throw only when status is rejected and log otherwise. Logic is straightforward and well-typed. | | src/integrations/claude-code/types.ts | Enriches ErrorMessage with optional nested error/subtype fields, and introduces the RateLimitEvent type with a well-typed rate_limit_info shape. Union export updated accordingly. No issues found. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[Claude Code CLI emits JSON line] --> B{Parse chunk type} B --> |system/init| C[Set isPaidUsage flag] B --> |error| D[Log + throw Error] B --> |rate_limit_event| E{status === rejected?} E --> |yes| F[Throw rate limit Error] E --> |no| G[Log status, continue] B --> |assistant| H[Yield text/thinking/tool_use blocks] B --> |result| I[Set hasReceivedResult = true Yield usage chunk] I --> J[Process exits] J --> K{exitCode === 0?} K --> |yes| L[Generator ends normally] K --> |no| M{hasReceivedResult && exitCode === 1?} M --> |yes| N[Suppress error Log max-turns message] M --> |no| O{Check stderr content} O --> |outdated CLI| P[Throw update message] O --> |ENOENT| Q[Throw path/install message] O --> |E2BIG/ENAMETOOLONG| R[Throw system prompt too long] O --> |other| S[Throw with stderr details] ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 2 src/integrations/claude-code/run.ts:117-120 The suppression check is too broad: any exit code 1 error after a result chunk is received is silently swallowed, even if the exit was caused by something unrelated to the max-turns limit (e.g. a plugin crash, OOM, or other runtime error). The log message also unconditionally claims "max_turns limit" regardless of the real reason. A targeted stderr check prevents masking unrelated failures while still handling the intended scenario. ```suggestion const isMaxTurnsExit = (err as any)?.exitCode === 1 && (processState.stderrLogs?.includes("Reached maximum number of turns") || (err as any)?.stderr?.includes("Reached maximum number of turns")) if (hasReceivedResult && isMaxTurnsExit) { Logger.log("Claude Code exited with max_turns limit — response already yielded, suppressing error.") return } ``` ### Issue 2 of 2 src/integrations/claude-code/run.ts:231-233 The original list included `"exit_plan_mode"` in snake_case. The new list removes it and adds `"EnterPlanMode"` / `"ExitPlanMode"` in PascalCase, consistent with the rest of the expansion. However, if the Claude Code CLI still registers this tool under its legacy snake_case name (which was the previously working entry), it would no longer be disallowed, potentially allowing the model to call it natively and trigger the max-turns error this PR is trying to fix. Worth keeping the snake_case alias until the tool registry name is confirmed. ```suggestion // Plan/worktree tools "EnterPlanMode", "ExitPlanMode", "exit_plan_mode", // legacy snake_case alias — keep until CLI tool registry name is confirmed ``` `````

The logic change is small, well-contained, and all existing callers pass string values so widening the parameter type introduces no regressions. The only gap is that the new non-string/non-array guard branch lacks a direct test case, leaving that contract slightly underdocumented in the test suite. The test file could cover the non-string/non-array guard branch more explicitly, but the implementation in array.ts itself is sound.

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a spurious error thrown by Cline when Claude Code exits with code 1 after reaching `--max-turns 1`, which happens when the model uses native tool-calling instead of XML text formatting. A `hasReceivedResult` flag is introduced to track whether the response was fully streamed; if so, the exit-code-1 error is suppressed. The PR also improves error diagnostics and adds newly available Claude Code tools to the disallowed-tools list. - The `hasReceivedResult` + `exitCode === 1` suppression correctly targets `ExecaError` objects, making the fix functional under execa's default reject-on-failure behavior. - Error message construction now falls back to execa-attached `stderr`/`stdout` when the stream listener captured nothing. - The tool-list additions (`PowerShell`, `Monitor`, `PushNotification`, `RemoteTrigger`, `ScheduleWakeup`) disallow newly released Claude Code built-ins, preserving Cline's custom tool format.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge with low risk; the suppression targets the known Claude Code max-turns behaviour and works correctly with execa's default configuration. The suppression heuristic does not verify the 'Reached maximum number of turns' stderr message, so any exit-code-1 error emitted after a result chunk would be silently dropped. This is a narrow edge case. The manually constructed Error lacking an exitCode property is moot under current execa settings but could become a silent failure if the configuration drifts. apps/vscode/src/integrations/claude-code/run.ts — specifically the suppression condition at line 117 and the manual error construction at lines 106-110.

Suppression condition checks only exitCode === 1 without verifying the max-turns stderr message. |

The fix looks correct and clean. The race condition is fully addressed:

- Single `useEffect` keyed on `[openAiBaseUrl, openAiApiKey]` — no more separate mount/onChange paths
- `ignore` flag set in the cleanup prevents stale responses from landing after a re-render
- `clearTimeout` in cleanup cancels the pending debounce timer if the effect re-runs before the 500ms fires — so only one request can ever be in-flight at a time

Both edge cases are covered: fast re-render before the debounce fires (timer cancelled), and slow network response (flag is `true` before `setOpenAiModels` runs). The deduplication of the fetch logic is a nice side-effect too.

Greptile Summary

This PR is a tactical workaround for SDK Nightly: when the VSCode extension maps SDK model metadata to the legacy `ModelInfo` shape, `maxInputTokens` is dropped, so compaction derives its threshold from the full 400K context window and exceeds the `openai-codex` OAuth 272K input cap. The fix threads `providerId` through `buildApiHandler` and adds a guarded `case 400_000:` in `getContextWindowInfo` that applies a 232K ceiling only for `openai-codex` providers. - `sdk-api-handler.ts` monkey-patches `handler.getModel` to inject `providerConfig.providerId`, and `ApiHandlerModel` gains an optional `providerId` field. - `context-window-utils.ts` branches on both context-window size (`400_000`) and provider (`openai-codex`) to set `maxAllowedSize = 272_000 − 40_000 = 232_000`; all other 400K models fall back to `defaultMaxAllowedSize` (unchanged behavior). - Two focused regression tests cover both sides of the guard.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — narrowly scoped workaround guarded by both provider id and context window size checks, with regression tests for both branches. The logic change is small and well-tested. Non-Codex 400K models keep their existing threshold, the optional `providerId` field is backward-compatible, and no data-loss or security paths are touched. No files require special attention beyond the deliberate workaround in `context-window-utils.ts`, which is clearly documented and tracked for future removal.

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a dual-source-of-truth bug where manually deleted session artifact directories could still appear in `listSessions` because their persisted DB/index rows remained. The fix makes missing artifacts authoritative: rows without backing files are filtered immediately from list results and pruned in the background. - **Pagination-based filtering**: `listRowsWithPersistedArtifacts` pages through the adapter with offset/limit rather than fetching a fixed window then filtering, ensuring stale rows near the top of the sorted list can no longer silently under-return valid results. - **Background cleanup**: `startBackgroundSessionCleanup` wires a periodic `pruneMissingArtifactSessions` run into both `HubServerTransport` and `createLocalHubScheduleRuntimeHandlers`, with disposal wiring via the new optional `dispose` on `HubScheduleRuntimeHandlers`. - **Live-session guard**: `pruneMissingArtifactSessions` skips rows whose PID is still alive before checking for missing artifacts, preventing deletion of sessions whose backing storage is transiently unavailable.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The change is safe to merge. The core pagination loop, live-session guard, and in-flight deduplication logic are all correct; the comprehensive new test suite covers the critical edge cases. All three algorithmic concerns from the previous review round (filter-before-slice under-return, live-process deletion, deduplication on promise identity) are now addressed. The `reconcileDeadRunningSession` early-return on missing artifacts prevents the pre-existing ENOENT crash when trying to write manifests to deleted directories. Disposal wiring for both hub transport and schedule runtime handlers is correct and idempotent. No files require special attention. The minor redundant `writeIndex` call in `file-session-service.ts` is the only noteworthy inefficiency and is harmless.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/core/src/session/services/persistence-service.ts | Core change: adds `hasPersistedArtifacts`, `listRowsWithPersistedArtifacts` (paginated), `pruneMissingArtifactSessions`, and `reconcileMissingArtifactSessions` with in-flight deduplication. Also guards `reconcileDeadRunningSession` against writing manifests to non-existent artifact directories. Logic is sound; a subtle edge in the `prunedRootSessionIds` optimisation for DESC-sorted child rows is noted but is harmless. | | sdk/packages/core/src/session/services/file-session-service.ts | Adds `offset` support to `FileSessionPersistenceAdapter.listSessions` and refactors `deleteSession` to continue cascade cleanup even when the parent row is already absent from the index. The `writeIndex` call now always fires at the end of `deleteSession` regardless of whether the primary row existed — harmless but slightly wasteful in the `cascade=false, no-op` path. | | sdk/packages/core/src/session/services/persistence-service.test.ts | Adds six new test scenarios: root-session prune for both SQLite and file stores, live-session guard, null-messagesPath child guard, and the critical pagination test that verifies valid sessions beyond a stale window are still returned. | | sdk/packages/core/src/hub/server/hub-server-transport.ts | Wires `startBackgroundSessionCleanup` into the self-constructed `CoreSessionService` path and calls `stopSessionCleanup` during `dispose`. Also calls the new optional `runtimeHandlers.dispose()` at shutdown. Correctly scoped to the self-constructed case only. | | sdk/packages/core/src/hub/daemon/runtime-handlers.ts | Creates the `CoreSessionService` and wires background cleanup before constructing `LocalRuntimeHost`. Adds an idempotent `dispose` that stops cleanup and disposes the session host. Clean implementation. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Caller participant UPS as UnifiedSessionPersistenceService participant Adapter as SessionPersistenceAdapter participant FS as Filesystem Caller->>UPS: listSessions(limit) UPS->>UPS: scheduleMissingArtifactCleanup(cleanupLimit) [fire-and-forget] UPS->>Adapter: "listSessions({status: idle/running/pending})" UPS->>FS: hasPersistedArtifacts per row [reconcileDeadSessions] loop "pagination pages (offset += pageSize)" UPS->>Adapter: "listSessions({limit: pageSize, offset})" loop each row in batch UPS->>FS: hasPersistedArtifacts(row) alt artifacts exist UPS->>UPS: push to results else missing UPS-->>UPS: skip row end end end UPS-->>Caller: rows with resolved metadata Note over UPS: Background cleanup (every 60s) UPS->>Adapter: "listSessions({limit: 2000})" loop each row UPS->>FS: hasPersistedArtifacts(row) alt missing AND not live PID UPS->>Adapter: deleteSession(id, cascade) end end ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 2 sdk/packages/core/src/session/services/file-session-service.ts:217-232 Unnecessary index write on no-op delete. When `existing` is `undefined` and `cascade` is `false`, the function scans and modifies nothing, then writes the unchanged index to disk. For the `(cascade=false, no row found)` path — which is the path hit during the service-level double-delete of a root session — this is a redundant file write on every call. An early-exit guard keeps the write scoped to cases that actually change state. ```suggestion async deleteSession(sessionId: string, cascade: boolean): Promise { const index = this.readIndex(); const existing = index.sessions[sessionId]; if (!existing && !cascade) { return false; } if (existing) { delete index.sessions[sessionId]; } if (cascade) { for (const row of Object.values(index.sessions)) { if (row.parentSessionId === sessionId) { delete index.sessions[row.sessionId]; } } } this.writeIndex(index); return !!existing; } ``` ### Issue 2 of 2 sdk/packages/core/src/session/services/persistence-service.ts:548-585 **`prunedRootSessionIds` optimisation rarely fires due to DESC ordering** Subagent sessions typically start *after* their parent, so in the `started_at DESC` sort they appear *before* the root row. When the loop reaches a child first and calls `deleteSession(child)`, the child is removed. When the root is reached later, `deleteSession(root)` cascades and attempts to remove the already-absent child — `deleteSession` returns `{ deleted: false }`, so `pruned` is not double-counted and nothing breaks. The `prunedRootSessionIds.add` path at line 580 therefore only triggers for children whose `started_at` predates their parent (unusual), providing negligible practical benefit. This is not a bug, but documenting the ordering assumption or restructuring the loop to process roots first would make the invariant clearer. `````

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes duplicate tool rows in the chat transcript by reusing the approval prompt row when the matching SDK tool lifecycle event (`content_start`/`content_end`) arrives, rather than appending a new row. It does so by recording the `(toolCallId → messageTs)` mapping at approval time and consuming it in the message translator. - **`SdkInteractionCoordinator`** stores the pending approval row's `toolCallId` and `messageTs`, then calls `recordApprovedToolMessage` only on an explicit "yes" click — auto-approvals and denials are correctly excluded. - **`MessageTranslatorState`** gains `recordApprovedToolMessageTs` / `consumeApprovedToolMessageTs` / `setStreamingToolTs` / `setSpawnAgentPromptsTs`; the map is cleared on iteration `reset()` and on `raiseCancelFence` to prevent stale entries from surviving task cancellation. - **Tests** now cover all four branches (generic tool, command, MCP, and subagent) as well as single-consumption and auto-approval/denial exclusion.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change is well-scoped, all approval/denial/auto-approve paths are correctly handled, and stale map entries are cleared on both iteration reset and task cancellation. The approved-row timestamp map uses consume-on-first-use semantics so duplicates cannot appear even if content_start fires more than once for the same toolCallId. Cancellation clears the map before bumping the epoch, and per-iteration reset also clears it — no stale entries can carry over. All four tool-type branches (generic, command, MCP, subagent) are covered by new tests, including the single-consumption invariant and exclusion of auto-approvals and denials. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

body:
I used robin's review-team skill to generate this:

## Review-team aggregated review

Ran a fleet of independent reviewers (correctness, architecture, code-quality, simplicity/scope, testing). Security/UX/perf/telemetry/api-compat/docs reviewers were skipped — this is an internal SDK-adapter bugfix with no surface in those areas.

The core mechanism — record `(toolCallId, approvalRowTs)` on approval, then reuse that ts at the matching tool `content_start` so the webview dedups in place — is sound for the common single-tool / command / MCP cases. Reviewers confirmed the `ask`→`say` ts-reuse transition is safe (the `say` row always carries a higher `seq` and wins the wholesale replace in both `task-proxy.ts` and `messageReducer.ts`), and that auto-approve and `ask_question` correctly record nothing. Three substantive issues and several cleanups remain.

### High / Medium — recommend addressing before merge

**1. Parallel `spawn_agent` approvals leave an orphaned, stale subagent row** *(flagged by correctness + architecture + testing)*
`message-translator.ts` (~L925-928, spawn_agent `content_start` branch). All parallel `spawn_agent` calls aggregate into one `use_subagents` row keyed by `spawnAgentPromptsTs`, but the fix calls `setSpawnAgentPromptsTs(approvedToolMessageTs)` for *each* approved call. The last approved call's ts wins; earlier approval rows are never reused and never finalized — they remain in the transcript as stale `partial` subagent rows that spin forever. This reintroduces the duplicate-row symptom the PR fixes, for the multi-subagent case.
*Fix:* only adopt the approved ts on the first call (when `spawnAgentPromptsTs` is still undefined), e.g. guard with `state.getSpawnAgentItems().length === 1`, or make `setSpawnAgentPromptsTs` a no-op once set.

**2. `approvedToolMessageTsByCallId` Map has no reset path — entries leak** *(correctness + architecture)*
`message-translator.ts` (~L125). Entries are removed only on a matching `consumeApprovedToolMessageTs`. If an approved tool never reaches a matching `content_start` (turn aborted/cancelled after approval, id mismatch), the entry persists for the whole session. `reset()` (per-iteration) and `clearSpawnAgents()` explicitly enumerate every other streaming pointer but **not** this Map, so a future maintainer adding a reset won't know to clear it. A later tool reusing the same `toolCallId` string would snap onto a dead approval ts.
*Fix:* clear the Map in the iteration/turn reset (and on cancel via the coordinator's `clearPending` path), or document explicitly why it must survive resets.

**3. Tests prove the two halves but not the actual regression** *(testing)*
- The only translator test covers the generic `editor` path; the **command**, **MCP**, and **spawn_agent** reuse paths are untested even though they read different ts pointers (`message-translator.test.ts` ~L164).
- No test for the **integrated** coordinator→translator flow — the added tests record ts manually (`state.recordApprovedToolMessageTs(.., 42)`) rather than proving the coordinator's recorded ts equals the real approval-row ts. This is precisely the invariant the PR exists to enforce.
- No test for **consume-once** (a second `content_start` with the same callId must mint a fresh ts), and no negative assertion that **auto-approve does NOT record**.
*Fix:* add sibling cases for command/MCP/spawn_agent reuse; one integration test wiring a real `MessageTranslatorState` as the `recordApprovedToolMessage` sink; a consume-once assertion; and `expect(recordApprovedToolMessage).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` in the auto-approve tests.

### Low — optional cleanups

**4. Simplicity: a `Map` models a single-slot handshake.** The coordinator tracks at most one pending approval (`pendingToolApprovalMessage` is a single field; approvals are serialized). A single `{ toolCallId, ts } | undefined` would make the leak window self-evident and match the producer's design.

**5. Implicit cross-branch coupling in `content_start "tool"`.** `approvedToolMessageTs` is consumed once at the top of the branch and re-applied ~50 lines later inside the spawn_agent branch; intervening branches silently inherit the top-level `setStreamingToolTs`. A new tool sub-branch reading a different ts pointer would silently fail to dedup. Add a one-line comment explaining the split, or centralize via a single `getToolRowTs(toolCallId)` helper.

**6. Naming/doc drift.** The coordinator option `recordApprovedToolMessage` drops the `Ts` suffix used everywhere else in the chain (`recordApprovedToolMessageTs`, `approvedToolMessageTsByCallId`), and lacks the "Optional for tests" JSDoc that sibling optionals (`getMinter?`, `setTurnPhase?`) carry (`sdk-interaction-coordinator.ts` ~L23). Consider making it required and passing a no-op in tests so a forgotten wiring fails loudly rather than silently reintroducing duplicates.

### Note on verification
`npm run test:vitest`, `tsc --noEmit`, and `npm run lint` were reported green — but they do not exercise findings #1–#3, which are the material gaps.

**Recommended action:** treat #1 (spawn_agent orphan) and #2 (map leak/reset) as the priority items, and add the #3 tests (especially the command/MCP path and the integrated flow) to lock the fix. #4–#6 are quick follow-up cleanups.

Fixes Cerebras follow-up request failures by stripping `reasoning` content parts from assistant history before the payload is sent to the Cerebras API, which rejects `assistant.reasoning_content` on multi-turn requests. The fix is scoped to Cerebras via provider-ID and base-URL detection, leaving reasoning replay intact for all other providers. - `isCerebrasProvider` inspects `request.providerId`, `context.config.providerId`, and `context.provider.id` plus the configured base URL; `toAiSdkMessages` gains an `includeReasoning` option toggled by the result, applied at both the cached and uncached call-sites. - A regression test in `gateway.test.ts` validates the three-message shape (user → assistant with reasoning+text → user) and asserts that the outgoing `streamText` call carries no `reasoning` key.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge for the common Cerebras multi-turn case; two minor edge cases (reasoning-only assistant turns and base-URL variants without `/v1`) are unlikely to occur in practice but worth hardening. The core fix is well-scoped: provider detection is applied consistently at both `toAiSdkMessages` call-sites, the option defaults to `true` so all other providers are unaffected, and the regression test confirms the expected message shape. The two gaps — an assistant turn whose entire content is reasoning (which would produce `content: ""` after stripping) and a Cerebras base URL configured without the `/v1` path suffix — are unlikely in the current product but are real code paths that could surface in edge deployments. Greptile Summary

This PR restores skill and workflow commands to the slash autocomplete dropdown by changing `visible` and `selectable` from dynamically computed (hidden for `user-command` execution type) to unconditionally `true` in `entryFromRuntimeCommand`. This makes `getVisibleUserSlashCommands` return enabled skills so the autocomplete hook can surface them in the dropdown, while `/skills` picker and manual expansion continue to work on the same paths as before. - **`entryFromRuntimeCommand`** (`slash-command-registry.ts`): removes the `const visible = execution !== \"user-command\"` gate and hard-codes both `visible: true` and `selectable: true` for all runtime entries (skills, workflows, plugins, and generic runtime commands). - **Tests** (`slash-command-registry.test.ts`): updates the renamed test case to assert both `visible: true` / `selectable: true` and that `getVisibleUserSlashCommands` now returns the expected skill/workflow names; adds an assertion for `formatSlashCommandAutocompleteValue`.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The change is a targeted one-line removal and two literal substitutions that restore previously-broken autocomplete visibility for skills and workflows; no functional regressions found. The fix is minimal and correct: removing the visibility gate that inadvertently hid all user-command entries restores autocomplete behaviour without touching expansion logic, the /skills picker, or submit-time processing. The only observation is that getInvokableUserSlashCommands and getVisibleUserSlashCommands now return identical results, leaving the two-function API with a distinction that no longer exists in practice. Greptile Summary

This PR patches two transitive CVEs introduced via `@opentui/core@0.1.102`: a DoS in `diff` (CVE-2026-24001) and a ReDoS in `marked` (AIKIDO-2026-10452). No upstream fix is available in `@opentui/core` yet, so the fixes are applied via forced version pinning. - `diff` is patched to `8.0.3` via a proper root-level `overrides` entry in `package.json`, which bun respects monorepo-wide (`bun.lock` confirms the global resolution bumped from 8.0.2 → 8.0.3). - `marked` is patched to `17.0.5` by pinning the CLI's direct dependency (changed from `^15.0.12`), relying on bun deduplication rather than a matching `overrides` entry; this also collapses two previously scoped `17.0.6` entries for `@cline/code` and `streamdown` down to the global `17.0.5`. The VS Code extension (`apps/vscode`) uses a separate npm tree with `diff@8.0.4` and `react-markdown` (not `marked` directly), so it is unaffected.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge for the diff fix; the marked upgrade carries a major-version jump (v15 → v17) for packages that previously resolved to the old global version, which could affect runtime rendering paths not covered by the CLI unit tests. The diff patch is clean and correctly implemented. The marked bump collapses two separate version lines (15.x global and 17.x scoped) into a single 17.x global — any code that previously ran against marked@15.x now runs against 17.x, a major version with renamed/removed APIs. The CLI unit tests exercise 95/98 cases but are unlikely to cover all rendering paths that depend on marked internals. Pay close attention to bun.lock — the collapsed marked entries (dropping scoped 17.0.6 for @cline/code and streamdown, and bumping the global from 15.0.12) are the highest-impact change and deserve manual verification of all rendering paths that consume marked at runtime.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | package.json | Adds overrides: { diff: 8.0.3 } to the bun/npm workspace root — correct mechanism for forcing a patched transitive dep monorepo-wide. | | sdk/apps/cli/package.json | Pins marked to exact 17.0.5 (was ^15.0.12) to force bun deduplication to the patched version; no root-level override added for marked unlike the diff fix. | | bun.lock | Reflects updated resolutions: global diff bumped to 8.0.3, global marked bumped from 15.0.12 to 17.0.5 (dropping scoped 17.0.6 entries for @cline/code and streamdown), and a new overrides block for diff. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A["CVE-2026-24001 / AIKIDO-2026-10452\n(diff + marked vulnerabilities\nin @opentui/core@0.1.102)"] --> B{Fix strategy} B --> C["diff fix\noverrides: diff → 8.0.3\nin root package.json"] B --> D["marked fix\nPins CLI direct dep\nto 17.0.5"] C --> E["bun.lock: global diff\n8.0.2 → 8.0.3"] D --> F["bun.lock: global marked\n15.0.12 → 17.0.5\n(drops @cline/code + streamdown\nscoped 17.0.6 entries)"] F --> G["mermaid (if transitive) now\ngoes from 15.x to 17.x\n⚠ major-version jump"] E --> H["VS Code ext already\nhas diff@8.0.4\n(separate npm tree, unaffected)"] ```

Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 1 package.json:63-65 The `diff` vulnerability is fixed via a root `overrides` entry, which enforces the patched version regardless of what any transitive dependent declares. The `marked` fix uses a different mechanism — pinning the CLI's direct dependency — which only works as long as bun deduplicates it to that single version. If the CLI's direct `marked` dep is ever removed or changed to a range that bun resolves differently, `@opentui/core`'s transitive copy could silently revert to a vulnerable version. Greptile Summary

This PR adds first-class support for installing official Cline plugins by short keyword (e.g. `cline plugin install web-search`), cloning `cline/plugins` under the hood and copying only the matching `plugins/` subdirectory into the install area. - Introduces an `"official"` parsed-source variant, `isOfficialPluginSlug` (lowercase-kebab regex), `installOfficialPlugin` (shallow-clone → copy → dep-install), and a dedicated `_installed/official` install path. - Adds a `CLINE_OFFICIAL_PLUGINS_REPO` override option in `PluginInstallOptions` and the claimed `CLINE_OFFICIAL_PLUGINS_REPO` env var for pointing at a local mirror; the env var reads work only through the programmatic API (tests pass it directly) but the variable is not actually read from `process.env` in `resolveOfficialPluginsRepo`, so CLI users cannot use it. - Five new integration-level tests cover slug install, package-plugin npm dep invocation, missing slug error, local-path disambiguation, and JSON output.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge after fixing the env var wiring; the core install flow and test coverage are solid. The official plugin install path is correctly implemented end-to-end, and the test suite covers the main scenarios well. The one concrete defect is that `resolveOfficialPluginsRepo` never reads `process.env.CLINE_OFFICIAL_PLUGINS_REPO`, so the advertised CLI-level env override silently does nothing — users pointing at a local mirror via this variable will get a live GitHub clone instead, with no warning. apps/cli/src/commands/plugin.ts — `resolveOfficialPluginsRepo` needs a `process.env` read to match the documented behavior.

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/cli/src/commands/plugin.ts | Adds official plugin slug parsing, install path routing, and `installOfficialPlugin` (shallow clone + copy + dependency install). Greptile Summary

This PR adds a `GatewayProviderRegistration` API that lets host extensions register custom LLM providers at activation time, and implements that API with a GitHub Copilot provider backed by the VS Code Language Model API. - **New `gateway-provider-registry.ts`** exposes `registerGatewayProvider` / `unregisterGatewayProvider` / `getRegisteredGatewayProviders` / `resetGatewayProviderRegistry` as a module-level singleton, re-exported through `@cline/llms` and `@cline/core`. - **`DefaultGateway` constructor** now reads the singleton registry and copies registered providers into its local `GatewayRegistry` alongside the built-ins, enabling streamed requests through custom providers. - **`extension.ts` example** registers GitHub Copilot (with dynamic model discovery via `vscode.lm.selectChatModels`), converts agent messages to VS Code LM format, handles streaming tool calls, and forces the hub to run in the extension host process so `vscode.lm` is accessible.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge for the Copilot-specific path, but the public registerGatewayProvider API has a silent ordering trap for external consumers. The Copilot integration itself works correctly because registerGitHubCopilotProvider() is called in activate() before any gateway construction. However, the new public API (registerGatewayProvider exported from @cline/core) is designed for external consumers who want to register additional providers at run time, yet DefaultGateway only reads the singleton once at construction. A consumer who creates a gateway first and registers their provider second will get a silent miss with no error thrown. sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/gateway.ts — the DefaultGateway constructor's one-time snapshot of getRegisteredGatewayProviders() is the source of the ordering constraint.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/gateway-provider-registry.ts | New module-level singleton map for runtime gateway provider registration. Clean and minimal, but the snapshot-at-construction pattern in DefaultGateway means late registrations are silently ignored. | | sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/gateway.ts | Integrates the new gateway provider registry by reading it once in DefaultGateway's constructor. The snapshot-at-construction design conflicts with the register-at-run-time intent of the public API. | | apps/examples/vscode/src/extension.ts | Adds GitHub Copilot as a gateway provider via the VS Code LM API. Addresses previously flagged issues (system prompt role, finish reason, estimateTokens). Minor ordering inefficiency in loadModels and the hub-owner label change pins all providers to the extension host process. | | sdk/packages/llms/src/index.ts | Re-exports the four new gateway registry functions alongside existing provider utilities. Clean pass-through with no issues. | | sdk/packages/llms/src/providers.ts | Barrel re-export for gateway-provider-registry functions. Straightforward addition with no issues. | | sdk/packages/core/src/index.ts | Promotes the four gateway registry functions to the @cline/core public surface as named exports alongside the existing Llms namespace re-export. Both paths reference the same module-level singleton so there is no divergence. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Ext as extension.ts (activate) participant Reg as gateway-provider-registry (singleton) participant GW as DefaultGateway (constructor) participant GWReg as GatewayRegistry participant Copilot as vscode.lm (Copilot) Ext->>Reg: registerGatewayProvider(copilotRegistration) Note over Reg: Map stores provider by manifest.id Ext->>GW: createGateway() / hub starts GW->>Reg: getRegisteredGatewayProviders() Reg-->>GW: [copilotRegistration] GW->>GWReg: registerProvider(copilotRegistration) Note over GW: snapshot taken – late registrations missed Ext->>GW: "stream({ providerId: 'github-copilot', ... })" GW->>GWReg: resolveModel + createProvider GW->>Copilot: model.sendRequest(messages, tools, token) Copilot-->>GW: stream chunks (TextPart / ToolCallPart) GW-->>Ext: AgentModelEvent stream (text-delta / tool-call-delta / finish) ```

Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 2 sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/gateway.ts:227-229 **Registry snapshot taken at construction, not at request time** `getRegisteredGatewayProviders()` is called once in the constructor and the results are copied into the local `GatewayRegistry`. Any provider registered via the new public `registerGatewayProvider()` API *after* a `DefaultGateway` (or `createGateway()`) instance is already created will be silently absent from that instance. The PR description explicitly markets this as "allows clients to register additional providers at run time," which implies dynamic registration, but the implementation only reflects the registry state at construction time. A consumer who calls `registerGatewayProvider(myProvider)` and then streams a request through an already-created gateway will get a "provider not found" error with no warning. body:
Blocking Vitest workspace issue

The new root `vitest.workspace.ts` is written in the old workspace shape:

```ts
export default [
	"sdk/packages/agents/vitest.config.ts",
	"sdk/packages/core/vitest.config.ts",
	"sdk/packages/hub/vitest.config.ts",
	"sdk/packages/llms/vitest.config.ts",
	"apps/cli/vitest.config.ts",
];
```

With the repo's current Vitest 4 install, that file is not a valid config when loaded directly. Repro from the repo root:

```sh
bunx vitest list --config vitest.workspace.ts --filesOnly --passWithNoTests
```

That fails with:

```text
config must export or return an object.
```

That means anyone trying to use the promoted root workspace file gets a config load failure instead of the SDK and CLI projects. Vitest 4 expects projects to be configured through `test.projects`, for example:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "vitest/config";

export default defineConfig({
	test: {
		projects: [
			"sdk/packages/agents/vitest.config.ts",
			"sdk/packages/core/vitest.config.ts",
			"sdk/packages/llms/vitest.config.ts",
			"apps/cli/vitest.config.ts",
		],
	},
});
```

There is one more issue in the same file: `sdk/packages/hub/vitest.config.ts` is listed, but that file does not exist on this branch. So even after changing to `test.projects`, the hub entry needs to be removed or corrected.

This is the only thing I would block on here because the PR is moving this config into the root, but the moved root config is not currently usable.

This PR fixes a broken `npm ci` step in the VS Code extension CI by removing a self-referential `\"workspaces\": [\".\"]` field from `apps/vscode/package.json` that caused npm to fail, and updates all four GitHub Actions workflows to install dependencies from the workspace root using `npm --prefix` rather than `cd`-relative commands. - **Root cause fix**: `apps/vscode/package.json` had `\"workspaces\": [\".\"]` pointing to itself; the entry is removed from `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, and `bun.lock`, and the root `package.json` now excludes `apps/vscode` from bun workspaces with `\"!apps/vscode\"`. - **Workflow updates**: All four CI workflows now run install steps from `${{ github.workspace }}` using `npm --prefix apps/vscode ci`, and the nightly workflow gains a missing job-level `defaults.run.working-directory: apps/vscode`. - **Supporting changes**: biome scripts now use explicit `--config-path ./biome.jsonc`, `check-types` drops `npx` in favour of local-bin `tsc`, `tsconfig.json` adds explicit `typeRoots`, and `biome.jsonc` adds `.vscode-test` to its ignore list.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the changes cleanly remove the self-referential workspace that was breaking npm ci and consistently update all four CI workflows to the new install pattern. The root cause (apps/vscode declaring itself as a workspace member) is correctly addressed across package.json, package-lock.json, and bun.lock. All four workflows now follow the same install pattern with explicit working-directory overrides and job-level defaults. The nightly workflow also gains the previously missing job-level working-directory default. No logic regressions were found. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/vscode/package.json | Removes self-referential workspaces:["."] (root cause of npm ci failure), updates biome scripts to use explicit --config-path and --since main, drops npx from tsc invocations. | | .github/workflows/ext-vscode-publish-nightly.yml | Adds job-level defaults.run.working-directory: apps/vscode (previously missing) and updates install steps to use npm --prefix with workspace-root working-directory override. | | .github/workflows/ext-vscode-test.yml | Updates all install steps to use npm --prefix with explicit working-directory across quality-checks, vscode-test, and test-platform-integration jobs. | | .github/workflows/ext-vscode-publish-stable.yml | Consistent with other workflows — install steps updated to npm --prefix with workspace-root override; publish job already had job-level working-directory default. | | .github/workflows/ext-vscode-test-e2e.yml | E2E workflow install steps updated to npm --prefix pattern; testing-platform install step also corrected. | | package.json | Adds !apps/vscode exclusion to the root bun workspaces array so bun no longer tries to manage the npm-only VS Code package. | | bun.lock | Removes the apps/vscode workspace entry and its full dependency tree, consistent with the workspace exclusion in the root package.json. | | apps/vscode/package-lock.json | Removes the self-referential workspaces field and node_modules/claude-dev self-link mirroring the removed workspaces:["."] in package.json. | | apps/vscode/tsconfig.json | Adds explicit typeRoots pointing to ./node_modules/@types and ./src/types; remaining changes are formatting-only. | | sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/vendors/anthropic.test.ts | Trivial change: adds a missing newline at end of file. |

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR adds `prompt_cache_key` support to the OpenAI provider by threading the session `ulid` through `createHandlerForProvider` and spreading it into the `chat.completions.create` call when present. However, two unintended changes were included: a new `apps/vscode/.vscode/settings.json` with Prettier settings that conflict with the project's Biome formatter, and a build-script change in `build-proto.mjs` that is unrelated to the feature. - **`src/core/api/index.ts` + `providers/openai.ts`**: Core feature — `ulid` is forwarded to `OpenAiHandler` and emitted as `prompt_cache_key: \"cline-{ulid}\"` in the streaming request, matching the pattern used by Vertex, Gemini, and LiteLLM providers. - **`apps/vscode/.vscode/settings.json`** (new file): Adds Prettier config (`tabWidth: 4`, spaces) that conflicts with the repo-wide Biome formatter (`indentStyle: tab`), causing the entire `build-proto.mjs` to be reformatted as a side-effect. - **`apps/vscode/scripts/build-proto.mjs`**: Besides the whitespace reformatting, the Windows `TS_PROTO_PLUGIN` path was changed from `.cmd` to `.exe` — a change that may break Windows proto compilation if the `.exe` binary is not present in `node_modules/.bin/`.

Confidence Score: 3/5

Not safe to merge as-is — two unintended files need to be reverted before the feature change can land cleanly. The prompt_cache_key feature itself is a small, well-scoped addition that follows the established pattern used by Gemini and LiteLLM. The problem is the two accidental inclusions: the new .vscode/settings.json (Prettier config that contradicts Biome) caused build-proto.mjs to be reformatted wholesale, and within that noise a .cmd → .exe change was introduced that could break Windows proto compilation. Both of these unrelated changes need to be dropped before the PR can be merged safely. apps/vscode/.vscode/settings.json and apps/vscode/scripts/build-proto.mjs both contain unintended changes that should be reverted.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/vscode/.vscode/settings.json | New file adds Prettier workspace settings that conflict with the project's Biome formatter (tabs), causing build-proto.mjs to be reformatted with spaces — should not be committed. | | apps/vscode/scripts/build-proto.mjs | Entirely reformatted from tabs to spaces (Prettier side-effect) plus one substantive change: Windows plugin path changed from .cmd to .exe, which may not exist in node_modules/.bin/ and could break Windows proto builds. | | apps/vscode/src/core/api/index.ts | Passes ulid from ApiConfiguration into OpenAiHandler options, consistent with how other caching-capable providers (Vertex, Gemini, LiteLLM) already receive it. | | apps/vscode/src/core/api/providers/openai.ts | Adds ulid option and spreads prompt_cache_key into the chat completions request when ulid is present; import order rewritten by Prettier. The unconditional injection to custom base-URL endpoints was already raised in a prior review thread. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Task as Cline Task participant Index as api/index.ts participant Handler as OpenAiHandler participant API as OpenAI API Task->>Index: createHandlerForProvider(options) Note over Index: options.ulid forwarded to OpenAiHandler Index->>Handler: "new OpenAiHandler({ ulid, ... })" Handler->>Handler: createMessage(systemPrompt, messages) Note over Handler: ulid present? alt ulid present Handler->>API: "chat.completions.create({ prompt_cache_key: cline-{ulid}, ... })" else ulid absent Handler->>API: "chat.completions.create({ ... })" end API-->>Handler: stream with cache_tokens in usage Handler-->>Task: yield chunks (text, usage, etc.) ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 2 apps/vscode/.vscode/settings.json:1-8 **Conflicts with project-wide Biome formatter, causing build-proto.mjs reformatting** This file introduces workspace-level Prettier configuration (`tabWidth: 4`, spaces), but the project uses Biome with `"indentStyle": "tab"` (enforced in `biome.json` and the root `.vscode/settings.json` which sets `"editor.defaultFormatter": "biomejs.biome"`). The direct consequence is visible in this PR's diff: `build-proto.mjs` was reformatted from tabs to 4-space indentation, bloating the diff with ~170 whitespace-only lines that make the two substantive changes (the `.cmd` → `.exe` line and the `prompt_cache_key` addition) harder to review. This file should not be committed. ### Issue 2 of 2 apps/vscode/scripts/build-proto.mjs:38-39 **Unrelated build-script change may break Windows proto compilation** The Windows plugin path was changed from `protoc-gen-ts_proto.cmd` to `protoc-gen-ts_proto.exe`. On Windows, `npm` creates `.cmd` (and `.ps1`) wrappers in `node_modules/.bin/` for Node.js executables — a `.exe` file is not normally generated there unless the package ships a prebuilt native binary. If `protoc-gen-ts_proto.exe` does not exist in `.bin/`, `execFileSync` will throw and the entire proto build will fail on Windows with a cryptic path-not-found error. This change is also unrelated to the PR's stated goal (`prompt_cache_key` support) and should be evaluated separately with confirmation that the file actually exists on a Windows npm install. `````

Greptile Summary

This PR guards `addRemoteServer` and `deleteServerRPC` with the existing `isUpdatingClineSettings` flag so the `chokidar` file watcher skips re-processing the settings file after those methods write it, preventing a race condition that could empty the server list. The pattern is identical to the one already used by `toggleToolAutoApproveRPC`, `toggleToolAutoApprove`, and `updateServerTimeoutRPC`. - `McpHub.ts`: Sets `isUpdatingClineSettings = true` before each method's body and clears it via `setTimeout(..., 300)` in the `finally` block, matching all pre-existing guarded writes. - `McpHub.deleteServerRPC.test.ts`: Adds four focused regression tests—list integrity, file persistence, flag timing with Sinon fake timers, and guard cleanup on throw.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change is a narrow, mechanical application of a guard pattern that already exists and is tested in four other write methods in the same file. The two modified methods now follow exactly the same `isUpdatingClineSettings` + 300ms `setTimeout` pattern used by every other settings-writing method in McpHub. The new test suite directly verifies the flag is live during the write, is still live immediately after, and is cleared on schedule — including the error path. No logic was restructured; only the missing guard was added. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/vscode/src/services/mcp/McpHub.ts | Adds `isUpdatingClineSettings = true` guard at the start of `addRemoteServer` and `deleteServerRPC`, with a matching 300ms `setTimeout` reset in `finally` blocks — consistent with the identical pattern already used by `toggleToolAutoApproveRPC`, `toggleToolAutoApprove`, and `updateServerTimeoutRPC`. | | apps/vscode/src/services/mcp/__tests__/McpHub.deleteServerRPC.test.ts | New regression test suite covering: remaining-server list integrity after delete, settings file persistence, flag-during-write assertion with fake timers, and guard cleanup on error paths. |

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a migration gap where Cline users who authenticated via OAuth (without a `clineApiKey`) were silently logged out when upgrading to the SDK-backed extension, because `collectCandidateProviderIds` only recognised the Cline provider when `clineApiKey` was present. - Adds a `cline:clineAccountId` check in `collectCandidateProviderIds` so OAuth-only Cline accounts are treated as valid migration candidates and their tokens land in `providers.json` with `tokenSource: \"migration\"`. - Normalises legacy seconds-based `expiresAt` timestamps to milliseconds in `resolveLegacyClineAuth` using a `< 10_000_000_000` heuristic, with regression tests for both the millisecond-preserve and seconds-normalise paths.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge; the change is narrowly scoped to a one-time startup migration path and cannot affect users who have already migrated or who have no legacy Cline data. The core fix is straightforward and the added test exercises the happy path end-to-end. The only open questions are cosmetic: the epoch boundary comment, a redundant JSON parse, and a test that doesn't pin how many providers are migrated when globalState names an unrelated active provider. sdk/packages/core/src/services/storage/provider-settings-legacy-migration.ts and its test file — specifically the integration test's implicit assumption about providerCount.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/core/src/services/storage/provider-settings-legacy-migration.ts | Two targeted changes: adds cline:clineAccountId as a candidate trigger in collectCandidateProviderIds (fixing the OAuth-only migration gap), and normalises seconds-based expiresAt values to milliseconds in resolveLegacyClineAuth. Logic is correct but the threshold comment does not explain the numeric boundary. | | sdk/packages/core/src/services/storage/provider-settings-legacy-migration.test.ts | Adds an integration test for OAuth-only Cline migration and a unit test for the seconds-to-milliseconds normalisation. Tests are correct but the integration test does not assert providerCount, leaving a gap around whether the unrelated anthropic candidate also migrates. | | bun.lock | Minor version bump of the vscode app from 3.86.2 to 3.87.0 in the lock file. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[migrateLegacyProviderSettings] --> B[resolveLegacyStorage] B --> C{secrets.json / globalState.json found?} C -- No --> Z[return migrated: false] C -- Yes --> D[collectCandidateProviderIds] D --> E{clineApiKey present?} E -- Yes --> F[add cline candidate] D --> G{cline:clineAccountId has accessToken / refreshToken / accountId?} G -- Yes --> F G -- No --> H[skip cline OAuth path] D --> I[other provider checks] F --> J[buildLegacyProviderSettings for cline] J --> K[resolveLegacyClineAuth normalise expiresAt s to ms] K --> L{expiresAt < 10_000_000_000?} L -- Yes seconds --> M[multiply x 1000] L -- No ms --> N[keep as-is] M --> O[ProviderSettings with auth] N --> O O --> P[write providers.json tokenSource: migration] ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 3 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 3 sdk/packages/core/src/services/storage/provider-settings-legacy-migration.ts:214-222 The `10_000_000_000` boundary lacks an inline explanation of what the two sides of the comparison actually represent. `10_000_000_000` seconds ≈ year 2286 (practically unreachable for any token expiry), while `10_000_000_000` ms ≈ April 2001 (safely in the past). A reader who doesn't know the epoch arithmetic must reverse-engineer the intent from the existing prose comment above. Adding a concise note makes the boundary self-documenting and prevents a future developer from adjusting it incorrectly. ```suggestion const expiresAt = typeof data.expiresAt === "number" && Number.isFinite(data.expiresAt) ? // Classic VS Code auth stored expiresAt in seconds; providers.json uses // milliseconds. The threshold 10_000_000_000 equals ~year 2286 in // seconds and ~April 2001 in milliseconds, so any realistic token // expiry timestamp is unambiguously one side or the other. data.expiresAt < 10_000_000_000 ? data.expiresAt * 1000 : data.expiresAt : undefined; ``` ### Issue 2 of 3 sdk/packages/core/src/services/storage/provider-settings-legacy-migration.ts:684-693 **Double-parsing of `cline:clineAccountId`** `resolveLegacyClineAuth` is called here in `collectCandidateProviderIds` to gate candidacy, and then called a second time inside `buildLegacyProviderSettings` (line ~481) for the actual settings construction. Because both call sites receive the same raw string, the JSON is parsed twice per migration run. No correctness impact, but if you want to avoid the redundancy the result could be threaded through as an optional parameter or resolved once at the top of `migrateLegacyProviderSettings`. ### Issue 3 of 3 sdk/packages/core/src/services/storage/provider-settings-legacy-migration.test.ts:180-228 **Integration test does not pin `providerCount`** The test's `globalState.json` sets `actModeApiProvider: "anthropic"`, which causes `collectCandidateProviderIds` to add "anthropic" as a candidate. `buildLegacyProviderSettings("anthropic", ...)` will succeed with only a default model (no `apiKey` required for `hasNonProviderFields`), so "anthropic" may also appear in the migrated providers alongside "cline". Adding `expect(result.providerCount).toBe(1)` (or `2` if the dual-provider outcome is intended) would make the test's exact scope explicit and guard against unexpected provider bleed-through. `````

This PR adds Slack socket mode as an alternative to webhook mode, allowing the connector to run without a public-facing URL. Connection mode is inferred automatically from the presence of `--base-url`: a non-empty value selects webhook mode, an absent or empty value selects socket mode. - **Connector** (`slack.ts`): `inferSlackConnectionMode` drives conditional logic for server startup, signing-secret/clientId/clientSecret scoping, state file fields, and shutdown; `bot.shutdown()` is now called in both modes. - **Wizard & Hub UI** (`platforms.ts`, `index.ts`, `connectors.ts`, `channels-view.tsx`): introduces `FieldCondition`/`shouldIncludeField` for conditional field rendering, `--base-url` becomes the mode switch, and the webview gains a `Select` component path and a `connectionMode` badge on active connectors.

Safe to merge. The socket/webhook branching is well-structured, the existing webhook path is preserved, and the new socket path is cleanly isolated. The implementation is thorough: mode inference is simple and tested, conditional field logic in the wizard and webview is symmetric, and bot.shutdown() is now called in both paths. The one non-blocking note is that socket-mode parse gains explicit required-arg guards while webhook mode does not get a parallel guard for signingSecret. apps/cli/src/connectors/adapters/slack.ts — the parseArgs validation asymmetry between socket and webhook modes is worth a follow-up.

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a bug where free-form user text typed while a tool-approval prompt was pending was incorrectly used as the denial reason, causing it to render as a red tool error instead of a normal chat message. The fix adds a sentinel-based suppression layer in the message translator and a new `messageResponse` branch in the interaction coordinator that denies the pending approval with a known sentinel reason, then returns control to the follow-up path so the user's text is routed correctly. - **`tool-approval-denial.ts`** (new): exports two sentinel constants and two predicates used to detect and suppress denial-related events. - **`sdk-interaction-coordinator.ts`**: adds a `messageResponse` early-exit branch that denies the approval with the sentinel reason and returns `false`, plus `recordDeniedToolApproval` calls on both the new and existing denial paths. - **`message-translator.ts`**: adds `deniedToolApprovalsByCallId` tracking and suppression checks at `content_start`, `content_end`, and `error` to prevent denied approvals from rendering as red tool failures.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change is well-scoped, all new code paths are covered by focused unit tests, and there are no correctness or data-integrity concerns on the changed paths. The fix is narrowly targeted: a new sentinel constant, a new early-exit branch in the approval resolver, and suppression guards in the message translator. Each path has dedicated tests that assert both the suppression and the follow-up routing. No pre-existing behaviour is regressed. apps/vscode/src/sdk/message-translator.ts — minor API duplication (isToolApprovalDenied / checkDeniedToolApproval) worth tidying, but not blocking.

The second `candidatesByInstallPath.set` call overwrites the first, leaving the final candidate with only the last entry's filename in `names`. A user running `cline plugin uninstall index` (to match `index.ts`) on such a plugin gets "No plugin found matching..." even though the plugin exists. `createInstalledCandidate` avoids this by calling `discoverEntriesWithin(installPath)` once and collecting all entries. The direct-candidate path should guard against overwriting an already-collected candidate with the same `installPath` — or resolve the install path first and skip if already registered. `````
