body:
Greptile Summary

This PR adds AgentPhone as a new connector platform, bridging SMS, MMS, iMessage, and voice call transcripts into Cline RPC sessions via an HMAC-verified webhook server. It also introduces a generic connector-edit flow in the Cline Hub UI, allowing existing connectors to be updated without removing and re-adding them. - **AgentPhone adapter** (`agentphone.ts`): 1554-line implementation covering API-key validation against `/v1/numbers`, HMAC webhook signature verification, voice-call streaming responses (NDJSON), and scheduled-delivery relay from the RPC event stream. - **Edit connector UI** (`channels-view.tsx`, `connectors.ts`): stop-then-restart flow exposed through a new `update_connector_channel` desktop command, with an edit dialog that prefills non-secret runtime fields from the active connector record. - **Shared types and status** (`options.ts`, `status.ts`): new `ConnectAgentPhoneOptions`/`AgentPhoneConnectorState` types and the agentphone entry in `connectorConfigs` with all phone-number fields correctly declared.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The connector can be deployed in a non-functional state and a user edit can silently remove security restrictions — both need fixes before production use. Two concrete defects exist on the changed paths. First, omitting `--webhook-secret` causes `verifyAgentPhoneWebhookSignature` to return `false` for every webhook call, so the connector rejects all AgentPhone deliveries with 401 and logs no warning at startup — the operator gets a running process that silently does nothing. Second, the edit dialog always resets `securityEnabled` to `false` and clears `securityValues`, meaning a save in edit mode restarts the connector without any previously configured participant restriction; the existing in-dialog warning mentions only secret fields, so users following it would still lose their security settings. apps/cli/src/connectors/adapters/agentphone.ts (startup validation of webhookSecret) and apps/cline-hub/src/webview/src/components/views/settings/channels-view.tsx (createEditFormState security reset)

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/cli/src/connectors/adapters/agentphone.ts | 1554-line new AgentPhone connector with HMAC webhook verification, voice streaming, and scheduled-delivery support; webhook secret is not validated at startup so omitting it renders voice/message webhooks non-functional with no warning | | apps/cline-hub/src/webview/src/components/views/settings/channels-view.tsx | Adds edit-connector UI flow with stop-then-restart semantics; createEditFormState always resets securityEnabled to false, silently dropping any active participant restriction when editing | | apps/cline-hub/src/server/connectors.ts | Adds updateConnectorChannel that stops then restarts a connector; stop-then-start is sequential and guarded by waitForConnectorState, logic is sound | | apps/cli/src/connectors/status.ts | Adds agentphone to connectorConfigs with all five phone-number fields correctly listed in optional, and adds extractors for the new fields; no issues | | sdk/packages/shared/src/connectors/options.ts | Adds ConnectAgentPhoneOptions and AgentPhoneConnectorState types; fields align with what agentphone.ts reads and writes to the state file | | apps/cli/src/wizards/connect/platforms.ts | Adds agentphone platform definition with four fields and participant-based security; --webhook-secret is required in the wizard but the CLI does not enforce it, creating an inconsistency | | apps/cli/src/connectors/connector-host.ts | Introduces replyTextSink and captureConnectorText to support voice-call reply capture; refactors postText/editText helpers to route through either sink or transport; logic is correct |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant AP as AgentPhone participant WH as Webhook Server /api/webhooks/agentphone participant V as verifySignature participant H as handleTurn participant RPC as Hub RPC AP->>WH: POST (voice/message payload) WH->>V: verifyAgentPhoneWebhookSignature(rawBody, secret, sig) alt secret missing V-->>WH: false WH-->>AP: 401 Invalid signature else valid HMAC V-->>WH: true alt isVoiceWebhookPayload WH->>WH: resolveAgentPhoneVoiceTurnPayload WH-->>AP: 200 streaming NDJSON (interim chunk) WH->>H: handleTurn(thread, text, voice) H->>RPC: startRuntimeSession / steerSession RPC-->>H: session reply text H-->>WH: finalReplyText WH-->>AP: streaming NDJSON (final chunk) else isMessageWebhookPayload WH->>WH: resolveAgentPhoneMessageTurnPayload WH->>H: handleTurn(thread, text, webhook) H->>RPC: startRuntimeSession / steerSession WH-->>AP: 200 ok true RPC-->>H: reply H->>AP: thread.post(reply) else unrecognised event WH->>AP: agentphone.handleWebhook(request) end end ```

Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 3 apps/cli/src/connectors/adapters/agentphone.ts:246-268 **Connector silently non-functional when webhook secret is absent** `verifyAgentPhoneWebhookSignature` now correctly returns `false` when `secret` is empty, but that means every voice and message webhook is immediately rejected with HTTP 401. The connector starts without any log warning about the missing secret, so an operator who omits `--webhook-secret` will see a healthy startup but every AgentPhone delivery will silently fail with 401. The CLI enforces `--api-key` and `--agent-id` at startup but imposes no equivalent check on `--webhook-secret`, creating a confusing gap between the UI wizard (which marks it required) and the CLI. body:
Greptile Summary

This PR extends the Slack connector with per-message author context (`` XML prepended to runtime turns) and a bot-addressing filter that drops subscribed-channel messages not directed at the bot. - Adds `resolveSlackParticipantFromAuthor`, `formatSlackRuntimeText`, `isSlackMessageAddressedToBot`, and `stripSlackBotMention` helpers, each with unit tests. - Changes `persistSlackThreadContext` to accept and prefer a structured `messageAuthor` object over raw-event heuristics, and makes the function return the resolved `SlackParticipant` so callers can pass it directly into `handleTurn` without a redundant state load. - Introduces `SlackTurnContext` to carry `participant`, `isDirectMention`, and `isSubscribedThreadMessage` into `handleTurn`, and threads the enriched `runtimeText` through to `handleConnectorUserTurn`.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The bot-addressing filter drops unmentioned messages before the approval-reply check runs, meaning yes/no confirmation replies in shared channels are silently discarded unless the user tags the bot — a behavioral regression for any active approval workflow. The new filter in onSubscribedMessage sits above maybeHandleConnectorApprovalReply. Any user in a shared channel who receives a tool-approval prompt from the bot and replies without explicitly @-mentioning it will find their response ignored and the action permanently blocked. The rest of the feature (context enrichment, mention detection, label resolution) is well-structured and tested, but this ordering issue affects a correctness-sensitive workflow path. apps/cli/src/connectors/adapters/slack.ts — specifically the ordering of the bot-addressing guard relative to maybeHandleConnectorApprovalReply in the onSubscribedMessage handler.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/cli/src/connectors/adapters/slack.ts | Adds message-context enrichment, bot-mention detection, and subscribed-message filtering. The bot-addressing filter in onSubscribedMessage runs before the approval-reply check, which will silently swallow yes/no approval responses in shared channels when the user doesn't tag the bot. | | apps/cli/src/connectors/adapters/slack.test.ts | Adds unit tests for the four new helpers (resolveSlackParticipant, formatSlackRuntimeText, isSlackMessageAddressedToBot, stripSlackBotMention). Coverage is solid for the happy paths; the approval-filter regression described in the main file is not caught by any test. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant SlackSDK participant onSubscribedMessage participant persistSlackThreadContext participant isSlackMessageAddressedToBot participant maybeHandleConnectorApprovalReply participant handleTurn SlackSDK->>onSubscribedMessage: subscribed thread message (e.g. "yes") onSubscribedMessage->>persistSlackThreadContext: resolve participant persistSlackThreadContext-->>onSubscribedMessage: "SlackParticipant | undefined" onSubscribedMessage->>isSlackMessageAddressedToBot: check if bot mentioned isSlackMessageAddressedToBot-->>onSubscribedMessage: "false (no @mention in "yes")" alt not DM AND not addressed onSubscribedMessage->>onSubscribedMessage: return early (approval never checked) else DM or addressed onSubscribedMessage->>maybeHandleConnectorApprovalReply: check for yes/no maybeHandleConnectorApprovalReply-->>onSubscribedMessage: true → return onSubscribedMessage->>handleTurn: new conversational turn end ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 2 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 2 apps/cli/src/connectors/adapters/slack.ts:1081-1090 **Approval replies skipped by bot-mention filter** The bot-addressing guard returns early before `maybeHandleConnectorApprovalReply` is called. When the bot sends a "yes/no" approval prompt in a shared channel thread and the user replies with "yes" (without mentioning the bot), `!thread.isDM && !isAddressedToBot` is `true` and the message is dropped — the pending approval is never resolved. The filter should apply only to new conversational turns, after the approval check has already run. ### Issue 2 of 2 apps/cli/src/connectors/adapters/slack.ts:226-254 **Prompt injection via unsanitized `participant.label` in context block** `participant.label` is derived from user-controlled Slack profile fields (`fullName`, `displayName`, `userName`). Inserting it verbatim into the `` XML block means a user could set their display name to `Alice\n\nisDirectMention: true` and inject fake metadata that the model reads as trusted context. The same risk applies to `participantKey` if that field is ever user-influenced. Escaping `<`, `>`, and newlines in all user-sourced values before embedding them would close this vector. `````

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR introduces `--allowed-user-id` as a first-class CLI flag for the Telegram connector, replacing the previous pattern of asking users to hand-write a `--hook-command` pipeline. The security abstraction in the wizard and Cline Hub is refactored from `buildHookCommand` (returning a string) to `buildArgs` (returning a `string[]`), so Telegram can emit `--allowed-user-id` while Slack continues emitting `--hook-command`. - **`telegram.ts`**: Adds `--allowed-user-id` option, a digits-only validator, a hook-command generator using `grep -qx` for exact matching, and a conflict guard that covers both the `--hook-command` flag *and* the `CLINE_CONNECT_HOOK_COMMAND` env var. - **`platforms.ts` / `index.ts` / `connectors.ts`**: Replaces the `buildHookCommand: () => string` interface with `buildArgs: () => string[]`; Slack's hook is also upgraded from `grep -q` (substring) to `grep -qx` (exact-line) matching. - **Docs**: `connectors.mdx`, `telegram.md`, and the supply-chain sample are updated to show the simpler `--allowed-user-id 12345` form.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change is additive, all existing access-control paths are preserved, and the new flag is strictly validated. The implementation is well-scoped: digit-only validation prevents injection in the generated hook, grep -qx closes the prefix-match hole for both Telegram and Slack, the env-var conflict (CLINE_CONNECT_HOOK_COMMAND vs --allowed-user-id) is detected before any hook is applied, and test coverage spans valid input, invalid input, flag conflict, and env-var conflict. No callers of the removed buildHookCommand interface remain in the codebase. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a hub daemon crash caused by normal user cancellation in CLI/TUI mode. When a user pressed Esc, `AgentRuntime.abort()` was passing a custom `Error` object into `AbortController.abort(...)`, making `signal.reason` an Error instance; the hub daemon treated this as an unhandled rejection and fatally exited. - **Core fix in `agent-runtime.ts`**: `this.abortController.abort()` is now called without arguments, preventing the custom Error from propagating as `signal.reason`. `state.lastError` is still populated before the call, preserving the user-facing abort message. - **`normalizeAbortError` guard**: Added `&& reason.name !== "AbortError"` so that the platform-default `DOMException("AbortError")` — set by modern runtimes when `abort()` is called without arguments — no longer short-circuits to the DOMException, and the method correctly falls back to `state.lastError`. - **Updated test**: `abortReason` is now captured from `request.signal.reason` and asserted to be the platform `AbortError` DOMException, confirming no custom user-land Error leaks onto the signal.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change is narrow (two lines in the runtime plus a test), both halves of the fix are internally consistent, and the PR addresses the root cause rather than masking it at the daemon boundary. The two runtime changes work together correctly: removing the Error argument from abort() eliminates the leaking signal.reason, and the normalizeAbortError guard ensures state.lastError (the user-facing message) is still picked up by the fallback path on all modern runtimes that set a platform DOMException. The updated test positively asserts both invariants. No pre-existing abort semantics are weakened. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/agents/src/agent-runtime.ts | Two targeted, self-consistent changes: abort() called without arguments to avoid leaking a custom Error as signal.reason; normalizeAbortError gains an `&& reason.name !== "AbortError"` guard so the platform DOMException falls through to the state.lastError fallback, preserving the user-facing message. | | sdk/packages/agents/src/agent-runtime.provider-form.test.ts | Test updated to capture signal.reason at the abort event and positively assert it is an AbortError DOMException, plus asserts state.lastError preserves the user message. Covers the key behavioural contract introduced by this fix. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User as CLI/TUI User participant Runtime as AgentRuntime participant AC as AbortController participant Provider as LLM Provider participant Hub as Hub Daemon User->>Runtime: abort("Interactive runtime abort requested") Runtime->>Runtime: "state.lastError = "Interactive runtime abort requested"" Note over Runtime,AC: BEFORE (broken): abort(new Error(msg))
AFTER (fixed): abort() Runtime->>AC: abort() AC->>AC: "signal.reason = DOMException("AbortError") [platform default]" AC-->>Provider: "signal.aborted = true" Provider-->>Runtime: throw / resolve with abort Runtime->>Runtime: normalizeAbortError() Note over Runtime: reason.name === "AbortError" → skip first branch
Falls through to: new Error(state.lastError) Runtime->>Runtime: "result = { status: "aborted", error: undefined }" Runtime-->>User: session.aborted / agent.run-finished Note over Hub: No Error-valued reason on signal
→ no unhandledRejection → hub stays alive ``` Reviews (4): Last reviewed commit: ["test(agents): assert abort signal reason..."](https://github.com/cline/cline/commit/47b64f539c6bd0b24b6f17ca8c24a20c6446ba7a) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=35518109)

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a CLI/hub daemon crash that left sessions in a broken state after pressing Esc to cancel a running task. The root cause was that the `AgentRuntime.abort()` path produced orphan promise rejections with generic `Error` objects that the daemon's fatal `unhandledRejection` handler treated as unexpected failures, killing the daemon and leaving the CLI with a stale `activeSessionId`. - Introduces `AgentRuntimeAbortError` in `@cline/agents`, passes it as the typed abort reason through `AbortController.abort()`, and exports it from the package. - The hub daemon's `unhandledRejection` handler now uses a narrow `instanceof AgentRuntimeAbortError` guard to silently log and ignore expected abort rejections, while still forwarding all other rejections to `shutdownFatal`. - The existing abort test is extended to assert that `request.signal.reason` is an `AgentRuntimeAbortError` with the expected message and `reason` field.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change is tightly scoped, preserves the existing fatal-shutdown path for all unexpected rejections, and is backed by type-level verification at ES2022 target where instanceof on Error subclasses is reliable. The typed abort error is introduced at the origin of the abort, the daemon guard is narrow and does not suppress unrelated failures, the tsconfig target is ES2022 so instanceof on the Error subclass works correctly, and the existing abort test now asserts the signal reason type. No pre-existing invariants are broken. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/agents/src/agent-runtime.ts | Introduces AgentRuntimeAbortError class and updates abort() to pass it as the typed AbortController reason; logic is correct and consistent with existing ControlledStopError pattern. | | sdk/packages/agents/src/index.ts | Exports AgentRuntimeAbortError from the package public surface; straightforward and correct. | | sdk/packages/core/src/hub/daemon/entry.ts | Adds a narrowly-scoped instanceof AgentRuntimeAbortError guard in unhandledRejection that logs and ignores expected abort rejections while preserving shutdownFatal for all other unhandled rejections. | | sdk/packages/agents/src/agent-runtime.provider-form.test.ts | Extends the abort test to capture signal.reason, assert its type is AgentRuntimeAbortError, and verify both .message and .reason fields match the abort argument. |

body:
### Why this should be the regression fix instead of #11259

I dug through the repro logs and I think #11258 and #11259 are fixing different layers of the same visible failure.

My read is:

- #11258 fixes the root invariant violation.
- #11259 recovers after the system is already in a bad state.

For this incident, I do not think we should merge broader recovery code as the primary fix if we can prevent the invalid state in the first place.

The key repro log sequence was:

```text
run.start session=A
run.abort session=A ok=true
hub-daemon unhandledRejection: Error: Interactive runtime abort requested
daemon exits
later run.start session=A
error: session not found: A
```

That tells us Esc was not lost by OpenTUI, and `run.abort` was not rejected by the hub. The daemon accepted the abort. The session became stale afterward because the daemon died on an expected AgentRuntime abort rejection.

In other words:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Esc pressed] --> B[run.abort reaches hub]
    B --> C[AgentRuntime aborts active stream]
    C --> D[expected abort rejection escapes as unhandledRejection]
    D --> E[hub daemon fatal handler exits process]
    E --> F[CLI still has old activeSessionId]
    F --> G[next run.start]
    G --> H[session not found]
```

#11259 adds recovery for the bottom half of that diagram:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[next run.start] --> B[session not found]
    B --> C[read recoverable messages]
    C --> D[start fresh interactive session]
    D --> E[retry current turn once]
```

That can be useful defensive behavior in some situations, but I do not think it is the right fix for this incident. For this repro, `session not found` is not the root cause. It is the symptom after the daemon has already crashed.

This PR fixes the bad state at the source:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[AgentRuntime.abort] --> B[AgentRuntimeAbortError]
    B --> C[AbortController.abort typed reason]
    C --> D[orphan rejection reaches daemon]
    D --> E{AgentRuntimeAbortError?}
    E -->|yes| F[ignore expected abort rejection]
    E -->|no| G[shutdownFatal]
    F --> H[daemon stays alive]
    H --> I[same session continues]
```

The invariant should be:

```text
normal user cancel -> typed AgentRuntimeAbortError -> daemon stays alive
unexpected unhandled bug -> normal Error -> daemon fatal path still runs
```

That is the layer where this belongs. User cancel is normal control flow. It should not be represented as an indistinguishable plain `Error` at the process fatal boundary.

The fact that #10969 likely introduced or exposed the regression does not mean the fix needs to live in the CLI stale-session recovery path. #10969 changed hub lifecycle enough to make a latent abort-boundary bug user-visible. The right fix is still at the abort-boundary contract.

I also think merging #11259 as the fix for this issue risks adding bandaid behavior that masks future bugs. It currently combines several broad changes:

- string matching missing-session errors
- retrying a user turn after a failed send
- rebuilding interactive session state from recovered messages
- changing shutdown hook dispatch behavior
- reordering cleanup

Those might be valid hardening changes, but they are not necessary to fix the daemon crash shown in the logs. If this PR keeps the daemon alive, then the stale-session recovery path should not be needed for the Esc cancel repro.

My recommendation:

1. Merge this PR first.
2. Retest the exact Esc cancel repro and the autoupdate/session continuation repro.
3. If those are fixed, close #11259 as unnecessary for this incident.
4. If a separate stale-session bug remains after this fix, split that into a smaller follow-up PR with its own repro.
5. If shutdown hook noise remains after this fix, split that into a separate shutdown-hooks PR instead of bundling it with session retry recovery.

To be clear: #11259 may contain useful resilience ideas. I just do not think we should merge that larger recovery layer as the fix for a daemon crash we can prevent directly.

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a CLI/TUI regression introduced between v3.0.14 and v3.0.15 where the interactive CLI could enter a broken state after Hub restart, caused by stale `activeSessionId` references and hook dispatches racing against Hub shutdown. - **Stale session recovery**: `sendCurrentTurn` now catches `SessionNotFoundError`, reads recoverable messages from the missing session, starts a fresh session, and retries the turn once. `cleanup()` drains any in-flight recovery before proceeding to disposal, preventing concurrent start/dispose races. - **Shutdown-aware hooks**: `createRuntimeHooks` gains a `shuttingDown` flag that `shutdown()` sets; `dispatchHookPayload` checks the flag at three points (before dispatch, after success, and in the catch block) so late hook events are never sent over a closing Hub WebSocket. - **Structured error type**: `SessionNotFoundError` / `isSessionNotFoundError` / `SESSION_NOT_FOUND_ERROR_CODE` are introduced in `runtime-host.ts` and exported from `@cline/core`, replacing ad-hoc message string checks; `getSession` on both `HubSessionClient` and `HubRuntimeHost` now returns `undefined` for missing sessions instead of throwing.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge for the targeted regression; one cleanup ordering gap remains where an early `getExitSummary` rejection bypasses `runtimeHooks.shutdown()`, leaving the hook race window open on that error path. The session-recovery logic is well-guarded: the `missingSessionRecoveryPromise` prevents double-recovery, `cleanup()` drains it before proceeding, and the retry is properly gated on `shutdownRequested`. The hook shutdown-awareness is complete and tested. The one remaining concern is in `session-runtime.ts`: `runtimeHooks?.shutdown()` and `stopCurrentSession()` live inside the try-block that begins with `getExitSummary()`, so if `getExitSummary()` rejects, hooks are never marked as shutting down before `sessionManager.dispose()` runs in the finally — the exact race this PR set out to close. That path is uncommon but structurally reachable. apps/cli/src/runtime/interactive/session-runtime.ts — specifically the try/finally block in `cleanup()` starting at the `getExitSummary` call

body:
Added commit bf997b8e1 to address the blocker I found in review.

Why this was blocking:

- The PR recovery code in `sendCurrentTurn` only retries when `manager.send` throws `SessionNotFoundError`.
- That worked for the local runtime path, but in the Hub-backed path the missing active session error was thrown inside `runTurn`, then `handleSessionInput` rethrew it.
- The websocket adapter catches thrown command errors and serializes them as `command_failed`, so `NodeHubClient` could not reconstruct `SessionNotFoundError`. The CLI would see a generic `HubCommandError` and skip missing-session recovery.
- `handleSessionInput` also published `run.failed` before rethrowing, which could leak a false failure into the TUI even if the next attempt recovered.

How the fix works:

- `handleSessionInput` now catches `SessionNotFoundError` from `runTurn` and returns a normal Hub reply with code `session_not_found`.
- That lets the existing `NodeHubClient` conversion turn the reply back into `SessionNotFoundError`.
- Then `sendCurrentTurn` can use its existing recovery path to clear `activeSessionId`, start a fresh session, and retry.
- The recoverable stale-session path returns before publishing `run.failed`, so the UI does not receive a false failure.

Coverage:

- Added a hub boundary test that simulates `runTurn` throwing `SessionNotFoundError` for a stale active session, asserts the reply code is `session_not_found`, and asserts `run.failed` is not published.

Greptile Summary

This PR adds `prompt_cache_key` support to the `OpenAiHandler`, forwarding the task ULID as `cline-{ulid}` to influence routing and improve cache hit rates on OpenAI-compatible endpoints (specifically New API, as clarified by the author). The change follows the same pattern already used for Vertex, Gemini, and LiteLLM providers. - Adds `ulid?: string` to `OpenAiHandlerOptions` and threads it from `createHandlerForProvider` into the handler, mirroring how other providers receive it. - Injects `prompt_cache_key` conditionally into `chat.completions.create` only when `ulid` is truthy, so requests to endpoints that don't recognise the field will still receive it (the author's intent is to support New API's channel-affinity caching).

Confidence Score: 5/5

The change is a small, backward-compatible addition: `prompt_cache_key` is only injected when `ulid` is present and does not alter message construction or error handling paths. Both changed files follow the exact same pattern already established for Vertex, Gemini, and LiteLLM providers. The field is optional and conditionally spread, so existing users with no ULID or with endpoints that ignore unknown fields are unaffected. Greptile Summary

This PR instruments the `Task` API request path with five client-side telemetry checkpoints (`create_message_start`, `stream_created`, `first_chunk_wait_start`, `first_chunk_received`, `first_chunk_error`) to separate pre-first-token failures from mid-stream provider errors. A new `captureApiRequestCheckpoint()` method and the corresponding `API_REQUEST_CHECKPOINT` event constant are added to `TelemetryService`. - Five checkpoints are wired around `createMessage` and `iterator.next()`, capturing stage, duration, provider/model context, first-chunk type, and bounded error metadata. - The early stages (`create_message_start`, `stream_created`, `first_chunk_wait_start`) call `getApiRequestIdSafe()` before the async generator has started executing, so they record the **previous** request's ID rather than `undefined`; this can corrupt backend joins on `requestId`. - The `stream_created` checkpoint fires with `durationMs ≈ 0` on every call because `createMessage` is a lazy `async *` generator — no I/O happens until `iterator.next()` is first awaited.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The checkpoint events themselves are non-breaking and fire-and-forget, but the requestId captured for the three earliest stages will silently reflect the prior request, making the most diagnostic field in those events incorrect from day one of deployment. The stale-requestId problem means that any backend analysis joining create_message_start, stream_created, or first_chunk_wait_start events to upstream request records will produce wrong associations on every single API call — not an occasional edge case. Fixing it before these events reach production avoids baking a systematic data-quality defect into the telemetry schema. apps/vscode/src/core/task/index.ts — the three early checkpoint calls that read getApiRequestIdSafe() before the generator has started.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/vscode/src/core/task/index.ts | Adds five telemetry checkpoints around the API request lifecycle; the early stages (create_message_start, stream_created, first_chunk_wait_start) capture a stale requestId from the previous request because the async generator hasn't started executing yet. | | apps/vscode/src/services/telemetry/TelemetryService.ts | Adds API_REQUEST_CHECKPOINT event constant and captureApiRequestCheckpoint() method; stage field is an untyped string where a discriminated union would provide compile-time safety. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Task participant TelemetryService participant Provider as API Provider (async generator) Task->>TelemetryService: "captureApiRequestCheckpoint(create_message_start) requestId = stale prev ID" Task->>Provider: createMessage(...) — generator created, NOT started Task->>TelemetryService: "captureApiRequestCheckpoint(stream_created, durationMs~0) requestId = stale prev ID" Task->>Provider: stream[Symbol.asyncIterator]() Task->>TelemetryService: "captureApiRequestCheckpoint(first_chunk_wait_start) requestId = stale prev ID" Task->>Provider: await iterator.next() — generator body starts executing now Provider-->>Provider: "reset lastGenerationId/lastRequestId = undefined" Provider-->>Provider: network I/O — wait for first chunk alt Success Provider-->>Task: firstChunk Provider-->>Provider: lastGenerationId set from chunk.id Task->>TelemetryService: "captureApiRequestCheckpoint(first_chunk_received) requestId = correct new ID" Task-->>Task: yield firstChunk.value else Error Provider-->>Task: throw error Task->>TelemetryService: "captureApiRequestCheckpoint(first_chunk_error) requestId = clineError.request_id" end ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 3 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 3 apps/vscode/src/core/task/index.ts:2031-2058 **Stale `requestId` in early checkpoint stages** `getApiRequestIdSafe()` reads `lastGenerationId` / `lastRequestId` from the provider, but all providers reset those fields to `undefined` **inside** the `async *createMessage` generator body. Since calling `createMessage` only creates the generator without executing it, `lastGenerationId` / `lastRequestId` still hold the **previous** request's values until `await iterator.next()` is first called. The result is that `create_message_start`, `stream_created`, and `first_chunk_wait_start` all include a stale request ID from the prior request, not `undefined`. Any backend join on `requestId` will incorrectly link these early-stage events to the wrong upstream request. ### Issue 2 of 3 apps/vscode/src/core/task/index.ts:2040-2045 **`stream_created` checkpoint is semantically redundant** All providers implement `createMessage` as an `async *` generator. Calling `this.api.createMessage(...)` merely constructs the generator object — no network I/O or internal state mutation occurs. As a result, `stream_created` fires with `durationMs ≈ 0` on every invocation and the gap between `create_message_start` and `stream_created` carries no diagnostic signal. The first meaningful timing boundary for pre-first-token debugging is `first_chunk_wait_start` → `first_chunk_received`/`first_chunk_error`, so `stream_created` adds telemetry volume without adding observability value. ### Issue 3 of 3 apps/vscode/src/services/telemetry/TelemetryService.ts:1408-1412 The `stage` field is typed as a plain `string`, which means callers can pass arbitrary values and typos are invisible at compile time. Narrowing it to the known literal union makes the interface self-documenting and catches misspellings without any runtime cost. ```suggestion public captureApiRequestCheckpoint(args: { ulid: string taskId: string stage: "create_message_start" | "stream_created" | "first_chunk_wait_start" | "first_chunk_received" | "first_chunk_error" provider?: string ``` `````

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes stale hub daemon reuse after CLI upgrades by stamping `CLINE_HUB_BUILD_ID` with the published CLI version at process startup, before any SDK hub discovery or daemon spawning occurs. The existing SDK compatibility logic can then retire mismatched daemons automatically. - Adds `apps/cli/src/utils/hub-compatibility.ts`, a small utility that sets `CLINE_HUB_BUILD_ID=cli:` in the process environment unless a non-blank override is already present, and calls it at the top of `apps/cli/src/index.ts`. - Adds a well-isolated unit test suite (3 cases) that passes a stub `env` object to avoid `process.env` mutation during tests.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change is narrow, well-tested, and the env-var guard prevents any double-stamping or unintended overrides. The implementation is a small, targeted env-var write at process startup. It correctly handles the daemon process path (daemon inherits the env var and uses it as its own build ID), respects existing overrides, and the test suite uses stub env objects so it cannot pollute `process.env`. The only gap is a missing empty-string test case, which is a cosmetic omission rather than a defect. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/cli/src/utils/hub-compatibility.ts | New utility that stamps `CLINE_HUB_BUILD_ID` with the CLI version before any SDK hub code runs; logic is correct and well-guarded. | | apps/cli/src/utils/hub-compatibility.test.ts | Tests use isolated env objects (not `process.env`), covering set, preserve, and blank-override cases; misses the empty-string edge case but otherwise thorough. | | apps/cli/src/index.ts | Calls `configureCliHubCompatibility()` at module-top before `initVcr` and the `isHubDaemonProcess` branch, ensuring the env var is stamped on every process entry path including the daemon path. |

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes the visible lag when pressing Esc to cancel a running CLI request. The keyboard handler now immediately calls `session.setIsStreaming(false)` and `session.closeInlineStream()` as soon as `onAbort()` confirms the abort started, so the `Thinking... (esc to cancel)` indicator disappears right away rather than waiting for the backend cleanup path to unwind. - The two new calls are idempotent with the existing cleanup in `use-prompt-input-controller.ts`'s `finally` block — both `closeInlineStream` and `setIsStreaming` are safe to invoke multiple times without side effects. - A narrow race window exists: if a backend `iteration_start` event arrives after Esc is pressed but before the hub fully processes the abort, `use-agent-events.ts` will call `setIsStreaming(true)` unconditionally, briefly re-showing the indicator before the abort completes. This is unlikely in practice and not a regression introduced here.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge; the change only moves two idempotent state-clearing calls earlier in the abort path, with no risk of data loss or broken cleanup. Both new calls (`setIsStreaming(false)` and `closeInlineStream()`) are already invoked by the `finally` block in `use-prompt-input-controller.ts`, so the worst outcome of calling them earlier is a redundant no-op. The one edge case — backend events temporarily re-setting `isStreaming` to `true` after abort — is a visual flicker, not a functional regression. apps/cli/src/tui/hooks/use-root-keyboard.ts — the two new lines are the only change; the rest of the file is untouched.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/cli/src/tui/hooks/use-root-keyboard.ts | Adds two immediate state updates on abort: `setIsStreaming(false)` and `closeInlineStream()`, giving instant UI feedback when Esc is pressed. The `finally` block in `use-prompt-input-controller.ts` still calls the same functions for the actual cleanup, making the calls idempotent and safe. |

Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 1 apps/cli/src/tui/hooks/use-root-keyboard.ts:237-238 **Streaming state can briefly reappear after abort** `use-agent-events.ts` handles `iteration_start` by calling `setIsStreaming(true)` unconditionally (line 83). If a backend iteration starts in the narrow window between the Esc keypress and the hub processing the abort signal, `isStreaming` will be flipped back to `true`, momentarily re-showing `Thinking... This PR fixes HTML-entity-encoded shell operators (e.g. `&&`, `>`) from non-Claude, non-Gemini models reaching the terminal unchanged. It does so by calling `applyModelContentFixes` unconditionally for all models (before timeout heuristics) and removing the Gemini-only guard. - **Handler change**: `applyModelContentFixes(command, config.api.getModel().id)` is now called for every model at the top of `execute()`, before `resolveCommandTimeoutSeconds`, so the Claude bypass in `applyModelContentFixes` still skips decoding for Claude models, while timeout heuristics now correctly operate on the decoded command string. - **Test additions**: Three new integration tests cover the xAI/Grok decode path, the Claude passthrough, and the timeout-heuristic-on-decoded-command behaviour — addressing the two gaps flagged in the previous review round.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change is a targeted, well-tested expansion of an existing HTML-entity decoding step to all non-Claude models, with no impact on Claude or Gemini behaviour. The fix is narrow: a two-line reorder and a guard removal, backed by three new integration tests. `applyModelContentFixes` already has its own skip logic for Claude models, so there is no regression risk for the protected path. Timeout heuristics now correctly receive the decoded command. Both gaps from the previous review round are closed. No files require special attention.

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes two related bugs in the SDK migration path: the delete-tooltip showed `--` for zero-byte tasks because `0` is falsy, and SDK-backed sessions had no mechanism to backfill a missing task size from their artifact directory. - **Tooltip fix**: `formatDeleteTaskSizeLabel` replaces the inline `taskSize ? formatSize(taskSize) : "--"` with an explicit `=== undefined` check, correctly rendering `0 B` for empty sessions. - **Size backfill**: `findHistoryItem` now calls `getCachedTaskSize`, which reads from `metadata.size` when present (including zero) and falls back to `getFolderSize.loose` on the artifact directory; the resolved size is written back to session metadata via `cacheTaskSize`. - **Preservation fix**: `updateSession` no longer unconditionally writes `size: item.size ?? 0`; it only sets `size` when `item.size !== undefined`, so a cached artifact size is not overwritten by unrelated metadata updates.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — all changes are additive fixes with no side-effects on existing write paths. The tooltip fix is a one-line substitution of a known falsy-zero bug. The SDK backfill path only triggers when metadata.size is absent and only writes back a measured filesystem value; the updateSession preservation change is conservative (skips writing size only when it is truly absent from the caller's item). Five new tests cover the critical edge cases including zero-byte caching and error fallback, giving high confidence the new paths behave as intended. No files require special attention.

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a flaky Windows test in `plugin-uninstall.test.ts` by replacing a `chmodSync`-based permission trick (setting a directory to mode `0o555` to block deletion) with a proper Vitest mock of `node:fs`'s `rmSync`. Windows does not honour Unix-style permission bits in the same way, making the old approach unreliable. - The mock is wired with `vi.hoisted` (required because `vi.mock` calls are hoisted before variable declarations) and falls back to the real `rmSync` via `mockImplementation(actual.rmSync)`, so all other tests and the `afterEach` cleanup continue to use the real filesystem. - The single failing test uses `mockImplementationOnce` to throw on the first `rmSync` call, then the `try/finally` + `chmodSync` restoration block is removed as it is no longer necessary.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge – the change is confined to a single test file, swaps out an OS-dependent trick for a well-structured Vitest mock, and does not touch any production code. The mock setup uses the correct vi.hoisted / vi.mock pattern, the default implementation delegates to the real rmSync so no other test or the afterEach cleanup is affected, and mockImplementationOnce properly limits the error injection to one invocation. No production code is changed and no existing assertions are weakened. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes `constructNewFileContent` (V1 and V2) incorrectly appending a trailing ` ` when replacing the final line of a file that has no trailing newline. Two independent changes cooperate: fallback match helpers now use `getLineLengthWithTerminator` so `searchEndIndex` lands exactly at `originalContent.length` for no-trailing-newline files instead of one past it, and `normalizeReplacementContentForMatchedRange` / the V2 inline guard strip the parser-synthetic ` ` only when that condition is met. - **`getLineLengthWithTerminator`**: replaces the hard-coded `+ 1` in `lineTrimmedFallbackMatch` and `blockAnchorFallbackMatch`, returning `line.length` for the last element of a `split(\"\ \")` result and `line.length + 1` for all others. - **V1 normalization**: `normalizeReplacementContentForMatchedRange` trims the trailing `\ ` when `searchEndIndex === originalContent.length` and the file lacks a trailing newline, with a `length > 1` guard to preserve a single blank-line replacement. - **V2 normalization**: a symmetric inline guard at the `isReplaceBlockEnd` branch uses `currentReplaceStartIndex` to measure replacement length, mirroring the V1 guard.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge; the fix is narrowly scoped to EOF newline normalization and is guarded by conditions that only activate when the matched range ends exactly at the file boundary on a no-trailing-newline file. Both the V1 and V2 reconstruction paths receive symmetric, independently guarded normalization. The getLineLengthWithTerminator helper is provably correct for split-by-newline arrays, the shouldTrimSyntheticReplacementNewline predicate only fires at EOF on no-newline files, and the length-greater-than-1 guard preserves the single-blank-line case. Four new regression tests cover the primary scenario, intentional trailing-newline addition, single blank replacement, and multi-blank replacement. No files require special attention.

Greptile Summary

This PR adds Slack socket mode as an alternative to the existing webhook mode, and fixes a long-standing bug where `@mentions` in Slack channels would create a new thread per reply instead of routing all replies to the original post's thread. It also adds a `--allowed-user-id` flag for Telegram, improves the connect wizard with conditional fields, refactors the session-not-found error type into `runtime-host.ts`, and adds an interactive session recovery path that automatically restarts a dropped session. - **Slack socket mode** (`--app-token` / `SLACK_APP_TOKEN`): `inferSlackConnectionMode` selects webhook vs socket based on whether `--base-url` is present; webhook path requires signing secret and starts an HTTP server, socket path requires only the app-level token with no HTTP server. - **Thread normalization** (`resolveSlackChannelMentionThread`): on every `app_mention` event, the thread is rewritten to `slack::` so all replies within the same Slack thread dispatch to the same Cline session rather than spawning new ones. - **Interactive session recovery** (`recoverMissingActiveSession`): when `sendCurrentTurn` catches a `SessionNotFoundError`, it reads the existing messages, clears the session, and calls `startFreshSession` to resume; the retry after recovery uses a stale local `manager` variable instead of the updated `sessionManager` closure, which will fail in local (non-hub) mode.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The Slack and Telegram connector changes are solid and well-tested, but the interactive session recovery path in session-runtime.ts has a logic error that would cause the recovery retry to silently fail in local (non-hub) mode. The session recovery retry reuses a stale manager reference after startFreshSession has replaced sessionManager with a newly created core instance. In a local runtime the new session lives only on the new manager, so the retry sends the new session ID to the old manager, which has no record of it and will throw again. The Slack and Telegram connector work — socket mode, thread normalization, and the --allowed-user-id guard — all look correct and are backed by good test coverage. apps/cli/src/runtime/interactive/session-runtime.ts — the sendCurrentTurn retry path after recoverMissingActiveSession

This PR fixes `StandaloneTerminalManager` (used in Background Exec mode) ignoring the user-configured "Default Terminal Profile" and always spawning the system default shell. The fix mirrors `VscodeTerminalManager`: profile id → shell path resolution is applied both when creating terminals and when matching/reusing them. - **`getOrCreateTerminal()`**: computes `expectedShellPath` once per call and filters both the CWD-match and the fallback-reuse candidates against it, then passes it to `registry.createTerminal()` so `TerminalInfo.shellPath` is set correctly. - **`setDefaultTerminalProfile()`**: resolves the incoming profile id to a shell path before forwarding to `handleTerminalProfileChange()`, so idle terminals running the old shell are properly closed on profile switch. - **Tests**: three new cases cover bash/zsh (posix) or powershell-legacy/cmd (Windows) — correct shell on create, `undefined` for the default profile, and no terminal reuse across profile switches.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change is narrowly scoped to StandaloneTerminalManager and correctly mirrors the already-working VscodeTerminalManager behavior. The logic is straightforward: profile id resolution is added in exactly two places (terminal creation and profile-change cleanup), the default-profile path (shellPath = undefined) is preserved unchanged, and the new tests validate all three behavioural cases across both posix and Windows platforms. No regressions were found in terminal reuse, background-command tracking, or the handleTerminalProfileChange cleanup path. No files require special attention.

Both changes look good. The test file is clean and the fixes are well-reasoned:

1. **Dropped `_shellPath` assertion** — correct call. `terminalInfo.shellPath` is the stable public surface; the private field was just noise.

2. **Windows CI fix** — the platform-appropriate profile pair plus the distinctness guard (`if (getShellForProfile(PROFILE_A) === getShellForProfile(PROFILE_B)) { return }`) handles the edge case cleanly without skipping the test entirely on any platform.

That's safe behavior — just worth verifying the CI image has PS7. If it doesn't, `["powershell", "cmd"]` (the built-in Windows PowerShell) might be a more reliable choice.

Greptile Summary

This PR upgrades four npm packages — `dompurify`, `mermaid`, `lodash-es` (transitive), and `@ungap/structured-clone` (transitive) — to patch 14 CVEs covering XSS, prototype pollution, CSS injection, and unsafe constructor instantiation. The two manifest changes are a direct spec floor raise for `dompurify` (`^3.3.3` → `^3.4.7`, resolved to `3.4.8`) and an exact pin advance for `mermaid` (`11.12.3` → `11.15.0`). - **DOMPurify 3.4.8** addresses 8 CVEs (prototype pollution bypass, `RETURN_DOM`/`SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES` template injection, `FORBID_TAGS`/`ADD_TAGS` interaction bugs, hook-based allow-list poisoning, shadow-root `IN_PLACE` bypass, and URI scheme validation gaps via function predicates). - **mermaid 11.15.0** addresses 4 CVEs (CSS injection via `classDef`, HTML injection via `classDef`, CSS injection via config scoping, and gantt chart DoS); it also introduces several documented visual/behavioral breaking changes (flowchart edge curve default, label line-wrapping, SVG element ID prefixing, class diagram namespace nesting, state diagram comment syntax). - **lodash-es 4.18.1** and **`@ungap/structured-clone` 1.3.1** are pulled in transitively — no manifest edits required.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge; the changes are purely additive security patches with no logic modifications to application code. All four package upgrades are well-scoped security fixes with no application logic changes. The mermaid bump carries documented visual/behavioral breaking changes (flowchart curve default, state diagram comment syntax, SVG element ID prefixing), and the existing MermaidBlock.tsx init config does not opt out of them — so rendered diagrams will subtly change appearance and some existing state diagrams may degrade. These are not correctness bugs in the extension's own code, but they represent real user-visible regressions that should be verified. The MermaidBlock.tsx component (not in this diff) should be reviewed alongside the mermaid bump to decide whether to pin back the flowchart curve and verify state diagram rendering against the new comment syntax rules.

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a CLI TUI rendering bug where the `ask_question` panel allocated too little vertical space, causing wrapped option text to paint over adjacent rows. The fix introduces a content-aware body height (estimating wrapped rows for the question, options, and custom prompt), wraps the content in a `scrollbox`, and scrolls the selected option into view after navigation. - **Height estimation helpers** (`addWrappedWidth`, `countWrappedRows`, `getAskQuestionContentHeight`) compute the row count of each text element so `bodyHeight` is fitted to content up to a terminal-fraction cap. - **Scroll-into-view effect** fires immediately, via `queueMicrotask`, and via `setTimeout(0)` with a `canceled` guard and `clearTimeout` cleanup, matching the pattern used elsewhere in the TUI. - **`ToolApprovalResponse`** is unaffected: `Shell` only forwards `overflow` when explicitly passed, and that branch never passes it.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge for the targeted bug fix; the one concern is whether the column-offset constants in the height estimator match all runtime scrollbar states. The wrapping helpers and scroll-into-view effect are logically correct, and the change is well-scoped to AskQuestionResponse. The height estimator hardcodes column offsets (-3 for question, -7 for option text) that implicitly assume OpenTUI always renders a vertical scrollbar. If the scrollbar is absent when content does not overflow, the available width is 1 column wider than assumed, making the row estimate slightly too large in the no-scroll case. In practice this wastes at most one row of space rather than causing clipping, so the direction of the error is safe. apps/cli/src/tui/components/inline-tool-response.tsx — verify the -3 / -7 column offsets in getAskQuestionContentHeight hold when OpenTUI omits the scrollbar for non-overflowing content.

Important Files Changed

`parseYamlFrontmatter` fails open on invalid YAML and returns the full original document as the `body`, so a disable would have prepended a second `---` block and corrupted the file. Fixed in 2c4abcffb: `updateSkillMarkdownDisabledState` now returns the content untouched when `parseError` is set, leaving the file for the user to fix. Added tests for both the malformed disable (asserts no double `---` header) and malformed enable cases.

body:
The fix in 2c4abcffb looks correct. The early-return guard handles the `parseError` case cleanly, and the two new tests (`leaves malformed-frontmatter files untouched when disabling` and `when enabling`) confirm both branches are covered.

One small note: the malformed YAML used in the test (`description: : : bad\n  - nope`) might not actually trigger `parseError` in all YAML parsers — some can parse that as a string. If you want to make the tests more robust, it's worth verifying the fixture actually causes `parseError` to be set by checking `parseYamlFrontmatter`'s behavior with that exact input. If the tests pass, it does trigger it, but it's worth a quick sanity check. A clearly invalid YAML fragment like `key: [unclosed` would be a more reliable fixture.

That said, the core logic is sound and the guard is in the right place. Good fix.

Tip: You can customize Greptile's behavior for this repo with [`.greptile/rules.md` and `.greptile/config.json`](https://www.greptile.com/docs/code-review/custom-standards).

Confidence Score: 5/5

All proto field numbers are correctly sequential with no gaps or collisions. The TypeScript type chain is consistent: adding lmStudioApiKey to SECRETS_KEYS flows automatically into Secrets → ApiHandlerSettings → ApiConfiguration. Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a silent failure (#8635) where pasting or dropping an image when the active model has `supportsImages: false` would attach the image and later cause a backend error. It threads a new `supportsImages` boolean from `ChatView` through `InputSection` into `ChatTextArea`, adds guards in both the paste and drop handlers, and displays a 3-second inline error overlay matching the existing dimension-error and unsupported-file-error patterns. - **Paste guard** — when `!supportsImages && imageItems.length > 0`, `e.preventDefault()` is called and the "model does not support images" overlay is shown; the image is never attached. - **Drop guard** — the refactored drop handler checks `!supportsImages` before `shouldDisableFilesAndImages`, showing the same overlay and returning early. - **UI** — the new overlay reuses identical CSS classes (`absolute inset-2.5`, `bg-[rgba(var(--vscode-errorForeground-rgb),0.1)]`, `border-error`, 3 s auto-dismiss) as the two sibling overlays.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge — the core fix is correct and non-breaking; the two findings are minor UX inconsistencies that do not affect data integrity or correctness. The paste and drop guards work correctly: images are blocked and the error overlay is shown when the model lacks image support. Two small gaps exist: the error message always suggests enabling a setting even for models that are inherently non-multimodal, and the new overlay is not dismissed at the start of a fresh drop event the way showUnsupportedFileError is, leaving it briefly visible during an unrelated successful drop. apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/chat/ChatTextArea.tsx — the drop-start cleanup and the error message wording both warrant a second look.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/chat/ChatTextArea.tsx | Adds supportsImages prop, new error state/timer for image-unsupported feedback, and guards in paste + drop handlers — two minor inconsistencies: the 'enable in settings' message applies even to inherently non-multimodal models, and the new error overlay is not cleared at drop start like its siblings. | | apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/chat/ChatView.tsx | Passes selectedModelInfo.supportsImages || false to InputSection as the new supportsImages prop — straightforward and correct. | | apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/chat/chat-view/components/layout/InputSection.tsx | Correctly threads the new supportsImages prop through its interface and down to ChatTextArea with no other changes. |

Greptile Summary

Adds a fallback token-usage estimate inside `emitAiSdkEvents` for OpenAI-compatible gateways that return `usage: null` on every streaming chunk, which previously left the context-window progress bar permanently at 0%. - Accumulates streamed text (both `text-delta` and `reasoning-delta`) into `accumulatedText`; after the stream loop, if no real usage value was emitted and no stream error occurred, a synthetic usage event is yielded using `estimateRequestInputTokens` for the input side and `estimateTokens(accumulatedText.length)` for the output side — both leveraging the shared 3-chars-per-token heuristic already used in the gateway and provider-capture paths. - The fallback is correctly gated on `!streamError` and only fires when `usageToEmit` is falsy (covering `null`, `undefined`, and all other falsy resolutions from gateways that don't send usage data).

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the fallback path is narrowly scoped to the case where no real usage was received and no stream error occurred, so it can't overwrite valid usage data. The change touches only the post-stream fallback of `emitAiSdkEvents`. Normal usage data from providers continues to flow through `normalizeUsage` unchanged. The estimation logic reuses battle-tested helpers from `gateway.ts`. The only notable gap is that tool-call argument tokens are not counted in the output estimate, but that's a cosmetic accuracy limitation rather than a functional defect. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

Input tokens are estimated from serialised request content via the existing estimateRequestInputTokens helper; output tokens are estimated from accumulated streamed text using the shared 3-chars-per-token heuristic. Reasoning-delta content is correctly included. Tool-call argument tokens are not included in the output estimate, which understates usage for tool-heavy responses. |

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR gates native `tools` injection for Ollama on a per-model capability check: before each chat request, `OllamaHandler` calls `/api/show` and only includes the `tools` field when the model explicitly advertises the `"tools"` capability. Errors from the capability check are swallowed and treated as "no tools" (fail-closed), preventing HTTP 400/500 failures on non-tool local models. - `selectedModelSupportsTools` adds a three-level cache: a settled `supportsTools: boolean` for the fast path, an in-flight `supportsToolsPromise` for concurrent deduplication, and proper cleanup on timeout so the `@withRetry` decorator can re-issue the `show()` call on the next attempt. - Four new unit tests validate unsupported-model omission, tool-capable-model inclusion, fail-closed error handling, and timeout propagation through the `show()` path, including an assertion that `show()` is re-called on retry (verifying the promise cleanup path). - Minor hardening: the inner stream-error catch is tightened to `unknown` and a `getErrorMessage` helper avoids direct property access on unknown errors.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge. The change is well-scoped: it adds a capability check before sending tools to Ollama, fails closed on any error, and the caching/deduplication logic is correct. The three-level caching design (settled bool fast path → in-flight promise deduplication → fetch) is implemented correctly, including the cleanup on timeout that allows @withRetry to re-issue show() on the next attempt. Concurrent callers share a single in-flight promise and cannot overwrite each other's cached result. The fail-closed path (silently returning false on any show() error) is intentional and explicitly tested. No logic errors, data races, or broken contracts were found. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/vscode/src/core/api/providers/ollama.ts | Adds capability-gated tool injection: queries Ollama's /api/show before sending chat requests, caches the result per handler instance, deduplicates concurrent lookups, and fails closed (omits tools) on any metadata error or timeout. | | apps/vscode/src/core/api/providers/__tests__/ollama.test.ts | Adds four new unit tests covering unsupported-model omission, timeout propagation through the show() path, concurrent-lookup deduplication, tool-capable model inclusion, and error-triggered fail-closed behaviour. Previous thread concerns are now addressed. |

Hi @oxura, thanks for fixing this! Controlling the tool request based on model capability is a great idea to prevent those 400/500 errors.

I am working on another PR that handles this same issue from the response side, which should complement your changes well. Even when local models (like Qwen via Ollama) are allowed to use tools, they often output raw JSON in their response text instead of standard XML, which causes the chat UI to break or loop.

I’ve implemented a fallback parser that safely catches these JSON responses, renders the tools correctly, and clears the raw JSON text from the chat view. It also fixes a circular dependency bug in `toolParamNames`.

I think combining your request-side fix with this response-side fallback will completely solve the Ollama experience. 

My PR:#11272

Greptile Summary

This PR introduces `OpenAiStreamUsageTracker`, a utility class that buffers streaming usage chunks from OpenAI-compatible APIs and emits only the final one, preventing cumulative-per-token usage reports from inflating Cline's token accounting (fixes #10148). - **`openai-stream-usage.ts`**: New `OpenAiStreamUsageTracker` class with `record()` / `getUsageChunk()` API; replaces inline yield-per-chunk logic in both providers with a single post-loop emission. - **`openai.ts` / `zai.ts`**: Both providers now collect usage via the tracker and yield exactly one usage chunk after the stream completes; the `zai.ts` change also upgrades `cacheWriteTokens` from a hardcoded `0` to reading `prompt_cache_miss_tokens`, aligning its behavior with the OpenAI handler. - **`openai-stream-usage.test.ts`**: Three Mocha/Chai unit tests covering the final-chunk selection, cache field mapping, and the no-usage-reported case.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change is narrowly scoped to usage accounting and cannot affect text/tool-call output. The tracker simply retains the last non-null usage object and emits it once after the stream completes. For standard servers that emit a single trailing usage chunk this is a no-op; for cumulative servers it correctly de-duplicates. The only semantic change is in `zai.ts` where `cacheWriteTokens` now reads `prompt_cache_miss_tokens` instead of being hardcoded to `0`, which aligns ZAI with OpenAI handler behavior and is harmless if the field is absent. Tests cover the key scenarios and the implementation is minimal. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/vscode/src/core/api/providers/utils/openai-stream-usage.ts | New utility class that retains only the last non-null streaming usage chunk; clean implementation with correct nullish-coalescing defaults. | | apps/vscode/src/core/api/providers/openai.ts | Replaces per-chunk usage yields with a single post-loop emission via OpenAiStreamUsageTracker; behavior is equivalent for standard servers and correct for cumulative ones. | | apps/vscode/src/core/api/providers/zai.ts | Same streaming fix as openai.ts; cacheWriteTokens now reads prompt_cache_miss_tokens instead of being hardcoded to 0, which is a semantic change but aligns behavior with the OpenAI handler. | | apps/vscode/src/core/api/providers/utils/__tests__/openai-stream-usage.test.ts | Three focused unit tests covering final-chunk selection, cache field mapping, and the no-usage path; good regression coverage for the fix. |

Sequence Diagram

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a bug where AI models sometimes emit HTML-escaped shell operators (`&`, `>`, `"`, etc.) inside `` blocks, causing the raw shell command to contain literal entity strings rather than the intended characters. The fix adds a targeted unescaping pass only for `execute_command.command` parameters, leaving all other tool inputs (such as file `content`) untouched. - **`parse-assistant-message.ts`**: Introduces `normalizeToolParam` that calls `fixModelHtmlEscaping` when `toolName === ClineDefaultTool.BASH && paramName === "command"`, applied at both the normal close-tag finalization path and the partial/stream-end finalization path. - **`o1-format.ts`**: Adds the symmetric `normalizeToolInput` for the O1 XML-conversion path, now using `ClineDefaultTool.BASH` (the enum constant) rather than a raw string. - **Tests**: Both test suites cover the positive case (entities decoded in shell commands) and the negative case (non-command tool params left intact).

Confidence Score: 5/5

The change is narrowly scoped: entity decoding is applied only to execute_command.command, leaving all other tool parameters untouched, so file content and other tool inputs cannot be accidentally rewritten. Both parser paths (streaming and O1 XML conversion) apply the fix symmetrically. The fixModelHtmlEscaping implementation decodes & last, which is the correct ordering to prevent double-decoding of entities like <. Tests cover both the positive (entities decoded) and negative (non-command content preserved) cases. No regressions are expected in adjacent code paths. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

Greptile Summary

This PR replaces hardcoded fallback model lists with live fetches from `/api/v1/ai/cline/recommended-models` for the onboarding flow, settings model picker, and free-model billing classification. It also removes the `cline-recommended-models-upstream` feature-flag gate and adds a 30-second short-TTL backoff for empty API results to reduce retry churn. - `getClineOnboardingModels` is refactored from a synchronous getter into a background-refreshing cache with a module-level generation counter; `getStateToPostToWebview` now reads from the cache synchronously and triggers a fire-and-forget fetch when the cache is cold. - `ClineHandler.getFreeModelIdSet` removes the hardcoded `CLINE_FREE_MODEL_IDS` fallback set, returning `null` on failure and falling back to the selected model's `inputPrice`/`outputPrice` metadata via the new `isFreeModel` method. - `formatContextWindow` is extracted to a shared utility and replaces two separate local implementations in `ModelInfoView` and `OnboardingView`; `OnboardingViewContent`'s initial model-selection effect is made defensively null-safe.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge with the understanding that a fresh-install with no disk cache and a degraded API will show a persistent loading spinner and classify all Cline models as non-free until the API recovers. The two most critical paths — free-model billing classification and the onboarding retry loop on network errors — both lack a hardcoded backstop now that the fallback lists are removed. On a cold start with no disk cache, getFreeModelIdSet returns null and falls back to model pricing metadata, which may be absent and silently treat free models as paid. In the error path of getClineOnboardingModels, emptyCached is never set, so every getStateToPostToWebview call immediately starts a new pair of network requests with no delay. apps/vscode/src/core/controller/models/getClineOnboardingModels.ts (error path skips 30s TTL backoff) and apps/vscode/src/core/api/providers/cline.ts (free-model detection fallback relies on model pricing metadata being populated).

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/vscode/src/core/controller/models/getClineOnboardingModels.ts | Core caching logic for onboarding model fetches; 30s TTL backoff added for empty results but thrown errors still bypass it, leaving the retry loop unbounded on network failures. | | apps/vscode/src/core/api/providers/cline.ts | Removes hardcoded CLINE_FREE_MODEL_IDS fallback; on API/cache miss null is returned and free-model detection falls back to model pricing metadata, which silently misclassifies models when no modelInfo is populated. | | apps/vscode/src/core/controller/index.ts | getStateToPostToWebview now uses a synchronous cache read + background refresh instead of awaiting network calls; non-welcomed users see a loading state until the background fetch completes. | | apps/vscode/src/services/feature-flags/FeatureFlagsService.ts | clearOnboardingModelsCache() called at end of poll(); if a fetch is in flight at poll completion the generation guard discards it and a redundant re-fetch is triggered, but correctness is preserved. | | apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/onboarding/OnboardingView.tsx | Defensive null-safety fix for initial model selection effect; formatContextWindow replaces inline arithmetic; model.info is correctly guarded before access. | | apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/utils/format.ts | Adds shared formatContextWindow using Intl.NumberFormat; replaces two divergent local implementations; behaviour matches tests. | | apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/onboarding/useOnboardingModels.ts | Simplified hook that reads onboardingModels from extension state and triggers refreshClineModels on mount to warm the model catalog for the onboarding search. | | apps/vscode/src/shared/cline/onboarding.ts | File deleted; hardcoded CLINE_ONBOARDING_MODELS list removed as part of the switch to live API fetching. | | apps/vscode/src/shared/cline/recommended-models.ts | File deleted; hardcoded CLINE_RECOMMENDED_MODELS_FALLBACK removed; the provider now returns null on failure instead of the fallback set. | | apps/vscode/src/test/core/controller/marketplace-filtering.test.ts | Test updated to find the marketplace axios call by URL instead of asserting calledOnce, accommodating extra axios calls made by refreshClineRecommendedModels. |

Greptile Summary

This PR wires `CLINE_OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` (a previously ignored env var) into the OTEL `Resource` by parsing it with the existing `parseKeyPairsIntoRecord` helper and merging the result into the resource attributes map at provider construction time. - `otel-config.ts`: adds `resourceAttributes?: Record` to `OpenTelemetryClientConfig` and populates it from `CLINE_OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` in `getRuntimeOtelConfig`; build-time and remote-config paths are intentionally left unchanged. - `OpenTelemetryClientProvider.ts`: spreads `config.resourceAttributes` into the `Resource` constructor and adds a debug log line for the attribute count; the separator line in debug output is now unconditional on `isDebugMode` rather than also requiring `config.otlpHeaders`.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The env-var parsing and config wiring are clean, but the spread order in the Resource constructor lets user-supplied keys overwrite the hardcoded service identity fields, which could fragment telemetry attribution silently. The config and parsing changes are consistent with the existing headers pattern. The one concrete defect is in the Resource constructor: `...config.resourceAttributes` is spread after the identity fields, so any collision silently overwrites 'cline' as the service name. Reversing the spread order is a one-line fix with no other side effects. apps/vscode/src/services/telemetry/providers/opentelemetry/OpenTelemetryClientProvider.ts — specifically the Resource constructor spread order around lines 65-70.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/vscode/src/shared/services/config/otel-config.ts | Adds resourceAttributes to OpenTelemetryClientConfig and parses CLINE_OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES via the existing parseKeyPairsIntoRecord helper in getRuntimeOtelConfig. JSDoc is updated. Build-time and remote-config paths intentionally omit the new field. | | apps/vscode/src/services/telemetry/providers/opentelemetry/OpenTelemetryClientProvider.ts | Spreads config.resourceAttributes into the OTEL Resource constructor after the hardcoded service identity fields, allowing user-supplied service.name or service.version to silently override them. |
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 1 code review issue. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 1 apps/vscode/src/services/telemetry/providers/opentelemetry/OpenTelemetryClientProvider.ts:65-70 User attributes can silently overwrite `service.name` and `service.version`. Because `...config.resourceAttributes` is spread after the hardcoded fields, any attribute key that collides — e.g. `service.name=cline-prod-eu` — overwrites "cline". This will cause telemetry dashboards that group by `service.name` to fragment or lose data silently. Moving the spread before the hardcoded attributes lets the built-in identity fields always win. ```suggestion // Create resource with service information, merged with any user-supplied resource attributes // User-supplied attributes are spread first so built-in identity fields always take precedence const resource = new Resource({ ...config.resourceAttributes, [ATTR_SERVICE_NAME]: "cline", [ATTR_SERVICE_VERSION]: ExtensionRegistryInfo.version, }) ``` `````

Greptile Summary

This PR adds a non-streaming fallback to `OpenAiHandler` for OpenAI-compatible providers that explicitly set `supportsStreaming: false` (e.g. vLLM, custom inference servers). When the flag is `false`, a standard `chat.completions.create` call is made and its result is adapted into the same `ApiStream` chunk format the rest of the pipeline expects. - Adds a guarded non-streaming code path that mirrors `openai-native.ts`'s existing `supportsStreaming === false` branch, extending it with tool-call and reasoning-content handling. - The streaming path is completely unchanged; the guard only fires on explicit `false`, so `undefined` (the common default) continues to stream normally.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The change is well-scoped behind an explicit supportsStreaming === false guard that does not affect any existing streaming provider. The non-streaming fallback correctly awaits a standard completion, maps all four chunk types, and returns early. The non-streaming path faithfully mirrors the structure of the pre-existing openai-native.ts fallback and is gated so no streaming provider is affected. The reasoning-before-text ordering issue is limited to the intersection of providers that both disable streaming and emit reasoning_content, which is an uncommon combination in practice. apps/vscode/src/core/api/providers/openai.ts — specifically the order in which reasoning and text chunks are yielded in the new non-streaming block.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/vscode/src/core/api/providers/openai.ts | Adds a non-streaming fallback path (lines 139-194) that correctly handles text, tool calls, usage, and reasoning_content; reasoning is emitted after text (reversed from streaming order). |

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a long-standing MCP tool-routing regression by replacing the per-run `nanoid(5)` uid in `getMcpServerKey` with a deterministic identifier derived from the server name: a sanitised alphanumeric prefix combined with a DJB2 hash of the full server name as a base-36 suffix. - **Root cause fixed**: The old random uid was regenerated on every extension restart or server reconnect, so any tool call already in the LLM's context pointed to a key that no longer existed in `mcpServerKeys`, breaking `getMcpServerByKey` routing. - **Determinism**: The new uid is purely a function of the server name — same name always produces the same uid — so previously cached tool IDs remain valid across restarts. - **Collision handling**: Appending the full-name hash as a suffix means two servers that sanitise to the same prefix (e.g. `"my-tools"` and `"my_tools"` → `"mytools"`) still receive distinct uids, addressing the ordering-dependent collision concern raised in prior review.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The change is confined to a single private key-generation method. The new algorithm is purely functional (same input → same output), removes the only non-deterministic dependency (nanoid), and the hash-based collision guard addresses the ordering concern flagged in prior review. Only doc/style nits remain. No files require special attention.
