body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes Ollama tool-calling by gating AI SDK tool injection behind a per-model `\"tools\"` capability check, preventing HTTP 400/500 errors from models that do not support native tool calling. - Adds `requiresExplicitModelToolsCapability: true` to the Ollama builtin spec and introduces `shouldSendRuntimeTools` in `ai-sdk.ts` to enforce the gate at stream time. - Refactors `model-source.ts` and `local-provider-service.ts` to carry `SourceModel` objects (with optional `capabilities[]`) through the full model-fetch and registry-write pipeline, so per-model capabilities from `/api/tags` are persisted alongside the model entry.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The core logic is structurally sound but rests on an assumption about Ollama's API that may not hold for all deployments. The entire tool-routing fix depends on Ollama's /api/tags endpoint returning a per-model capabilities array. Ollama's documentation shows that field only in /api/show, not /api/tags. For any Ollama installation where /api/tags omits capabilities, every model is stored with capabilities: undefined and no Ollama model ever receives tools — a silent, total regression in tool calling with no error surfaced to the user. sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/builtins.ts and sdk/packages/core/src/services/providers/model-source.ts

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/builtins.ts | Adds requiresExplicitModelToolsCapability: true to the Ollama builtin spec; works correctly when Ollama /api/tags returns capabilities per model, but silently disables all tool calls if the endpoint omits that field. | | sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/ai-sdk.ts | Introduces shouldSendRuntimeTools helper gating tool injection on per-model capability; logic is clean but buildToolCallMetadata still uses only providerDisablesExternalToolExecution for executionMode. | | sdk/packages/core/src/services/providers/model-source.ts | Refactors model list parsing to preserve per-model capabilities; toModelCapability normalization only handles the structured-output case and would silently drop other name variations. | | sdk/packages/core/src/services/providers/local-provider-service.ts | Migrates from string-only model IDs to SourceModel objects throughout resolveModels and buildProviderModels, correctly preserving per-model capabilities through add and update flows. | | sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/gateway.test.ts | Adds two focused gateway tests for the new capability gate; correctly verify streamText call with and without tools based on model capability declaration. | | sdk/packages/core/src/services/providers/local-provider-service.test.ts | New test correctly verifies per-model capabilities from a mocked source are preserved in the registry, including filtering out unknown capability strings like completion. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A["Ollama /api/tags fetch"] --> B["parseModelList: extract id + capabilities"] B --> C["resolveModels: merge explicit + fetched"] C --> D["buildProviderModels: model.capabilities ?? fallback"] D --> E["Write to models registry"] E --> F["Gateway stream request"] F --> G{"providerDisablesExternalToolExecution?"} G -- yes --> H["tools = undefined"] G -- no --> I{"requiresExplicitModelToolsCapability?"} I -- no --> J["tools = toAiSdkTools"] I -- yes --> K{"model has 'tools' capability?"} K -- yes --> J K -- no --> H J --> L["streamText with tools"] H --> M["streamText without tools"] ```

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a crash with Amazon Bedrock (and potentially other providers) that reject replayed conversation history containing messages with empty content arrays or whitespace-only string content — a state that can occur after an interrupted task is resumed. The fix replaces empty/whitespace content with an `"ERROR: EMPTY CONTENT"` placeholder text block at two layers: the AI SDK formatter (`ai-sdk-format.ts`) and the agent message codec (`agent-message-codec.ts`). - `EMPTY_CONTENT_TEXT` is defined in `ai-sdk-format.ts` and exported from `@cline/shared` so both packages share the same constant value. - `formatMessagesForAiSdk` now injects the placeholder for empty string and empty-array content before the parts loop, and `normalizeContentBlocks` in the codec now uses `.trim()` so whitespace-only strings also resolve to empty. - New unit tests cover the empty string, whitespace-only string, and empty-array cases at both layers.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change is narrowly scoped to degenerate empty-content messages that would otherwise cause provider rejections, and all normal content paths are unaffected. Both the codec and the AI SDK formatter correctly handle the three empty-content variants (empty array, empty string, whitespace-only string) at both layers, with matching test coverage for each case. The constant is defined once in @cline/shared and imported by @cline/core, keeping a single source of truth. The round-trip through agentMessageToMessageWithMetadata preserves the placeholder correctly, and the normal content fast-paths are unchanged. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR makes `cline doctor` aware of connector and hub-daemon processes that are running but have no corresponding state files, and wires them into `cline doctor --fix` so they can be killed. It also removes the `resolveDefaultCliRpcAddress()` default from every connector's CLI option (making `rpcAddress` optional in shared types) and removes the port-0 fallback from `ensureDetachedHubServer`, letting the daemon always bind its resolved default port. - **Unmanaged connector detection** (`listUnmanagedConnectorProcesses`): scans all `connect`-matching processes and filters them through `isClineCliPrefix` + the connector catalog to identify genuine cline connector processes that lack state files; sensitive flag values are redacted before surfacing in output. - **Orphaned hub-daemon detection** (`listOrphanedHubDaemonProcesses`): finds processes matching `cline-hub-daemon` or `/hub/daemon/entry.ts` and marks any that are not the active, healthy hub as orphaned; both categories are killable via `doctor --fix`. - **`rpcAddress` made optional**: removing the commander default (`resolveDefaultCliRpcAddress()`) corrects an unintended side-effect where connectors were always setting `hasExplicitEndpoint = true`, preventing `rememberRecoverableLocalHubUrl` from being called on the resolved hub URL. - **Build-env-scoped hub owner label**: `resolveSharedHubOwnerContext` now appends the build environment to the owner label (`shared:cline:production` vs `shared:cline:development`), isolating prod and dev hubs from each other.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge; the new detection paths are well-guarded and do not affect the happy path when connectors and hubs are running normally. The new isClineCliPrefix guard correctly rejects non-cline processes before killing them, the rpcAddress optional change preserves functional behaviour via parseHubEndpointOverride(undefined) returning {}, and the orphaned-daemon detection only considers processes outside the active-and-healthy hub set. Tests cover non-cline process exclusion, token redaction, fix-path kill targeting, and the new hub-owner isolation. No files require special attention; the kill-target deduplication in doctor.ts and the isClineCliPrefix launcher list have minor gaps worth a look but do not affect the primary use-cases.

The isClineCliPrefix guard addresses the earlier process-anchor concern by verifying cline binary or known entrypoint paths before classifying a process as a managed connector. | | apps/cli/src/commands/doctor.test.ts | Adds comprehensive test cases for hub daemon orphan detection, unmanaged connector detection with redaction, and fix-path kill logic; non-cline process exclusion (62002) and token-redaction assertions are explicitly verified. | | sdk/packages/shared/src/connectors/options.ts | rpcAddress made optional (string → string | undefined) across all six connector option types; correctly aligns with parseHubEndpointOverride accepting undefined, which returns {} and falls through to default endpoint resolution. | | sdk/packages/core/src/hub/daemon/index.ts | Removes port-0 fallback from both prewarmDetachedHubServer and ensureDetachedHubServer; daemon now always spawns on the resolved default port after retiring an incompatible hub. body:
I think we should restore the non-explicit-port fallback before merging. I originally thought this was mostly a narrow follow-up, but after tracing the startup and upgrade path more carefully, I think the fallback is cheap insurance, was already tested behavior, and protects an awkward hub upgrade edge case.

Plain-English context for folks less familiar with this system:

Cline has a local background server called the hub. It is a WebSocket server running on the user's machine. CLI commands and connector processes talk to it so they can share runtime state and avoid starting everything from scratch each time.

When the hub starts, it writes a discovery record. Conceptually that record says:

```txt
I am running at ws://127.0.0.1:25463/hub
My pid is 12345
Here is my auth token
```

Later CLI processes read that discovery record so they can reconnect to the existing hub instead of starting another one.

This PR changes the shared discovery owner to include the build environment. That seems directionally right because it avoids production and development builds accidentally sharing the same hub/discovery record. But it also means there can be a transition state where:

```txt
An old hub is still running on the default port.
The new CLI looks in a different discovery location.
The new CLI does not find the old hub's discovery record/token.
```

So the old hub process can still exist, but the new CLI may not have the discovery record it needs to safely reuse it.

The old behavior handled this kind of situation defensively:

```txt
If the default hub port is busy, and the user did not explicitly ask for that port,
start the new detached hub on any free port instead.
```

That is what `port: 0` does. It lets the operating system pick an available port. Then the new hub writes a fresh discovery record, and future CLI processes know where to find it.

The new behavior removes that fallback:

```txt
If the default hub port is busy, still try to start the new detached hub on that same default port.
```

If the old hub is still occupying that port, the new detached daemon can fail to bind. Since detached daemon startup goes through `startHubWebSocketServer()` directly, it does not get the `allowPortFallback` behavior from `ensureHubWebSocketServer()`. Then `ensureDetachedHubServer()` can sit waiting for discovery and eventually time out.

The risky path is roughly:

```txt
1. Old hub is already listening on the default port.
2. New CLI cannot find or use the old discovery record.
3. New CLI probes the default URL and sees something there.
4. If that hub looks compatible, retireIncompatibleHub() leaves it alone.
5. New CLI tries to spawn another detached hub on the same fixed default port.
6. The new daemon cannot bind because the old hub owns the port.
7. ensureDetachedHubServer() times out waiting for a new discovery record.
```

One subtle detail: hub compatibility uses hub `buildId`, which appears to default to the `@cline/core` package version rather than the CLI package version. So I do not think we should assume every CLI upgrade necessarily makes the old hub look incompatible. That does not mean we need to solve every old-hub compatibility question in this PR, but it does make the removed port fallback more important as a safety net.

I think the important distinction is:

```txt
Reusing an old same-build hub may already have been possible before this PR.

But failing to start a replacement hub because the old one blocks the default port is the new risk introduced by removing the fallback.
```

The previous fallback was small and already covered by a test. Restoring it keeps explicit port behavior strict while preserving the safer managed/default startup behavior.

Something like this would preserve the old behavior:

```ts
const hasExplicitPort =
	endpointOverrides.port !== undefined || !!process.env.CLINE_HUB_PORT?.trim();

const spawnEndpoint =
	!hasExplicitPort && endpoint.port !== 0
		? { ...endpoint, port: 0 }
		: endpoint;

await spawnDetachedHubServerWithRetry(workspaceRoot, spawnEndpoint);
```

That means:

```txt
User explicitly sets CLINE_HUB_PORT or --rpc-address:
  Respect it strictly.

Cline is managing the default hub port automatically:
  If the default port is already occupied, fall back to an ephemeral port.
```

I think restoring this before merge is the safest option. It keeps the intended prod/dev discovery separation while avoiding a class of "I upgraded and Cline got stuck waiting for hub startup" failures.

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR fixes two distinct bugs in the connector layer: (1) messages from different chat threads routed to the wrong active session because participant identity was used as the primary conversation binding key, and (2) stale persisted session IDs being reused after a hub restart without verifying the session still exists. - **Thread-scoped routing**: Bindings, queue keys, and active-turn lookups now use `thread.id` as the primary key across all six adapters (Slack, Discord, Telegram, Google Chat, Linear, WhatsApp). Participant key is retained only as searchable metadata, and the cross-thread steer guard adds a `threadId` equality check before treating a follow-up as a steer message. - **Stale session validation**: `getOrCreateSessionId` now calls `client.getSession(existing)` before reusing a persisted session ID; if the hub returns `undefined` the stored ID is cleared and a fresh session is started. - **Backward-compat schedule delivery**: The new `findBindingForDeliveryTarget` helper provides a layered lookup (exact binding key → participant key scan → thread ID → participant key) so pre-existing schedules whose `bindingKey` was a participant key continue to resolve correctly.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The changes are safe to merge. The root-cause fix (thread-ID as binding key) is well-scoped, backward compatibility for existing schedules is handled through a layered delivery-target lookup, and two new regression tests cover the exact failure modes described in the PR. All six adapters receive the same mechanical change (queue key → thread.id, schedule delivery → findBindingForDeliveryTarget), the cross-thread steer guard addition is narrow and well-tested, and the stale session recovery path has a dedicated test that validates the getSession → clear → start-fresh flow. The only noted concern is a redundant lookup path in findBindingForDeliveryTarget that has no observable effect on correctness. No files require special attention; thread-bindings.ts has the most complexity from the keying overhaul but is covered by targeted unit tests.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/cli/src/connectors/thread-bindings.ts | Core binding store refactored: keying changed from participant key to thread ID, participant-key dedup loop removed, findBindingForThread DM-fallback restricted to isDM === true, new findBindingForDeliveryTarget helper added for schedule backward compat. | | apps/cli/src/connectors/session-runtime.ts | Adds hub-side session validation before reusing a persisted session ID; stale IDs are cleared and a fresh session is started. getSession call lacks error handling (previously flagged). | | apps/cli/src/connectors/connector-host.ts | Active-turn steer guard now checks turn.threadId === input.thread.id; deliveryBindingKey in schedule metadata changed from participant key to thread ID; loadThreadState call in schedule list removed in favor of direct thread.id comparison. | | apps/cli/src/connectors/adapters/slack.ts | Queue key simplified to thread.id; schedule delivery updated to use findBindingForDeliveryTarget; loadThreadState for participant-key-based queue key removed (state still loaded for teamId). | | apps/cli/src/connectors/connector-host.test.ts | Two new regression tests added: cross-thread active session isolation and stale session recovery. Existing tests updated to reflect bindingKey: threadId schema. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant A as Adapter (Slack/Telegram/etc.) participant CH as connector-host participant TB as thread-bindings participant SR as session-runtime participant Hub as Hub Client Note over A,Hub: New message arrives on thread-1 A->>CH: "handleConnectorUserTurn(thread.id=thread-1)" CH->>TB: loadThreadState(thread-1) TB-->>CH: sessionId stale-or-existing CH->>CH: "activeTurns.get(thread-1) OR find(turn.sessionId && turn.threadId === thread-1)" alt Active turn found for THIS thread CH->>Hub: sendRuntimeSession(steer) else No active turn for this thread CH->>SR: getOrCreateSessionId(thread-1) SR->>Hub: getSession(stale-or-existing) alt Session exists in hub Hub-->>SR: sessionId existing SR->>TB: persistMergedThreadState(sessionId: existing) SR-->>CH: existing else Session missing (hub restarted) Hub-->>SR: undefined SR->>TB: persistMergedThreadState(sessionId: undefined) SR->>Hub: startRuntimeSession() Hub-->>SR: sessionId new-session SR->>TB: persistMergedThreadState(sessionId: new-session) SR-->>CH: new-session end CH->>Hub: sendRuntimeSession(normal turn) end ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 1 code review issue. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 1 apps/cli/src/connectors/thread-bindings.ts:480-511 **`findBindingForParticipantKey` called with a thread ID when exact binding key misses** When `input.bindingKey` is a new-style thread ID (e.g. `"C123:111.222"`) and `bindings[bindingKey]` is absent (the binding was evicted or the store was reset), the code falls through to `findBindingForParticipantKey(bindings, bindingKey)`. That call scans every binding for `participantKey === "C123:111.222"`, which will never match a real participant key. The result is silently `undefined`, so the function continues to the `threadId` branch and the final `participantKey` fallback — which is the correct recovery path. The concern is that after the `findBindingForParticipantKey` no-op, the `threadId` branch tries `bindings[threadId]` where `threadId === bindingKey` (they're the same value for new schedules). That lookup is identical to the one that already failed above. There is no observable bug, but the two duplicate lookups add noise; the `findBindingForParticipantKey` call inside the `bindingKey` block is dead code when `bindingKey` is a thread ID. `````

Greptile Summary

Adds a persisted `autoUpdateEnabled` global setting (defaulting to `true`) that gates CLI startup auto-updates, while leaving manual `cline update` calls unaffected. Toggle UI is wired into both the Cline Hub General settings view and the TUI `cline config` General tab via the shared `global-settings` service. - **Core change**: `GlobalSettingsSchema` gains `autoUpdateEnabled: boolean` (default `true`, `.catch(true)`); `isAutoUpdateEnabledGlobally` / `setAutoUpdateEnabledGlobally` helpers follow the existing `telemetryOptOut` pattern exactly. - **CLI guard**: `autoUpdateOnStartup` gains a third early-exit via `isAutoUpdateEnabledGlobally()`; `checkForUpdates` (manual path) is intentionally not gated. - **UI**: Hub settings view adds an optimistic-update toggle with rollback; TUI config view reads the setting synchronously at mount and writes on toggle.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge; the new guard is correctly placed and the overall feature works as described, but one test claims to cover the new guard without actually reaching it. The test 'skips startup auto update when disabled globally' would pass even if the isAutoUpdateEnabledGlobally() call were deleted — the function exits earlier at the !updateCommand check because CLINE_WRAPPER_PATH is not set. This leaves the guard untested and vulnerable to silent regression. apps/cli/src/commands/update.test.ts — the startup auto-update skip test needs a valid wrapper path so the new guard is what actually prevents the fetch.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | sdk/packages/core/src/services/global-settings.ts | Adds autoUpdateEnabled boolean field (default true) to GlobalSettingsSchema and exposes isAutoUpdateEnabledGlobally / setAutoUpdateEnabledGlobally helpers; follows the existing telemetryOptOut pattern exactly. | | apps/cli/src/commands/update.ts | Adds isAutoUpdateEnabledGlobally() guard as a third early-exit in autoUpdateOnStartup; checkForUpdates (manual path) is correctly left untouched. | | apps/cli/src/commands/update.test.ts | The new 'skips startup auto update when disabled globally' test passes vacuously — no CLINE_WRAPPER_PATH means getInstallationInfo returns UNKNOWN with no updateCommand, so autoUpdateOnStartup exits before the isAutoUpdateEnabledGlobally check is relevant. | | apps/cline-hub/src/server/desktop-commands.ts | Adds set_auto_update_enabled command handler with boolean validation; mirrors the set_telemetry_opt_out pattern and returns fresh readGlobalSettings() on success. | | apps/cline-hub/src/webview/src/components/views/settings/settings-view.tsx | Adds auto-update toggle to GeneralSettingsContent with optimistic UI, rollback on error, and loading/saving disabled states; follows the existing telemetry toggle pattern. | | apps/cli/src/tui/views/config-view.tsx | Adds auto-update toggle to TUI General tab; reads initial value synchronously from readGlobalSettings() and persists via setAutoUpdateEnabledGlobally. | | sdk/packages/core/src/services/global-settings.test.ts | Adds autoUpdateEnabled to all existing expected objects and a new dedicated round-trip test; thorough coverage of schema defaults and persistence. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[CLI startup] --> B{IS_DEV=true?} B -- yes --> Z[Skip auto-update] B -- no --> C{CLINE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1?} C -- yes --> Z C -- no --> D{isAutoUpdateEnabledGlobally?} D -- false --> Z D -- true --> E{updateCommand available?} E -- no --> Z E -- yes --> F[fetch latest version from npm] F --> G{newer version?} G -- no --> Z G -- yes --> H[spawn detached install process] H --> I[restartHubServerIfRunning] J[User: cline update] --> K[checkForUpdates] K --> L[fetch latest version] L --> M[run install command interactively] N[Hub UI / TUI toggle] --> O[setAutoUpdateEnabledGlobally] O --> P[writes global-settings.json] P --> D ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 1 code review issue. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 1 apps/cli/src/commands/update.test.ts:125-138 **Test passes vacuously — `isAutoUpdateEnabledGlobally()` guard is never reached** `autoUpdateOnStartup` bails out at `if (!updateCommand) return` before the async IIFE where `fetch` would be called. Because `CLINE_WRAPPER_PATH` is not set in this test, `getInstallationInfo` returns `{ packageManager: UNKNOWN }` with no `updateCommand`, so the early return fires before the `isAutoUpdateEnabledGlobally()` check even matters. The `fetch` spy would never be called even if the new guard were removed entirely. To make this test actually exercise the `autoUpdateEnabled` guard, set `CLINE_WRAPPER_PATH` to a path under `node_modules/` so `getInstallationInfo` returns a valid `updateCommand`, then confirm `fetch` is still not called when `autoUpdateEnabled: false`. `````

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a silent content-drop bug in `groupLowStakesTools` where any `text` message arriving after a low-stakes tool group had started was discarded via `continue`, making agent content (e.g., a code review written after `readFile` calls) invisible to the user. - **Core fix** (`messageUtils.ts`): When `messageType === "text"` and `hasTools` is `true`, the old `continue` is replaced with `commitToolGroup() + flushPending() + result.push(message) + continue`, so the tool group is sealed and the text is rendered as a new row below it. - **Tests** (`messageUtils.test.ts`): The previously incorrect assertion ("ignores text") is corrected, and a targeted regression test is added for the exact issue-9719 scenario (`text → readFile → readFile → analysis-text → completion_result`).

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change is a one-branch correction inside a deterministic grouping function, the existing state machine is otherwise untouched, and a regression test directly covers the previously broken path. The diff is small and surgical: a single `continue` replaced with three lines that correctly seal the active tool group before rendering the text message. All other branches of `groupLowStakesTools` are unmodified. The fix is consistent with every other place in the function that calls `commitToolGroup` + `flushPending` before emitting a non-tool row, and the two tests exercise the exact code path. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/chat/chat-view/utils/messageUtils.ts | Single-line logic change replacing a silent `continue` with `commitToolGroup() + flushPending() + result.push(message)` to surface text content that follows a low-stakes tool group. | | apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/chat/chat-view/utils/messageUtils.test.ts | Updates the corrected test and adds a regression test for issue #9719. | | .changeset/fix-content-before-attempt-completion.md | Patch-level changeset entry; no issues. |

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a bug where MCP metadata requests (`tools/list`, `resources/list`, `resources/templates/list`, `prompts/list`, `prompts/get`) always used the hardcoded `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` (5 s) regardless of the user's `timeout` setting in `cline_mcp_settings.json`, causing slow-starting servers to fail initialization even when the user had explicitly configured a longer timeout. - **`getTimeoutForServer` helper** — reads `config.timeout` from the raw stored JSON, clamps it to `MIN_MCP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` via `Math.max`, converts to ms, and falls back to the supplied default when the field is absent or the JSON is malformed. - **Metadata requests** — all five list/get call sites now delegate to `getTimeoutForServer(connection)`, which falls back to 5 s when no user timeout is set, preserving the original fail-fast behaviour for unconfigured servers. - **`callTool` refactor** — the previously inline config-parsing block is replaced by `getTimeoutForServer(connection, secondsToMs(DEFAULT_MCP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS))`, eliminating duplicated logic while keeping the 60 s default for tool calls.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the helper correctly reads, clamps, and converts the user-configured timeout for all affected call sites, and the fallback behaviour for unconfigured servers is preserved. The core change is a small, well-scoped helper that replaces a hardcoded constant with the user's configured value. The Math.max / MIN_MCP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS clamp is in place, JSON parse failures are caught and logged, and the default paths for both metadata requests (5 s) and tool calls (60 s) are unchanged. Greptile Summary

This PR restores the ephemeral-port fallback that was removed from the hub daemon startup path by a parent cleanup PR. Without it, the detached daemon could be spawned on the same default port already held by an older hub, causing it to fail binding and `ensureDetachedHubServer` to time out waiting for discovery. - **`daemon/index.ts`**: Introduces `hasExplicitPort` in both `prewarmDetachedHubServer` and `ensureDetachedHubServer`. When no explicit port is configured (neither from the call argument nor from `CLINE_HUB_PORT`), the daemon is spawned with `port: 0` so the OS assigns a free port; explicit ports are passed through unchanged. - **`client/index.ts`**: Adds `resolveManagedDetachedHubSpawnEndpoint()` which returns `{ port: 0 }` for managed startups without an explicit port, and `undefined` (no endpoint override) when `CLINE_HUB_PORT` is set, letting the env var propagate to the daemon through the inherited environment. - **Tests**: The occupied-default-port regression test is restored in `daemon/index.test.ts`; a new explicit-port fixed-bind test is added; `client/index.test.ts` adds matching coverage for both the host+pathname override and explicit-port strict paths, plus proper env-var teardown in `afterEach`.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge; the change is a targeted restoration of a defensive startup behaviour with matching regression tests. Both changed functions correctly compute hasExplicitPort before resolving the endpoint and apply shouldUseFallbackPort consistently. The client-side helper gates only on CLINE_HUB_PORT, with host/pathname propagating via the inherited daemon env, which matches the test assertions. No pre-existing behaviours are removed; the regression test that was dropped in the parent PR is now restored. No issues were found that affect correctness, data integrity, or security. No files require special attention.

body:
Greptile Summary

Fixes a TUI transcript duplication bug by scoping the agent-event subscription to the active session ID instead of subscribing globally to the session manager. The subscription is now created (or rotated) in `applyStartedSession` whenever a session starts or resumes, and torn down in `clearActiveSession` when the active session is cleared. - `subscribeToAgentEvents` is called with `{ sessionId: started.sessionId }` inside `applyStartedSession`, replacing the single global call that was made once at manager creation time. - `clearActiveSession` now calls `unsubscribeAgent()` before zeroing the active session ID, ensuring no events from the outgoing session leak into the next TUI transcript. - A focused regression test asserts the session-scoped subscription contract; existing tests for reset, resume, fork, and recovery scenarios continue to pass.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge. The routing fix is logically sound and all code paths that start or resume a session go through applyStartedSession, so the scoped subscription is consistently applied. The subscription rotation in applyStartedSession correctly unsubscribes before re-subscribing, and clearActiveSession tears down the subscription before zeroing the session ID. The `if (sessionManager)` guard inside applyStartedSession could silently skip both the unsubscribe and the re-subscribe in a scenario that should be unreachable in practice, leaving unsubscribeAgent in a stale state. The regression test validates the initial subscription scope but does not cover session-transition rotation, so a future regression in that path would go undetected. apps/cli/src/runtime/interactive/session-runtime.ts — the `if (sessionManager)` guard in applyStartedSession is worth a second look; apps/cli/src/runtime/interactive/session-runtime.test.ts — subscription rotation across session transitions is not exercised.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/cli/src/runtime/interactive/session-runtime.ts | Core fix: agent-event subscription moved from manager creation (global) to applyStartedSession/clearActiveSession (per-session), with sessionId filter. Checkpoint restore, fork, and resume paths all flow through applyStartedSession so they also get the scoped subscription. Minor: applyStartedSession's `if (sessionManager)` guard can silently leave unsubscribeAgent in an inconsistent state if the guard ever fires. | | apps/cli/src/runtime/interactive/session-runtime.test.ts | Mocks for subscribeToAgentEvents/subscribeToPendingPromptEvents promoted to hoisted named mocks; new regression test asserts session-scoped subscription. The test covers the happy path but not subscription rotation across session transitions. |

The live `unsubscribeAgent` reference is then neither called nor replaced, so the *next* call to `clearActiveSession` will attempt to invoke the stale unsubscriber a second time (after it was already orphaned). In practice `sessionManager` is always set before any path that reaches `applyStartedSession`, but the asymmetry between `clearActiveSession` (which always resets the variable) and `applyStartedSession` (which only does so under the guard) is a maintenance trap worth closing with an unconditional early-return or an assertion.

Greptile Summary

This PR restricts the `openExternal` hostbridge handler to only allow `http`, `https`, and `mailto` URI schemes, blocking dangerous schemes like `command:` that could let an AI agent trigger arbitrary VS Code commands. Regression tests are added for the happy path and the blocked `command:` case. - `openExternal.ts`: Introduces `ALLOWED_EXTERNAL_URI_SCHEMES` and rejects any URI whose scheme is not in the set before calling `vscode.env.openExternal`. - `openExternal.test.ts`: New test file verifying that `https` URIs pass through and `command:` URIs throw with the expected message; `http` and `mailto` allowlist entries are untested.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge — the core fix correctly blocks `command:` and other dangerous schemes before calling `vscode.env.openExternal`. The allowlist logic is straightforward and the ordering (parse → validate → open) is correct. The two open questions are whether `mailto:` with pre-filled fields is an acceptable capability for an AI agent, and whether non-strict URI parsing could silently swallow malformed input. Neither blocks the intended security fix, but both deserve a deliberate decision before the PR lands. `openExternal.ts` deserves a second look on the `mailto` decision and strict-mode parsing.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/vscode/src/hosts/vscode/hostbridge/env/openExternal.ts | Adds a URI scheme allowlist (`http`, `https`, `mailto`) before calling `vscode.env.openExternal`, correctly blocking `command:` and other dangerous schemes; `mailto` phishing risk and non-strict URI parsing are worth reviewing. | | apps/vscode/src/hosts/vscode/hostbridge/env/openExternal.test.ts | New test file covering the happy path (`https`) and a blocked `command:` URI; missing coverage for the `http` and `mailto` schemes that are explicitly in the allowlist. |

Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 3 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 3 apps/vscode/src/hosts/vscode/hostbridge/env/openExternal.test.ts:15-21 **Allowlist coverage gap in tests** The test for "opens browser-safe URL schemes" only exercises `https`. Both `http` and `mailto` are in `ALLOWED_EXTERNAL_URI_SCHEMES` but have no corresponding test. If either were accidentally removed from the set, no test would catch the regression. A minimal additional assertion (e.g. stub is called for `mailto:user@example.com` and `http://example.com`) would close this gap. ### Issue 2 of 3 apps/vscode/src/hosts/vscode/hostbridge/env/openExternal.ts:4 **`mailto:` could be abused for phishing via pre-filled body/subject** `mailto:victim@corp.com?subject=Urgent&body=Click+here+http%3A%2F%2Fmalicious.example` is a valid `mailto` URI that will open the user's default mail client with attacker-controlled content. If an AI agent can call `openExternal` with arbitrary values, allowing `mailto` gives it a social-engineering vector (pre-filled phishing emails) even though the scheme itself is technically "safe" from a code-execution standpoint. Consider whether this trade-off is intentional, or whether the scheme list should be restricted to `http`/`https` only. ### Issue 3 of 3 apps/vscode/src/hosts/vscode/hostbridge/env/openExternal.ts:7 `vscode.Uri.parse` is called in non-strict mode by default, which silently ignores malformed URIs instead of throwing. Passing `true` as the second argument enables strict mode and rejects clearly invalid input early, giving callers a more actionable error before the allowlist check is even reached. ```suggestion const uri = vscode.Uri.parse(request.value, true) ``` `````

Greptile Summary

This PR adds a configurable thinking-mode dropdown to the Ollama provider settings, letting users choose between Default (omit the parameter), Enabled/Disabled (boolean), or the three `gpt-oss`-specific effort levels (`high`/`medium`/`low`). The implementation is well-structured: the proto field is correctly typed as `optional string`, the lookup table in `OllamaHandler` maps stored strings to the values the Ollama JS library expects (`boolean | "high" | "medium" | "low"`), and the state default of `undefined` means the `think` parameter is omitted for users who never touch the setting. - **`api-configuration-conversion.ts`**: `ollamaThinking` is written into the proto store (`convertApiConfigurationToProto`, line 462) but the reciprocal read in `convertProtoToApiConfiguration` (~line 643) is still absent, so the user's choice reverts to `undefined` on every extension reload. - **`ollama.ts`**: The spread guard `this.options.ollamaThinking !== undefined` passes when the stored value is `\"\"` (Default), resulting in `{ think: undefined }` being added to the request object before JSON serialization drops it — functionally harmless but a minor clarity concern. - **`OllamaProvider.tsx`**: Dropdown, bindings, and option values all look correct; the `gpt-oss` effort-level labels accurately reflect the Ollama API's documented model-specific behaviour.

Confidence Score: 3/5

Not ready to merge — the thinking-mode preference is silently discarded on every extension reload because the deserialization side of the proto round-trip was not updated. The feature itself is correctly wired end-to-end in memory: the dropdown, state key, handler option, and lookup table all behave as intended. However, `convertProtoToApiConfiguration` never reads `ollamaThinking` back from the proto store, so the user's chosen value is lost every time the extension reloads and re-hydrates its configuration. Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a class of `400 Assistant message must contain either 'content' or 'tool_calls'` errors caused by OpenAI-compatible providers receiving reasoning-only streamed responses or history messages that contained binary/control characters. The fix has two pillars: adding `sanitizeTextForModelInput` to strip ANSI escapes and unsafe control characters from all prompt-bound text, and converting thinking-only assistant history entries into valid text content instead of leaving the message empty. - Adds `sanitizeTextForModelInput` and `extractReasoningText` utilities, applied consistently at tool-result construction, command output return sites, OpenAI-format conversion, and R1-format conversion. - In `openai-format.ts`, thinking blocks are now bucketed separately and their text is used as a `content` fallback when the assistant message would otherwise have no content and no tool calls; a `"[redacted reasoning]"` sentinel covers the redacted-thinking case. - In `index.ts`, `hasReasoningContent` is added to the `assistantHasContent` guard so reasoning-only streamed turns are stored in history and don't trigger the empty-message path.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge. The core logic — converting thinking-only assistant history to text content and stripping control characters from prompt-bound strings — is correct and well-tested. The refactor in `index.ts` that hoists `reasonsHandler` calls is safe because `reasonsHandler` was already in scope from line 2800. All changed code paths are covered by new unit tests. The regex handles both CSI and OSC escape sequences (the OSC test confirms this). The four sanitization call-sites in `CommandOrchestrator` each operate on distinct code paths with no double-application. The only gap is the `reasoning_content` field in `addReasoningContent` (unchanged code), which is a minor coverage hole rather than a regression. No files require special attention. The `r1-format.ts` `addReasoningContent` function (not modified by this PR) is the only place where thinking content flows into a provider payload without sanitization.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/vscode/src/utils/string.ts | Adds `sanitizeTextForModelInput` (strips ANSI/control chars, preserves normal whitespace) and `extractReasoningText` (collects and sanitizes `reasoning.text` entries). The ANSI regex covers both CSI and OSC sequences (verified by the new OSC test), and the control-character class correctly preserves TAB/LF/CR. | | apps/vscode/src/core/api/transform/openai-format.ts | Separates thinking blocks from `nonToolMessages`, computes `thinkingContent` from them, and uses it as a fallback `content` when the assistant message has no text and no tool calls — preventing the "must contain either content or tool_calls" 400 error. Also sanitizes all text paths (tool results, text blocks, reasoning_detail entries). | | apps/vscode/src/core/api/transform/r1-format.ts | Adds thinking-block handling with a summary fallback (via `extractReasoningText`) and sanitizes all text content paths. The `addReasoningContent` helper is unchanged and does not sanitize `reasoning_content`, leaving a minor coverage gap for DeepSeek Reasoner. | | apps/vscode/src/core/task/index.ts | Hoists `redactedThinkingContent` and `thinkingBlock` to before the `assistantHasContent` check, and extends that check with `hasReasoningContent`. The `reasonsHandler` variable was already in scope at line 2800, so the hoist is safe. | | apps/vscode/src/core/task/tools/utils/ToolResultUtils.ts | Extracts `sanitizeToolResponseContent` as a private static that sanitizes both string and array-of-text tool responses, then applies it before building the history block. The description string is separately sanitized via `sanitizeTextForModelInput`. | | apps/vscode/src/integrations/terminal/CommandOrchestrator.ts | Sanitizes command output at each of the four distinct exit paths (two early cancellations, the timeout branch, and the main path). Each path calls `sanitizeTextForModelInput` exactly once on its own `result` variable, so there is no double-sanitization. | | apps/vscode/src/utils/string.test.ts | Adds coverage for `sanitizeTextForModelInput` (ANSI/control stripping, OSC sequences, whitespace preservation) and `extractReasoningText` (sanitize + join, non-array guard). Tests are straightforward and match the implementation. | | apps/vscode/src/core/api/transform/__tests__/thinking-traces.test.ts | Adds `convertToOpenAiMessages` thinking-only history test, plus two `convertToR1Format` tests (non-empty thinking and empty-thinking-with-summary fallback). All assertions are consistent with the new behavior. | | apps/vscode/src/core/api/transform/__tests__/tool-parsing.test.ts | Adds a test verifying that ANSI and NUL characters are stripped from tool-result content when converted to OpenAI format. |

Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 1 apps/vscode/src/core/api/transform/r1-format.ts:36-48 **`reasoning_content` not sanitized in `addReasoningContent`** The PR sanitizes thinking text in `convertToR1Format` (which turns it into regular text content), but `addReasoningContent` maps thinking blocks directly to `reasoning_content` without calling `sanitizeTextForModelInput`. Greptile Summary

This PR replaces the temporary string-matching approach to Cline-specific provider errors with a structured `SdkErrorInfo` metadata pipeline that flows from the provider stream all the way to the CLI renderer. It introduces `SdkErrorInfo` types in `@cline/shared`, a Cline-specific error parser in `@cline/llms`, propagates the metadata through `AgentRuntime` finish events and the `RuntimeEventAdapter`, and switches the CLI TUI and text-event output to render credits-depleted and auth-required states as purpose-built UI blocks instead of raw error strings. - **`SdkErrorInfo` pipeline**: new `error-info.ts` types and guards in `@cline/shared` propagate structured error metadata from AI SDK `onError`/catch through `AgentModelEvent.finish → AgentRuntime.lastErrorInfo → run-failed event → AgentErrorEvent → ChatEntry`. - **Cline error parser**: `cline-errors.ts` walks nested error objects with a WeakSet cycle guard, extracting `code`, `status`, `requestId`, and detail fields; `cline.ts` wraps the existing OpenAI-compatible provider with this resolver. - **CLI rendering**: `special-errors.ts` maps `SdkErrorInfo` to typed `SpecialErrorDisplay` variants; `chat-entry.tsx` and `events.ts` switch on these to render credits-depleted blocks with a dashboard link and auth-required prompts pointing to `/account`, while unknown errors fall back to the existing generic path.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change is additive metadata threading with no mutations to existing data shapes beyond new optional fields. Every layer of the new pipeline (provider parser, agent runtime state, event adapter, CLI renderer) has dedicated unit tests covering the key paths, including double-encoded JSON payloads, thrown auth errors, and both text and JSON output modes. The structural changes are all opt-in optional fields on existing events and run results, so callers that don't look for errorInfo see no behavioral difference. No files require special attention.

Well-structured with correct discriminated-union design. | | sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/cline-errors.ts | New file implementing deep structured-error parsing from nested AI SDK error objects. WeakSet cycle guard is correct; DETAIL_IDENTITY_KEYS and DETAIL_STRUCTURAL_KEYS exclusion logic is consistent. | | sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/ai-sdk.ts | Refactors capturedError from {current: string} to {error, message}, adds resolveAiSdkProviderError helper, and threads errorInfo through emitAiSdkEvents and the outer catch. streamErrorInfo is guarded with if (!streamErrorInfo) to prevent overwrites. | | sdk/packages/agents/src/agent-runtime.ts | Adds lastErrorInfo state, populates it from finish events (error reason only), and falls back to getSdkErrorInfo on thrown errors. Greptile Summary

This PR adds `cline-pass` as a new built-in provider that reuses Cline's WorkOS OAuth credentials while maintaining its own dynamically-fetched model list. It introduces a `storageProviderId` indirection in the auth registry and token manager so that a separate provider can share a single OAuth token store, and extends `ProviderSettingsManager` to merge auth fields from the storage provider on read. - **Auth sharing**: `createClineAuthHandler` registers both `cline` and `cline-pass` against the same WorkOS login/refresh functions. Credentials are stored under the `cline` key; `resolveProviderSettings` in `ProviderSettingsManager` transparently merges auth/baseUrl into any cline-pass read, fixing the bypass issue noted in the prior review. - **Model catalog**: A new `catalog-cline-recommended.ts` module fetches cline-pass models from the Cline API at catalog-generation time and enriches them with capabilities from the matched OpenRouter entry. `firstGeneratedModelId` now returns `""` instead of `undefined` when the catalog is absent, mitigating the crash risk raised in the prior review. - **Session bootstrap**: `applyInitialOAuthCredentials` on `LocalRuntimeHost` resolves OAuth tokens before a session starts, so cline-pass sessions with no explicit `apiKey` get a valid token injected upfront.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge for production users; the one unresolved gap is in the catalog-generation script rather than in the runtime path. The three bugs identified in the prior review (single-flight returning the wrong provider identity, getLastUsedProviderSettings bypassing auth resolution, and firstGeneratedModelId returning undefined) have all been addressed. The remaining open issue is that when the Cline recommended-models API call fails during catalog generation, no warning is emitted — the catalog is written silently without cline-pass entries. In the worst case this leads to an empty defaultModelId for the clinePass builtin and a broken model picker for that provider on the next build, but it does not affect running sessions whose catalog was generated successfully. sdk/packages/llms/scripts/generate-models.ts — the cline-recommended catch block lacks a console.warn, so partial catalog failures are invisible during CI runs.

### Please revert the apps/vscode formatting churn

Of the +4,703/-3,144 diff, roughly 3,650 insertions across 15 files in `apps/vscode/` are pure formatting noise: semicolons added, reflow to ~80 columns, `import` -> `import type`, trailing commas. I verified this mechanically by formatting both sides with the repo's own biome config and word-diffing the result: the residue is exclusively `type` keywords and commas, zero logic changes. Two files (`precompact-executor.ts`, `message-filter.ts`) are byte-identical after formatting alone.

The reformat also contradicts the project's own config: `apps/vscode/biome.jsonc` specifies `semicolons: "asNeeded"` and `lineWidth: 130`, while these files now have semicolons at ~80 columns, so it looks like a different formatter (default prettier/biome settings) ran over them. `apps/vscode/src/core/task/index.ts` alone has ~3,330 churned lines, which will conflict with every in-flight PR touching the task runner and pollute blame. Checking these 15 files out from main should drop the diff to ~1,000 real lines.

### Catalog regen bundles unrelated drift

The `catalog.generated.ts` regen removes ~14 models unrelated to this PR (`zai-org/GLM-5`, the moonshotai Kimi turbo/K2.5 variants, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2` variants, the Qwen `-fast` variants, `PrimeIntellect/INTELLECT-3`, etc.) and adds `kimi-k2.7-code`. Users with saved configs pointing at removed model ids may be affected. Consider regenerating on main as a separate PR, or at least calling the removals out explicitly here.

### Silent failure path in generate-models.ts

A failed fetch of the cline recommended-models endpoint only aborts generation if the entire catalog is empty. Otherwise the script silently produces a catalog with no `cline-pass` section, and since the spec's `defaultModelId` comes from `firstGeneratedModelId("cline-pass")`, cline-pass would ship with an empty default model. This specific fetch failing should probably fail the script (or at minimum warn loudly).

Related: `firstGeneratedModelId` makes the default model whatever key happens to come first in the generated object. Fine with today's single model (`cline-pass/glm-5.1`), fragile once the server returns more. An explicit default (or a server-marked default) would be sturdier.

### Questions / minor

- cline-pass models inherit full OpenRouter pricing (glm-5.1 at $0.98/$3.08 per Mtok) while display is hidden via `usageCostDisplay: "hide"`. Cost still flows through internal accounting/telemetry; is that intended rather than zeroing it? Also, the OpenRouter capability lookup in `catalog-cline-recommended.ts` matches by bare slug (`glm-5.1`) and the name map is last-write-wins, so two labs shipping the same slug would silently pick the wrong lab's capabilities/pricing.
- `startSession` now resolves OAuth credentials upfront (`applyInitialOAuthCredentials`), so a failed token refresh (expired refresh token, network error) throws out of `startSession` rather than surfacing later at request time. The happy path has a test; the failure path doesn't. Worth confirming CLI/connector callers handle `OAuthReauthRequiredError` from session start gracefully.
- In `resolveProviderSettings`, direct cline-pass settings spread after the shared cline auth, so a stale `apiKey`/`auth` ever written directly under `cline-pass` would shadow the refreshed shared token. No normal flow writes auth there today, but excluding auth fields from the direct overlay would make this bulletproof.
- The `"cline-pass"` literal is independently defined in `builtins.ts`, `local-provider-service.ts`, and `catalog-cline-recommended.ts`, plus hardcoded in `isClineProvider`. `BUILT_IN_PROVIDER.CLINE_PASS` exists; within core/llms it'd be good to reuse it (shared can't import llms, so the duplication there is understandable).

body:
Blocking issue still present after refreshing the branch.

`clineMiniMaxM3GatewayReasoningRule` still hard-codes `input.request.providerId === "cline"`, while the sibling Cline gateway reasoning rules use `isClineProvider(input.request.providerId)`. That means `cline-pass` MiniMax M3 requests miss this rule and can leak the generic thinking/effort options that this rule is meant to suppress.

Current code:

```ts
applies: (input) =>
	input.request.providerId === "cline" && isMiniMaxM3(input),
```

This should use `isClineProvider(input.request.providerId)` so Cline Pass follows the same Cline gateway routing behavior.

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes Azure AI Foundry deployment-style URLs for the CLI by threading `azure.apiVersion` from provider settings all the way through to a lightweight fetch-wrapping layer that appends `?api-version=` exclusively to `/openai/deployments/…` request paths, leaving standard `/openai/v1` URLs untouched. - **Core fetch wrapper** (`openai-compatible.ts`): `createAzureApiVersionFetch` wraps the configured (or global) `fetch` and delegates URL rewriting to `withAzureApiVersion`, which handles all three `FetchInput` variants (`string`, `URL`, `Request`) and skips paths that already carry `api-version`. - **Gateway options bridge** (`handler-factory.ts`): `buildGatewayProviderOptions` now maps `config.azure.apiVersion` / `useIdentity` into provider options, gated by `usesOpenAICompatibleClient`, so no other provider receives Azure-specific keys. - **UI & CLI setup** (`provider-config-fields.ts`, `auth.ts`, TUI onboarding/picker): exposes an optional `azureApiVersion` field for `openai-compatible` in all three setup paths (TUI onboarding, provider-picker dialog, `cline auth --azure-api-version`), with correct clearing semantics via `resolveProviderConfigAzure` returning `{ apiVersion: "" }` which `applySettingsObjectPatch` treats as a key deletion.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the change is narrow and additive, touching only the openai-compatible provider path and the CLI/TUI configuration surfaces. The Azure API version is propagated through a well-tested chain: CLI flag parsing, TUI field wiring, gateway options bridge, and a fetch-wrapping layer. Each segment is covered by focused unit tests. The URL rewriting is gated on the /openai/deployments/ path prefix and the absence of an existing api-version param, so it cannot affect non-Azure or already-versioned requests. The clearing path (empty string → applySettingsObjectPatch deletion) is explicitly verified in tests. No existing provider behavior is altered. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

URL manipulation handles all three FetchInput variants (string, URL, Request) correctly. | | sdk/packages/core/src/services/llms/handler-factory.ts | Adds usesOpenAICompatibleClient guard to map azure.apiVersion and azure.useIdentity into gateway options; gated so non-openai-compatible providers are unaffected. compactOptions already filters undefined values. | | sdk/packages/core/src/services/providers/provider-config-fields.ts | Adds azureApiVersion as an optional ProviderConfigFieldKey and exposes it only for openai-compatible via PROVIDER_CONFIG_FIELD_METADATA; merge mode preserves other fields (apiKey, baseUrl). | | apps/cli/src/tui/utils/provider-config-values.ts | Adds resolveProviderConfigAzure which intentionally returns {apiVersion: ''} for blank input; the empty-string sentinel flows into applySettingsObjectPatch to clear the stored apiVersion. body:
Confirmed against the branch: the runtime fix works when `azure.apiVersion` is set, which flows `settings.azure.apiVersion` -> `config.azure.apiVersion` -> gateway `options.apiVersion`, read by `createAzureApiVersionFetch` in `openai-compatible.ts`. The injection is also correctly gated on the path being under `/openai/deployments/` with no existing `api-version`.

The remaining gap is CLI/TUI setup: there is no menu field to set it. `ProviderConfigFieldKey` has no Azure/API-version key, and for `openai-compatible` only `apiKey` + `baseUrl` are exposed. Both submit paths (`provider-picker.tsx` and onboarding `controller.ts`) persist only `apiKey`/`baseUrl`/`aws`/`sap` and never write `azure`. So a fully menu-only fresh setup can still send a deployment URL with no `api-version` and fail with `Resource not found` unless `providers.json` is edited or seeded separately.

Two follow-ups worth tracking:

1. Add an Azure API version input for `openai-compatible` and wire it through provider settings into `azure.apiVersion`.
2. Document or validate that Base URL should stop at `/openai/deployments/<deployment>`, because a full `.../chat/completions?api-version=...` is not the expected Base URL shape.
